fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-des-mar.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Clos des Maréchaudes
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-des-mar.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-des-mar.summary: The Clos des Maréchaudes is a walled 1.5 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru on the lower slope below Corton Maréchaudes. The wine is a supple, fruity Aloxe.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-des-mar.terroir: Southeast-facing at 220 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton and Corton Les Maréchaudes and beside La Maréchaude and Les Maréchaudes.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-des-mar.nerd_note: It sits among a tight cluster of small premier crus at the eastern foot of the hill.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-du-chap.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Clos du Chapitre
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-du-chap.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-du-chap.summary: The Clos du Chapitre is a walled 1.9 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru at the southern foot of the hill of Corton, next to the Corton Clos des Meix. As the name says, it was a property of a cathedral chapter. Follin-Arbelet, Louis Latour and Génot-Boulanger make it.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-du-chap.terroir: South-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-clos-du-chap.nerd_note: The clos sits just below Corton's Clos des Meix, so the grand cru boundary runs along its wall.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-coutiere.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru La Coutière
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-coutiere.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-coutiere.summary: La Coutière is a 2.5 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru at the eastern foot of the hill, near Ladoix. The wine is soft and fruity.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-coutiere.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton, Corton Les Grandes Lolières and Corton Le Rognet et Corton and beside La Toppe au Vert.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-coutiere.nerd_note: It lies in the commune of Ladoix-Serrigny but is sold as Aloxe-Corton premier cru.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-marechaud.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru La Maréchaude
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-marechaud.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-marechaud.summary: La Maréchaude is a 1.0 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru at the eastern foot of the hill, below Les Maréchaudes. The wine is soft and fruity.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-marechaud.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 220 to 230 m, on brown clay soils. On the map it lies below Les Paulands and beside Clos des Maréchaudes and Les Maréchaudes.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-marechaud.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus of Aloxe-Corton.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-toppe-au-.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru La Toppe au Vert
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-toppe-au-.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-toppe-au-.summary: La Toppe au Vert is a 1.7 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru at the eastern foot of the hill of Corton, below the Corton climat of the same name. The wine is a supple, fruity red.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-toppe-au-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 220 to 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-la-toppe-au-.nerd_note: Its upper edge meets the Corton climats Les Vergennes and La Toppe au Vert, so the same name is both grand cru and premier cru.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-chaillot.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Chaillots blanc
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-chaillot.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-chaillot.summary: Les Chaillots is a 4.6 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru below Corton Grèves and Perrières. Louis Latour is a major holder. The wine is a sturdy, red-fruited Aloxe.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-chaillot.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton and Corton Les Grèves, above Les Fournières and beside Les Valozières.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-chaillot.nerd_note: The name is usually traced to an old word for pebbles, and the soil is indeed stony.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-fournier.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Fournières
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-fournier.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-fournier.summary:
Les Fournières is a 5.6 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru below Corton Perrières, on the southern side of the hill. Tollot-Beaut makes a fine, fruity version.

It lies on the gentle slope below Corton Les Perrières, between Les Chaillots and the Clos du Chapitre. Tollot-Beaut's Fournières, from a family estate in Chorey-lès-Beaune, is the most widely seen and shows the ripe, red-fruited, approachable side of Aloxe.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-fournier.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The slope is gentle, about 6% on average, and the soil is deeper here than on the grand cru above, which is the main reason the wine is rounder and readier.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-fournier.nerd_note: It sits about 30 m below Corton Les Perrières, a measure of how quickly the grand cru gives way to premier cru on the gentler lower slope.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-guerets.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Guérets
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-guerets.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-guerets.summary: Les Guérets is a 2.6 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru at the southern edge of the commune, near Les Vercots. The wine is a soft, red-fruited Aloxe.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-guerets.terroir: Flat, southeast exposure at about 245 m, on brown clay soils. On the map it lies beside Les Vercots.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-marechau.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Maréchaudes
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-marechau.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-marechau.summary: Les Maréchaudes is a 1.3 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru on the lower slope below Corton Maréchaudes, toward Ladoix. The wine is a supple, red-fruited Aloxe.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-marechau.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 220 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton and Corton Les Maréchaudes and beside Clos des Maréchaudes and La Maréchaude.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-marechau.nerd_note: The name appears four times in the classification: a grand cru, two premier crus and a clos.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-moutotte.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Moutottes
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-moutotte.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-moutotte.summary: Les Moutottes is a 1.1 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru on the Ladoix side of the hill, beside the Corton climat of the same name. The wine is firm and red-fruited.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-moutotte.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton, above Les Petites Folières and beside Ladoix's Bois Roussot and Corton Les Moutottes.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-moutotte.nerd_note: Like several neighbours, it lies in Ladoix-Serrigny but takes the Aloxe-Corton name.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-paulands.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Paulands
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-paulands.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-paulands.summary: Les Paulands is a 1.6 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru below Corton Bressandes; the upper part of the lieu-dit is grand cru Corton. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-paulands.terroir: East-facing at 230 to 245 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton, Les Valozières and Corton Les Paulands and beside Corton Les Maréchaudes.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-paulands.nerd_note: The Corton Les Paulands climat sits directly upslope.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-petites-.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Petites Folières
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-petites-.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-petites-.summary: Les Petites Folières is a 1.6 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru on the Ladoix side of the hill. The wine is a supple, red-fruited Aloxe.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-petites-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-petites-.nerd_note: Like several premier crus on this side of the hill, it lies in the commune of Ladoix-Serrigny but is sold as Aloxe-Corton.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-valozier.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Valozières
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-valozier.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-valozier.summary:
Les Valozières is a 6.6 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru just below Corton Bressandes, on the south side of the hill. Its red is firm and spicy, close to a light Corton.

Les Chaillots and Les Paulands lie alongside, and its wines are a good-value glimpse of red Corton: spicy, firm and dark-fruited, ready a few years earlier than the grand cru.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-valozier.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, iron-rich brown limestone-clay. The gradient flattens to about 8% here, and the iron-stained brown soil is deeper than on the Bressandes slope just above, giving fleshier, earlier wines.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-valozier.nerd_note: It sits directly below Corton Les Bressandes, at the point where the slope flattens out.

fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-vercots.name: Aloxe-Corton premier cru Les Vercots
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-vercots.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-vercots.summary:
Les Vercots is a 4.3 ha Aloxe-Corton premier cru at the southern edge of the commune, toward Savigny. Follin-Arbelet and Antonin Guyon make it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.

Its neighbour Les Guérets and Savigny's Les Lavières share the same flatter ground, and its wines are softer and more red-fruited than the premiers crus under the grand cru. Follin-Arbelet's version is a reliable reference.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-vercots.terroir: Almost flat, south exposure at about 245 m, on brown limestone-clay. Being away from the hill of Corton, it lacks the marl and iron of the grand cru slopes, which is why its wines are lighter and more fruit-led.
fr-aloxe-corton-premier-cru-les-vercots.nerd_note: Its neighbour Les Guérets is the other premier cru on the Savigny side of Aloxe.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-bas-des-du.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru Bas des Duresses
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-bas-des-du.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-bas-des-du.summary: Bas des Duresses is a 2.4 ha premier cru below Les Duresses, toward Meursault. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-bas-des-du.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Duresses and above Les Ecussaux.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-bas-des-du.nerd_note: *Bas* means lower: it sits below Les Duresses.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-climat-du-.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru Climat du Val
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-climat-du-.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-climat-du-.summary: The Climat du Val is the largest and best-known premier cru of Auxey-Duresses, a 9.3 ha slope on the south-facing side of Mont Melian, the hill above the village. The wine is fine and red-fruited, with a firm, mineral finish; white is also made.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-climat-du-.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 275 to 335 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils with marl.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-climat-du-.nerd_note: Its south-southwest exposure gives it good ripeness despite the cool valley.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-clos-du-va.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru Clos du Val
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-clos-du-va.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-clos-du-va.summary: The Clos du Val is a walled 0.92 ha premier cru within the Climat du Val, on the south-facing slope above Auxey. Michel Prunier makes a reference version. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-clos-du-va.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 275 to 320 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-clos-du-va.nerd_note: The Prunier family has several branches in Auxey, and several make a Clos du Val.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-la-chapell.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru La Chapelle
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-la-chapell.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-la-chapell.summary: La Chapelle is a small 1.3 ha premier cru on the Auxey slope, named after a chapel. The Lafouge family makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-la-chapell.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 265 to 295 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Les Grands Champs and beside Reugne and Les Bréterins.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-la-chapell.nerd_note: It sits between Reugne and Les Bréterins.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-breter.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru Les Bréterins
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-breter.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-breter.summary: Les Bréterins is a 1.9 ha premier cru on the Auxey slope, below the Climat du Val. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-breter.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Clos du Val, above Les Grands Champs and beside La Chapelle and Reugne.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-breter.nerd_note: It lies at the foot of Mont Melian.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-duress.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru Les Duresses
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-duress.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-duress.summary: Les Duresses gave Auxey half its name: the village became Auxey-Duresses in 1924. At 7.9 ha it lies on the slope toward Monthélie. The wine is firm and red-fruited.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-duress.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 320 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Bas des Duresses, Les Grands Champs and Les Ecussaux and beside Reugne.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-duress.nerd_note: The climat continues into Monthélie's Les Duresses.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-ecussa.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru Les Ecussaux
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-ecussa.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-ecussa.summary: Les Ecussaux is a 3.2 ha premier cru at the eastern end of the Auxey slope, toward Meursault. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-ecussa.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Bas des Duresses, Les Grands Champs and Les Duresses.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-ecussa.nerd_note: It is the lowest premier cru in Auxey-Duresses.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-grands.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru Les Grands Champs
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-grands.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-grands.summary: Les Grands Champs is a 4.0 ha premier cru on the lower part of the Auxey slope. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-les-grands.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 255 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Reugne, Les Bréterins, Les Duresses and La Chapelle.

fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-reugne.name: Auxey-Duresses premier cru Reugne
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-reugne.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-reugne.summary: Reugne is a 3.0 ha premier cru on the Auxey slope, near La Chapelle. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-reugne.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 265 to 305 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Les Grands Champs and beside La Chapelle, Les Duresses and Les Bréterins.
fr-auxey-duresses-premier-cru-reugne.nerd_note: It sits between La Chapelle and Les Duresses on the south-facing slope of Mont Melian.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-a-l-ecu.name: Beaune premier cru A l'Ecu
fr-beaune-premier-cru-a-l-ecu.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-a-l-ecu.summary: A l'Ecu is a 2.3 ha premier cru below the Clos de l'Ecu, on the northern part of Beaune's slope. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-a-l-ecu.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 290 m, steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Clos de l'Ecu and Les Bressandes, above Les Fèves and beside Les Perrières.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-a-l-ecu.nerd_note: It shares its name with Faiveley's monopole Clos de l'Ecu just above.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-coucherias.name: Beaune premier cru Aux Coucherias
fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-coucherias.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-coucherias.summary: Aux Coucherias is a 8.8 ha premier cru high on the central slope of Beaune, above Aux Cras. The wine is firm and fresh, red or white.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-coucherias.terroir: Steep, south-southwest-facing at 255 to 315 m, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Montée Rouge, La Mignotte and Aux Cras and beside Clos de la Feguine.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-coucherias.nerd_note: Its south-southwest exposure is unusual for a Beaune premier cru.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cras.name: Beaune premier cru Aux Cras
fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cras.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cras.summary: Aux Cras is a 5.0 ha premier cru in the centre of Beaune, above Les Teurons. Jacques Prieur's Clos de la Feguine is inside it. The wine is firm and red-fruited.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cras.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 275 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Clos de la Feguine, above Les Teurons and beside Champs Pimont and La Mignotte.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-belissand.name: Beaune premier cru Belissand
fr-beaune-premier-cru-belissand.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-belissand.summary: Belissand is a 4.9 ha premier cru at the foot of Beaune's slope, near the town. The wine is soft and early-drinking.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-belissand.terroir: Flat, east-southeast exposure at 225 to 235 m, deep brown clay. On the map it lies below Les Avaux and Les Tuvilains and beside Les Sceaux and Les Reversés.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-belissand.nerd_note: It lies just above the ring road that circles Beaune.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-blanches-fleurs.name: Beaune premier cru Blanches Fleurs
fr-beaune-premier-cru-blanches-fleurs.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-blanches-fleurs.summary: Blanches Fleurs is a 3.1 ha premier cru on the lower northern slope of Beaune, next to the Clos du Roi. The wine is supple and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-blanches-fleurs.terroir: Almost flat, south exposure at 235 to 245 m, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Clos du Roi.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-blanches-fleurs.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus at the northern end of Beaune.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-champs-pimont.name: Beaune premier cru Champs Pimont
fr-beaune-premier-cru-champs-pimont.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-champs-pimont.summary: Champs Pimont is a large 16.4 ha premier cru on the central slope of Beaune, below Montée Rouge. The wine is supple and red-fruited, and some white is also made.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-champs-pimont.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 300 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Aigrots, above La Mignotte and Clos des Avaux and beside Montée Rouge.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-champs-pimont.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Guigone de Salins includes Champs Pimont.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-l-ecu.name: Beaune premier cru Clos de l'Ecu
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-l-ecu.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-l-ecu.summary: The Clos de l'Ecu is a walled 2.4 ha monopole of Faiveley, high on the northern part of Beaune's slope. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-l-ecu.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 315 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Les Bressandes, A l'Ecu and Les Perrières.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-l-ecu.nerd_note: With the Clos des Cortons Faiveley it is one of Faiveley's two Côte de Beaune monopoles.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-feguine.name: Beaune premier cru Clos de la Feguine
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-feguine.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-feguine.summary: The Clos de la Feguine is a walled 1.8 ha monopole of Domaine Jacques Prieur, within Aux Cras. Prieur makes both red and white. The wine is fine and perfumed.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-feguine.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 265 to 295 m, steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Aux Cras and beside Aux Coucherias.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-feguine.nerd_note: Prieur's Clos de la Feguine blanc is one of the few white Beaune monopoles.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-mousse.name: Beaune premier cru Clos de la Mousse
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-mousse.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-mousse.summary:
The Clos de la Mousse is a walled 3.4 ha monopole of Bouchard Père et Fils, on the lower central slope of Beaune. The wine is supple and red-fruited.

Les Teurons and Les Avaux lie alongside. Bouchard, one of the largest owners of Beaune premiers crus, makes a supple, perfumed wine from it that drinks well after five years.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-mousse.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 230 to 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-de-la-mousse.nerd_note: The *mousse* in the name probably means moss, not the foam on a glass.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-avaux.name: Beaune premier cru Clos des Avaux
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-avaux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-avaux.summary: The Clos des Avaux is a walled 4.2 ha premier cru on the lower central slope of Beaune, owned by the Hospices de Beaune and sold at its November auction as the cuvée Clos des Avaux.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-avaux.terroir: East-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-avaux.nerd_note: It is one of the few Hospices cuvées drawn from a single walled clos.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-ursules.name: Beaune premier cru Clos des Ursules
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-ursules.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-ursules.summary:
The Clos des Ursules is a walled 1.3 ha monopole of Maison Louis Jadot within Les Vignes Franches, at the southern end of Beaune. It belonged to the Ursuline nuns before the Revolution, and the Jadot family bought it in 1826, decades before the négociant house was founded in 1859. The wine is firm, dark-fruited and long-lived.

The clos sits on the southern part of Beaune's slope, within Les Vignes Franches, with Les Aigrots above and Les Pertuisots alongside, on iron-rich brown soil. Jadot's red is darker and firmer than most Beaunes, with a Pommard-like structure from the southern end of the appellation, and it ages for 15 years or more.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-ursules.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 270 m, moderately steep. Brown limestone-clay with iron.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-des-ursules.nerd_note: It was the Jadot family's first vineyard, and the house still treats it as its flagship Beaune.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-du-roi.name: Beaune premier cru Clos du Roi
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-du-roi.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-du-roi.summary:
The Clos du Roi is a 13.3 ha premier cru at the northern end of Beaune, below Les Marconnets. Like its namesake in Corton, it is thought to have passed from the Dukes of Burgundy to the French crown. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.

En Genêt, Blanches Fleurs and Les Cents Vignes lie alongside, and its wines are firm and dark-fruited; Tollot-Beaut's and Chanson's versions show the more structured side of northern Beaune.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-du-roi.terroir: Gentle south slope at 230 to 245 m, brown limestone-clay. The gradient is very gentle, about 2%, and the deeper soil at the foot of the Marconnets slope gives the wine its fleshy core.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-du-roi.nerd_note: It is one of the few Beaune premier crus facing almost due south.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-saint-landry.name: Beaune premier cru Clos Saint-Landry
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-saint-landry.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-saint-landry.summary: The Clos Saint-Landry is a walled 2.0 ha monopole of Bouchard Père et Fils on the lower southern slope of Beaune, planted with Chardonnay. The wine is a fresh, fruity white Beaune.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-saint-landry.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Pertuisots, above Les Tuvilains and beside Les Sizies and Les Chouacheux.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-clos-saint-landry.nerd_note: Saint Landry was a 7th-century bishop of Paris.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-genet.name: Beaune premier cru En Genêt
fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-genet.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-genet.summary: En Genêt is a 4.3 ha premier cru on the lower northern slope of Beaune. The wine is supple and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-genet.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Marconnets and En l'Orme, above Les Cents Vignes and beside Clos du Roi.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-genet.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Nicolas Rolin includes En Genêt.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-l-orme.name: Beaune premier cru En l'Orme
fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-l-orme.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-l-orme.summary: En l'Orme ('the elm') is a 2.0 ha premier cru on the northern part of Beaune's slope, below Les Marconnets. The wine is a supple Beaune.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-l-orme.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 275 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Perrières, above En Genêt and beside Les Marconnets.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-en-l-orme.nerd_note: Elms once lined the roads through the Côte before Dutch elm disease.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-la-mignotte.name: Beaune premier cru La Mignotte
fr-beaune-premier-cru-la-mignotte.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-la-mignotte.summary: La Mignotte is a 2.4 ha premier cru on the central slope of Beaune, below Aux Coucherias. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-la-mignotte.terroir: South-facing at 240 to 255 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Champs Pimont, Montée Rouge and Aux Coucherias and beside Aux Cras.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-la-mignotte.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Dames Hospitalières and Hugues et Louis Bétault both include La Mignotte.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-bas-des-teurons.name: Beaune premier cru Le Bas des Teurons
fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-bas-des-teurons.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-bas-des-teurons.summary: Le Bas des Teurons is a 6.7 ha premier cru below Les Teurons, on the lower slope. The wine is supple and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-bas-des-teurons.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, deep brown clay. On the map it lies below Les Grèves and Les Teurons.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-bas-des-teurons.nerd_note: *Bas* means lower: the same climat continues upslope as Les Teurons.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-clos-des-mouche.name: Beaune premier cru Le Clos des Mouches
fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-clos-des-mouche.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-clos-des-mouche.summary:
Le Clos des Mouches is Beaune's most famous premier cru and one of the few Côte de Beaune climats equally celebrated for red and white. It lies at the southern end of the appellation, against the Pommard boundary, and at 25.3 ha it is one of the larger premier crus of the Côte. The *mouches* are usually said to be honeybees (*mouches à miel*), once kept in hives on the slope.

Maison Joseph Drouhin built its reputation here: Maurice Drouhin began buying parcels in 1921, and the house now owns more than half the climat, about 14 ha. Its white Clos des Mouches, from the upper slope, is rich and nutty with a mineral finish, a Beaune white that can rival Meursault; its red is perfumed, round and silky. Chanson also makes both colours.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-clos-des-mouche.terroir: Southeast-facing at 250 to 310 m, moderately steep. White marl and limestone on the upper slope, where most Chardonnay is planted; brown, iron-tinged limestone-clay lower down for Pinot Noir.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-le-clos-des-mouche.nerd_note: The upper, marly slope is planted mostly to Chardonnay and the lower slope to Pinot Noir, so one climat name covers what are really two different vineyards.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-aigrots.name: Beaune premier cru Les Aigrots
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-aigrots.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-aigrots.summary:
Les Aigrots is a large 18.7 ha premier cru on the upper southern slope of Beaune, above Les Vignes Franches. Michel Lafarge makes both red and white. The wine is fresh and fine.

It sits high on the southern part of Beaune's slope, above Les Vignes Franches and the Clos des Ursules and beside the Clos des Mouches, on stony limestone with marl. It is one of the few Beaune premier crus where white is as important as red, and Lafarge's white Clos des Aigrots is a good example.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-aigrots.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 310 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils with marl. The upper slope here climbs above 300 m, and the white marl that appears there is the reason Chardonnay does so well.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-aigrots.nerd_note: The upper slope's marl suits Chardonnay, which is why Les Aigrots makes good white.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-avaux.name: Beaune premier cru Les Avaux
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-avaux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-avaux.summary: Les Avaux is a large 11.1 ha premier cru on the lower central slope of Beaune. The wine is supple and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-avaux.terroir: Gentle east-southeast slope at 230 to 250 m, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Sizies, above Belissand and beside Clos des Avaux and Les Tuvilains.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-avaux.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Maurice Drouhin includes Les Avaux.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.name: Beaune premier cru Les Boucherottes
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.summary:
Les Boucherottes is a 8.6 ha premier cru at the southern end of Beaune, against the Pommard boundary. The wine is firm and dark-fruited, close to Pommard in style.

It runs into Pommard's Les Boucherottes and Les Petits Epenots, below the Clos des Mouches and beside Les Epenotes. Its wines have something of Pommard's depth in a more perfumed Beaune frame, and Jadot's version is a reliable reference.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, iron-rich brown limestone-clay.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.nerd_note: The same climat name continues into Pommard.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-bressandes.name: Beaune premier cru Les Bressandes
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-bressandes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-bressandes.summary:
Les Bressandes is a large 17.2 ha premier cru on the upper slope at the northern end of Beaune, above Les Cents Vignes and Les Toussaints. The wine is firm, perfumed and structured, one of Beaune's longest-lived reds.

It sits high on the northern part of Beaune's slope, above Les Toussaints, Les Cents Vignes and Les Fèves and below the woods, on thin, stony soil. That steep, stony position gives one of Beaune's firmest and longest-lived reds; Albert Morot's version, from a family estate in Beaune's old Château de la Creusotte, is a classic.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-bressandes.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 240 to 310 m, slope around 20%. Stony limestone soils, thin on the upper slope.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-bressandes.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Guigone de Salins and Dames Hospitalières both include Bressandes.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-cents-vignes.name: Beaune premier cru Les Cents Vignes
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-cents-vignes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-cents-vignes.summary:
Les Cents Vignes ('hundred vines') is a large 23.5 ha premier cru on the lower slope at the northern end of Beaune. The wine is supple, fruity and early-drinking.

Les Bressandes and Les Fèves lie above it, Les Toussaints and the Clos du Roi alongside. Its deeper soil gives ripe, round wines that drink early; the Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Nicolas Rolin and Rousseau-Deslandes both draw on it.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-cents-vignes.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at 225 to 240 m, deep brown limestone-clay. At about 225 to 240 m on an almost flat gradient, it is one of the lowest of Beaune's northern premier crus, and its deep soil retains water well in dry summers.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-cents-vignes.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Nicolas Rolin includes Cents Vignes.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-chouacheux.name: Beaune premier cru Les Chouacheux
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-chouacheux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-chouacheux.summary: Les Chouacheux is a 5.0 ha premier cru on the lower southern slope of Beaune. Jadot makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-chouacheux.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Vignes Franches and Les Boucherottes and beside Les Tuvilains and Clos Saint-Landry.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-chouacheux.nerd_note: It is one of the lesser-known Beaune premier crus in Jadot's range.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-epenotes.name: Beaune premier cru Les Epenotes
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-epenotes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-epenotes.summary:
Les Epenotes is a 8.0 ha premier cru at the southern end of Beaune, on the boundary with Pommard's Epenots. The wine is supple and perfumed, a Beaune with some of Pommard's depth.

It runs straight into Pommard's Les Petits Epenots and Les Boucherottes. The Beaune side of the Epenots makes a slightly softer, more perfumed wine than the Pommard side, but the two share the same deep, gravelly brown soil.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-epenotes.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at 235 to 245 m, brown limestone-clay. The flat ground, around 3% gradient, and deep soil give a soft, generous structure; the climat is one of the easiest places to taste the transition from Beaune to Pommard.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-epenotes.nerd_note: Spelled Epenotes in Beaune and Epenots in Pommard, it is one climat split by the commune line.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-feves.name: Beaune premier cru Les Fèves
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-feves.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-feves.summary:
Les Fèves is a 4.8 ha premier cru on the northern part of Beaune's slope, below Les Bressandes. Chanson's Clos des Fèves monopole fills most of it. The wine is fine and perfumed.

Les Bressandes and A l'Ecu lie above it and Les Cents Vignes below. Chanson's Clos des Fèves, which occupies most of it, is one of Beaune's most refined reds: perfumed, red-fruited and silky.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-feves.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-feves.nerd_note: Chanson's Clos des Fèves is its flagship Beaune premier cru.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-greves.name: Beaune premier cru Les Grèves
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-greves.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-greves.summary:
Les Grèves is the heart of Beaune and its largest premier cru, about 31 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 31.3 ha), on the middle of the slope above the town. *Grèves* means gravel, and the soil is gravelly and well-drained, which gives some of the most complete reds of Beaune: perfumed, ripe and spicy, with a firm, fine tannin.

Its best-known parcel is Bouchard Père et Fils' 'Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus', a 3.9 ha monopole within the climat whose name recalls the 17th-century Carmelite nun Marguerite du Saint-Sacrement, who is said to have predicted the birth of Louis XIV. Jadot makes a white Beaune Grèves 'Le Clos Blanc'.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-greves.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 300 m, moderately steep. Gravelly limestone soils over Bathonian limestone, with iron-stained clay in the lower part.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-greves.nerd_note: The Vigne de l'Enfant Jésus was owned by the Carmelites until the Revolution; Bouchard bought it in 1791.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-marconnets.name: Beaune premier cru Les Marconnets
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-marconnets.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-marconnets.summary:
Les Marconnets is a 9.4 ha premier cru at the northern end of Beaune, against the Savigny boundary. The wine is firm and dark-fruited, one of the more structured Beaunes.

The Clos du Roi and En Genêt lie below it and En l'Orme beside it. Its iron-rich soils give one of Beaune's most structured reds, darker and firmer than the central premiers crus, and Bouchard's and Chanson's versions need several years to open.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-marconnets.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 290 m, moderately steep. Iron-rich brown limestone-clay.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-marconnets.nerd_note: The same climat name continues into Savigny-lès-Beaune.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-montrevenots.name: Beaune premier cru Les Montrevenots
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-montrevenots.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-montrevenots.summary: Les Montrevenots is a 8.5 ha premier cru high on the slope above the Clos des Mouches, at the southern end of Beaune. Jean-Marc Boillot makes it. The wine is fresh and fine, red or white.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-montrevenots.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 295 to 335 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-montrevenots.nerd_note: At over 300 m it is the highest premier cru in Beaune.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-perrieres.name: Beaune premier cru Les Perrières
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-perrieres.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-perrieres.summary: Les Perrières is a 3.2 ha premier cru on the northern part of Beaune's slope, on stony ground once quarried. The wine is firm and mineral.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-perrieres.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 245 to 295 m, slope around 22%, stony limestone soils.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-perrieres.nerd_note: Perrières is one of the commonest climat names on the Côte d'Or, always marking a former quarry.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-reverses.name: Beaune premier cru Les Reversés
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-reverses.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-reverses.summary: Les Reversés is a 4.8 ha premier cru on the lower central slope of Beaune. The wine is soft and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-reverses.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Clos de la Mousse and Les Teurons and beside Les Sceaux and Belissand.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-reverses.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus in Beaune.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sceaux.name: Beaune premier cru Les Sceaux
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sceaux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sceaux.summary: Les Sceaux is a 3.1 ha premier cru at the foot of Beaune's central slope, next to the town. The wine is soft and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sceaux.terroir: Flat, east-southeast exposure at about 225 m, deep brown clay.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sceaux.nerd_note: At around 225 m it is one of the lowest premier crus in Beaune, almost at the edge of the town.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-seurey.name: Beaune premier cru Les Seurey
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-seurey.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-seurey.summary: Les Seurey is a small 1.2 ha premier cru on the lower central slope of Beaune. The wine is supple and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-seurey.terroir: Southwest-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Champs Pimont and beside Les Avaux, Clos de la Mousse and Clos des Avaux.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-seurey.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Guigone de Salins includes Les Seurey.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sizies.name: Beaune premier cru Les Sizies
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sizies.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sizies.summary: Les Sizies is a 8.6 ha premier cru on the lower southern slope of Beaune. The wine is supple and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sizies.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Aigrots, above Les Avaux and Les Tuvilains and beside Pertuisots.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-sizies.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Hugues et Louis Bétault includes Les Sizies.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-teurons.name: Beaune premier cru Les Teurons
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-teurons.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-teurons.summary:
Les Teurons is a large 21.5 ha premier cru in the centre of Beaune, below Aux Cras and next to Les Grèves. The wine is perfumed, ripe and round, with red fruit and a silky tannin, one of Beaune's most charming premier crus.

It sits in the centre of Beaune's slope, with Aux Cras and Champs Pimont above, Les Grèves to the north and Le Bas des Teurons below. Its gravelly soil gives ripe, perfumed wines with fine tannin, and it is often ranked just behind Les Grèves among Beaune's central premier crus.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-teurons.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 225 to 265 m, gentle slope. Gravelly brown limestone-clay.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-teurons.nerd_note: Les Teurons and Le Bas des Teurons together make up the second-largest premier cru area in Beaune after Les Grèves.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-toussaints.name: Beaune premier cru Les Toussaints
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-toussaints.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-toussaints.summary: Les Toussaints is a 6.4 ha premier cru on the lower slope between Les Grèves and Les Cents Vignes. Albert Morot makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-toussaints.terroir: East-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Grèves and Les Bressandes and beside Les Cents Vignes.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-tuvilains.name: Beaune premier cru Les Tuvilains
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-tuvilains.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-tuvilains.summary: Les Tuvilains is a 8.9 ha premier cru on the lower southern slope of Beaune. The wine is soft and fruity.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-tuvilains.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Sizies and Clos Saint-Landry, above Belissand and beside Les Avaux.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-tuvilains.nerd_note: It sits on the flat ground at the foot of the southern slope, between the Clos Saint-Landry and Les Chouacheux.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-vignes-franche.name: Beaune premier cru Les Vignes Franches
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-vignes-franche.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-vignes-franche.summary:
Les Vignes Franches is a 8.5 ha premier cru on the southern slope of Beaune, toward Pommard. Jadot's Clos des Ursules is inside it. The wine is firm and dark-fruited, with Pommard's structure.

It sits at the southern end of Beaune, with Les Aigrots and the Clos des Mouches above and Les Boucherottes and Les Chouacheux alongside, on iron-rich brown soil. Its wines are firm and dark, with a Pommard-like structure, and Jadot's Clos des Ursules inside it is the most famous wine of the climat.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-vignes-franche.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 270 m, moderately steep, iron-rich brown limestone-clay. Iron oxides give the soil a reddish tinge similar to Pommard's Rugiens, and the gradient steepens toward the Clos des Mouches above.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-les-vignes-franche.nerd_note: *Franches* is usually explained as 'free': vines once exempt from feudal dues.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-montee-rouge.name: Beaune premier cru Montée Rouge
fr-beaune-premier-cru-montee-rouge.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-montee-rouge.summary: Montée Rouge is a 4.7 ha premier cru high on the central slope of Beaune, named for its red, iron-stained soil. The wine is firm and fresh.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-montee-rouge.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 245 to 300 m, iron-rich red soils. On the map it lies below Aux Coucherias, above La Mignotte and beside Champs Pimont.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-montee-rouge.nerd_note: *Montée* means rise: the slope here climbs sharply toward the woods.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-pertuisots.name: Beaune premier cru Pertuisots
fr-beaune-premier-cru-pertuisots.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-pertuisots.summary: Les Pertuisots is a 5.3 ha premier cru on the southern slope of Beaune, near Les Vignes Franches. Domaine des Croix makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-pertuisots.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Aigrots and Clos des Ursules, above Clos Saint-Landry and beside Les Sizies.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-pertuisots.nerd_note: A *pertuis* is a narrow passage, perhaps an old path through the vines.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves.name: Beaune premier cru Sur les Grèves
fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves.summary: Sur les Grèves ('above the Grèves') is a steep 3.8 ha premier cru above Les Grèves. The wine is firm and fresh, with red fruit and a stony finish.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 260 to 310 m, slope around 25%. Thin, stony limestone soils.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves.nerd_note: Its walled northern section, the Clos Sainte-Anne, has a premier cru name of its own.

fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves-clo.name: Beaune premier cru Sur les Grèves - Clos Saint-Anne
fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves-clo.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves-clo.summary: The Clos Sainte-Anne is a 0.77 ha walled section of Sur les Grèves, above Beaune's Les Grèves. Maison Jaffelin makes it as a monopole. The wine is firm and red-fruited.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves-clo.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 275 to 310 m, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Sur les Grèves and Les Grèves.
fr-beaune-premier-cru-sur-les-greves-clo.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest named premier crus in Beaune.

fr-blagny-premier-cru-hameau-de-blagny.name: Blagny premier cru Hameau de Blagny
fr-blagny-premier-cru-hameau-de-blagny.summary: Hameau de Blagny ('the hamlet of Blagny') is a 4.2 ha premier cru around the hamlet, on the Puligny side. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru; white is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-hameau-de-blagny.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 315 to 340 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-hameau-de-blagny.nerd_note: The hamlet has only a handful of houses and a chapel.

fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-garenne.name: Blagny premier cru La Garenne
fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-garenne.summary: The red side of La Garenne: 9.9 ha high above Puligny, near the hamlet of Blagny. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru; white is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-garenne.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 375 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Puligny-Montrachet's Sous le Puits and above Puligny-Montrachet's Champ Gain, Puligny-Montrachet's Hameau de Blagny and Saint-Aubin's Les Murgers des dents de chien.

fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-jeunellotte.name: Blagny premier cru La Jeunellotte
fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-jeunellotte.summary: The red side of La Jeunellotte: 5.0 ha high above Meursault, in the hamlet of Blagny. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-jeunellotte.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 325 to 355 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Puligny-Montrachet's Sous le Puits and Meursault's Les Ravelles and above Meursault's Blagny and Meursault's La Pièce sous le Bois.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-jeunellotte.nerd_note: White from the same vines is Meursault premier cru.

fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-piece-sous-le-b.name: Blagny premier cru La Pièce sous le Bois
fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-piece-sous-le-b.summary: The red side of La Pièce sous le Bois: 11.3 ha high above Meursault, in the hamlet of Blagny. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru, a firm, red-fruited Pinot Noir.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-piece-sous-le-b.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 310 to 345 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-la-piece-sous-le-b.nerd_note: Blagny AOC is red-only, while white from the same slopes takes the name of Meursault or Puligny-Montrachet.

fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-blagny.name: Blagny premier cru Sous Blagny
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-blagny.summary: The red side of Sous Blagny: 2.2 ha just below the hamlet. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-blagny.terroir: East-facing at 300 to 335 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Meursault's Blagny and La Jeunellotte and above Meursault's Sous le Dos d'Ane and Puligny-Montrachet's Les Chalumaux.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-blagny.nerd_note: White from the same vines is Meursault premier cru.

fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-le-dos-d-ane.name: Blagny premier cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-le-dos-d-ane.summary: The red side of Sous le Dos d'Ane: 5.2 ha below the hamlet of Blagny. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-le-dos-d-ane.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 320 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Meursault's Blagny, Meursault's La Pièce sous le Bois and Sous Blagny and above Meursault's Perrières.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-le-dos-d-ane.nerd_note: White from the same vines is Meursault premier cru.

fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-le-puits.name: Blagny premier cru Sous le Puits
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-le-puits.summary: The red side of Sous le Puits: 6.8 ha high above Puligny, at the top of the Blagny slope. Red wine from here is Blagny premier cru; white is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-le-puits.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 400 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils.
fr-blagny-premier-cru-sous-le-puits.nerd_note: At around 400 m at its top it is one of the highest premier crus in the Côte d'Or.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-beauroy.name: Chablis premier cru Beauroy
fr-chablis-premier-cru-beauroy.summary: Beauroy is a left-bank premier cru west of Chablis around Poinchy and Beine, on slopes facing south-east; this polygon is drawn from the lieu-dit Sous Boroy. Its satellites Troesmes and Côte de Savant may be sold under the Beauroy name. The wines are fresh, floral and quite delicate, often good value among the premiers crus.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-beauroy.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 160 to 195 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing east to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-beauroy.classification: Chablis premier cru: one of the 17 principal climats of the cahier des charges, which can also cover satellite climats.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-berdiot.name: Chablis premier cru Berdiot
fr-chablis-premier-cru-berdiot.summary: Berdiot is a small 3.6 ha premier cru on the right bank, near Fyé, standing on its own rather than as part of a larger group. Its wines are fresh and mineral.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-berdiot.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 175 to 210 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-berdiot.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premiers crus of Chablis.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-beugnons.name: Chablis premier cru Beugnons
fr-chablis-premier-cru-beugnons.summary: Les Beugnons is a 14.5 ha satellite of Vaillons on the left bank southwest of Chablis, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its wines are fresh and mineral.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-beugnons.terroir: Southeast-facing at 200 to 265 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies above Chatains and Roncières.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-beugnons.nerd_note: It is one of the higher sites of the Vaillons group.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-butteaux.name: Chablis premier cru Butteaux
fr-chablis-premier-cru-butteaux.summary: A satellite climat of Montmains, higher up the left-bank slope and facing south-east, drawn here from the lieux-dits Le Bout and Le Milieu des Buttaux. Raveneau's Butteaux, from old vines, is one of the most admired left-bank Chablis: lean and stony when young, deep and long with age.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-butteaux.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 220 to 265 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-butteaux.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Montmains, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-chapelot.name: Chablis premier cru Chapelot
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chapelot.summary: A satellite of Montée de Tonnerre on the right bank of the Serein, facing south-west. It may be sold as Montée de Tonnerre or under its own name; Raveneau bottles a Chapelot, a slightly rounder companion to its Montée de Tonnerre.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chapelot.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 165 to 195 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chapelot.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Montée de Tonnerre, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-chatains.name: Chablis premier cru Chatains
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chatains.summary: Les Châtains is a 7.3 ha satellite of Vaillons on the left bank southwest of Chablis, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its wines are fresh and mineral.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chatains.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 205 to 250 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies below Beugnons and above Roncières and Vaillons.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chatains.nerd_note: The name refers to chestnut trees (*châtaigniers*).

fr-chablis-premier-cru-chaume-de-talvat.name: Chablis premier cru Chaume de Talvat
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chaume-de-talvat.summary: Chaume de Talvat is a small 1.1 ha Chablis premier cru in Courgis, on the left bank west of the town. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chaume-de-talvat.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 295 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies above Côte de Jouan.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-chaume-de-talvat.nerd_note: At just over a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus in Chablis.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-brechain.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Bréchain
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-brechain.summary: Côte de Bréchain is a 11.1 ha satellite of Montée de Tonnerre on the right bank of the Serein, at the northern end of that group, and its wine may be sold under the Montée de Tonnerre name. It shares the group's saline, mineral style.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-brechain.terroir: West-northwest-facing at 170 to 225 m, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-brechain.nerd_note: The Bréchain valley here separates the Montée de Tonnerre group from the grand cru Blanchot, so the premier cru sits directly across a small combe from the grands crus.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-cuisy.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Cuisy
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-cuisy.summary: A satellite of Les Beauregards in Courgis, on the left bank far to the south-west of Chablis (Côte de Cuissy and Vallée de Cuissy in the land register), on slopes facing south-east and south at about 235 to 290 m. It may be sold as Beauregards or under its own name; the Courgis premiers crus give lean, fresh, citrus-driven Chablis.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-cuisy.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 235 to 290 m, with a mean slope of about 21%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-cuisy.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Les Beauregards, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-fontenay.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Fontenay
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-fontenay.summary: A satellite of Fourchaume in Fontenay-près-Chablis (La Côte in the land register), on the right bank north of the grands crus, facing south-east. It may be sold as Fourchaume or under its own name, and shares the group's rounder, riper style.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-fontenay.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 150 to 185 m, with a mean slope of about 21%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-fontenay.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Fourchaume, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-jouan.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Jouan
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-jouan.summary: Côte de Jouan is a 12.6 ha Chablis premier cru in Courgis, west of the town on the left bank of the Serein. The wine is fresh, crisp and mineral.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-jouan.terroir: Southeast-facing at 215 to 290 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-jouan.nerd_note: Courgis, high on the left bank, has three premier crus: Côte de Jouan, Les Beauregards and Chaume de Talvat.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-lechet.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Léchet
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-lechet.summary: Côte de Léchet is a large 53.9 ha premier cru on the left bank above the hamlet of Milly, west of Chablis. Its steep, east-southeast-facing slope gives a tense, mineral Chablis with a stony finish.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-lechet.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 150 to 225 m, slope around 20%, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-lechet.nerd_note: Milly, like Fyé and Poinchy, is a hamlet of the commune of Chablis.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-savant.name: Chablis premier cru Côte de Savant
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-savant.summary: Côte de Savant is a small 1.4 ha satellite of Beauroy in Beine, on the left bank west of Chablis, sold as Beauroy or under its own name.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-savant.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 180 to 220 m, slope around 29%, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-de-savant.nerd_note: With Troesmes it is one of the two satellites of Beauroy.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-des-pres-gir.name: Chablis premier cru Côte des Prés-Girots
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-des-pres-gir.summary: A satellite of Les Fourneaux in Fleys, on the right bank east of Chablis (Côte des Prés Girot in the land register), on slopes facing south and south-west near Mont de Milieu. It is usually sold as Les Fourneaux, a firm, saline right-bank premier cru.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-des-pres-gir.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 195 to 230 m, with a mean slope of about 21%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-cote-des-pres-gir.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Les Fourneaux, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-forets.name: Chablis premier cru Forêts
fr-chablis-premier-cru-forets.summary: Les Forêts (also La Forest) is a 22.5 ha satellite of Montmains on the left bank southwest of Chablis, sold as Montmains or under its own name. Vincent Dauvissat's La Forest and Raveneau's Forêts made it famous: taut, deep and long-lived, among the finest left-bank wines.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-forets.terroir: Southeast-facing at 180 to 225 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-forets.nerd_note: With Butteaux it is one of two Montmains satellites that leading growers prefer to bottle under their own names.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-fourchaume.name: Chablis premier cru Fourchaume
fr-chablis-premier-cru-fourchaume.summary:
Fourchaume is the largest and one of the most celebrated Chablis premier crus, a long band of slopes on the right bank of the Serein running north from the grands crus. The INAO delimitation of the main name covers 99.4 ha across Maligny, La Chapelle-Vaupelteigne and Fontenay-près-Chablis, and satellite climats such as Vaupulent, Côte de Fontenay, Vaulorent and L'Homme Mort may also be sold as Fourchaume. Its southern end, Vaulorent, touches the grand cru Les Preuses and is often ranked among the very best premier crus of Chablis.

Fourchaume is the richest, roundest of the premier crus: ripe citrus, white peach and a creamy texture over the classic Chablis spine of oyster-shell minerality. It is approachable earlier than Montée de Tonnerre or Mont de Milieu.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-fourchaume.terroir: Southwest-facing slopes at 130 to 195 m, catching afternoon sun. Kimmeridgian marl and limestone full of tiny fossil oysters (*Exogyra virgula*), the same formation as the grands crus.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-fourchaume.nerd_note: Fourchaume faces west and southwest, so its grapes ripen in warm afternoon light, one reason its wines are fuller than the southeast-facing premier crus of Fleys.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-l-homme-mort.name: Chablis premier cru L'Homme Mort
fr-chablis-premier-cru-l-homme-mort.summary: L'Homme Mort ('the dead man') is a 25.3 ha satellite of Fourchaume in Maligny, at the northern end of the Fourchaume slopes, sold as Fourchaume or under its own name. Its wines are ripe and round.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-l-homme-mort.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 130 to 175 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-l-homme-mort.nerd_note: The macabre name is old, and no one is sure of its origin.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-beauregards.name: Chablis premier cru Les Beauregards
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-beauregards.summary: Les Beauregards is a 21.3 ha Chablis premier cru in Courgis, on the left bank west of the town. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-beauregards.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 230 to 300 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-epinottes.name: Chablis premier cru Les Épinottes
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-epinottes.summary: Les Epinottes is a 26.9 ha satellite of Vaillons on the lower left-bank slopes near the town of Chablis, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its wines are fresh and supple.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-epinottes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 155 to 190 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-epinottes.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier cru sites of the left bank.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.name: Chablis premier cru Les Fourneaux
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.summary: Les Fourneaux is a 35.8 ha Chablis premier cru in Fleys, east of Mont de Milieu, on the right bank of the Serein. Its satellites include Morein and Côte des Prés Girots. The wine is fresh, mineral and fruity.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 180 to 240 m, steep in places, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.nerd_note: *Fourneaux* refers to old kilns; Savigny and Mercurey have premier crus with the same name.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-lys.name: Chablis premier cru Les Lys
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-lys.summary: Les Lys is a 14.5 ha satellite of Vaillons on the left bank of the Serein, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its north-northeast tilt makes it one of the cooler premier cru sites, and its wines are lean, floral and racy.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-lys.terroir: North-northeast-facing at 190 to 235 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-les-lys.nerd_note: Its cooler exposure, unusual for a premier cru, gives some of the most austere Chablis in youth.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-melinots.name: Chablis premier cru Mélinots
fr-chablis-premier-cru-melinots.summary: A satellite of Vaillons on the left bank west of Chablis, between Roncières and Beugnons, facing south-east. No cadastral lieu-dit carries the name, so it is drawn here from Les Minos. It is usually sold as Vaillons.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-melinots.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 200 to 235 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-melinots.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Vaillons, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-mont-de-milieu.name: Chablis premier cru Mont de Milieu
fr-chablis-premier-cru-mont-de-milieu.summary:
Mont de Milieu is one of the classic right-bank Chablis premier crus, an 18.2 ha slope in Fleys, east of Montée de Tonnerre. Its name, 'the middle hill', is usually explained by its old position on the frontier between the Duchy of Burgundy and the County of Champagne. Its wines are among the most structured and long-lived of Chablis: tight, saline and mineral in youth, opening after five to ten years into citrus, hazelnut and iodine.

Les Fourneaux lies further east on the same right-bank slopes. Billaud-Simon's and Pinson's versions are references.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-mont-de-milieu.terroir: Southeast-facing at 175 to 235 m, moderately steep. Kimmeridgian marl and limestone with fossil oysters; the southeast exposure gives ripeness while keeping acidity.
producers: Domaine Alice et Olivier De Moor
fr-chablis-premier-cru-mont-de-milieu.nerd_note: Mont de Milieu and Montée de Tonnerre are the two right-bank premier crus most often compared with the grands crus.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-mont-de-milieu-ch.name: Chablis premier cru Mont de Milieu (Chablis commune)
fr-chablis-premier-cru-mont-de-milieu-ch.summary: The part of the premier cru Mont de Milieu that lies in the commune of Chablis (lieu-dit Les Monts de Milieu), beside the larger section in Fleys. The slope faces south and south-east on the right bank of the Serein east of Montée de Tonnerre, and gives structured, long-lived, saline Chablis.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-mont-de-milieu-ch.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 170 to 225 m, with a mean slope of about 14%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-mont-de-milieu-ch.classification: Chablis premier cru: one of the 17 principal climats of the cahier des charges, which can also cover satellite climats.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-montee-de-tonnerr.name: Chablis premier cru Montée de Tonnerre
fr-chablis-premier-cru-montee-de-tonnerr.summary:
Montée de Tonnerre is usually ranked the finest premier cru of Chablis, the one most often described as a grand cru in all but name. It lies on the right bank of the Serein just east of the grand cru slope, separated from Blanchot by a small side valley, on the old road toward Tonnerre that gives it its name. This polygon is the lieu-dit itself, 5.5 ha; the principal name also covers Chapelot, Pied d'Aloup and Côte de Bréchain, which may all be sold as Montée de Tonnerre.

Its wines combine the grands crus' density with a cool, saline cut: citrus, white flowers and oyster shell in youth, then hazelnut and iodine after eight to ten years. Raveneau's Montée de Tonnerre and Chapelot are among the most sought-after white wines in France.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-montee-de-tonnerr.terroir: West-facing at 160 to 200 m, with the warm afternoon exposure of the right bank. Kimmeridgian marl and limestone full of small fossil oysters (*Exogyra virgula*), the same formation as the grands crus next door.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-montee-de-tonnerr.nerd_note: Raveneau bottles Chapelot separately from its Montée de Tonnerre, which is one of the few chances to taste a Chablis satellite climat on its own.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-montmains.name: Chablis premier cru Montmains
fr-chablis-premier-cru-montmains.summary: Montmains is one of the great left-bank premiers crus of Chablis, a long slope south-west of the town facing south-east, on thin, stony Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. This polygon is the lieu-dit itself (Les Monts-Mains in the land register); the principal name also covers Forêts and Butteaux, which may be sold as Montmains or under their own names. The wines are taut, saline and mineral, with less flesh than the right bank but great precision.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-montmains.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 170 to 210 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-montmains.classification: Chablis premier cru: one of the 17 principal climats of the cahier des charges, which can also cover satellite climats.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-morein.name: Chablis premier cru Morein
fr-chablis-premier-cru-morein.summary: Morein is a 10.4 ha satellite of Les Fourneaux in Fleys, on the right bank east of Chablis, sold as Les Fourneaux or under its own name.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-morein.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 180 to 235 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies below Les Fourneaux.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-morein.nerd_note: With Côte des Prés Girots it makes up the Fourneaux group.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-pied-d-aloup.name: Chablis premier cru Pied d'Aloup
fr-chablis-premier-cru-pied-d-aloup.summary: A satellite of Montée de Tonnerre on the right bank (Pied d'Aloue and Sous Pied d'Aloue in the land register), on slopes facing south and south-west. It is usually sold as Montée de Tonnerre, the most admired premier cru of Chablis.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-pied-d-aloup.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 200 to 235 m, with a mean slope of about 13%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-pied-d-aloup.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Montée de Tonnerre, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-roncieres.name: Chablis premier cru Roncières
fr-chablis-premier-cru-roncieres.summary: Les Roncières is a 22.4 ha climat of the Vaillons group on the left bank southwest of Chablis, sold as Vaillons or under its own name. Its wines are supple and mineral.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-roncieres.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 175 to 205 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies below Vaillons, Chatains and Beugnons and above Les Épinottes.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-roncieres.nerd_note: *Ronces* are brambles; Nuits-Saint-Georges has a premier cru called Roncière.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-secher.name: Chablis premier cru Sécher
fr-chablis-premier-cru-secher.summary: Sécher (also spelt Séchet) is a 12.2 ha satellite of Vaillons on the left bank southwest of Chablis, and its wine may be sold as Vaillons. Vincent Dauvissat's Séchet is the reference: taut, citrus-scented and long.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-secher.terroir: Southeast-facing at 185 to 210 m, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-secher.nerd_note: The geodata used for this map lists Sécher under Roncières; the BIVB listing places both Sécher and Roncières in the Vaillons group.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-troesmes.name: Chablis premier cru Troesmes
fr-chablis-premier-cru-troesmes.summary: A satellite of Beauroy in Beine, on the left bank west of Chablis (Côte de Trouëmes in the land register), on a fairly steep slope facing south and south-east. It may be sold as Beauroy or under its own name.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-troesmes.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 160 to 205 m, with a mean slope of about 21%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-troesmes.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Beauroy, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaillons.name: Chablis premier cru Vaillons
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaillons.summary:
Vaillons is the best-known premier cru of the left bank of the Serein, on the slopes southwest of the town of Chablis. This polygon is the lieu-dit Les Vaillons, 7.5 ha; the principal name also covers Châtains, Sécher, Beugnons, Les Lys, Mélinots, Roncières and Les Epinottes, so a bottle labelled Vaillons can come from a wide spread of slopes.

Left-bank Chablis faces southeast and gets the morning sun, and Vaillons is the archetype: lean, citrus-driven and mineral when young, with less weight than the right-bank premiers crus but great precision and a long, chalky finish. It is one of the most widely produced premiers crus and a good test of a grower.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaillons.terroir: Southeast-facing at 185 to 225 m, on Kimmeridgian marl and limestone; the soils are a little stonier and lighter than on the right bank.
producers: Domaine Christian Moreau Père et Fils
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaillons.nerd_note: The Vaillons group is one of the largest in Chablis; growers increasingly label its satellites, such as Séchet or Beugnons, separately to show the differences between them.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vau-de-vey.name: Chablis premier cru Vau de Vey
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vau-de-vey.summary: Vau de Vey is a 13.2 ha premier cru in Beine, on the left bank west of Chablis, with Vaux Ragons as its satellite. Its steep slope gives a fresh, mineral Chablis.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vau-de-vey.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 155 to 230 m, slope around 27%, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vau-de-vey.nerd_note: It is one of the steepest premier cru slopes of Chablis.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vau-ligneau.name: Chablis premier cru Vau Ligneau
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vau-ligneau.summary: Vau Ligneau is a 10.3 ha premier cru in Beine, on the left bank west of Chablis, standing on its own. Its wines are fresh and mineral.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vau-ligneau.terroir: Southeast-facing at 185 to 225 m, steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vau-ligneau.nerd_note: *Vau* means a small valley, a common word in Chablis climat names.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaucoupin.name: Chablis premier cru Vaucoupin
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaucoupin.summary: Vaucoupin is a 47.4 ha Chablis premier cru in Chichée, southeast of the town, on the right bank of the Serein. The wine is fresh and mineral, with good ripeness from its south-southwest exposure.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaucoupin.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 165 to 265 m, moderately steep, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaucoupin.nerd_note: Grossot's Vaucoupin is one of the reference versions of this lesser-known right-bank site.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaugiraut.name: Chablis premier cru Vaugiraut
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaugiraut.summary: Vaugiraut is a 7.0 ha satellite of Vosgros in Chichée, southeast of Chablis. Its wine may be sold as Vosgros.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaugiraut.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 185 to 205 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies below Vosgros.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaugiraut.nerd_note: It may carry its own name or Vosgros'.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaulorent.name: Chablis premier cru Vaulorent
