fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaulorent.summary: The southern end of the Fourchaume group, directly north of the grand cru Les Preuses on the same slope, often ranked among the very best premiers crus of Chablis. No cadastral lieu-dit carries the name, so it is drawn here from the premier cru land of Les Quatre Chemins. William Fèvre's Fourchaume Vignoble de Vaulorent is the reference.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaulorent.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 165 to 215 m, with a mean slope of about 14%, facing west to north-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaulorent.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Fourchaume, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaupulent.name: Chablis premier cru Vaupulent
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaupulent.summary: Vaupulent is a 2.6 ha satellite of Fourchaume in La Chapelle-Vaupelteigne, on the right bank north of the grands crus. Its wine is usually sold as Fourchaume. The style is the same: ripe, round Chablis with a mineral core.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaupulent.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 155 to 205 m, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaupulent.nerd_note: Like Vaulorent and L'Homme Mort, it may carry either its own name or Fourchaume's.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaupulent-chablis.name: Chablis premier cru Vaupulent (Chablis commune)
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaupulent-chablis.summary: The part of Vaupulent, a satellite of Fourchaume, that lies in the commune of Chablis (Les Vaupulans in the land register), on the right bank north of the grands crus, facing south and south-west. It is usually sold as Fourchaume, the richest and roundest of the right-bank premiers crus.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaupulent-chablis.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 140 to 185 m, with a mean slope of about 13%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaupulent-chablis.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Fourchaume, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaux-ragons.name: Chablis premier cru Vaux Ragons
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaux-ragons.summary: A satellite of Vau de Vey in Beine (Vignes des Vaux Ragons in the land register), on a steep slope facing east. It may be sold as Vau de Vey or under its own name, and gives fresh, mineral Chablis.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaux-ragons.terroir: The mapped climat lies at about 190 to 235 m, with a mean slope of about 33%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vaux-ragons.classification: Chablis premier cru climat. It may be labelled under its own name or under the principal climat Vau de Vey, to which the cahier des charges attaches it.

fr-chablis-premier-cru-vosgros.name: Chablis premier cru Vosgros
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vosgros.summary: Vosgros is a 22.6 ha Chablis premier cru in Chichée, southeast of the town, with its satellite Vaugiraut. The wine is fresh, mineral and citrus-driven.
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vosgros.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 185 to 215 m, gentle slope, Kimmeridgian marl and limestone. On the map it lies above Vaugiraut.
producers: Domaine Gilbert Picq et ses Fils
fr-chablis-premier-cru-vosgros.nerd_note: Its west-southwest exposure gives afternoon sun, like Fourchaume's.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-bea.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Aux Beaux Bruns
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-bea.summary: Aux Beaux Bruns is a 1.5 ha premier cru below the village, near the Route des Grands Crus. The name means 'fine browns', probably for its soil colour. Barthod's Beaux Bruns is the best-known; the wine is deeper and more structured than most lower-slope Chambolle.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-bea.terroir: Flat, southeast exposure at about 265 m, on deep brown clay over limestone.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-bea.nerd_note: Barthod's Beaux Bruns is often the most solidly built of her premier crus, a sign of its deeper soil.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-com.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Aux Combottes
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-com.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.83 ha on the lower slope near the Route des Grands Crus, not to be confused with Les Combottes nearby or with Gevrey's Aux Combottes. The wine is a supple Chambolle premier cru.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-com.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 260 m, almost flat, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-com.nerd_note: Chambolle has two premier crus called Combottes, a reminder that Burgundy's climats were named by farmers, not marketers.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-ech.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Aux Echanges
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-ech.summary: A small premier cru of 0.93 ha on the lower slope near the Route des Grands Crus. The name records a land exchange. The wine is a soft, red-fruited Chambolle premier cru.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-ech.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 260 m, nearly flat, on brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Aux Combottes, Aux Beaux Bruns and Les Groseilles.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-aux-ech.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus in Chambolle.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-derrier.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Derrière la Grange
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-derrier.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.47 ha just north of the village, behind an old barn (*grange*). Amiot-Servelle's version is the best-known. The wine is perfumed and fine-boned.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-derrier.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 275 m, on thin limestone soils.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-derrier.nerd_note: With Les Lavrottes and Les Fuées it forms the group of small premier crus just north of the village houses.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-la-comb.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru La Combe d'Orveau
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-la-comb.summary:
La Combe d'Orveau lies at the southern end of Chambolle, beside Musigny, on the side of the small combe that separates Chambolle from Vosne's En Orveaux. The INAO delimitation gives 2.2 ha of premier cru; much of the lieu-dit is village Chambolle. The wine is cool, perfumed and fine, close to Musigny's elegance in the best parcels.

The combe is a small, cool side valley, and the premier cru vines sit on its north-facing flank next to Musigny, on thin, stony soil. In ripe vintages that coolness gives wines of exceptional poise and perfume; Bruno Clavelier's old-vine bottling and Perrot-Minot's are often compared to a junior Musigny.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-la-comb.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 295 m, moderately steep. Thin, stony limestone soils, cooled by air from the combe.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-la-comb.nerd_note: Musigny itself includes a slice of the Combe d'Orveau lieu-dit, so a few growers own Combe d'Orveau vines that are grand cru.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-amo.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Amoureuses
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-amo.summary:
Les Amoureuses is the most famous premier cru in Burgundy and, on price, often beats grands crus such as Clos de Vougeot and Echezeaux. It lies directly below Musigny, separated from it only by a narrow track, and runs down to the walls of Clos de Vougeot. The INAO delimitation measures 5.3 ha; the planted area is usually given as 5.4 ha.

The wine is the purest expression of Chambolle: pale to mid ruby, intensely perfumed (rose, violet, raspberry, wild strawberry), silky and weightless in the mouth but very long, with a fine, almost invisible tannin. Where Musigny adds depth and gravity, Amoureuses gives grace and lift.

The largest holder is Domaine Robert Groffier (about 1.1 ha); others include de Vogüé, Mugnier, Roumier, Drouhin and Amiot-Servelle, and for each it is one of the most sought-after wines in the cellar.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-amo.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 240 to 280 m. Thin, pebbly soil over hard Comblanchien and Bathonian limestone, with very little clay at the surface and fissured rock close below. The vineyard falls away in a slight bowl toward Clos de Vougeot, so drainage is excellent.
producers: Domaine Robert Groffier Père et Fils
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-amo.nerd_note: Groffier's 1.1 ha make it the Amoureuses most often seen; the half-hectare holdings of Mugnier and de Vogüé and Roumier's even smaller parcel yield only a few barrels a year.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-bau.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Baudes
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-bau.summary:
Les Baudes sits just below Bonnes-Mares, at 3.5 ha. Its wines have the structure of their grand cru neighbour: firm, darker-fruited Chambolle, often slow to open.

Les Baudes lies just below the southern tip of Bonnes-Mares, between Les Sentiers and Les Noirots, and its wines carry something of the grand cru's structure and dark fruit. Barthod's Baudes is among the firmest of her nine-odd Chambolle premier crus and usually needs several years to open.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-bau.terroir: East-facing at about 270 m, on brown limestone-clay over Comblanchien limestone. The soil here contains more clay than in the southern premier crus of Chambolle, the same feature that gives Bonnes-Mares its power.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-bau.nerd_note: Les Baudes, Les Sentiers and Les Fuées are the premier crus that touch Bonnes-Mares, and all three share some of its firmness.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-bor.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Borniques
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-bor.summary: Les Borniques is a 1.4 ha premier cru touching Musigny on its northern side, above Les Amoureuses. The wine shares some of Musigny's depth and perfume and is one of the less-known gems of the village.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-bor.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 275 to 285 m, on thin, stony limestone soils.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-bor.nerd_note: It is one of three premier crus that touch Musigny, with Les Amoureuses and La Combe d'Orveau.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-car.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Carrières
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-car.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.52 ha near Les Chatelots, named for an old quarry. The wine is a perfumed Chambolle premier cru, rarely bottled alone.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-car.terroir: East-facing at about 265 m on stony limestone. On the map it lies beside Les Chatelots and Les Gruenchers.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-car.nerd_note: Quarries were dug all along the Côte for building stone and for the lime kilns that made mortar.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Chabiots
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.summary: A 1.5 ha premier cru above Les Amoureuses and near Les Borniques, south of the village. It gives a perfumed, fine-boned Chambolle with good tension.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 270 to 280 m on stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Borniques and above Les Amoureuses, Les Plantes and Les Hauts Doix.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.nerd_note: Its neighbour Les Amoureuses lies just downslope.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Charmes
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.summary:
Les Charmes is one of Chambolle's largest premier crus, at 9.3 ha, on the gentle lower slope east of the village between Les Amoureuses and the Route des Grands Crus. The name refers to *chaume*, fallow land, rather than charm, though the wine has plenty: soft, round, cherry-fruited Chambolle that drinks well young.

It lacks the tension of Les Amoureuses or Les Cras, but good growers make a deeply perfumed wine with Chambolle's velvet texture.

Les Charmes is also a good illustration of how Chambolle's premier crus change with altitude: the lower, flatter end near the Route des Grands Crus gives softer, fruit-forward wines, while the upper end toward Les Chabiots and Les Feusselottes, on thinner soil, gives more perfume and tension. Labels rarely say which end, so the producer matters.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.terroir: Almost flat, east exposure at 250 to 270 m. Deeper brown limestone-clay than the upper premier crus, over Comblanchien limestone.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.nerd_note: Barthod's Charmes is a good place to start a tasting of the domaine's nine-odd Chambolle premier crus.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Chatelots
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.summary: Les Chatelots is a 3.0 ha premier cru just east of the village, on the gentle slope toward Les Charmes. It gives a perfumed, medium-bodied Chambolle with red fruit and fine tannin.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.terroir: Gentle east-northeast slope at about 265 m, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cha.nerd_note: Barthod bottles it separately, which lets you compare it with her Charmes and Beaux Bruns just downslope.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-com.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Combottes
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-com.summary: A 0.72 ha premier cru on the gentle slope between Les Charmes and the village. Roumier's Combottes is the best-known. The wine is perfumed, red-fruited and silky.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-com.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 265 m, on brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Charmes, Les Chatelots, Les Plantes and Aux Combottes.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-com.nerd_note: Roumier makes only a few barrels of it each year, and it is one of the domaine's least-known wines.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cra.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Cras
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cra.summary:
Les Cras lies above the village, on the slope toward the Combe d'Ambin, at 3.4 ha. *Cras* means stony ground, and the soil here is thin and pebbly. The wine is Chambolle's most mineral and structured premier cru after Les Amoureuses: red cherry, violet and crushed stone, with a firm, fine tannin that needs time. Roumier and Barthod make the reference wines.

It sits on the upper slope northwest of the village, above Derrière la Grange and beside Les Fuées, in the cool air that drains out of the Combe d'Ambin. That position explains its later ripening and its austere youth; patient drinkers are rewarded with one of the most complex wines of Chambolle after Les Amoureuses.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cra.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 305 m, moderately steep. Thin, stony soil on hard limestone, cooled by air from the Combe d'Ambin.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-cra.nerd_note: Roumier's Les Cras is often its most austere wine in youth, and one of the best agers of the domaine.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-feu.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Feusselottes
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-feu.summary:
Les Feusselottes is a 4.4 ha premier cru just east of the village, between Les Chatelots and Les Charmes. The wine is perfumed, fine and red-fruited, a classic mid-slope Chambolle.

It sits on the mid-slope band with Les Chatelots above and Les Charmes and Les Plantes below. Mugneret-Gibourg's version, one of only two premiers crus the Vosne estate makes, has given the climat a following well beyond its modest reputation.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-feu.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, on brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 4%, and the soil is moderately deep brown limestone-clay, giving a wine that sits between the plush lower slope and the stony upper climats.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-feu.nerd_note: It lies between Les Chatelots and Les Charmes, part of the broad mid-slope band that makes up most of Chambolle's premier cru area.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-fue.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Fuées
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-fue.summary:
Les Fuées sits directly above Bonnes-Mares, at 4.4 ha, on the north side of the Combe d'Ambin. It is Chambolle's most structured premier cru in the north of the village, and its wine resembles a lighter Bonnes-Mares: dark cherry, spice and a firm tannin. Mugnier's Fuées is the benchmark.

With Les Baudes and Les Sentiers it is one of the three premiers crus that touch Bonnes-Mares, and the most highly regarded of them. The soil is thin and stony, so its wines combine Bonnes-Mares' structure with Chambolle's lifted perfume.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-fue.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 275 to 310 m, moderately steep, with thin soil over hard Bathonian limestone. The lower edge touches the white marl of Bonnes-Mares.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-fue.nerd_note: Mugnier's Fuées is often the darkest wine in its cellar after Musigny and Bonnes-Mares.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-gro.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Groseilles
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-gro.summary: Les Groseilles ('redcurrants') is a 1.4 ha premier cru below the village. The wine is soft, red-fruited and early-drinking, a Chambolle that lives up to its name.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-gro.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 265 m, nearly flat, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-gro.nerd_note: Redcurrant bushes were often planted along vineyard edges in Burgundy, and the name may record such a hedge.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-gru.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Gruenchers
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-gru.summary:
Les Gruenchers is a 2.8 ha premier cru just east of the village, close to Les Chatelots. Dujac and Fourrier both bottle it. The wine is perfumed, red-fruited and silky.

It sits just east of the village among a dense patchwork of small premier crus, with Les Chatelots, Les Groseilles and Les Noirots around it. Fourrier's old-vine Gruenchers and Dujac's version show a silky, perfumed side of Chambolle that sits between the plush lower slope and the austere Cras.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-gru.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 265 m on brown limestone-clay.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-gru.nerd_note: Morey-Saint-Denis has a smaller premier cru with the same name.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-hau.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Hauts Doix
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-hau.summary:
Les Hauts Doix is a 1.7 ha premier cru just north of Les Amoureuses. It shares the same thin, stony soils, and its wines are perfumed and silky with a firmer core. Groffier and Drouhin make the best-known versions.

It shares its neighbour's thin, pebbly soil over hard limestone, with Les Charmes and Les Chabiots alongside. Many tasters find it the closest in style to Amoureuses of all Chambolle's premiers crus, with a little more firmness and a little less flamboyance, at a fraction of the price.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-hau.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 275 m, on stony limestone soils. Like Les Amoureuses, it has thin soil over fissured hard limestone, and its slight east-southeast tilt gives it good morning sun.
producers: Domaine Robert Groffier Père et Fils
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-hau.nerd_note: Groffier's Hauts Doix is often described as the domaine's most underrated wine.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-lav.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Lavrottes
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-lav.summary: A small premier cru of 0.92 ha just north of the village, below Les Fuées. Its wine is a firm, perfumed Chambolle premier cru.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-lav.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 275 m on stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below the grand cru Bonnes-Mares, above Les Noirots and Les Gruenchers and beside Les Baudes.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-lav.nerd_note: The name probably comes from *lave*, the flat limestone slabs once used to roof vineyard huts.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-noi.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Noirots
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-noi.summary: Les Noirots is a 2.9 ha premier cru below Bonnes-Mares and Les Baudes, near the village. The name suggests dark soil. The wine is a firm, medium-bodied Chambolle premier cru.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-noi.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-noi.nerd_note: It sits between Les Baudes and Les Groseilles, at the point where Chambolle's northern premier crus start to lose the structure that Bonnes-Mares lends them.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-pla.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Plantes
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-pla.summary: A 2.6 ha premier cru on the lower slope near Les Charmes. The name refers to new plantings. The wine is a soft, red-fruited Chambolle premier cru.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-pla.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 270 m, gentle slope, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-pla.nerd_note: *Plantes* is a common climat name in Burgundy: it marks land planted to vines later than its neighbours.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-sen.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Sentiers
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-sen.summary:
Les Sentiers lies at the northern edge of Chambolle, at 4.9 ha, just below Bonnes-Mares and next to Morey's La Bussière. It gives a more structured Chambolle than the premier crus near Musigny, with dark fruit and firm tannin.

It sits just below Bonnes-Mares, with Les Baudes to the south and Morey's Les Ruchots and La Bussière across the commune line, on deeper, more clay-rich soil than the southern premier crus. Its wines are darker and firmer than most Chambolle premier crus, a reminder that the north of the village leans toward Morey in style.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-sen.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with more clay than the southern premier crus.
producers: Domaine Robert Groffier Père et Fils
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-sen.nerd_note: Les Sentiers is one of the few Chambolle premier crus to touch Morey-Saint-Denis.

fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-ver.name: Chambolle-Musigny premier cru Les Véroilles
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-ver.summary: Les Véroilles is a tiny, steep premier cru of 0.42 ha high above Bonnes-Mares, at the edge of the Combe d'Ambin. Only this part of the lieu-dit is premier cru; the rest is village Chambolle. The wine is lean, cool and mineral.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-ver.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 300 to 320 m, slope around 22%. Thin, stony soil over hard limestone.
fr-chambolle-musigny-premier-cru-les-ver.nerd_note: It is the highest of Chambolle's premier crus.

fr-champagne-ailleville.name: Ailleville
fr-champagne-ailleville.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-ailleville.summary: Ailleville is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar has no chalk: here Pinot Noir grows on Kimmeridgian marls and limestone, closer to Chablis than to Épernay, and gives round, fruit-rich wines.
fr-champagne-ailleville.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-allemant.name: Allemant
fr-champagne-allemant.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-allemant.summary: Allemant is a Champagne village of the Côte de Sézanne, about 8 km north-east of Sézanne. On the east and south-east-facing Côte de Sézanne, Chardonnay grows on chalk under a cover of clay and silt; houses use its ripe, soft fruit to round off blends.
fr-champagne-allemant.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-ambonnay.name: Ambonnay
fr-champagne-ambonnay.summary:
Ambonnay sits on the south-eastern flank of the Montagne de Reims, where the slope turns to face south and south-east over the Marne plain, next door to Bouzy. It is one of the great Pinot Noir villages of Champagne: its grapes are ripe, full and vinous, with a red-fruited depth that gives backbone to blends and makes Ambonnay a favourite for blanc de noirs and rosé. The village also makes still red Coteaux Champenois.

Krug's Clos d'Ambonnay, a walled plot of 0.68 ha first released with the 1995 vintage, is a pure Pinot Noir and one of the most expensive Champagnes made. Egly-Ouriet, whose long-aged, low-dosage wines are references for grower Champagne, Marguet (biodynamic), Paul Déthune and Eric Rodez are based here.
fr-champagne-ambonnay.terroir: South and south-east-facing slopes of chalk under a thin cover of limestone scree and clay, at the foot of the forested Montagne plateau.
fr-champagne-ambonnay.nerd_note: Krug's Clos d'Ambonnay is about a third of the size of its Clos du Mesnil, and the first vintage took 13 years to reach the market.
fr-champagne-ambonnay.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-arcis-le-ponsart.name: Arcis-le-Ponsart
fr-champagne-arcis-le-ponsart.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-arcis-le-ponsart.summary: Arcis-le-Ponsart is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Vallée de l'Ardre), about 9 km north-west of Ville-en-Tardenois. The Ardre valley and the Tardenois plateau grow mostly Meunier, with some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, on sands and clays over deep chalk; most of the grapes go to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-arcis-le-ponsart.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-arconville.name: Arconville
fr-champagne-arconville.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-arconville.summary: Arconville is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 9 km south of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. In the Bar-sur-Aubois, the eastern half of the Côte des Bar, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and limestone, the Jurassic rocks of Chablis rather than the chalk of the Marne; the wines are ripe and fruity.
fr-champagne-arconville.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-argancon.name: Argançon
fr-champagne-argancon.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-argancon.summary: Argançon is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 8 km west of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. Its south-facing slopes in the valleys around Bar-sur-Aube are planted mainly to Pinot Noir on Jurassic marl and limestone; much of the fruit has long gone to the houses of the Marne.
fr-champagne-argancon.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-arrentieres.name: Arrentières
fr-champagne-arrentieres.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-arrentieres.summary: Arrentières is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 4 km north-east of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar has no chalk: here Pinot Noir grows on Kimmeridgian marls and limestone, closer to Chablis than to Épernay, and gives round, fruit-rich wines.
fr-champagne-arrentieres.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-arsonval.name: Arsonval
fr-champagne-arsonval.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-arsonval.summary: Arsonval is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 6 km north-west of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. In the Bar-sur-Aubois, the eastern half of the Côte des Bar, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and limestone, the Jurassic rocks of Chablis rather than the chalk of the Marne; the wines are ripe and fruity.
fr-champagne-arsonval.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-aubilly.name: Aubilly
fr-champagne-aubilly.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-aubilly.summary: Aubilly is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Vallée de l'Ardre), about 6 km north-east of Ville-en-Tardenois. The Ardre valley and the Tardenois plateau grow mostly Meunier, with some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, on sands and clays over deep chalk; most of the grapes go to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-aubilly.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-aulnay-aux-planches.name: Aulnay-aux-Planches
fr-champagne-aulnay-aux-planches.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-aulnay-aux-planches.summary: Aulnay-aux-Planches is a Champagne village of the Côte des Blancs (Southern Côte des Blancs (Mont Aimé, Val-des-Marais)), about 10 km south of Vertus. Around the Mont Aimé and the Val-des-Marais, where the Côte des Blancs escarpment fades out to the south, Chardonnay dominates on chalk under clay and silt.
fr-champagne-aulnay-aux-planches.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%. Associated commune of Val-des-Marais; inside the AOC commune list as part of Val-des-Marais.

fr-champagne-aulnizeux.name: Aulnizeux
fr-champagne-aulnizeux.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-aulnizeux.summary: Aulnizeux is a Champagne village of the Côte des Blancs (Southern Côte des Blancs (Mont Aimé, Val-des-Marais)), about 11 km south-west of Vertus. This is the southern tail of the Côte des Blancs: Chardonnay on chalky slopes and gentle land, fresher and lighter than in the grand crus.
fr-champagne-aulnizeux.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%. Associated commune of Val-des-Marais; inside the AOC commune list as part of Val-des-Marais.

fr-champagne-avenay-val-d-or.name: Avenay-Val-d'Or
fr-champagne-avenay-val-d-or.summary: A premier cru (93%) in the Val d'Or, a side valley that opens onto the Marne near Aÿ, planted mainly with Pinot Noir and Meunier. Its sheltered, south-facing slopes give rounder, riper fruit than the exposed northern face of the Montagne de Reims.
fr-champagne-avenay-val-d-or.terroir: Sheltered, south-facing slopes of the Val d'Or on chalk under marl, opening onto the Marne near Aÿ.
fr-champagne-avenay-val-d-or.classification: Premier cru village: rated 93% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-avirey-lingey.name: Avirey-Lingey
fr-champagne-avirey-lingey.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-avirey-lingey.summary: Avirey-Lingey is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 11 km south-west of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. Its slopes belong to the Barséquanais, where Pinot Noir grows on Jurassic marl and limestone, the same rocks as Chablis, giving ripe, fruit-driven wines with a firm limestone edge. Champagne Serge Mathieu is based here.
fr-champagne-avirey-lingey.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-avize.name: Avize
fr-champagne-avize.summary:
Avize is the heart of the Côte des Blancs, on the east-facing escarpment south of Cramant. Its Chardonnay is rich, saline and deep, with more body than Le Mesnil and more tension than Cramant, from chalk with a little more clay than its neighbours.

It is the home of the Lycée Viticole de la Champagne and of Anselme Selosse, who took over his father's vines in 1974 and changed Champagne by vinifying in barrels, farming for low yields and treating Champagne as a wine of place; his Substance is a solera begun in 1986. Agrapart, De Sousa and Varnier-Fannière are notable growers, and the Union Champagne cooperative (Champagne De Saint Gall) is based here. Big houses prize Avize fruit for blanc de blancs and prestige cuvées.
fr-champagne-avize.terroir: East-facing slopes of Belemnite chalk close to the surface, with a little more clay in the topsoil than in Le Mesnil.
fr-champagne-avize.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-ay.name: Aÿ
fr-champagne-ay.summary:
Aÿ is the historic capital of Pinot Noir in Champagne and part of the UNESCO-listed Champagne Hillsides, Houses and Cellars (2015). Its steep, south-facing slopes above the Marne give powerful, ripe and vinous Pinot Noir that underpins the blends of the greatest houses. The wines of Aÿ were famous at the courts of France long before sparkling Champagne existed; Henri IV is said to have called himself 'Sire d'Aÿ'.

Bollinger, Deutz and Ayala are based here, and Henri Giraud and Gatinois are notable growers. Bollinger's Vieilles Vignes Françaises comes from small plots of ungrafted Pinot Noir in Aÿ, and its La Côte aux Enfants is a still red Coteaux Champenois. In April 1911 rioting growers burned houses in Aÿ suspected of using grapes from outside the region, which led to the delimitation of the Champagne zone. Since 2016 Aÿ forms the commune of Aÿ-Champagne with Mareuil-sur-Aÿ and Bisseuil.
fr-champagne-ay.terroir: Steep south-facing slopes above the Marne, chalk under limestone scree and marl.
fr-champagne-ay.nerd_note: Bollinger's ungrafted Vieilles Vignes Françaises vines survived phylloxera in walled plots and are trained en foule, the old layered planting method of Champagne.
fr-champagne-ay.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-azy-sur-marne.name: Azy-sur-Marne
fr-champagne-azy-sur-marne.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-azy-sur-marne.summary: Azy-sur-Marne is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 5 km south-west of Château-Thierry, in the Aisne department. Like the rest of the western Marne valley it grows mainly Meunier, on slopes of clay, marl and sand with the chalk buried deep below; the wines are supple and fruity, and much of the fruit goes to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-azy-sur-marne.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-bagneux-la-fosse.name: Bagneux-la-Fosse
fr-champagne-bagneux-la-fosse.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-bagneux-la-fosse.summary: Bagneux-la-Fosse is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 15 km south-west of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. Its slopes belong to the Barséquanais, where Pinot Noir grows on Jurassic marl and limestone, the same rocks as Chablis, giving ripe, fruit-driven wines with a firm limestone edge.
fr-champagne-bagneux-la-fosse.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-balnot-sur-laignes.name: Balnot-sur-Laignes
fr-champagne-balnot-sur-laignes.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-balnot-sur-laignes.summary: Balnot-sur-Laignes is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 9 km south of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar around Bar-sur-Seine grows mostly Pinot Noir on Kimmeridgian marl; once a supplier of grapes to the Marne, it now has many grower-producers of its own.
fr-champagne-balnot-sur-laignes.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-bar-sur-aube.name: Bar-sur-Aube
fr-champagne-bar-sur-aube.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-bar-sur-aube.summary: Bar-sur-Aube is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar has no chalk: here Pinot Noir grows on Kimmeridgian marls and limestone, closer to Chablis than to Épernay, and gives round, fruit-rich wines. In 1911 Bar-sur-Aube was the centre of the Aube growers' revolt against their exclusion from the Champagne zone; the Aube was fully admitted in 1927.

fr-champagne-beaumont-sur-vesle.name: Beaumont-sur-Vesle
fr-champagne-beaumont-sur-vesle.summary:
A small grand cru on gentle, low-lying slopes at the north-eastern edge of the Montagne de Reims, on the Vesle river east of Sillery, planted with Pinot Noir and some Chardonnay. It is the least known grand cru: its vineyard is small, its slopes are gentle and close to the valley floor, and almost all its grapes go to the Reims houses, so a Champagne labelled with the village name is a rarity.

Its 100% rating reflects the échelle's logic, which rated villages partly on the price their grapes fetched: the chalky, well-drained soils and the demand from the houses kept Beaumont at 100%.
fr-champagne-beaumont-sur-vesle.terroir: Gentle slopes and flats of chalk along the Vesle, at the foot of the Montagne's north-eastern corner.
fr-champagne-beaumont-sur-vesle.nerd_note: With Sillery and Puisieulx it forms a trio of grand crus on the Vesle side of the Montagne, away from its classic slopes.
fr-champagne-beaumont-sur-vesle.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

The échelle rated its white grapes 95% and its black grapes 90%. Chardonnay here is ripe and supple, and the hilltop of Mont Aimé is crowned by the ruins of a medieval castle.
fr-champagne-bergeres-les-vertus.terroir: Chalk slopes at the foot of the Mont Aimé, south of Vertus.
fr-champagne-bergeres-les-vertus.classification: Premier cru village: rated 95% for white grapes, 90% for black on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

Bouzy is a south-facing grand cru on the southern flank of the Montagne de Reims, between Ambonnay and Louvois, and the most famous name for still red wine in Champagne: Bouzy Rouge, a Coteaux Champenois made from its ripest Pinot Noir. Its Pinot gives full, ripe, red-fruited Champagne with a vinous depth.

Paul Bara, Benoit Lahaye (a biodynamic grower), Barnaut, André Clouet and Pierre Paillard are local growers, and the big houses own and buy extensively here.
fr-champagne-bouzy.terroir: South-facing slopes of chalk with a thin topsoil, warm and well exposed.
fr-champagne-bouzy.nerd_note: Bouzy Rouge needs a warm year and low yields; in cool vintages growers often turn the same Pinot Noir into Champagne or blanc de noirs instead.
fr-champagne-bouzy.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-chouilly.name: Chouilly
fr-champagne-chouilly.summary:
Chouilly lies at the northern end of the Côte des Blancs, just east of Épernay, around the Butte de Saran and the hill of Montaigu. Its Chardonnay is a little rounder, earlier-maturing and more open than Cramant's, which makes it a useful component of blends and of approachable blanc de blancs. Under the old échelle only its white grapes were rated 100%; its Pinot Noir was rated 95%, and the whole commune has counted as grand cru since 2010.

Many houses own vines here, and Moët & Chandon's Château de Saran stands on the hill. The Centre Vinicole Champagne Nicolas Feuillatte, one of the largest cooperative groups in Champagne, has its winery in Chouilly; Legras & Haas and Vazart-Coquart are local growers.
fr-champagne-chouilly.terroir: East and north-east-facing slopes and gentle land of chalk, with deeper soils on the lower ground.
fr-champagne-chouilly.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru. Before 2010 the échelle rated its white grapes 100% and its black grapes 95%. Before 2010 the échelle rated Chouilly 100% for white grapes but 95% for black; today the whole commune is grand cru.

fr-champagne-coligny.name: Coligny

fr-champagne-coligny.terroir: Chalk slopes on the south side of the Mont Aimé, the outlier hill that ends the Côte des Blancs.
fr-champagne-coligny.nerd_note: The premier cru covers only the former commune of Coligny; the other villages merged into Val-des-Marais are autres crus.
fr-champagne-coligny.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% (white grapes only) on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-colombe-la-fosse.name: Colombé-la-Fosse
fr-champagne-colombe-la-fosse.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier

fr-champagne-colombe-le-sec.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier

Meunier, which buds late and copes with the frost-prone valley, dominates the clay and marl slopes here; the base wines are round and fruit-forward, the softening element of many blends.
fr-champagne-connigis.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

On the hills north-west of Reims around the Massif de Saint-Thierry, sandy and clay soils over chalk carry Meunier, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; the area was one of the historic vineyards of Reims.
fr-champagne-cormicy.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-cormontreuil.terroir: Gentle, chalky land at the northern foot of the Montagne de Reims, on the edge of the city, where housing and roads have taken much of the old vineyard.
fr-champagne-cormontreuil.classification: Premier cru village: rated 94% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-cormoyeux.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-cormoyeux.summary: Cormoyeux is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite), about 8 km north-west of Épernay. Its vineyards belong to the right bank of the Marne valley, where Meunier dominates on clay, marl and sand over chalk and gives generous, fruity wine; side valleys add cooler exposures.
fr-champagne-cormoyeux.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-coulommes-la-montagne.name: Coulommes-la-Montagne
fr-champagne-coulommes-la-montagne.summary: A small premier cru of the Petite Montagne de Reims west of the city, on slopes of sand and clay over chalk where Meunier is the main grape.
fr-champagne-coulommes-la-montagne.terroir: Slopes facing mostly north and east toward Reims, on sand and clay over chalk, below the forest that caps the Petite Montagne; Meunier copes best with these cooler, heavier soils.
fr-champagne-coulommes-la-montagne.nerd_note: Coulommes and Vrigny sit on the northern edge of the Petite Montagne, where the hill breaks down toward the Vesle valley.
fr-champagne-coulommes-la-montagne.classification: Premier cru village: rated between 90% and 99% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-courcelles-sapicourt.name: Courcelles-Sapicourt
fr-champagne-courcelles-sapicourt.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay

In the Saint-Thierry hills and along the Vesle west of Reims, Meunier leads on sands and clays over chalk, with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir on the chalkier slopes.
fr-champagne-courcelles-sapicourt.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-courmas.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

Its slopes belong to the Barséquanais, where Pinot Noir grows on Jurassic marl and limestone, the same rocks as Chablis, giving ripe, fruit-driven wines with a firm limestone edge. Champagne Fleury, which converted to biodynamics in 1989, the first in Champagne, is based here.

fr-champagne-courthiezy.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-courthiezy.summary: Courthiézy is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive gauche), about 4 km south-west of Dormans. The south side of the Marne valley is Meunier territory, on clay and marl over chalk, with cooler exposures than the right bank and fresh, fruity base wines.
fr-champagne-courthiezy.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-couvrot.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-cramant.name: Cramant
fr-champagne-cramant.summary:
A Chardonnay grand cru on a spur of the Côte des Blancs between Chouilly and Avize, known for creamy, floral, finely textured blanc de blancs. Its east and south-east-facing slopes of pure chalk give wines with less austerity than Le Mesnil and an aromatic, almost exotic ripeness in warm years.

Mumm's famous low-pressure 'Crémant de Cramant' had to be renamed Mumm de Cramant when the word crémant was reserved for sparkling wines from other French regions. Diebolt-Vallois, Lilbert-Fils, Bonnaire and Aurélien Suenen are notable growers, and the houses prize Cramant fruit for blanc de blancs and prestige blends.
fr-champagne-cramant.terroir: East to south-east-facing slopes of Belemnite chalk, with very thin topsoil on the upper slopes.
fr-champagne-cramant.nerd_note: Mumm de Cramant was traditionally bottled at lower pressure than standard Champagne, for a softer mousse, as the old crémant style required.
fr-champagne-cramant.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-crezancy.name: Crézancy
fr-champagne-crezancy.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay

fr-champagne-cuchery.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-cuis.name: Cuis
fr-champagne-cuis.summary: A premier cru at the northern end of the Côte des Blancs, mostly Chardonnay, on slopes higher and cooler than the grand crus nearby. Its wines have sharper acidity and lighter body, useful for freshness in blends. The échelle rated its white grapes 95% and its black grapes 90%. Pierre Gimonnet & Fils, a reference grower for blanc de blancs, is based in Cuis.
fr-champagne-cuis.classification: Premier cru village: rated 95% for white grapes, 90% for black on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-cuisles.name: Cuisles
fr-champagne-cuisles.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-cuisles.summary: Cuisles is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite), about 12 km north-east of Dormans. On the right bank of the Marne the main slopes face south toward the river; Meunier is the leading grape on clay and marl over chalk, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay on the best sites. Cédric Moussé of Moussé Fils, a grower known for Meunier-led Champagnes, works here.
fr-champagne-cuisles.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-cumieres.name: Cumières
fr-champagne-cumieres.summary: A Marne premier cru (93%) with steep, south-facing slopes right above the river, west of Dizy. It ripens early and is often the first village to start the harvest in Champagne, and it is known for still red Coteaux Champenois as well as rich, ripe Pinot Noir and Meunier for Champagne. René Geoffroy and Georges Laval are well-known growers with vines here.
fr-champagne-cumieres.classification: Premier cru village: rated 93% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-cunfin.name: Cunfin
fr-champagne-cunfin.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier

The Côte des Bar around Bar-sur-Seine grows mostly Pinot Noir on Kimmeridgian marl; once a supplier of grapes to the Marne, it now has many grower-producers of its own.
fr-champagne-cunfin.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-damery.name: Damery

Gaston Chiquet is a long-established grower here.
fr-champagne-dizy.terroir: South-facing slopes of the Grande Vallée de la Marne, chalk under marl and clay, between the Aÿ grand cru and Hautvillers.
fr-champagne-dizy.classification: Premier cru village: rated 95% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-domptin.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-domptin.summary: Domptin is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 10 km west of Château-Thierry, in the Aisne department. Meunier, which buds late and copes with the frost-prone valley, dominates the clay and marl slopes here; the base wines are round and fruit-forward, the softening element of many blends.
fr-champagne-domptin.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-dormans.name: Dormans
fr-champagne-dormans.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-dormans.summary: Dormans is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive gauche). On the left bank of the Marne many slopes face north or west toward the river, so the fruit is fresher; Meunier dominates on clay-rich soils over chalk. The town's Memorial of the Battles of the Marne, a chapel and ossuary, recalls the fighting of 1914 and 1918 along the valley.
fr-champagne-dormans.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-ecueil.name: Écueil
fr-champagne-ecueil.summary: A premier cru (90%) in the Petite Montagne de Reims, in a bowl of vineyards south-west of Reims below the forest. Unusually for the Petite Montagne, Pinot Noir is important here.
fr-champagne-ecueil.terroir: Slopes facing mostly north and east toward Reims, on sand and clay over chalk, below the forest that caps the Petite Montagne; Meunier copes best with these cooler, heavier soils.
fr-champagne-ecueil.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-eguilly-sous-bois.name: Éguilly-sous-Bois
fr-champagne-eguilly-sous-bois.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-eguilly-sous-bois.summary: Éguilly-sous-Bois is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 12 km east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. In the Barséquanais, the valleys of the Seine, Ource, Arce and Laignes around Bar-sur-Seine, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and Portlandian limestone; growers here led the rise of Côte des Bar grower Champagne.
fr-champagne-eguilly-sous-bois.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-engente.name: Engente
fr-champagne-engente.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-engente.summary: Engente is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 7 km north-east of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. In the Bar-sur-Aubois, the eastern half of the Côte des Bar, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and limestone, the Jurassic rocks of Chablis rather than the chalk of the Marne; the wines are ripe and fruity.
fr-champagne-engente.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-epernay.name: Épernay
fr-champagne-epernay.summary: Épernay is the second capital of Champagne: Moët & Chandon, Pol Roger, Perrier-Jouët, Mercier, De Castellane and many other houses line the Avenue de Champagne, part of the UNESCO listing of 2015, above dozens of kilometres of cellars dug into the chalk. The commune also has vineyards of its own on the slopes around the town.
fr-champagne-epernay.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-essomes-sur-marne.name: Essômes-sur-Marne
fr-champagne-essomes-sur-marne.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-essomes-sur-marne.summary: Essômes-sur-Marne is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 5 km west of Château-Thierry, in the Aisne department. Like the rest of the western Marne valley it grows mainly Meunier, on slopes of clay, marl and sand with the chalk buried deep below; the wines are supple and fruity, and much of the fruit goes to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-essomes-sur-marne.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-essoyes.name: Essoyes
fr-champagne-essoyes.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-essoyes.summary: Essoyes is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 14 km east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. Its slopes belong to the Barséquanais, where Pinot Noir grows on Jurassic marl and limestone, the same rocks as Chablis, giving ripe, fruit-driven wines with a firm limestone edge. Essoyes was the family home of the painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir, who spent summers here and is buried in the village; his studio is open to visitors.
fr-champagne-essoyes.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-etampes-sur-marne.name: Étampes-sur-Marne
fr-champagne-etampes-sur-marne.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-etampes-sur-marne.summary: Étampes-sur-Marne is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), in the Aisne department. This is Meunier country: the chalk lies too deep to matter, and the clay-rich slopes along the valley give fleshy, early-maturing wines, many of them sold to the cooperatives of the Aisne.
fr-champagne-etampes-sur-marne.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-etoges.name: Étoges
fr-champagne-etoges.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-etoges.summary: Étoges is a Champagne village of the Côte de Sézanne (Val du Petit Morin), about 11 km west of Vertus. The Petit Morin valley links the Côte des Blancs to the Côte de Sézanne; its slopes grow mainly Chardonnay on chalk with clay. Its seventeenth-century château, surrounded by moats, is now a hotel.
fr-champagne-etoges.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-etrechy.name: Étréchy
fr-champagne-etrechy.summary: A small premier cru, historically for Chardonnay only (90%), on the slopes west of Bergères-lès-Vertus at the southern end of the Côte des Blancs. Its Chardonnay is fresh and lean, mostly sold to the houses.
fr-champagne-etrechy.terroir: Chalk slopes facing east and south-east near the Mont Aimé, at the southern end of the Côte des Blancs.
fr-champagne-etrechy.nerd_note: Like Coligny, Étréchy was historically rated premier cru for Chardonnay only.
fr-champagne-etrechy.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% (white grapes only) on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru. Historically premier cru for Chardonnay only; the cahier now lists the commune without restriction.

fr-champagne-faverolles-et-coemy.name: Faverolles-et-Coëmy
fr-champagne-faverolles-et-coemy.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-faverolles-et-coemy.summary: Faverolles-et-Coëmy is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Vallée de l'Ardre), about 7 km north of Ville-en-Tardenois. In the valley of the Ardre, a tributary of the Vesle west of Reims, Meunier dominates on sandy and clay soils over chalk; the vines are scattered among woods and fields, and the wines are supple and fruity.
fr-champagne-faverolles-et-coemy.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-ferebrianges.name: Fèrebrianges
fr-champagne-ferebrianges.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-ferebrianges.summary: Fèrebrianges is a Champagne village of the Côte de Sézanne (Val du Petit Morin), about 13 km west of Vertus. In the valley of the Petit Morin and around the Saint-Gond marshes, between the Côte des Blancs and Sézanne, Chardonnay dominates with some Meunier and Pinot Noir on chalk and clay.
fr-champagne-ferebrianges.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-festigny.name: Festigny
fr-champagne-festigny.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-festigny.summary: Festigny is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive gauche), about 12 km south-east of Dormans. The south side of the Marne valley is Meunier territory, on clay and marl over chalk, with cooler exposures than the right bank and fresh, fruity base wines.
fr-champagne-festigny.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-fleury-la-riviere.name: Fleury-la-Rivière
fr-champagne-fleury-la-riviere.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-fleury-la-riviere.summary: Fleury-la-Rivière is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite), about 9 km north-west of Épernay. On the right bank of the Marne the main slopes face south toward the river; Meunier is the leading grape on clay and marl over chalk, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay on the best sites. Its Cave aux Coquillages, a cellar cut into a bank of Lutetian limestone packed with fossil shells, shows the Tertiary sea beds that lie over the chalk in this part of the valley.
fr-champagne-fleury-la-riviere.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-fontaine.name: Fontaine
fr-champagne-fontaine.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-fontaine.summary: Fontaine is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 3 km south-east of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. Its south-facing slopes in the valleys around Bar-sur-Aube are planted mainly to Pinot Noir on Jurassic marl and limestone; much of the fruit has long gone to the houses of the Marne.
fr-champagne-fontaine.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-fontaine-denis-nuisy.name: Fontaine-Denis-Nuisy
fr-champagne-fontaine-denis-nuisy.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-fontaine-denis-nuisy.summary: Fontaine-Denis-Nuisy is a Champagne village of the Côte de Sézanne, about 10 km south of Sézanne. The Côte de Sézanne continues the Côte des Blancs escarpment south of the Saint-Gond marshes; Chardonnay dominates on chalk covered with clay and silt, and the wines are riper and rounder than in the Côte des Blancs.
fr-champagne-fontaine-denis-nuisy.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-fontaine-sur-ay.name: Fontaine-sur-Ay
fr-champagne-fontaine-sur-ay.summary: Fontaine-sur-Ay is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Grande Vallée de la Marne), about 9 km north-east of Épernay. Its vineyards share the slopes of the Grande Vallée de la Marne with the premier and grand crus below, with Pinot Noir and Meunier on chalk under marl.
fr-champagne-fontaine-sur-ay.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-fontette.name: Fontette
fr-champagne-fontette.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-fontette.summary: Fontette is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 18 km east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar around Bar-sur-Seine grows mostly Pinot Noir on Kimmeridgian marl; once a supplier of grapes to the Marne, it now has many grower-producers of its own.
fr-champagne-fontette.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-germaine.name: Germaine
fr-champagne-germaine.summary: Germaine is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Grande Montagne de Reims), about 15 km south of Reims. It lies on the Grande Montagne de Reims among grand and premier crus, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay on chalk under the forested plateau.
fr-champagne-germaine.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-germigny.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-germigny.summary: Germigny is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Vallée de l'Ardre), about 8 km north-east of Ville-en-Tardenois. The Ardre valley and the Tardenois plateau grow mostly Meunier, with some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, on sands and clays over deep chalk; most of the grapes go to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-germigny.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-gionges.name: Gionges
fr-champagne-gionges.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-gionges.summary: Gionges is a Champagne village of the Côte des Blancs, about 4 km north-west of Vertus. Its slopes belong to the Côte des Blancs escarpment, planted mostly to Chardonnay on chalk.
fr-champagne-gionges.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%. Former commune merged into Blancs-Coteaux (2018); the AOC commune list names Blancs-Coteaux as a whole.

fr-champagne-givry-les-loisy.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-givry-les-loisy.summary: Givry-lès-Loisy is a Champagne village of the Côte des Blancs (Southern Côte des Blancs (Mont Aimé, Val-des-Marais)), about 7 km west of Vertus. Around the Mont Aimé and the Val-des-Marais, where the Côte des Blancs escarpment fades out to the south, Chardonnay dominates on chalk under clay and silt.

fr-champagne-glannes.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-glannes.summary: Glannes is a Champagne village of the Vitryat, about 7 km west of Vitry-le-François. Its vines belong to the small Vitryat outpost, mostly Chardonnay on chalk slopes, sold largely to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-glannes.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-grauves.name: Grauves
fr-champagne-grauves.summary: A premier cru in a side valley west of Cramant and Avize, behind the main slope of the Côte des Blancs, with Chardonnay on cooler, more varied exposures. The échelle rated its white grapes 95% and its black grapes 90%; its wines are lean and fresh, good material for blends.
fr-champagne-grauves.terroir: Chalk slopes of the Grauves valley behind the main escarpment, with more varied exposures than Cramant or Avize.
fr-champagne-grauves.classification: Premier cru village: rated 95% for white grapes, 90% for black on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-gueux.name: Gueux
fr-champagne-gueux.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-gueux.summary: Gueux is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Petite Montagne de Reims), about 9 km west of Reims. The Petite Montagne's slopes face mostly north and east toward Reims; on sands and clays over chalk, Meunier gives fresh, fruity base wines. Jérôme Prévost's La Closerie, a cult Meunier grower, farms Les Béguines here on sandy soils.
fr-champagne-gueux.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-gye-sur-seine.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier

fr-champagne-hautvillers.name: Hautvillers
fr-champagne-hautvillers.summary:
The hilltop village of the Benedictine abbey of Saint-Pierre, where Dom Pierre Pérignon was cellarer from 1668 until his death in 1715, and part of the UNESCO-listed Champagne hillsides. Its slopes face south over the Marne and give ripe Pinot Noir and Meunier; it was rated 93% on the échelle.

Moët & Chandon owns the abbey, where Dom Pérignon is buried, and wrought-iron signs on the village houses show trades and wine scenes.
fr-champagne-hautvillers.classification: Premier cru village: rated 93% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-hermonville.name: Hermonville
fr-champagne-hermonville.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-hermonville.summary: Hermonville is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Massif de Saint-Thierry and the Vesle), about 12 km north-west of Reims. In the Saint-Thierry hills and along the Vesle west of Reims, Meunier leads on sands and clays over chalk, with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir on the chalkier slopes.
fr-champagne-hermonville.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-jaulgonne.name: Jaulgonne
fr-champagne-jaulgonne.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-jaulgonne.summary: Jaulgonne is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 8 km west of Dormans, in the Aisne department. Meunier, which buds late and copes with the frost-prone valley, dominates the clay and marl slopes here; the base wines are round and fruit-forward, the softening element of many blends.
fr-champagne-jaulgonne.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-jonchery-sur-vesle.name: Jonchery-sur-Vesle
fr-champagne-jonchery-sur-vesle.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-jonchery-sur-vesle.summary: Jonchery-sur-Vesle is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Massif de Saint-Thierry and the Vesle), about 10 km east of Fismes. In the Saint-Thierry hills and along the Vesle west of Reims, Meunier leads on sands and clays over chalk, with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir on the chalkier slopes.
fr-champagne-jonchery-sur-vesle.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-jonquery.name: Jonquery
fr-champagne-jonquery.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-jonquery.summary: Jonquery is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite), about 14 km north-east of Dormans. On the right bank of the Marne the main slopes face south toward the river; Meunier is the leading grape on clay and marl over chalk, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay on the best sites.
fr-champagne-jonquery.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-jouy-les-reims.name: Jouy-lès-Reims
fr-champagne-jouy-les-reims.summary: A premier cru (90%) of the Petite Montagne de Reims, home of L. Aubry Fils, known for reviving the old Champagne varieties Arbane, Petit Meslier and Pinot Blanc alongside the main three.
fr-champagne-jouy-les-reims.terroir: Slopes facing mostly north and east toward Reims, on sand and clay over chalk, below the forest that caps the Petite Montagne; Meunier copes best with these cooler, heavier soils.
fr-champagne-jouy-les-reims.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-la-celle-sous-chantemerle.name: La Celle-sous-Chantemerle
fr-champagne-la-celle-sous-chantemerle.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-la-celle-sous-chantemerle.summary: La Celle-sous-Chantemerle is a Champagne village of the Côte de Sézanne, about 13 km south of Sézanne. The Côte de Sézanne continues the Côte des Blancs escarpment south of the Saint-Gond marshes; Chardonnay dominates on chalk covered with clay and silt, and the wines are riper and rounder than in the Côte des Blancs.
fr-champagne-la-celle-sous-chantemerle.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-la-chapelle-monthodon.name: La Chapelle-Monthodon
fr-champagne-la-chapelle-monthodon.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-la-chapelle-monthodon.summary: La Chapelle-Monthodon is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 6 km south of Dormans, in the Aisne department. This is Meunier country: the chalk lies too deep to matter, and the clay-rich slopes along the valley give fleshy, early-maturing wines, many of them sold to the cooperatives of the Aisne.
fr-champagne-la-chapelle-monthodon.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-la-neuville-aux-larris.summary: La Neuville-aux-Larris is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite), about 14 km north-west of Épernay.
