fr-champagne-la-neuville-aux-larris.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-lagery.name: Lagery
fr-champagne-lagery.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-lagery.summary: Lagery is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Vallée de l'Ardre), about 5 km north-west of Ville-en-Tardenois. The Ardre valley and the Tardenois plateau grow mostly Meunier, with some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, on sands and clays over deep chalk; most of the grapes go to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-lagery.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-landreville.name: Landreville
fr-champagne-landreville.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-landreville.summary: Landreville is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 8 km south-east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. In the Barséquanais, the valleys of the Seine, Ource, Arce and Laignes around Bar-sur-Seine, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and Portlandian limestone; growers here led the rise of Côte des Bar grower Champagne. Charles Dufour, a grower known for low-intervention Champagnes, is based here.
fr-champagne-landreville.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-le-breuil.name: Le Breuil
fr-champagne-le-breuil.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-le-breuil.summary: Le Breuil is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive gauche), about 9 km south of Dormans. The south side of the Marne valley is Meunier territory, on clay and marl over chalk, with cooler exposures than the right bank and fresh, fruity base wines.
fr-champagne-le-breuil.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-le-mesnil-sur-oger.name: Le Mesnil-sur-Oger
fr-champagne-le-mesnil-sur-oger.summary:
The most austere and long-lived of the Chardonnay grand crus, on almost pure chalk at the southern end of the Côte des Blancs. Le Mesnil's wines are lean, piercing and saline when young and need years to show their depth; they are the reference for long-ageing blanc de blancs.

Salon, the original blanc de blancs, is made only from Le Mesnil grapes and only in exceptional years, and its sister house Delamotte is based here too. Krug's Clos du Mesnil, a walled vineyard of 1.85 ha first enclosed in 1698 and bought by Krug in 1971, gave its first vintage in 1979. Pierre Péters, Robert Moncuit, Guy Charlemagne, Pertois-Moriset and Jacques Selosse also make wines from it.
fr-champagne-le-mesnil-sur-oger.terroir: East-facing slopes of Belemnite chalk with very thin topsoil.
fr-champagne-le-mesnil-sur-oger.nerd_note: Pierre Péters' Les Chétillons, from three old parcels of Le Mesnil, is one of the most sought-after grower blanc de blancs.
fr-champagne-le-mesnil-sur-oger.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-les-mesneux.name: Les Mesneux
fr-champagne-les-mesneux.summary: A small premier cru (90%) at the foot of the Petite Montagne de Reims just south-west of the city.
fr-champagne-les-mesneux.terroir: Slopes facing mostly north and east toward Reims, on sand and clay over chalk, below the forest that caps the Petite Montagne; Meunier copes best with these cooler, heavier soils.
fr-champagne-les-mesneux.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-les-riceys.name: Les Riceys
fr-champagne-les-riceys.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-les-riceys.summary: Les Riceys is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 14 km south of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. In the Barséquanais, the valleys of the Seine, Ource, Arce and Laignes around Bar-sur-Seine, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and Portlandian limestone; growers here led the rise of Côte des Bar grower Champagne. Les Riceys is the largest wine commune of Champagne and the only one with three appellations: Champagne, Coteaux Champenois and the rare still Rosé des Riceys, made from Pinot Noir. Olivier Horiot and Alexandre Bonnet are leading producers.
fr-champagne-les-riceys.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-leuvrigny.name: Leuvrigny
fr-champagne-leuvrigny.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-leuvrigny.summary: Leuvrigny is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive gauche), about 11 km east of Dormans. On the left bank of the Marne many slopes face north or west toward the river, so the fruit is fresher; Meunier dominates on clay-rich soils over chalk.
fr-champagne-leuvrigny.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-lhery.name: Lhéry
fr-champagne-lhery.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-lhery.summary: Lhéry is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Vallée de l'Ardre), about 4 km north-west of Ville-en-Tardenois. The Ardre valley and the Tardenois plateau grow mostly Meunier, with some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, on sands and clays over deep chalk; most of the grapes go to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-lhery.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-lignol-le-chateau.name: Lignol-le-Château
fr-champagne-lignol-le-chateau.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-lignol-le-chateau.summary: Lignol-le-Château is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 9 km east of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar has no chalk: here Pinot Noir grows on Kimmeridgian marls and limestone, closer to Chablis than to Épernay, and gives round, fruit-rich wines.
fr-champagne-lignol-le-chateau.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-lisse-en-champagne.name: Lisse-en-Champagne
fr-champagne-lisse-en-champagne.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-lisse-en-champagne.summary: Lisse-en-Champagne is a Champagne village of the Vitryat, about 11 km north-east of Vitry-le-François. The Vitryat is an isolated vineyard around Vitry-le-François, east of the Côte des Blancs, planted almost entirely to Chardonnay on chalk.
fr-champagne-lisse-en-champagne.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-loches-sur-ource.name: Loches-sur-Ource
fr-champagne-loches-sur-ource.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-loches-sur-ource.summary: Loches-sur-Ource is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 11 km south-east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. Its slopes belong to the Barséquanais, where Pinot Noir grows on Jurassic marl and limestone, the same rocks as Chablis, giving ripe, fruit-driven wines with a firm limestone edge.
fr-champagne-loches-sur-ource.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-loisy-en-brie.name: Loisy-en-Brie
fr-champagne-loisy-en-brie.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-loisy-en-brie.summary: Loisy-en-Brie is a Champagne village of the Côte des Blancs (Southern Côte des Blancs (Mont Aimé, Val-des-Marais)), about 9 km west of Vertus. This is the southern tail of the Côte des Blancs: Chardonnay on chalky slopes and gentle land, fresher and lighter than in the grand crus.
fr-champagne-loisy-en-brie.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-loisy-sur-marne.name: Loisy-sur-Marne
fr-champagne-loisy-sur-marne.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-loisy-sur-marne.summary: Loisy-sur-Marne is a Champagne village of the Vitryat, about 4 km north-west of Vitry-le-François. The Vitryat is an isolated vineyard around Vitry-le-François, east of the Côte des Blancs, planted almost entirely to Chardonnay on chalk.
fr-champagne-loisy-sur-marne.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-louvois.name: Louvois
fr-champagne-louvois.summary:
A Pinot Noir grand cru at the southern edge of the Montagne de Reims, in a gap of the forest north of Bouzy. Its vineyard is small and partly enclosed by woods, which keeps it cooler than Bouzy, and its Pinot is fresh, firm and red-fruited.

The village is dominated by the château built in the seventeenth century for the Marquis de Louvois, Louis XIV's minister of war. Most of the grapes go to the houses, so village-named bottles are rare.
fr-champagne-louvois.terroir: Chalk slopes at the foot of the Montagne's forest, cooler and later-ripening than Bouzy and Ambonnay.
fr-champagne-louvois.nerd_note: The Marquis de Louvois, François-Michel Le Tellier, was Louis XIV's secretary of state for war.
fr-champagne-louvois.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-ludes.name: Ludes
fr-champagne-ludes.summary: A premier cru (94%) on the northern face of the Montagne de Reims between Chigny-les-Roses and Mailly-Champagne. Canard-Duchêne, founded in 1868, is based here, and Raphaël and Vincent Bérêche of Bérêche et Fils, a leading grower family, farm vines around the village.
fr-champagne-ludes.terroir: North-facing slopes of the Montagne de Reims, with chalk close to the surface on the steeper parts and sandier, clay-rich soils near the forest edge; the cool exposure gives fresh, firm fruit.
fr-champagne-ludes.classification: Premier cru village: rated 94% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-mailly-champagne.name: Mailly-Champagne
fr-champagne-mailly-champagne.summary:
A Pinot Noir grand cru on the northern slopes of the Montagne de Reims between Verzenay and Ludes, facing mostly north and north-east toward Reims. The cool exposure gives fresh, structured, tightly wound Pinot Noir with less ripeness but more tension than the south-facing villages, prized in blends for backbone and length.

The village is famous for its cooperative, Mailly Grand Cru, founded in 1929 by growers during the Depression, which sells only Champagne from Mailly's own grand cru vineyards and ages it in deep cellars dug into the chalk.
fr-champagne-mailly-champagne.terroir: North and north-east-facing slopes of chalk close to the surface on the Montagne's northern flank.
fr-champagne-mailly-champagne.nerd_note: Mailly's cellars were dug by the members themselves, much of it by hand, from the 1930s onward.
fr-champagne-mailly-champagne.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-mancy.name: Mancy
fr-champagne-mancy.summary: Mancy is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Coteaux Sud d'Épernay), about 7 km south of Épernay. On the slopes south of Épernay, where the Marne valley meets the Côte des Blancs, all three main grapes grow: Meunier is the tradition, with Chardonnay on the chalkier slopes.
fr-champagne-mancy.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-mardeuil.name: Mardeuil
fr-champagne-mardeuil.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-mardeuil.summary: Mardeuil is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive gauche), about 3 km north-west of Épernay. The south side of the Marne valley is Meunier territory, on clay and marl over chalk, with cooler exposures than the right bank and fresh, fruity base wines. The Beaumont des Crayères cooperative, known for good-value Champagne, is based here.
fr-champagne-mardeuil.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-mareuil-le-port.name: Mareuil-le-Port
fr-champagne-mareuil-le-port.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-mareuil-le-port.summary: Mareuil-le-Port is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive gauche), about 7 km east of Dormans. The south side of the Marne valley is Meunier territory, on clay and marl over chalk, with cooler exposures than the right bank and fresh, fruity base wines.
fr-champagne-mareuil-le-port.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-mareuil-sur-ay.name: Mareuil-sur-Aÿ
fr-champagne-mareuil-sur-ay.summary: A Pinot Noir premier cru along the Marne east of Aÿ, rated 99% on the old échelle, just short of grand cru, and since 2016 part of the commune of Aÿ-Champagne. It is the home of Billecart-Salmon and of Philipponnat, whose Clos des Goisses, a steep 5.5-ha walled slope facing south over the canal, is one of the most famous single vineyards in Champagne and is made in almost every year, a sign of how warm the site is.
fr-champagne-mareuil-sur-ay.nerd_note: 'Goisses' is said to come from an old local word for a very steep slope, and the Clos is one of the steepest vineyards in Champagne.
fr-champagne-mareuil-sur-ay.classification: Premier cru village: rated 99% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-marfaux.name: Marfaux
fr-champagne-marfaux.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-marfaux.summary: Marfaux is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Vallée de l'Ardre), about 7 km east of Ville-en-Tardenois. In the valley of the Ardre, a tributary of the Vesle west of Reims, Meunier dominates on sandy and clay soils over chalk; the vines are scattered among woods and fields, and the wines are supple and fruity.
fr-champagne-marfaux.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-merfy.name: Merfy
fr-champagne-merfy.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-merfy.summary: Merfy is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Massif de Saint-Thierry and the Vesle), about 6 km north-west of Reims. On the hills north-west of Reims around the Massif de Saint-Thierry, sandy and clay soils over chalk carry Meunier, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; the area was one of the historic vineyards of Reims. Chartogne-Taillet makes single-parcel Champagnes here that show the sandy soils of the Saint-Thierry hills.
fr-champagne-merfy.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-merlaut.name: Merlaut
fr-champagne-merlaut.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-merlaut.summary: Merlaut is a Champagne village of the Vitryat, about 7 km north-east of Vitry-le-François. The Vitryat is an isolated vineyard around Vitry-le-François, east of the Côte des Blancs, planted almost entirely to Chardonnay on chalk.
fr-champagne-merlaut.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-merrey-sur-arce.name: Merrey-sur-Arce
fr-champagne-merrey-sur-arce.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-merrey-sur-arce.summary: Merrey-sur-Arce is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 3 km south-east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar around Bar-sur-Seine grows mostly Pinot Noir on Kimmeridgian marl; once a supplier of grapes to the Marne, it now has many grower-producers of its own.
fr-champagne-merrey-sur-arce.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-meurville.name: Meurville
fr-champagne-meurville.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-meurville.summary: Meurville is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 8 km south-west of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. In the Bar-sur-Aubois, the eastern half of the Côte des Bar, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and limestone, the Jurassic rocks of Chablis rather than the chalk of the Marne; the wines are ripe and fruity.
fr-champagne-meurville.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-mezy-moulins.name: Mézy-Moulins
fr-champagne-mezy-moulins.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-mezy-moulins.summary: Mézy-Moulins is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 8 km east of Château-Thierry, in the Aisne department. fr-champagne-oger.name: Oger

For generations its grapes were a major supply for the big houses.

Jean Milan is the best-known local grower, and the walled Clos Cazals of Claude Cazals lies in the village.
fr-champagne-oger.terroir: East-facing slopes of Belemnite chalk, slightly warmer than Le Mesnil.
fr-champagne-oger.nerd_note: Oger and Le Mesnil share the southern end of the grand cru Côte des Blancs; Oger's slightly warmer, more sheltered slopes help explain its rounder style.
fr-champagne-oger.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

Oiry was one of the five villages promoted to grand cru in 1985 (with Chouilly, Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Oger and Verzy), which shows how the échelle reflected the market for grapes as much as the slope itself.
fr-champagne-oiry.terroir: Flat to gently sloping chalk land at the foot of the Côte des Blancs, next to the Marne plain.

fr-champagne-passy-sur-marne.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-pavant.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay

This is Meunier country: the chalk lies too deep to matter, and the clay-rich slopes along the valley give fleshy, early-maturing wines, many of them sold to the cooperatives of the Aisne.
fr-champagne-pavant.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-pierry.summary: A premier cru (90%) just south of Épernay, on the slopes at the meeting of the Marne valley and the Côte des Blancs, so it grows all three main grapes. Pierry is also the burial place of Brother Jean Oudart, the Benedictine cellarer often paired with Dom Pérignon in Champagne lore.
fr-champagne-pierry.nerd_note: Jean Oudart (died 1742) worked at the abbey's Pierry estate and is credited with improving the bottling and corking of sparkling wine.
fr-champagne-pierry.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-plaines-saint-lange.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier

The Côte des Bar around Bar-sur-Seine grows mostly Pinot Noir on Kimmeridgian marl; once a supplier of grapes to the Marne, it now has many grower-producers of its own.

In the Barséquanais, the valleys of the Seine, Ource, Arce and Laignes around Bar-sur-Seine, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and Portlandian limestone; growers here led the rise of Côte des Bar grower Champagne. Dominique Moreau's Marie-Courtin, a biodynamic grower, makes single-vineyard Champagnes here.
fr-champagne-polisot.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

Its small vineyard lies on the Monts de Berru, an outlier hill east of Reims, on chalk with a sandy capping; most of the grapes are sold to the Reims houses.

Its south-facing slopes in the valleys around Bar-sur-Aube are planted mainly to Pinot Noir on Jurassic marl and limestone; much of the fruit has long gone to the houses of the Marne.
fr-champagne-proverville.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-puisieulx.name: Puisieulx
fr-champagne-puisieulx.summary:
The smallest grand cru, with a few dozen hectares on the gentle north-eastern slopes of the Montagne de Reims close to Sillery and the Vesle. Its vineyards, mostly Pinot Noir with Chardonnay, are almost all sold to the big Reims houses, so a village-named bottle is a rarity.

Puisieulx belonged to the old 'Sillery' growth that made the reputation of Champagne's still wines in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
fr-champagne-puisieulx.terroir: Gentle, chalky slopes at the north-eastern foot of the Montagne de Reims.
fr-champagne-puisieulx.nerd_note: The Fort de la Pompelle, a First World War fort that defended Reims and is now a museum, stands on the commune's land beside the vines.
fr-champagne-puisieulx.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-reims.name: Reims
fr-champagne-reims.summary: Reims is the historic capital of Champagne, where French kings were crowned in the cathedral, and the seat of many great houses: Veuve Clicquot, Ruinart, Taittinger, Pommery, Krug, Louis Roederer, Charles Heidsieck, Mumm, Lanson and Henriot. Their cellars run through Gallo-Roman chalk pits (crayères) under the Saint-Nicaise hill, part of the UNESCO listing of 2015. The commune itself has only a small vineyard.
fr-champagne-reims.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

On the right bank of the Marne the main slopes face south toward the river; Meunier is the leading grape on clay and marl over chalk, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay on the best sites.
fr-champagne-reuil.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-rilly-la-montagne.terroir: North-facing slopes of the Montagne de Reims, with chalk close to the surface on the steeper parts and sandier, clay-rich soils near the forest edge; the cool exposure gives fresh, firm fruit.
fr-champagne-rilly-la-montagne.nerd_note: Rilly sits at the northern end of the Reims to Épernay railway tunnel that runs under the Montagne de Reims.
fr-champagne-rilly-la-montagne.classification: Premier cru village: rated 94% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-sacy.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-sermiers.nerd_note: Sermiers is one of the larger communes of the Petite Montagne, with hamlets spread through the forest edge.

fr-champagne-sillery.name: Sillery
fr-champagne-sillery.summary:
In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries 'Sillery' was the most famous name in Champagne, used for the still and sparkling wines of the Brûlart family, marquis de Sillery, and of the villages around them. Today it is a small grand cru on the gentle slopes and plain by the Vesle and the canal, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

Like its neighbours Puisieulx and Beaumont-sur-Vesle, Sillery sends almost all its grapes to the Reims houses.
fr-champagne-sillery.terroir: Low, gentle chalk slopes by the Vesle at the north-eastern foot of the Montagne de Reims.
fr-champagne-sillery.nerd_note: Grand cru status here, as in Puisieulx and Beaumont-sur-Vesle, reflects the historic reputation and prices of these Vesle villages more than any dramatic slope.
fr-champagne-sillery.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-soulieres.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier

Around the Mont Aimé and the Val-des-Marais, where the Côte des Blancs escarpment fades out to the south, Chardonnay dominates on chalk under clay and silt.
fr-champagne-soulieres.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-taissy.terroir: Gentle, chalky land at the northern foot of the Montagne de Reims, on the edge of the city, where housing and roads have taken much of the old vineyard.
fr-champagne-taissy.classification: Premier cru village: rated 94% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-talus-saint-prix.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier

Its sheltered slopes give ripe, full Pinot Noir close in quality to its grand cru neighbours, and most of it goes to the big houses.
fr-champagne-tauxieres-mutry.terroir: Sheltered, mostly south-facing slopes of chalk under clay and scree, in a fold of the Montagne between the forest and the Marne.
fr-champagne-tauxieres-mutry.classification: Premier cru village: rated 99% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

In the Saint-Thierry hills and along the Vesle west of Reims, Meunier leads on sands and clays over chalk, with Chardonnay and Pinot Noir on the chalkier slopes.
fr-champagne-thil.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-tours-sur-marne.name: Tours-sur-Marne
fr-champagne-tours-sur-marne.summary:
A grand cru on the Marne at the south-eastern foot of the Montagne de Reims, below Bouzy, and the home of Laurent-Perrier, founded in Tours in 1812. Its vineyards are mostly low-lying Pinot Noir.

Before 2010 the échelle rated Tours-sur-Marne's black grapes 100% but its white grapes only 90%, a reminder that the old scale could rate grapes by variety; today the whole commune is grand cru.
fr-champagne-tours-sur-marne.terroir: Low slopes and flats of chalk and alluvium beside the Marne.
fr-champagne-tours-sur-marne.nerd_note: The de Nonancourt family bought Laurent-Perrier in 1939, and Bernard de Nonancourt, who ran it from 1949, launched Grand Siècle and the Cuvée Rosé Brut.
fr-champagne-tours-sur-marne.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru. Before 2010 the échelle rated its black grapes 100% and its white grapes 90%. In the hills on the north side of the Marne, Meunier rules on clay-rich soils over deeper chalk, with some Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; the wines are round and aromatic.
fr-champagne-verneuil.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-verpillieres-sur-ource.name: Verpillières-sur-Ource
fr-champagne-verpillieres-sur-ource.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-verpillieres-sur-ource.summary: Verpillières-sur-Ource is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 18 km south-east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. In the Barséquanais, the valleys of the Seine, Ource, Arce and Laignes around Bar-sur-Seine, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and Portlandian limestone; growers here led the rise of Côte des Bar grower Champagne.
fr-champagne-verpillieres-sur-ource.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-vert-toulon.name: Vert-Toulon
fr-champagne-vert-toulon.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-vert-toulon.summary: Vert-Toulon is a Champagne village of the Côte des Blancs (Southern Côte des Blancs (Mont Aimé, Val-des-Marais)), about 10 km south-west of Vertus. Around the Mont Aimé and the Val-des-Marais, where the Côte des Blancs escarpment fades out to the south, Chardonnay dominates on chalk under clay and silt.
fr-champagne-vert-toulon.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-vertus.name: Vertus
fr-champagne-vertus.summary: The largest premier cru, at the southern end of the Côte des Blancs, with Chardonnay and some Pinot Noir. Vertus Chardonnay is a little rounder than Le Mesnil's, and the village also has a tradition of red Coteaux Champenois. Larmandier-Bernier, a biodynamic pioneer, Veuve Fourny, Doyard, Pascal Doquet and the house of Duval-Leroy are based here.
fr-champagne-vertus.terroir: East-facing slopes of chalk at the southern end of the Côte des Blancs, with more clay in the lower parts.
fr-champagne-vertus.classification: Premier cru village: rated 95% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-verzenay.name: Verzenay
fr-champagne-verzenay.summary:
A north-facing Pinot Noir grand cru on the Montagne de Reims, between Verzy and Mailly-Champagne, known for structured, nervy, long-lived Pinot that gives blends backbone and freshness rather than richness. The village climbs up the slope to its windmill, Mumm's Moulin de Verzenay.

The Phare de Verzenay, a lighthouse built in 1909 among the vines by Joseph Goulden as advertising for his Champagne, is now a museum of the vine. The big houses own and buy extensively here; Jean Lallement and Michel Arnould are local growers.
fr-champagne-verzenay.terroir: North and north-east-facing slopes of chalk close to the surface.
fr-champagne-verzenay.nerd_note: Verzenay Pinot Noir is prized by the big houses for acidity and structure rather than fruit; Mumm, owner of the Moulin de Verzenay, is among the houses with vines here.
fr-champagne-verzenay.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-verzy.name: Verzy
fr-champagne-verzy.summary:
A grand cru on the north-eastern slopes of the Montagne de Reims next to the forest of the Faux de Verzy, whose twisted dwarf beeches are a natural curiosity. Verzy's Pinot Noir is firm and fresh, and it has more Chardonnay than most Montagne villages, giving lean, mineral wines.

It was one of the five villages promoted to grand cru in 1985. Most of its grapes go to the houses, but the village's growers bottle Verzy under its own name.
fr-champagne-verzy.terroir: North-east-facing slopes of chalk under the forested plateau of the Montagne.
fr-champagne-verzy.nerd_note: The Faux de Verzy are a rare population of dwarf, twisted beeches (and some oaks and chestnuts) with a genetic mutation; the forest is protected.
fr-champagne-verzy.classification: Grand cru village: rated 100% on the échelle des crus. One of 17 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Grand Cru.

fr-champagne-ville-dommange.name: Ville-Dommange
fr-champagne-ville-dommange.summary: A premier cru (90%) of the Petite Montagne de Reims, overlooked by the chapel of Saint-Lié on its hilltop, a landmark seen from Reims. Meunier dominates its slopes.
fr-champagne-ville-dommange.terroir: Slopes facing mostly north and east toward Reims, on sand and clay over chalk, below the forest that caps the Petite Montagne; Meunier copes best with these cooler, heavier soils.
fr-champagne-ville-dommange.nerd_note: The chapel of Saint-Lié, on a wooded mound above the vines, was a place of pilgrimage and is a classic viewpoint over Reims and its cathedral.
fr-champagne-ville-dommange.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-ville-en-tardenois.name: Ville-en-Tardenois
fr-champagne-ville-en-tardenois.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-ville-en-tardenois.summary: Ville-en-Tardenois is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Vallée de l'Ardre). In the valley of the Ardre, a tributary of the Vesle west of Reims, Meunier dominates on sandy and clay soils over chalk; the vines are scattered among woods and fields, and the wines are supple and fruity.
fr-champagne-ville-en-tardenois.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-ville-sur-arce.name: Ville-sur-Arce
fr-champagne-ville-sur-arce.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-ville-sur-arce.summary: Ville-sur-Arce is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 5 km east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. In the Barséquanais, the valleys of the Seine, Ource, Arce and Laignes around Bar-sur-Seine, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and Portlandian limestone; growers here led the rise of Côte des Bar grower Champagne.
fr-champagne-ville-sur-arce.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-villenauxe-la-grande.name: Villenauxe-la-Grande
fr-champagne-villenauxe-la-grande.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-villenauxe-la-grande.summary: Villenauxe-la-Grande is a Champagne village of the Côte de Sézanne, about 19 km south-west of Sézanne, in the Aube department. The Côte de Sézanne continues the Côte des Blancs escarpment south of the Saint-Gond marshes; Chardonnay dominates on chalk covered with clay and silt, and the wines are riper and rounder than in the Côte des Blancs.
fr-champagne-villenauxe-la-grande.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-villeneuve-renneville-chevi.name: Villeneuve-Renneville-Chevigny
fr-champagne-villeneuve-renneville-chevi.summary: A premier cru (95%) on the flat to gently sloping land east of Vertus and Voipreux at the foot of the Côte des Blancs, planted almost entirely to Chardonnay on chalk. Its grapes go mostly to houses and cooperatives.
fr-champagne-villeneuve-renneville-chevi.terroir: Flat to gently sloping chalk land east of Vertus at the foot of the Côte des Blancs.
fr-champagne-villeneuve-renneville-chevi.classification: Premier cru village: rated 95% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-villers-allerand.name: Villers-Allerand
fr-champagne-villers-allerand.summary: A premier cru (90%) on the northern slopes of the Montagne de Reims west of Rilly-la-Montagne, at the forest edge. Its fruit is fresh and firm, mostly sold to the Reims houses.
fr-champagne-villers-allerand.terroir: North-facing slopes of the Montagne de Reims, with chalk close to the surface on the steeper parts and sandier, clay-rich soils near the forest edge; the cool exposure gives fresh, firm fruit.
fr-champagne-villers-allerand.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-villers-aux-noeuds.name: Villers-aux-Nœuds
fr-champagne-villers-aux-noeuds.summary: A small premier cru (90%) south-west of Reims at the northern foot of the Montagne, between the city and the Petite Montagne villages.
fr-champagne-villers-aux-noeuds.terroir: Gentle, chalky land at the northern foot of the Montagne de Reims, on the edge of the city, where housing and roads have taken much of the old vineyard.
fr-champagne-villers-aux-noeuds.classification: Premier cru village: rated 90% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-villers-franqueux.name: Villers-Franqueux
fr-champagne-villers-franqueux.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-villers-franqueux.summary: Villers-Franqueux is a Champagne village of the Montagne de Reims (Massif de Saint-Thierry and the Vesle), about 10 km north-west of Reims. On the hills north-west of Reims around the Massif de Saint-Thierry, sandy and clay soils over chalk carry Meunier, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay; the area was one of the historic vineyards of Reims.
fr-champagne-villers-franqueux.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-villers-marmery.name: Villers-Marmery
fr-champagne-villers-marmery.summary: A premier cru (95%) on the eastern edge of the Montagne de Reims, almost entirely Chardonnay, giving fresh, citrusy blanc de blancs. With Trépail it forms a small white-grape enclave on a hill otherwise known for Pinot Noir.
fr-champagne-villers-marmery.terroir: East-facing slopes at the eastern end of the Montagne de Reims, on chalk under a thin cover of clay and scree, cooler than the south-facing grand crus.
fr-champagne-villers-marmery.classification: Premier cru village: rated 95% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-villers-sous-chatillon.name: Villers-sous-Châtillon
fr-champagne-villers-sous-chatillon.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-villers-sous-chatillon.summary: Villers-sous-Châtillon is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite), about 12 km north-west of Épernay. Its vineyards belong to the right bank of the Marne valley, where Meunier dominates on clay, marl and sand over chalk and gives generous, fruity wine; side valleys add cooler exposures.
fr-champagne-villers-sous-chatillon.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-villevenard.name: Villevenard
fr-champagne-villevenard.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-villevenard.summary: Villevenard is a Champagne village of the Côte de Sézanne (Val du Petit Morin), about 13 km north-east of Sézanne. In the valley of the Petit Morin and around the Saint-Gond marshes, between the Côte des Blancs and Sézanne, Chardonnay dominates with some Meunier and Pinot Noir on chalk and clay.
fr-champagne-villevenard.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-villiers-saint-denis.name: Villiers-Saint-Denis
fr-champagne-villiers-saint-denis.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-villiers-saint-denis.summary: Villiers-Saint-Denis is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Château-Thierry and the western Marne valley), about 12 km south-west of Château-Thierry, in the Aisne department. This is Meunier country: the chalk lies too deep to matter, and the clay-rich slopes along the valley give fleshy, early-maturing wines, many of them sold to the cooperatives of the Aisne.
fr-champagne-villiers-saint-denis.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-vinay.name: Vinay
fr-champagne-vinay.summary: Vinay is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Coteaux Sud d'Épernay), about 6 km south-west of Épernay. The Coteaux Sud d'Épernay mix chalk with clay and flint-bearing marl, and the vineyards grow Meunier, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir side by side.
fr-champagne-vinay.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-vincelles.name: Vincelles
fr-champagne-vincelles.grapes: Meunier, with Pinot Noir and Chardonnay
fr-champagne-vincelles.summary: Vincelles is a Champagne village of the Vallée de la Marne (Vallée de la Marne rive droite). Its vineyards belong to the right bank of the Marne valley, where Meunier dominates on clay, marl and sand over chalk and gives generous, fruity wine; side valleys add cooler exposures.
fr-champagne-vincelles.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-vindey.name: Vindey
fr-champagne-vindey.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-vindey.summary: Vindey is a Champagne village of the Côte de Sézanne, about 3 km south-west of Sézanne. On the east and south-east-facing Côte de Sézanne, Chardonnay grows on chalk under a cover of clay and silt; houses use its ripe, soft fruit to round off blends.
fr-champagne-vindey.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-vitry-en-perthois.name: Vitry-en-Perthois
fr-champagne-vitry-en-perthois.grapes: Chardonnay, with some Pinot Noir and Meunier
fr-champagne-vitry-en-perthois.summary: Vitry-en-Perthois is a Champagne village of the Vitryat, about 4 km north-east of Vitry-le-François. Its vines belong to the small Vitryat outpost, mostly Chardonnay on chalk slopes, sold largely to cooperatives and houses.
fr-champagne-vitry-en-perthois.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-vitry-le-croise.name: Vitry-le-Croisé
fr-champagne-vitry-le-croise.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-vitry-le-croise.summary: Vitry-le-Croisé is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 14 km south-west of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar has no chalk: here Pinot Noir grows on Kimmeridgian marls and limestone, closer to Chablis than to Épernay, and gives round, fruit-rich wines.
fr-champagne-vitry-le-croise.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-viviers-sur-artaut.name: Viviers-sur-Artaut
fr-champagne-viviers-sur-artaut.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-viviers-sur-artaut.summary: Viviers-sur-Artaut is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Barséquanais), about 9 km east of Bar-sur-Seine, in the Aube department. In the Barséquanais, the valleys of the Seine, Ource, Arce and Laignes around Bar-sur-Seine, Pinot Noir dominates on Kimmeridgian marl and Portlandian limestone; growers here led the rise of Côte des Bar grower Champagne.
fr-champagne-viviers-sur-artaut.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-voigny.name: Voigny
fr-champagne-voigny.grapes: Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay and some Meunier
fr-champagne-voigny.summary: Voigny is a Champagne village of the Côte des Bar (Bar-sur-Aubois), about 5 km east of Bar-sur-Aube, in the Aube department. The Côte des Bar has no chalk: here Pinot Noir grows on Kimmeridgian marls and limestone, closer to Chablis than to Épernay, and gives round, fruit-rich wines.
fr-champagne-voigny.classification: Autre cru: a Champagne village outside the grand and premier crus. In its final form the échelle des crus, which set grape prices for much of the twentieth century and was dropped in 2010, rated such villages between 80% and 89%.

fr-champagne-voipreux.name: Voipreux
fr-champagne-voipreux.summary: A small premier cru (95%) on the gentle eastern foot of the Côte des Blancs below Vertus, with Chardonnay on chalk. Its fruit is mostly sold to houses and cooperatives.
fr-champagne-voipreux.terroir: Gentle slopes and flat land of chalk at the eastern foot of the Côte des Blancs below Vertus.
fr-champagne-voipreux.nerd_note: Its 95% rating matched that of Vertus, its larger neighbour up the slope.
fr-champagne-voipreux.classification: Premier cru village: rated 95% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-champagne-vrigny.name: Vrigny
fr-champagne-vrigny.summary: A premier cru of the Petite Montagne de Reims, known among enthusiasts through Egly-Ouriet's Les Vignes de Vrigny, a Meunier from old vines that helped change opinion about the grape.
fr-champagne-vrigny.terroir: Slopes facing mostly north and east toward Reims, on sand and clay over chalk, below the forest that caps the Petite Montagne; Meunier copes best with these cooler, heavier soils.
fr-champagne-vrigny.classification: Premier cru village: rated between 90% and 99% on the échelle des crus (dropped in 2010). One of 42 communes whose vineyards may be labelled Champagne Premier Cru.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-abba.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Abbaye de Morgeot
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-abba.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-abba.summary:
Abbaye de Morgeot is the 11.4 ha heart of Morgeot, around the old abbey farm of Maizières. Its best-known wine is the Clos de la Chapelle, a monopole of the Duc de Magenta made by Louis Jadot, in both colours.

It sits in the heart of the Morgeot area, between Morgeot, Les Brussonnes, Les Grands Clos and La Chapelle, on brown limestone-clay with marl. The Duc de Magenta's Clos de la Chapelle, made by Jadot, is the best-known wine, and its reds are among Chassagne's most structured.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-abba.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. Clay and marl are more abundant here than in the north of the commune, which suits the Pinot Noir still planted in parts of the climat.
producers: Domaine du Duc de Magenta (Louis Jadot)
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-abba.nerd_note: The abbey's chapel still stands in the vineyard.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-blan.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Blanchot dessus
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-blan.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-blan.summary:
Blanchot Dessus is a 1.2 ha premier cru directly south of Le Montrachet and next to Criots-Bâtard-Montrachet, the closest premier cru in Chassagne to the great grand cru. The wine is rich and mineral.

It shares the grands crus' band of stony limestone-clay, and its wines are rich and mineral, with something of their density. Darviot-Perrin's version is a rare chance to taste the Montrachet neighbourhood at premier cru prices.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-blan.terroir: South-southwest-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay like the grands crus next door. Its almost flat ground at around 240 m is the same level as the lower part of Le Montrachet, and the soil changes little across the boundary.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-bois.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Bois de Chassagne
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-bois.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-bois.summary: Bois de Chassagne is a 13.6 ha premier cru high on the slope toward Santenay, and an umbrella for Les Baudines and Les Embazées. The wines are fresh and mineral, mainly white.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-bois.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 330 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-bois.nerd_note: The woods (*bois*) that gave it its name still cap the hill.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cail.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Cailleret
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cail.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cail.summary:
Les Caillerets (Cailleret in the register, with En Cailleret alongside) is one of Chassagne's finest white premier crus, on the slope just south of the village. At 5.6 ha it gives a fine, mineral, floral Chassagne with more tension than Morgeot: citrus, white flowers and a long, stony finish. The umbrella also covers Les Combards and Vigne Derrière.

Vigne Derrière and En Cailleret lie alongside and Les Champs Gain below. Its wines have more tension than Morgeot, and they are often ranked with La Romanée and Les Grandes Ruchottes as Chassagne's finest whites.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cail.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 295 m, moderately steep. Stony limestone soils with scree over hard limestone.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cail.nerd_note: Puligny's Le Cailleret, next to Montrachet, shares the name, but the two sites are 2 km apart.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cham.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Champs Jendreau
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cham.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cham.summary: Champs Jendreau is a 2.1 ha part of La Boudriotte and Morgeot, on the lower slope. The wine is usually blended.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cham.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Morgeot and La Boudriotte and beside Les Chaumes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-cham.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as La Boudriotte, or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Chassagne
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.summary: Chassagne is a 4.1 ha premier cru just south of the village, between La Maltroie and Cailleret. Its name is the village's own.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 280 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Cailleret and Vigne Derrière and above La Maltroie and Les Macherelles.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.nerd_note: The village name is usually derived from Latin *cassanea*, a place of oaks.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.summary: Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean is a 2.0 ha part of the Clos Saint-Jean umbrella, above the village.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Clos Saint-Jean, Chassagne and Les Murées and beside Cailleret.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-chas.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Clos Saint-Jean.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Clos Chareau
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.summary: The Clos Chareau is a 2.0 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area, at the southern edge of Chassagne.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Grande Borne and beside Morgeot, Les Brussonnes and La Cardeuse.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as Les Brussonnes, or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Clos Pitois
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.summary: The Clos Pitois is a 3.0 ha premier cru at the southern edge of Chassagne, against Santenay. Domaine Roger Belland makes it as a monopole, in red and white.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Santenay's La Comme and Bois de Chassagne, above Les Brussonnes and beside Francemont.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.nerd_note: It may also be sold as Les Brussonnes or Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Clos Saint-Jean
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.summary:
The Clos Saint-Jean is a 13.4 ha premier cru above the village, and an umbrella for Les Rebichets, Les Murées and Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean. It has long been known for both colours: Ramonet's red Clos Saint-Jean is a classic, and its whites are fine and mineral.

Les Rebichets and Les Vergers lie to the north and Cailleret to the south. Its wines can be red or white, and Ramonet's red Clos Saint-Jean, firm and red-fruited, is a classic.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-clos.nerd_note: Wines from Les Rebichets, Les Murées and Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean may all be sold under the Clos Saint-Jean name.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-dent.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Dent de Chien
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-dent.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-dent.summary: Dent de Chien ('dog's tooth') is a tiny 0.57 ha premier cru above Le Montrachet, on the Chassagne side. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-dent.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 240 to 260 m, steep, thin stony soil over hard limestone.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-dent.nerd_note: Saint-Aubin's Les Murgers des Dents de Chien lies just above, on the other side of the hill.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-c.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru En Cailleret
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-c.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-c.summary: En Cailleret is a 5.1 ha premier cru alongside Cailleret, on the slope just south of the village. The wine is a fine, mineral Chassagne.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-c.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 295 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils with scree. On the map it lies above Vigne Derrière, Morgeot and La Boudriotte and beside Cailleret.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-r.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru En Remilly
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-r.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-r.summary: En Remilly is a small 1.6 ha Chassagne premier cru on the slope above Chevalier-Montrachet, continuing Saint-Aubin's En Remilly. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-r.terroir: South-facing at 280 to 305 m, steep, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above the grand cru Chevalier-Montrachet.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-r.nerd_note: Most of En Remilly lies in Saint-Aubin.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-v.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru En Virondot
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-v.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-v.summary: En Virondot is a steep 2.3 ha premier cru within La Grande Montagne, high above Morgeot. Marc Morey's Virondot is the best-known. The wine is taut and mineral.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-v.terroir: Very steep, east-southeast-facing at 290 to 330 m, slope around 26%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above La Grande Montagne and En Cailleret.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-en-v.nerd_note: It is one of the steepest premier crus in Chassagne.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Ez Crets
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.summary: Ez Crets is a 2.3 ha part of La Maltroie, just south of the village.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Chassagne and beside La Maltroie and Les Places.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as La Maltroie.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Ez Crottes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.summary: Ez Crottes is a 2.4 ha part of Morgeot, on the lower slope.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Boudriotte and Abbaye de Morgeot and beside Les Chaumes and Guerchère.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-ez-c.nerd_note: *Ez* is the old Burgundian form of 'aux'.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-fran.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Francemont
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-fran.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-fran.summary: Francemont is a 2.4 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-fran.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Bois de Chassagne, above Les Brussonnes and Les Grands Clos and beside Clos Pitois.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-fran.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as Les Brussonnes, or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-guer.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Guerchère
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-guer.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-guer.summary: Guerchère is a 2.2 ha part of Morgeot, on the lowest part of the slope.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-guer.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 220 to 230 m, almost flat, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Boudriotte and beside Ez Crottes, Les Chaumes and La Chapelle.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-guer.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-b.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Boudriotte
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-b.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-b.summary:
La Boudriotte is a 15.6 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area, and itself an umbrella for several smaller climats (Les Chaumes, Les Fairendes, Champs Jendreau, La Roquemaure, Les Petites Fairendes). It is famous for red: Ramonet's Boudriotte rouge is one of the best reds of the Côte de Beaune south of Volnay.

It sits on the gentle slope in the Morgeot area, with Les Fairendes above and Les Chaumes and Champs Jendreau below, on brown limestone-clay. Ramonet's red Boudriotte, deep, firm and long-lived, is a reminder that Chassagne was a red-wine village until the late 20th century.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-b.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with more clay than Chassagne's white-wine climats.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-b.nerd_note: It may be sold as La Boudriotte or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Cardeuse
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.summary: La Cardeuse is a 0.97 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area. Bernard Moreau makes a red La Cardeuse as a monopole.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Les Boirettes and beside Les Brussonnes, La Grande Borne and Clos Chareau.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.nerd_note: Moreau's La Cardeuse is one of the few single-climat red Chassagnes.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Chapelle
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.summary: La Chapelle is a 4.6 ha premier cru within the Abbaye de Morgeot, around the abbey's chapel. The Duc de Magenta's Clos de la Chapelle lies here.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Abbaye de Morgeot, Morgeot, Les Boirettes and Les Brussonnes.
producers: Domaine du Duc de Magenta (Louis Jadot)
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-c.nerd_note: It may be sold as Abbaye de Morgeot or Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Grande Borne
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.summary: La Grande Borne ('the big boundary stone') is a 1.7 ha premier cru at the southern edge of Chassagne, against Santenay's Clos de Tavannes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 245 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Clos Chareau and beside La Cardeuse, Santenay's Clos de Tavannes and Santenay's Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.nerd_note: The boundary stone probably marked the commune line with Santenay.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Grande Montagne
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.summary: La Grande Montagne is a steep 8.3 ha premier cru above Morgeot, below the quarries that give Chassagne its pale, pinkish building stone. It is an umbrella for La Romanée, Les Grandes Ruchottes, En Virondot and Tonton Marcel. The wines are taut and mineral.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 255 to 330 m, slope around 24%. Thin stony soil over hard limestone.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-g.nerd_note: The Chassagne quarries above the vines have supplied building stone for centuries.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-m.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Maltroie
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-m.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-m.summary: La Maltroie is a 11.7 ha premier cru just south of the village, and an umbrella for Ez Crets and Les Places. The Château de la Maltroye takes its name from it. The wine is a fine, round Chassagne, in both colours.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-m.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-m.nerd_note: The château is spelled with a 'y'; the climat with an 'i'.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Romanée
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.summary:
Chassagne's La Romanée is a steep 3.4 ha premier cru within La Grande Montagne, above Morgeot. Its whites are among the most mineral and refined of the village, with citrus, white flowers and a stony finish. Paul Pillot and Morey-Coffinet make reference versions.

It sits on the steep slope of La Grande Montagne above Morgeot, with Bois de Chassagne alongside and the old quarries above. The thin soil over hard limestone gives the most mineral, tense Chassagne, and many growers rank it with Les Caillerets and Les Grandes Ruchottes as the village's finest whites.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 255 to 320 m, slope around 24%. Thin, stony soil over hard limestone.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.nerd_note: There are three Romanées in Burgundy's classification: the Vosne grand cru, a Gevrey premier cru and this one.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru La Roquemaure
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.summary: La Roquemaure is a tiny 0.61 ha part of La Boudriotte and Morgeot.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Fairendes and beside La Boudriotte, Vigne Blanche and Les Petites Fairendes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-la-r.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as La Boudriotte, or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Baudines
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Baudines is a 3.6 ha premier cru within Bois de Chassagne, high above Morgeot. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 285 to 335 m, steep, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above Bois de Chassagne, Les Embazées and Santenay's La Comme.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Bois de Chassagne.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Boirettes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Boirettes is a 2.8 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Morgeot and Les Brussonnes, above La Chapelle and beside Abbaye de Morgeot.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as Les Brussonnes, or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Bondues
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Bondues is a 1.7 ha part of Les Chenevottes, near Blanchot Dessus and the grands crus.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-northeast-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Macherelles and beside Les Chenevottes and Blanchot dessus.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Chenevottes.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Brussonnes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Brussonnes is a 15.8 ha premier cru in the Morgeot area and an umbrella for Clos Chareau, Clos Pitois, Francemont, La Cardeuse, La Grande Borne and Les Boirettes. The wines are generous, red or white.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold as Les Brussonnes or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Champs gain
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Champs Gain is a 4.6 ha premier cru just south of the village, below Cailleret. The wine is a fine, fresh Chassagne.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Cailleret and beside La Maltroie, Morgeot and La Boudriotte.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: Puligny has a premier cru called Champ Gain.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Chaumées
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Chaumées is a 7.3 ha premier cru above Les Vergers, toward Saint-Aubin. The wine is a fresh, mineral Chassagne.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-facing at 265 to 315 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Saint-Aubin's Le Charmois and above Saint-Aubin's Les Combes, Les Vergers and Clos Saint-Jean.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It sits at the boundary with Saint-Aubin's Les Combes.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Chaumes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Chaumes is a 2.7 ha part of La Boudriotte and Morgeot, on the lower slope. The wine is usually sold as La Boudriotte or Morgeot.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Morgeot and La Boudriotte and beside Champs Jendreau and Ez Crottes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: *Chaumes* means stubble or fallow land.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Chenevottes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary:
Les Chenevottes is a 11.0 ha premier cru on the lower slope north of the village, toward Puligny and the grands crus. It is an umbrella for Les Bondues and Les Commes. Its whites are fine and floral, among the best of the northern Chassagne premier crus.

Blanchot Dessus and Les Bondues lie nearby, and its gentle, moderately deep ground gives a rounder white than the steep southern climats. Niellon's and Jean-Noël Gagnard's versions are references.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay over limestone. Its gentle slope, about 4%, and moderately deep soil give a rounder white than the steep upper climats of the south.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: *Chenevottes* refers to hemp (*chanvre*), once grown here.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Combards
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Combards is a small 0.65 ha part of the Cailleret umbrella, above the village.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 285 to 300 m, steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Cailleret, Chassagne, Vigne Derrière and Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Cailleret.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Commes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Commes is a 1.0 ha part of Les Chenevottes, toward Saint-Aubin.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: South-southwest-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Saint-Aubin's Les Combes, Saint-Aubin's Les Combes au Sud and Les Vergers and beside Les Chenevottes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Chenevottes.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Embazées
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Embazées is a 5.2 ha premier cru within Bois de Chassagne. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 300 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Bois de Chassagne and Les Baudines and above Morgeot and Les Brussonnes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Bois de Chassagne.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Fairendes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Fairendes is a 7.1 ha part of La Boudriotte and Morgeot. The wine is a supple Chassagne, red or white.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Grandes Ruchottes and beside Morgeot, La Boudriotte and Les Petits Clos.
