fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as La Boudriotte, or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Grandes Ruchottes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary:
Les Grandes Ruchottes is a 2.1 ha premier cru within La Grande Montagne, above Morgeot. Ramonet and Paul Pillot make reference versions. The wine is taut, mineral and long-lived.

It sits on the slope of La Grande Montagne below La Grande Montagne itself and above Morgeot and Les Petits Clos, on thin stony soil. Its whites are taut and mineral, with real ageing potential, and Ramonet's Ruchottes is one of the most sought-after premier cru Chassagnes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 285 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils. The gradient is steep, around 18%, and the soil thin enough that roots reach the fissured limestone quickly, which accounts for the wine's tension.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It sits on the steep band of thin soil below the old Chassagne quarries, the same band as La Romanée.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Grands Clos
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Grands Clos is a 3.9 ha part of Morgeot. The wine is a fine Chassagne, red or white.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Tête du Clos, above Abbaye de Morgeot and beside Les Petits Clos and Les Brussonnes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Macherelles
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Macherelles is a 5.2 ha premier cru below the village, near Les Chenevottes. The wine is a supple Chassagne.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 245 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Chassagne and Les Vergers and beside Les Chenevottes and La Maltroie.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It lies at the foot of the slope near the old Route nationale.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Murées
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Murées ('walled') is a 1.6 ha part of the Clos Saint-Jean umbrella, above the village.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 270 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Clos Saint-Jean and Chassagne du Clos Saint-Jean, above La Maltroie and beside Les Rebichets.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Clos Saint-Jean.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Pasquelles
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Pasquelles is a 2.5 ha part of Les Vergers, north of the village.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 255 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Vergers and Saint-Aubin's Les Combes, above Les Chenevottes and beside Saint-Aubin's Pitangeret.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Vergers.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Petites Fairendes
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Petites Fairendes is a small 0.82 ha part of La Boudriotte and Morgeot.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside La Boudriotte, Les Petits Clos, Les Fairendes and La Roquemaure.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as La Boudriotte, or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Petits Clos
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Petits Clos is a 5.1 ha part of Morgeot, on the slope above the abbey. The wine is a fine, mineral Chassagne.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 270 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Grande Montagne and beside Morgeot, La Boudriotte and Les Fairendes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Places
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Places is a 2.4 ha part of La Maltroie, just south of the village.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Chassagne and beside La Maltroie and Ez Crets.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as La Maltroie.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Rebichets
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary: Les Rebichets is a 4.7 ha part of the Clos Saint-Jean umbrella, above the village.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 270 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Clos Saint-Jean, above Chassagne and beside Les Vergers and Les Murées.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Clos Saint-Jean.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Les Vergers
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.summary:
Les Vergers ('the orchards') is a 9.5 ha premier cru north of the village, toward Saint-Aubin, and an umbrella for Les Pasquelles and Petingeret. Its whites are fine and mineral, among the best of the northern Chassagne premier crus.

Les Chenevottes lies below and Les Chaumées above. Niellon's and Ramonet's versions show the elegant, mineral side of Chassagne.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 270 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-les-.nerd_note: It continues into Saint-Aubin's Pitangeret across the commune line.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-morg.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Morgeot
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-morg.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-morg.summary:
Morgeot is the great southern premier cru of Chassagne-Montrachet and, as an umbrella name, the largest premier cru area of the commune: the INAO delimitation covers 56.4 ha, and wines from about twenty lieux-dits (Les Petits Clos, Les Grands Clos, Tête du Clos, La Boudriotte, Les Brussonnes, Vigne Blanche, Guerchère and others) may be sold as Morgeot. The name comes from the Abbaye de Morgeot, a farm of the Cistercian abbey of Maizières whose chapel still stands among the vines.

Morgeot white is the broadest and most generous of Chassagne: ripe citrus, hazelnut and a round, mouth-filling texture with a firm mineral spine. It is also one of the few Côte de Beaune premier crus with a serious red tradition: until the 1970s Chassagne was mostly a red-wine village, and Morgeot rouge is sturdy and dark-fruited.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-morg.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 225 to 265 m, gentle slope at the southern end of the commune toward Santenay. Brown limestone-clay, with more clay and marl than the northern premier crus, over Bathonian limestone.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-morg.nerd_note: Because so many lieux-dits can use the name, a Chassagne 'Morgeot' can come from very different sites: check the small print for the lieu-dit.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-peti.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Petingeret
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-peti.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-peti.summary: Petingeret is a 1.8 ha part of Les Vergers, at the Saint-Aubin boundary.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-peti.terroir: East-facing at 255 to 270 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Saint-Aubin's Pitangeret and Les Pasquelles and beside Les Vergers and Saint-Aubin's Les Combes.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-peti.nerd_note: Saint-Aubin's Pitangeret is the same climat across the commune line.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tete.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Tête du Clos
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tete.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tete.summary: Tête du Clos is a 2.1 ha part of Morgeot, at the top of Les Grands Clos.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tete.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 275 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Bois de Chassagne, above Les Grands Clos and Les Brussonnes and beside Francemont.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tete.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tont.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Tonton Marcel
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tont.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tont.summary: Tonton Marcel ('Uncle Marcel') is a tiny 0.50 ha premier cru within La Grande Montagne, on the steep upper slope. It is one of the most improbable names in the Burgundy classification.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tont.terroir: Very steep, east-southeast-facing at 305 to 340 m, slope around 30%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above La Grande Montagne.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-tont.nerd_note: The name presumably honours a former owner.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vide.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Vide Bourse
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vide.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vide.summary: Vide Bourse ('empty purse') is a 1.3 ha premier cru just south of Bâtard-Montrachet and Criots-Bâtard-Montrachet. Fernand et Laurent Pillot make a well-known version. The wine is rich and mineral.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vide.terroir: Almost flat, south exposure at about 240 m, brown limestone-clay.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vide.nerd_note: The name may refer to the cost of farming it, or to the price paid for it.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Vigne Blanche
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.summary: Vigne Blanche is a 2.2 ha part of Morgeot. The name suggests it was always a white-wine site.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, pale limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Petits Clos and beside Morgeot, La Boudriotte and Abbaye de Morgeot.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Morgeot.

fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.name: Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru Vigne Derrière
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.summary: Vigne Derrière is a 3.8 ha part of the Cailleret umbrella, just south of the village.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Cailleret and En Cailleret and above Chassagne and Les Champs gain.
fr-chassagne-montrachet-premier-cru-vign.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Cailleret.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-beau-renard-nord.name: Beau Renard Nord
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-beau-renard-nord.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-beau-renard-nord.summary: Part of the Beau Renard sector east of the village, on gentle slopes of galets and clay. Domaine de Beaurenard, the Coulon family estate, takes its name from it.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-beau-renard-nord.terroir: The lieu-dit's 47.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-beau-renard-nord.nerd_note: Beau Renard is split into a north and a south part in the land register.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-beau-renard-nord.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-bois-lauzon.name: Bois-Lauzon
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-bois-lauzon.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-bois-lauzon.summary: A flat lieu-dit in the commune of Orange at the northern edge of the appellation, on galets and sand, which gave its name to Mas de Boislauzon.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-bois-lauzon.terroir: The lieu-dit's 61.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 55 to 65 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-bois-lauzon.nerd_note: In 1923 Baron Pierre Le Roy of Château Fortia drew up local rules for Châteauneuf-du-Pape that became a model for the French AOC system; the AOC followed in 1936.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-bois-lauzon.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-cabrieres.name: Cabrières
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-cabrieres.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-cabrieres.summary: The largest lieu-dit of the appellation, more than 200 ha of AOC land on the plateau in the north, around the Mont de Cabrières and across into Orange. Deep galets over red clay and the full force of the mistral give ripe, structured Grenache. Château Cabrières takes its name from it.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-cabrieres.terroir: The lieu-dit's 217.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 50 to 125 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing broadly north (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-cabrieres.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-chapouin.name: Chapouin
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-chapouin.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-chapouin.summary: A flat lieu-dit in Courthézon on sandy soils. Domaine de la Janasse's Cuvée Chaupin, a pure old-vine Grenache, takes its name and fruit from here and shows the perfumed, supple side of sand-grown Grenache.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-chapouin.terroir: The lieu-dit's 42.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 55 to 60 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-chapouin.nerd_note: Sandy soils of the Courthézon side ripen Grenache more slowly than the pebble plateaus, which is why several estates keep their sand-grown old vines separate.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-chapouin.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-coudoulet.name: Coudoulet
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-coudoulet.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-coudoulet.summary: A large, flat lieu-dit in Courthézon at the north-eastern edge of the appellation, close to the Perrin family's Château de Beaucastel. The family's Côtes du Rhône Coudoulet de Beaucastel takes its name from the vineyards just outside the Châteauneuf boundary on the other side of the motorway.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-coudoulet.terroir: The lieu-dit's 84.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 55 to 60 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-coudoulet.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-font-de-michelle.name: Font de Michelle
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-font-de-michelle.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-font-de-michelle.summary: A lieu-dit in Bédarrides on the eastern edge of the appellation, on slopes facing east toward the Ouvèze. Domaine Font de Michelle, the Gonnet family estate, takes its name from it.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-font-de-michelle.terroir: The lieu-dit's 30.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 60 to 100 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-font-de-michelle.nerd_note: Vieux Télégraphe and Font de Michelle are both based in Bédarrides, one of the five communes of the appellation.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-font-de-michelle.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau.name: La Crau
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau.summary:
La Crau is the high, exposed plateau in the east of Châteauneuf-du-Pape, the classic image of the appellation: a thick layer of *galets roulés*, rounded quartzite pebbles left by the ancient Rhône, over red clay. The stones store the day's heat and protect the soil from drying, the clay holds water for dry summers, and the mistral blows through unhindered. Grenache here gives powerful, spicy, long-lived wine with garrigue and kirsch.

The plateau runs across the commune boundary into Bédarrides and Courthézon (mapped as separate La Crau units). Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe, named after the optical telegraph tower built on the plateau in the 1790s, Domaine du Pegau and Henri Bonneau's Réserve des Célestins draw on La Crau.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau.terroir: The lieu-dit's 37.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 95 to 125 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, facing broadly south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau.nerd_note: The Brunier family of Vieux Télégraphe have farmed the plateau since 1898; their estate takes its name from the Chappe telegraph station that stood on La Crau.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-est-bedar.name: La Crau Est (Bédarrides)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-est-bedar.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-est-bedar.summary: The eastern edge of the La Crau plateau in Bédarrides, where the galet-covered terrace begins to slope toward the Ouvèze. The same deep pebbles over red clay as the rest of La Crau.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-est-bedar.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 85 to 110 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-est-bedar.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-ouest-bed.name: La Crau Ouest (Bédarrides)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-ouest-bed.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-ouest-bed.summary: The part of the La Crau plateau that lies in the commune of Bédarrides, on the same deep layer of galets over red clay. Much of Domaine du Vieux Télégraphe's vineyard is in this sector, around the site of the old telegraph tower.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-ouest-bed.terroir: The lieu-dit's 26.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 100 to 110 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-ouest-bed.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-sud-court.name: La Crau Sud (Courthézon)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-sud-court.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-sud-court.summary: The part of the La Crau plateau that lies in Courthézon, north of the Bédarrides sector, on galets over clay and sand.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-sud-court.terroir: The lieu-dit's 41.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 65 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, facing north to north-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-crau-sud-court.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-font-du-loup-c.name: La Font du Loup (Courthézon)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-font-du-loup-c.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-font-du-loup-c.summary: A lieu-dit in Courthézon on sandy and clay slopes facing north-east, home of Château de la Font du Loup, whose wines are known for their elegance rather than power.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-font-du-loup-c.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 65 to 105 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
producers: Château de la Font du Loup
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-font-du-loup-c.nerd_note: Font du Loup ('wolf's spring') is split between Courthézon and Bédarrides in the land register.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-font-du-loup-c.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-gardine.name: La Gardine
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-gardine.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-gardine.summary: A lieu-dit west of the village on gentle slopes of galets and clay, home of Château La Gardine, the Brunel family estate, whose Cuvée des Générations comes from old vines here.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-gardine.terroir: The lieu-dit's 25.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 75 to 105 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, facing south-west to west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-gardine.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-jannasse.name: La Jannasse
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-jannasse.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-jannasse.summary: A lieu-dit in Courthézon, in the north-east of the appellation, which gave its name to Domaine de la Janasse, the Sabon family estate founded in 1973 and now one of the references of the appellation.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-jannasse.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 45 to 55 m, with a mean slope of about 4%, facing south-west to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-jannasse.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-nerthe.name: La Nerthe
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-nerthe.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-nerthe.summary: The lieu-dit of Château La Nerthe, one of the oldest estates of Châteauneuf-du-Pape, south-east of the village, whose history is documented from the sixteenth century. In the eighteenth century the Tulle de Villefranche family sold La Nerthe's wine under its own name, and Commandant Joseph Ducos rebuilt the vineyard after phylloxera, studying the role of each variety.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-nerthe.terroir: The lieu-dit's 19.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 90 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-nerthe.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-petite-crau.name: La Petite Crau
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-petite-crau.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-petite-crau.summary: A small lieu-dit in Bédarrides at the edge of the La Crau plateau, sharing its pebble-covered terrace soils.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-petite-crau.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 65 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-petite-crau.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-roquette.name: La Roquette
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-roquette.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-roquette.summary: A small lieu-dit on the plateau east of the village, on galets over clay. Domaine La Roquette, owned by the Brunier family of Vieux Télégraphe since 1986, takes its name from it.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-roquette.terroir: The lieu-dit's 7.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 110 to 125 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-roquette.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-solitude.name: La Solitude
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-solitude.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-solitude.summary: A lieu-dit south of the village, home of Domaine de la Solitude, owned by the Lançon family, descendants of the Barberini family that came to the papal Comtat in the seventeenth century.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-solitude.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 85 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-la-solitude.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-bois-de-boursa.name: Le Bois de Boursan
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-bois-de-boursa.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-bois-de-boursa.summary: A low-lying lieu-dit in the south of the appellation, near the Sorgues side, which gave its name to Domaine Bois de Boursan, known for its traditional Châteauneuf.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-bois-de-boursa.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 30 to 40 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-bois-de-boursa.nerd_note: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's decree names 13 varieties (18 counting colour variants), but Grenache dominates the vineyard.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-bois-de-boursa.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-cristia-courth.name: Le Cristia (Courthézon)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-cristia-courth.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-cristia-courth.summary: A lieu-dit in Courthézon on the sandy, gently sloping eastern side of the appellation, which gave its name to Domaine de Cristia, the Grangeon family estate.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-cristia-courth.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 60 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 13%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-cristia-courth.nerd_note: The appellation covers five communes: Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Courthézon, Bédarrides, Orange and Sorgues.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-cristia-courth.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-gres.name: Le Grès
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-gres.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-gres.summary: A small lieu-dit in Courthézon whose name refers to sandstone (*grès*) and sand rather than the famous pebbles. On sandy soils Grenache ripens more slowly and keeps more perfume and finesse, which is why sand-grown Châteauneuf, as at nearby Rayas, is prized by growers looking for elegance.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-gres.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 60 to 100 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing east to north-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-gres.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-rayas.name: Le Rayas
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-rayas.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-rayas.summary:
The lieu-dit of Château Rayas, the most singular estate in Châteauneuf-du-Pape. Unlike the stony plateaus, Rayas lies on sandy soils (weathered sandstone) in clearings among pine and oak woods, on slopes that face north. Cool, sheltered and low-yielding, it gives Grenache of extraordinary perfume and transparency, closer to great Burgundy than to the dark, heady style of the appellation.

The Reynaud family has owned Rayas since the late nineteenth century; Jacques Reynaud made it a cult wine, and since 1997 his nephew Emmanuel Reynaud has run it, also making Château des Tours and Château de Fonsalette.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-rayas.terroir: The lieu-dit's 15.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 65 to 110 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing broadly north (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-rayas.nerd_note: Château Rayas red is essentially pure Grenache from old vines, rare in an appellation of blends.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-rayas.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-village.name: Le Village
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-village.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-village.summary: The vineyards around the village of Châteauneuf-du-Pape and below the ruined papal castle, built for Pope John XXII in the fourteenth century as a summer residence, on the slopes of limestone and sand that surround the hilltop.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-village.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 20%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-le-village.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-brusquieres.name: Les Brusquières
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-brusquieres.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-brusquieres.summary: A flat lieu-dit on the high plateau of the appellation, at about 110 to 125 m, on galets over clay and sand. Domaine de la Charbonnière's Les Hautes Brusquières, a dense, spicy Châteauneuf, comes from this sector.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-brusquieres.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 110 to 125 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-brusquieres.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-terres-blanch.name: Les Terres Blanches
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-terres-blanch.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-terres-blanch.summary: A lieu-dit whose name, 'white earths', refers to pale limestone and marl soils rather than pebbles. On limestone, Grenache and Mourvèdre keep fresher acidity and give tighter, more mineral wines, and white Châteauneuf does well.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-terres-blanch.terroir: The lieu-dit's 56.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 125 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-les-terres-blanch.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-montredon.name: Montredon
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-montredon.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-montredon.summary: A broad lieu-dit in the north-west of the appellation, on a plateau of galets roulés over clay that falls gently toward the west. It is the home of Château Mont-Redon, one of the largest single estates of Châteauneuf-du-Pape, whose Grenache-based reds are a reliable classic.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-montredon.terroir: The lieu-dit's 78.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 75 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing west to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-montredon.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pierre-a-feu.name: Pierre à Feu
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pierre-a-feu.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pierre-a-feu.summary: A lieu-dit whose name ('fire stone') refers to flint and quartzite stones that spark when struck, a nod to the galets that cover much of Châteauneuf-du-Pape.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pierre-a-feu.terroir: The lieu-dit's 34.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 30 to 40 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, facing broadly west-south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pierre-a-feu.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pignan.name: Pignan
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pignan.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pignan.summary: A lieu-dit next to Rayas, on sandy soils among woods, straddling Châteauneuf-du-Pape and Courthézon. Château Rayas bottles a second Châteauneuf called Pignan from younger vines and lots, a lighter, perfumed Grenache in the Rayas style.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pignan.terroir: The lieu-dit's 54.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 70 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-pignan.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-relagnes.name: Relagnes
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-relagnes.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-relagnes.summary: A lieu-dit west of the village on slopes facing west toward the Rhône. Domaine des Relagnes, the Boiron family estate, takes its name from it.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-relagnes.terroir: The lieu-dit's 13.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 55 to 85 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing west to north-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-relagnes.nerd_note: The western slopes toward the Rhône have more sand and clay and fewer pebbles than the eastern plateaus.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-relagnes.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-vaudieu.name: Vaudieu
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-vaudieu.grapes: Grenache with Syrah, Mourvèdre and the other permitted varieties (13 named in the decree)
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-vaudieu.summary: A lieu-dit south-east of the village, home of Château de Vaudieu, an eighteenth-century château built by an admiral of Louis XVI's navy, surrounded by vines on galets and sandy soils.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-vaudieu.terroir: The lieu-dit's 49.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 85 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-vaudieu.nerd_note: The papal summer castle that gave the village its name was built for John XXII in the fourteenth century; its ruined keep still dominates the vineyard.
fr-chateauneuf-du-pape-vaudieu.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Châteauneuf-du-Pape when all the grapes come from it.

fr-condrieu-chery.name: Chéry
fr-condrieu-chery.summary: One of the great Condrieu slopes, just south of the town, facing south on granite with a topsoil of weathered mica and sand (*arzelle*). Chéry gives rich but precise Viognier, with apricot and violet and a stony finish. André Perret's Coteau de Chéry is a reference, and several other growers bottle it.
fr-condrieu-chery.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 185 to 260 m, with a mean slope of about 40%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-condrieu-chery.nerd_note: Condrieu shrank to about 8 ha in the mid-1960s; growers such as Georges Vernay replanted the terraces, and today it has around 200 ha.
fr-condrieu-chery.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Condrieu AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Condrieu when all the grapes come from it.

fr-condrieu-verlieu.name: Verlieu
fr-condrieu-verlieu.summary: A large lieu-dit in Chavanay, the southern part of the Condrieu appellation, on steep granite slopes facing south-east. Chavanay is also part of Saint-Joseph, so its growers make both Viognier and Syrah.
fr-condrieu-verlieu.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 165 to 265 m, with a mean slope of about 39%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-condrieu-verlieu.nerd_note: Château-Grillet, a tiny Viognier appellation of its own, is enclosed within Condrieu at Vérin.
fr-condrieu-verlieu.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Condrieu AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Condrieu when all the grapes come from it.

fr-condrieu-vernon.name: Vernon
fr-condrieu-vernon.summary: The steep granite slope above the town of Condrieu that includes the Coteau de Vernon, source of Georges Vernay's most famous Viognier, from vines planted in the 1930s and 1940s. The wine is mineral, tight and long-lived, a rebuttal to the idea that Condrieu must be drunk young.
fr-condrieu-vernon.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 43%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-condrieu-vernon.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Condrieu AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Condrieu when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cornas-chaban.name: Chaban
fr-cornas-chaban.summary: One of the highest lieux-dits of Cornas, at about 360 to 460 m on the plateau edge west of the village, on granite, cooler and later-ripening than the slopes above the village.
fr-cornas-chaban.terroir: The lieu-dit's 56.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 360 to 460 m, with a mean slope of about 22%, facing east to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cornas-chaban.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cornas-chaillot.name: Chaillot
fr-cornas-chaillot.summary: A lieu-dit at the northern edge of Cornas, on granite with a sandy topsoil (*gore*), facing south-east and east. It is the source of Thierry Allemand's Chaillot, the more aromatic of his two Cornas, and of Franck Balthazar's Chaillot.
fr-cornas-chaillot.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 29%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cornas-chaillot.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cornas-champelrose.name: Champelrose
fr-cornas-champelrose.summary: A small, east-facing lieu-dit on the lower slopes near the village, where limestone appears among the granite. Domaine Courbis bottles a Cornas Champelrose, a rounder counterpart to its La Sabarotte.
fr-cornas-champelrose.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 165 m, with a mean slope of about 12%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cornas-champelrose.nerd_note: Cornas has been pure Syrah since its AOC of 1938; no white grapes or Viognier are allowed.
fr-cornas-champelrose.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cornas-les-eygas.name: Les Eygas
fr-cornas-les-eygas.summary: A large lieu-dit (often spelled Les Eygats) on the high slopes north-west of the village, at about 230 to 390 m, on granite. The higher ground gives fresher, more aromatic Cornas than the hot slopes by the village.
fr-cornas-les-eygas.terroir: The lieu-dit's 60.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 385 m, with a mean slope of about 28%, facing broadly north-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cornas-les-eygas.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cornas-les-mazards.name: Les Mazards
fr-cornas-les-mazards.summary: A gently sloping lieu-dit at the foot of the Cornas slopes near the village, on deeper soils with alluvium and granite debris, which give rounder, earlier wines than the terraces above.
fr-cornas-les-mazards.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 175 m, with a mean slope of about 12%, facing east to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cornas-les-mazards.nerd_note: The lower, flatter lieux-dits near the Rhône give rounder Cornas, often blended with the granite terraces.
fr-cornas-les-mazards.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cornas-reynard.name: Reynard
fr-cornas-reynard.summary: A steep granite slope just above the village of Cornas, facing south and south-east, worked on terraces. Reynard is the most famous lieu-dit of the appellation, made famous by Thierry Allemand's Cornas Reynard, a dense, mineral Syrah made without added sulphur in some vintages. Auguste Clape also uses Reynard fruit, and the Geynale parcel, made famous by Robert Michel and farmed by his nephew Vincent Paris, lies on this hillside.
fr-cornas-reynard.terroir: The lieu-dit's 22.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 300 m, with a mean slope of about 38%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cornas-reynard.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cornas-saint-pierre.name: Saint-Pierre
fr-cornas-saint-pierre.summary: A large lieu-dit on the slopes above Cornas, mostly facing south-east, on granite. Paul Jaboulet Aîné's Cornas Domaine de Saint-Pierre takes its name from it.
fr-cornas-saint-pierre.terroir: The lieu-dit's 55.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 275 to 405 m, with a mean slope of about 26%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cornas-saint-pierre.nerd_note: Cornas is said to take its name from a Celtic word for 'burnt earth', a nod to its hot, south-facing amphitheatre.
fr-cornas-saint-pierre.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Cornas AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Cornas when all the grapes come from it.

fr-corton-basses-mourottes.name: Corton Basses Mourottes
fr-corton-basses-mourottes.summary: Les Basses Mourottes is a small 0.94 ha Corton climat on the northeast face of the hill, in Ladoix. The wine is firm and fresh.
fr-corton-basses-mourottes.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 285 to 305 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton-Charlemagne and Corton Hautes Mourottes, above the grand cru Corton and beside Ladoix's Basses Mourottes.
fr-corton-basses-mourottes.nerd_note: The Ladoix premier cru of the same name lies beside it.

fr-corton-clos-des-meix.name: Corton Clos des Meix
fr-corton-clos-des-meix.summary:
The Clos des Meix is a walled 2.2 ha Corton climat on the southwest face of the hill, a monopole of Domaine Comte Senard, which makes red Corton here and some white.

The clos lies on the southwest side of the hill, beside Les Combes and La Vigne au Saint and just above Aloxe's Clos du Chapitre. Senard, based in Aloxe, has owned it for generations and makes a supple, red-fruited Corton from it, as well as one of the rare white Cortons.
fr-corton-clos-des-meix.terroir: Southwest-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The southwest exposure, unusual on the Côte, gives the clos warm afternoons and a ripe, round style.
fr-corton-clos-des-meix.nerd_note: Senard is one of the few estates to make a white wine labelled Corton rather than Corton-Charlemagne.

fr-corton-hautes-mourottes.name: Corton Hautes Mourottes
fr-corton-hautes-mourottes.summary: Les Hautes Mourottes is a 1.9 ha Corton climat high on the northeast face of the hill, in Ladoix. The wine is lean and fresh.
fr-corton-hautes-mourottes.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 300 to 330 m, slope around 18%, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Ladoix's Hautes Mourottes and above the grand cru Corton-Charlemagne, Corton Le Rognet et Corton and Corton Basses Mourottes.
fr-corton-hautes-mourottes.nerd_note: The Ladoix premier cru of the same name lies beside it.

fr-corton-la-toppe-au-vert.name: Corton La Toppe au Vert
fr-corton-la-toppe-au-vert.summary: La Toppe au Vert is a tiny 0.11 ha Corton climat on the lower east face of the hill, above the Aloxe-Corton premier cru of the same name.
fr-corton-la-toppe-au-vert.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 230 to 240 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay.
fr-corton-la-toppe-au-vert.nerd_note: At barely an eighth of a hectare it is the smallest Corton climat on the map; the Aloxe-Corton premier cru La Toppe au Vert lies just below.

fr-corton-la-vigne-au-saint.name: Corton La Vigne au Saint
fr-corton-la-vigne-au-saint.summary: La Vigne au Saint is a 2.5 ha Corton climat on the southwest face of the hill. Louis Latour bottles its walled heart as Corton Clos de la Vigne au Saint, a monopole. The wine is firm and red-fruited.
fr-corton-la-vigne-au-saint.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-corton-la-vigne-au-saint.nerd_note: Latour's Château Corton Grancey, the estate's other Corton, is a blend of several climats, while the Clos de la Vigne au Saint is a single site.

fr-corton-le-clos-du-roi.name: Corton Le Clos du Roi
fr-corton-le-clos-du-roi.summary:
Le Clos du Roi is the climat most often named the finest red of Corton. It lies mid-slope on the southeast face of the hill, at 10.9 ha, and takes its name from the Dukes of Burgundy, whose vineyard it was before passing to the French crown in 1477.

Its wines combine Corton's structure with unusual finesse: dark cherry, spice and a firm but fine tannin that needs ten years. Comte Senard, Follin-Arbelet, de Montille and the Prince de Mérode (whose holding has been leased to the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti since 2009) are leading holders.
fr-corton-le-clos-du-roi.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 325 m, moderately steep. Brown limestone-clay with iron, over Bathonian limestone, below the band of marl that carries Corton-Charlemagne.
fr-corton-le-clos-du-roi.nerd_note: The DRC's Corton is a blend of Clos du Roi, Bressandes and Renardes from the Mérode lease.

fr-corton-le-corton.name: Corton Le Corton
fr-corton-le-corton.summary:
Le Corton is the climat at the top of the hill's southeast face, at 11.7 ha, just below the woods that crown the hill. It gives some of the most structured red Cortons.

Le Corton occupies the upper part of the southeast face, just below the Bois de Corton, with Les Renardes and Le Clos du Roi below it and Corton-Charlemagne's white-wine marls alongside. Its steep, thin soils give a firm, sometimes austere red that can be one of the longest-lived Cortons; Bouchard Père et Fils' 'Le Corton' is the most widely seen.
fr-corton-le-corton.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 310 to 365 m, slope around 24%. Thin marl and limestone soils.
fr-corton-le-corton.nerd_note: Le Corton sits right under the Bois de Corton, the cap of woodland that keeps the hilltop cool and feeds it cold air at night.

fr-corton-le-meix-lallemand.name: Corton Le Meix Lallemand
fr-corton-le-meix-lallemand.summary: Le Meix Lallemand is a small 0.55 ha Corton climat on the southwest face of the hill. The wine is usually blended with other Corton climats.
fr-corton-le-meix-lallemand.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-corton-le-meix-lallemand.nerd_note: A *meix* is a plot attached to a house: this was once a garden-vineyard on the edge of Aloxe.

fr-corton-le-rognet-et-corton.name: Corton Le Rognet et Corton
fr-corton-le-rognet-et-corton.summary:
Le Rognet et Corton is a 11.8 ha Corton climat on the hill's east face, in Ladoix-Serrigny. Faiveley's monopole Clos des Cortons Faiveley is inside it, and Méo-Camuzet makes a Corton Clos Rognet.

Le Rognet et Corton is the largest Corton climat on the Ladoix side of the hill, on the east face below the Ladoix premier cru of the same name and beside Les Renardes. Faiveley's walled Clos des Cortons Faiveley, about 3 ha, is the most famous wine from it: dense, spicy and long-lived.
fr-corton-le-rognet-et-corton.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 320 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl.
fr-corton-le-rognet-et-corton.nerd_note: The Clos des Cortons Faiveley is the only climat in Burgundy allowed to carry its owner's name as part of the vineyard name.

fr-corton-les-bressandes.name: Corton Les Bressandes
fr-corton-les-bressandes.summary:
Les Bressandes is the largest red climat of Corton, at 17.2 ha, on the lower and middle slope of the hill's southeast face. It is often ranked with Clos du Roi as the finest: its wines are generous, red-fruited and perfumed, with a softer, more approachable tannin than Clos du Roi.

Its position below Le Clos du Roi and Les Renardes and above Aloxe's Les Valozières explains its generosity: where Clos du Roi is firm and Renardes wild, Bressandes is the most immediately charming red Corton, though the best bottles still age for twenty years. Tollot-Beaut and Chandon de Briailles make classic, perfumed versions.
fr-corton-les-bressandes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 250 to 275 m, gentle slope, deeper brown limestone-clay with some red iron-rich soil.
fr-corton-les-bressandes.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's Corton cuvées Charlotte Dumay and Docteur Peste both draw on Bressandes vines.

fr-corton-les-carrieres.name: Corton Les Carrières
fr-corton-les-carrieres.summary: Les Carrières is a small 0.48 ha Corton climat on the east face of the hill, in Ladoix. The name refers to old quarries.
fr-corton-les-carrieres.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 295 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton-Charlemagne, above Ladoix's Bois Roussot and beside the grand cru Corton and Corton Le Rognet et Corton.
fr-corton-les-carrieres.nerd_note: Its neighbours Le Rognet and Les Moutottes complete the Ladoix side of the grand cru.

fr-corton-les-chaumes.name: Corton Les Chaumes
fr-corton-les-chaumes.summary: Les Chaumes (officially Les Chaumes et la Voierosse) is a 6.7 ha Corton climat on the southwest face of the hill, toward Pernand. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-corton-les-chaumes.terroir: Southwest-facing at 245 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Charlemagne, the grand cru Corton-Charlemagne and Corton Les Pougets and above Corton La Vigne au Saint.

fr-corton-les-combes.name: Corton Les Combes
fr-corton-les-combes.summary: Les Combes is a 1.7 ha Corton climat at the southwest foot of the hill. The wine is supple and fruity.
fr-corton-les-combes.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Corton La Vigne au Saint and beside Corton Clos des Meix.
fr-corton-les-combes.nerd_note: *Combes* refers to small valleys in the hill.

fr-corton-les-fietres.name: Corton Les Fiètres
fr-corton-les-fietres.summary: Les Fiètres is a small 1.1 ha Corton climat on the southwest face of the hill. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-corton-les-fietres.terroir: South-facing at about 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Corton Les Perrières, above Corton Clos des Meix and beside Corton Les Chaumes and Corton Le Meix Lallemand.
fr-corton-les-fietres.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's Corton cuvée Docteur Peste includes vines here.

fr-corton-les-grandes-lolieres.name: Corton Les Grandes Lolières
fr-corton-les-grandes-lolieres.summary: Les Grandes Lolières is a 3.0 ha Corton climat on the lower east face of the hill, in Ladoix. The wine is supple for a Corton.
fr-corton-les-grandes-lolieres.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Corton Le Rognet et Corton and Corton Les Moutottes, above Aloxe-Corton's La Coutière and beside Aloxe-Corton's Les Petites Folières.
fr-corton-les-grandes-lolieres.nerd_note: Its lower edge meets the Aloxe-Corton premier crus La Coutière and Les Petites Folières.

fr-corton-les-greves.name: Corton Les Grèves
fr-corton-les-greves.summary:
Les Grèves is a 2.3 ha Corton climat on the southern slope of the hill, near Les Perrières. *Grèves* means gravel. The wine is fine and red-fruited.

Les Grèves is a small climat on the southern face, between Les Perrières and Les Bressandes, on gravelly limestone (*grèves*). It makes one of the finer, more perfumed red Cortons, and the Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Docteur Peste blends it with Bressandes, Chaumes, Fiètres and Clos du Roi.
fr-corton-les-greves.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 275 m, gentle slope, gravelly limestone soils.
fr-corton-les-greves.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's Corton cuvée Docteur Peste includes vines in Les Grèves.

fr-corton-les-languettes.name: Corton Les Languettes
fr-corton-les-languettes.summary:
Les Languettes is a 7.2 ha Corton climat on the south face of the hill, below Corton-Charlemagne. Most of it is planted with Chardonnay and sold as Corton-Charlemagne; the red is rare.

It sits on the steep south face below the Bois de Corton, between Le Corton and Les Pougets, on thin white marl, the soil that gives Corton-Charlemagne its tension. Its narrow strips are planted mostly to Chardonnay, which is why a red Corton Languettes is one of the rarest names in the grand cru.
fr-corton-les-languettes.terroir: Steep, south-southeast-facing at 285 to 355 m, slope around 21%. Thin white marl soils. At 285 to 355 m and with a median gradient near 21%, it is one of the steepest climats on the hill.
fr-corton-les-languettes.nerd_note: The name describes the narrow, tongue-like strips the parcels form on the slope.

fr-corton-les-marechaudes.name: Corton Les Maréchaudes
fr-corton-les-marechaudes.summary:
Les Maréchaudes is a 4.4 ha Corton climat on the lower east face of the hill, toward Ladoix. The wine is supple and fruity for a Corton.

It is the point where the grand cru gives way to the Aloxe-Corton premiers crus of the same name, with Les Bressandes and Les Vergennes above. Its deeper soils give a softer, rounder Corton that drinks earlier than the climats higher up.
fr-corton-les-marechaudes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The gradient is moderate, about 13%, and the deeper soil at the foot of the hill holds more water than the stony upper climats.
fr-corton-les-marechaudes.nerd_note: Mérode kept its Maréchaudes when it leased its other Corton vines to the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti in 2009.

fr-corton-les-moutottes.name: Corton Les Moutottes
fr-corton-les-moutottes.summary: Les Moutottes is a small 0.81 ha Corton climat on the east face of the hill, in Ladoix, beside the Aloxe-Corton premier cru of the same name.
fr-corton-les-moutottes.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Corton Le Rognet et Corton, above Corton Les Grandes Lolières and Aloxe-Corton's Les Petites Folières and beside Aloxe-Corton's Les Moutottes.
fr-corton-les-moutottes.nerd_note: Part of the lieu-dit is grand cru and part premier cru.

fr-corton-les-paulands.name: Corton Les Paulands
fr-corton-les-paulands.summary: Les Paulands is a small 1.1 ha Corton climat above the Aloxe-Corton premier cru of the same name, on the lower slope of the hill.
fr-corton-les-paulands.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton and Corton Les Bressandes, above Aloxe-Corton's Les Paulands and beside Aloxe-Corton's Les Valozières.
fr-corton-les-paulands.nerd_note: Its lower section is classed only as Aloxe-Corton premier cru.

fr-corton-les-perrieres.name: Corton Les Perrières
fr-corton-les-perrieres.summary:
Les Perrières is a 10.0 ha Corton climat on the southern slope of the hill, below Les Pougets. The name refers to old quarries. The wine is firm and mineral.

With Les Pougets and Les Languettes above and Les Grèves alongside, it makes a firm, mineral red, more linear than Bressandes, and Méo-Camuzet's version has helped make the name better known.
fr-corton-les-perrieres.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, gentle slope, stony limestone soils. Old quarry workings and limestone rubble give it some of the stoniest soil among the red Corton climats.
fr-corton-les-perrieres.nerd_note: Its lower edge touches Aloxe-Corton's premier crus Les Fournières and Les Chaillots.

fr-corton-les-pougets.name: Corton Les Pougets
fr-corton-les-pougets.summary:
Les Pougets is a 9.8 ha Corton climat on the southwest face of the hill, below Corton-Charlemagne. Louis Jadot's Corton Pougets is the reference: a fine, perfumed red.

Les Pougets lies on the southwest side of the hill, toward Pernand, below Les Languettes and above Les Chaumes, on marly limestone that is equally good for Chardonnay. Jadot farms both colours here: the red Corton Pougets is perfumed and fine, and Chardonnay from the upper part goes into its Corton-Charlemagne.
fr-corton-les-pougets.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 270 to 325 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. The southwest-facing side of the hill warms in the afternoon, which helps both Pinot Noir and Chardonnay ripen fully on this marly soil.
fr-corton-les-pougets.nerd_note: The upper part of Les Pougets is planted with Chardonnay and sold as Corton-Charlemagne.

fr-corton-les-renardes.name: Corton Les Renardes
fr-corton-les-renardes.summary:
Les Renardes ('the foxes') is a large 14.3 ha Corton climat on the upper part of the hill's east face, toward Ladoix. Its wines are the most gamey and wild of Corton, with dark fruit, earth and a firm tannin.

Its neighbours are Le Corton above, Le Clos du Roi to the southwest and Le Rognet toward Ladoix, and the iron-rich soil with marl is what gives the wine its earthy depth. The Prince de Mérode vines leased to the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti since 2009 form part of the DRC's Corton.
fr-corton-les-renardes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 335 m, moderately steep, iron-rich brown limestone-clay.
fr-corton-les-renardes.nerd_note: Tasters often say the name fits the wine: Renardes has a feral, foxy note.

fr-corton-les-vergennes.name: Corton Les Vergennes
fr-corton-les-vergennes.summary:
Les Vergennes is a 3.5 ha Corton climat on the east face of the hill, toward Ladoix. The Hospices de Beaune's Corton Vergennes cuvée Paul Chanson is a white Corton.

It sits below Le Rognet and above the Aloxe premier cru La Toppe au Vert. The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Paul Chanson, from this climat, is a white Corton, which shows that the hill's whites are not confined to Corton-Charlemagne.
fr-corton-les-vergennes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 270 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl. The marl here, close to that of Corton-Charlemagne, is why the Hospices chose to plant Chardonnay.
fr-corton-les-vergennes.nerd_note: The Hospices' cuvée Paul Chanson is one of the few white wines sold under the Corton name rather than Corton-Charlemagne.

fr-cote-rotie-bertholon.name: Bertholon
fr-cote-rotie-bertholon.summary: A small lieu-dit on the plateau above Ampuis, at about 330 m, bottled separately by Michel et Stéphane Ogier as an example of the fresher, higher-altitude Côte-Rôtie.
fr-cote-rotie-bertholon.terroir: The lieu-dit's 1.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 325 to 335 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-bertholon.nerd_note: The plateau above the slopes is included in the AOC; its gentler, higher sites give lighter wines than the coteaux.
fr-cote-rotie-bertholon.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-chavaroche.name: Chavaroche
fr-cote-rotie-chavaroche.summary: A steep lieu-dit of the Côte Brune above Ampuis, on dark schist. Bernard Levet's La Chavaroche, from old vines and made with whole bunches in old casks, is a reference for the wild, savoury, traditional side of Côte-Rôtie.
fr-cote-rotie-chavaroche.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 205 to 310 m, with a mean slope of about 39%, facing south-west to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-chavaroche.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-cognet.name: Cognet
fr-cote-rotie-cognet.summary: A steep, south-facing slope in Ampuis, one of the parcels bottled separately by Michel et Stéphane Ogier.
fr-cote-rotie-cognet.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 275 m, with a mean slope of about 35%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-cognet.nerd_note: Côte-Rôtie allows up to 20% Viognier, co-fermented with the Syrah, a tradition from the days of mixed plantings.
fr-cote-rotie-cognet.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-cote-bodin.name: Côte Bodin
fr-cote-rotie-cote-bodin.summary: A steep slope in Ampuis facing south-east and east, bottled as a single lieu-dit by Michel et Stéphane Ogier.
fr-cote-rotie-cote-bodin.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 180 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 39%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-cote-bodin.nerd_note: The Ogiers' 2019 'sélection de lieux-dits' bottled nine single sites, an unusual exercise in a region where most wines are blends of several slopes.
fr-cote-rotie-cote-bodin.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-cote-brune.name: Côte Brune
fr-cote-rotie-cote-brune.summary:
The cadastral Côte Brune is a small, very steep lieu-dit above Ampuis that gave its name to the whole northern half of Côte-Rôtie. Legend says the Seigneur de Maugiron left his slopes to two daughters, one dark and one fair, hence Côte Brune and Côte Blonde. The brown, iron-rich schist here gives firm, dark, savoury Syrah that needs a decade.

Domaine Jamet's Côte Brune is the modern reference, and the Gentaz-Dervieux Côte Brune of the 1970s to 1990s is a legend among collectors; Gilles Barge also bottles a Côte Brune.
fr-cote-rotie-cote-brune.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 170 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 43%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-cote-brune.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-cote-rozier.name: Côte Rozier
fr-cote-rotie-cote-rozier.summary: A steep, south-east-facing slope in the north of the appellation, below the Rozier plateau, on schist. Côte Rozier is one of the classic sites of the northern Côte-Rôtie, giving dark, firm, spicy wines, and its fruit goes into several famous blends as well as single-site bottlings.
fr-cote-rotie-cote-rozier.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 40%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-cote-rozier.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-coteaux-de-bassenon.name: Coteaux de Bassenon
fr-cote-rotie-coteaux-de-bassenon.summary: The southernmost slopes of Côte-Rôtie, in Tupin-et-Semons toward Condrieu, facing south and south-west. The soils are granitic, as in Condrieu next door, and some Viognier grows among the Syrah, as the Côte-Rôtie rules allow.
fr-cote-rotie-coteaux-de-bassenon.terroir: The lieu-dit's 19.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 155 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 37%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-coteaux-de-bassenon.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-coteaux-de-tupin.name: Coteaux de Tupin
fr-cote-rotie-coteaux-de-tupin.summary: Steep slopes in Tupin-et-Semons, the southern commune of Côte-Rôtie, facing south-east and south. The southern sector has more granite and gneiss than the Côte Brune, and the wines are finer and more perfumed, closer to the Côte Blonde style.
fr-cote-rotie-coteaux-de-tupin.terroir: The lieu-dit's 14.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 180 to 310 m, with a mean slope of about 48%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-coteaux-de-tupin.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-fongeant.name: Fongeant
fr-cote-rotie-fongeant.summary: A broad lieu-dit on the upper slopes of Ampuis, facing south and south-west. Fongeant is one of the parcels Michel et Stéphane Ogier have bottled separately to show the variety of their Côte-Rôtie holdings.
fr-cote-rotie-fongeant.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 330 m, with a mean slope of about 25%, facing south-west to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-fongeant.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-grandes-places.name: Grandes Places
fr-cote-rotie-grandes-places.summary: Les Grandes Places is a steep slope in the north of Côte-Rôtie, near Vérenay, on dark schist. Clusel-Roch's Les Grandes Places, from old vines of the local Sérine selection of Syrah, is one of the most admired traditional Côte-Rôties, dense and spicy; Jean-Michel Gerin also makes a Grandes Places.
fr-cote-rotie-grandes-places.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 270 to 325 m, with a mean slope of about 24%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-grandes-places.nerd_note: Sérine is the old, small-berried Syrah selection of the northern Rhône; several growers propagate it by massal selection from their own vines.
fr-cote-rotie-grandes-places.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-la-brocarde.name: La Brocarde
fr-cote-rotie-la-brocarde.summary: A small, steep lieu-dit in Ampuis facing south-east, on the Côte Blonde side, where lighter, granitic soils give finer, more perfumed Syrah.
fr-cote-rotie-la-brocarde.terroir: The lieu-dit's 4.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 165 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 35%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-la-brocarde.nerd_note: Côte-Rôtie's terraces are held by dry-stone walls; many were rebuilt after the vineyard shrank sharply in the mid-twentieth century.
fr-cote-rotie-la-brocarde.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-la-landonne.name: La Landonne
fr-cote-rotie-la-landonne.summary:
La Landonne is the most famous lieu-dit of the Côte Brune, the northern half of Côte-Rôtie, on a slope so steep (the terrain model averages about 50%) that it is worked on narrow terraces held by dry-stone walls. Its dark mica-schist, rich in iron oxides, gives the most powerful, tannic and long-lived wines of the appellation: black fruit, smoke, olive and iron, with little of the floral lift of the southern slopes.

Marcel Guigal assembled La Landonne from dozens of small plots in the 1970s and released the first Guigal La Landonne with the 1978 vintage; with La Mouline and La Turque it forms the trio of 'La La' wines that made Côte-Rôtie world-famous in the 1980s. Unlike its siblings it is pure Syrah. René Rostaing, Jean-Michel Gerin and Delas also bottle La Landonne.
fr-cote-rotie-la-landonne.terroir: The lieu-dit's 4.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 185 to 270 m, with a mean slope of about 50%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-la-landonne.nerd_note: Guigal's La Turque comes from the Côte Brune and La Mouline from the Côte Blonde; neither name is a cadastral lieu-dit, which is why they do not appear as separate units on this map.
fr-cote-rotie-la-landonne.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-la-vialliere.name: La Viallière
fr-cote-rotie-la-vialliere.summary: A steep slope in the north of the appellation toward Vérenay, facing south-east, on schist with some granite. La Viallière gives perfumed, structured Côte-Rôtie with a bright, peppery line. It has become one of the most frequently named lieux-dits on labels: René Rostaing, Clusel-Roch, Domaine de Bonserine and Michel et Stéphane Ogier all bottle it separately.
fr-cote-rotie-la-vialliere.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 185 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 37%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-la-vialliere.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-lancement.name: Lancement
fr-cote-rotie-lancement.summary: A slope in the south of Ampuis on the Côte Blonde side, where lighter, more granitic soils give finer, more aromatic wine. Michel et Stéphane Ogier's Lancement is one of the estate's flagship wines: perfumed, silky and long.
fr-cote-rotie-lancement.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 340 m, with a mean slope of about 25%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-lancement.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-le-champon.name: Le Champon
fr-cote-rotie-le-champon.summary: A lieu-dit on the upper, gentler ground of Ampuis near the plateau, at about 310 to 340 m. Michel et Stéphane Ogier bottle Le Champon separately; the higher position gives a lighter, more aromatic style.
fr-cote-rotie-le-champon.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 305 to 340 m, with a mean slope of about 18%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-le-champon.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-le-mollard.name: Le Mollard
fr-cote-rotie-le-mollard.summary: A steep slope in Ampuis facing south-east, worked on terraces of schist; one of the many lieux-dits whose fruit goes into the blends of the Ampuis growers.
fr-cote-rotie-le-mollard.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 170 to 290 m, with a mean slope of about 46%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-le-mollard.nerd_note: Many Côte-Rôtie lieux-dits are farmed in tiny parcels by several growers, so their names appear mainly in blends.
fr-cote-rotie-le-mollard.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-leyat.name: Leyat
