fr-cote-rotie-leyat.summary: A slope in Ampuis on the Côte Brune side. Leyat is one of the parcels Michel et Stéphane Ogier have bottled as a single lieu-dit in their 'sélection de lieux-dits'.
fr-cote-rotie-leyat.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 250 to 315 m, with a mean slope of about 28%, facing broadly east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-leyat.nerd_note: Most Côte-Rôtie estates own small parcels in several lieux-dits and blend them; single-lieu-dit bottlings are a recent trend.
fr-cote-rotie-leyat.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-montlis.name: Montlis
fr-cote-rotie-montlis.summary: A steep lieu-dit in Saint-Cyr-sur-le-Rhône, the northern commune of Côte-Rôtie, facing south-east. Montlis is one of the single-lieu-dit wines of Michel et Stéphane Ogier, and shows the cooler, fresher side of the northern extension of the appellation.
fr-cote-rotie-montlis.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 175 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 38%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-montlis.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-montmain.name: Montmain
fr-cote-rotie-montmain.summary: A steep, south-facing slope in Ampuis, one of the lieux-dits Michel et Stéphane Ogier bottle separately. Steep schist and full sun give dark, concentrated Syrah.
fr-cote-rotie-montmain.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 190 to 310 m, with a mean slope of about 41%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-montmain.nerd_note: The appellation runs along about 8 km of the right bank, on the communes of Saint-Cyr-sur-le-Rhône, Ampuis and Tupin-et-Semons.
fr-cote-rotie-montmain.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-rochins.name: Rochins
fr-cote-rotie-rochins.summary: A steep lieu-dit of the Côte Brune above Ampuis, facing south-west, on dark schist. Domaine Garon bottles Les Rochins, and Patrick and Christophe Bonnefond's 'Les Rochains' comes from the same slope.
fr-cote-rotie-rochins.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 180 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 42%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-rochins.nerd_note: 'Les Rochains' and 'Rochins' are two spellings of the same place, a common confusion in northern Rhône names.
fr-cote-rotie-rochins.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-rozier.name: Rozier
fr-cote-rotie-rozier.summary: The plateau and upper slopes above the Côte Rozier in the north of the appellation, at about 300 to 330 m. The higher, gentler land was planted later than the steep coteaux and gives a fresher, lighter style; it shows how Côte-Rôtie's vineyards have spread from the steep coteaux onto the higher, gentler ground.
fr-cote-rotie-rozier.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 330 m, with a mean slope of about 17%, facing south-west to west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-rozier.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-cote-rotie-verenay.name: Vérenay
fr-cote-rotie-verenay.summary: The lower slopes around the hamlet of Vérenay, at the northern end of the Ampuis commune, where Côte-Rôtie's northern coteaux begin. Several growers are based in the hamlet, including Clusel-Roch.
fr-cote-rotie-verenay.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 155 to 180 m, with a mean slope of about 19%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-cote-rotie-verenay.nerd_note: Vérenay marks the northern end of the Côte Brune slopes; the hamlet sits at the foot of the coteaux.
fr-cote-rotie-verenay.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Côte-Rôtie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Côte-Rôtie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fixin-premier-cru-arvelets.name: Fixin premier cru Arvelets
fr-fixin-premier-cru-arvelets.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-fixin-premier-cru-arvelets.summary: A small upper-slope premier cru of 3.3 ha next to Les Hervelets, at the northern end of Fixin. Because the appellation rules allow its wine to be sold as Les Hervelets, the name Arvelets rarely appears on a label. The style is the same: firm, red-fruited Fixin with a mineral grip.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-arvelets.terroir: East-southeast exposure at 315 to 345 m, on thin limestone and stony scree.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-arvelets.nerd_note: Arvelets and Hervelets sit side by side at almost the same altitude, and many growers treat them as one vineyard.

fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perriere.name: Fixin premier cru Clos de la Perrière
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perriere.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perriere.summary:
The Clos de la Perrière is the grandest wine of Fixin and, by old reputation, one of the best sites of the whole northern Côte. It sits above the hamlet behind the walls of the Manoir de la Perrière, which monks of Cîteaux built around 1142 with stone from a quarry just up the hill (the *perrière* of the name). The monks farmed it until 1622, and the boundaries are thought to be unchanged since they planted it. In the 19th century it was ranked a *tête de cuvée*, the only one outside Chambertin and Clos de Bèze in this part of the Côte, and it sold at the same price.

The Joliet family has owned it since 1853, and Bénigne Joliet, the sixth generation, bought out his relatives in 2004 to make it a true monopole. The INAO delimitation measures 5.9 ha, of which about 4 ha are planted, and a corner reaches into Brochon. The wine is darker and more rustic than Gevrey's grands crus, with black cherry, iron and a firm, slightly wild tannin that needs eight to ten years; since 2005, with lower yields and more care, it has been chasing its old reputation.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perriere.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing slope at 320 to 360 m, among the highest premier crus in Fixin. Thin brown limestone soils over Bajocian and Bathonian rock with very little clay. A breeze from the Combe de Fixin cools the upper vines, which ripen several days after the lower ones.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perriere.nerd_note: The 12th-century vaulted cuverie still holds the monks' original beam press, last used in 1959.

fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-du-chapitre.name: Fixin premier cru Clos du Chapitre
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-du-chapitre.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-du-chapitre.summary: A walled clos that once belonged to a cathedral chapter, hence its name, and one of Fixin's six premier crus. At 4.8 ha it lies just below and beside the Clos de la Perrière and the Clos Napoléon, on the gentler part of the slope; an 1855 description said its wine resembled La Perrière's and that only a wall separated them. Its wines are sturdy and dark-fruited, with Fixin's slightly rustic tannin but more flesh than the steeper climats above.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-du-chapitre.terroir: East-facing at 305 to 330 m. Brown calcareous clay over limestone, deeper than the soils of the Clos de la Perrière.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-du-chapitre.nerd_note: Gevrey-Chambertin also has a premier cru called Clos du Chapitre: both recall the ecclesiastical chapters that owned so much of the Côte before 1789.

fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-napoleon.name: Fixin premier cru Clos Napoléon
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-napoleon.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-napoleon.summary:
Fixin's Clos Napoléon is a shrine as much as a vineyard. Claude Noisot, a captain of Napoleon's Imperial Guard who followed the emperor to Elba, retired to Fixin, renamed his walled vineyard (formerly Aux Cheusots) in his honour and in 1847 commissioned François Rude's bronze 'Napoleon Awakening to Immortality', which still stands in the Parc Noisot above the vines. The clos is today a monopole of Domaine Pierre Gelin, at 1.8 ha.

The wine is a little rounder and earlier than the Clos de la Perrière next door, with red and black fruit, a savoury, earthy edge and Fixin's characteristic firm finish. It is one of the few places on the Côte de Nuits where a premier cru from a serious estate still sells at a village-wine price.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-napoleon.terroir: Mid-slope, east-southeast exposure at 310 to 325 m, just below the Clos de la Perrière. Brown limestone soils with more clay than the clos above, over Bajocian marl and limestone.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-clos-napoleon.nerd_note: Noisot asked to be buried standing up, facing his emperor's statue; his tomb is in the park beside the vines.

fr-fixin-premier-cru-hervelets.name: Fixin premier cru Hervelets
fr-fixin-premier-cru-hervelets.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-fixin-premier-cru-hervelets.summary:
Les Hervelets is the most widely seen Fixin premier cru, partly because the neighbouring Arvelets may be sold under its name. It occupies 3.7 ha of the upper slope at the northern end of the commune, toward Brochon, and gives a slightly finer, more perfumed Fixin than the Clos du Chapitre, with red cherry, spice and a mineral, stony finish.

Les Hervelets lies on the upper slope just south of Brochon, above Les Meix Bas and next to Les Arvelets, and its altitude and thin soil make it the most aromatic of Fixin's premier crus. It is often the best entry to the village's style: firm, red-fruited and long-lived, a cheaper and wilder cousin of the Côte de Nuits' more famous names.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-hervelets.terroir: Southeast-facing at 310 to 350 m. Thin, stony limestone soils with a little marl, cooled by air from the Combe de Fixin.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-hervelets.nerd_note: Fixin's rules let Les Arvelets be labelled Les Hervelets, which is why the larger name is the one you see in shops.

fr-fixin-premier-cru-les-meix-bas.name: Fixin premier cru Les Meix Bas
fr-fixin-premier-cru-les-meix-bas.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-fixin-premier-cru-les-meix-bas.summary: The smallest of Fixin's premier crus at only 0.49 ha, a sliver below Les Hervelets. A *meix* in Burgundian dialect is a plot attached to a house, so this was once a garden-vineyard on the edge of the hamlet. Little is bottled separately; most goes into Fixin premier cru blends.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-les-meix-bas.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 310 to 320 m, on brown limestone soils with some clay washed down from Les Hervelets.
fr-fixin-premier-cru-les-meix-bas.nerd_note: Fixin also permits white wine from its premier crus, though almost none is made.

fr-fleurie-champagne.name: Champagne
fr-fleurie-champagne.summary: A large climat of Fleurie on gentle slopes south-east of the village, on pink granite sand. Its name, like other Champagnes in Burgundy and Beaujolais, means open country (Latin *campania*).
fr-fleurie-champagne.terroir: The lieu-dit's 43.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-champagne.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-fonfotin.name: Fonfotin
fr-fleurie-fonfotin.summary: One of the highest climats of Fleurie, at about 375 to 460 m on granite, facing south-east and south-west, on the hills west of the village.
fr-fleurie-fonfotin.terroir: The lieu-dit's 21.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 375 to 460 m, with a mean slope of about 24%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-fonfotin.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-grand-cour.name: Grand'Cour
fr-fleurie-grand-cour.summary: A small climat around the Clos de la Grand'Cour, the Dutraive family's walled estate, a reference of the natural wine school of Beaujolais.
fr-fleurie-grand-cour.terroir: The lieu-dit's 7.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 285 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-grand-cour.nerd_note: Jean-Louis Dutraive farms the walled Clos de la Grand'Cour organically and makes his wines with whole bunches and little or no sulphur.
fr-fleurie-grand-cour.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-grille-midi-nord.name: Grille Midi Nord
fr-fleurie-grille-midi-nord.summary: The northern part of Grille-Midi, a steep, sun-trap slope ('grill at noon') above the village. Grille-Midi is one of the best-known Fleurie climats, giving ripe, intense Gamay.
fr-fleurie-grille-midi-nord.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 315 to 410 m, with a mean slope of about 18%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-grille-midi-nord.nerd_note: Grille-Midi is split into a north and a south part in the land register; both are mapped here.
fr-fleurie-grille-midi-nord.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-grille-midi-sud.name: Grille Midi Sud
fr-fleurie-grille-midi-sud.summary: The southern part of Grille-Midi, the sun-trap slope above Fleurie village (the name means 'grill at noon'); one of the best-known climats of the cru.
fr-fleurie-grille-midi-sud.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 310 to 360 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing north-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-grille-midi-sud.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-la-chapelle-des-bois.name: La Chapelle des Bois
fr-fleurie-la-chapelle-des-bois.summary: A climat in the south of Fleurie toward Morgon and Chiroubles, on granite sands. Clos de Mez bottles a Fleurie La Chapelle des Bois.
fr-fleurie-la-chapelle-des-bois.terroir: The lieu-dit's 46.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 275 to 335 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-la-chapelle-des-bois.nerd_note: Fleurie is sometimes called the 'queen of Beaujolais' for its perfume and grace.
fr-fleurie-la-chapelle-des-bois.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-la-madone.name: La Madone
fr-fleurie-la-madone.summary: The granite hill above Fleurie village, crowned by the nineteenth-century chapel of La Madone. Its slopes face south-east and east on pink granite sands, at about 330 to 430 m, and give the classic Fleurie: floral, silky and bright. La Madone is one of the lieux-dits in Fleurie's premier cru application. Domaine de la Madone and Domaine Chignard bottle it.
fr-fleurie-la-madone.terroir: The lieu-dit's 52.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 335 to 430 m, with a mean slope of about 20%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-la-madone.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-la-presle.name: La Presle
fr-fleurie-la-presle.summary: A steep climat of Fleurie, at about 330 to 445 m on granite, among the steepest slopes of the cru.
fr-fleurie-la-presle.terroir: The lieu-dit's 29.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 325 to 445 m, with a mean slope of about 26%, facing north-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-la-presle.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-la-roilette.name: La Roilette
fr-fleurie-la-roilette.summary: A climat bordering Moulin-à-Vent with more clay than most of Fleurie, known for the Coudert family's Clos de la Roilette, whose fuller, firmer wine was long sold as Fleurie but tastes closer to its neighbour.
fr-fleurie-la-roilette.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 275 m, with a mean slope of about 14%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-la-roilette.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-le-vivier.name: Le Vivier
fr-fleurie-le-vivier.summary: A climat on the lower, gentle land of Fleurie at about 225 to 250 m, on granite sand and alluvium toward the Saône plain.
fr-fleurie-le-vivier.terroir: The lieu-dit's 21.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-le-vivier.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-les-garants.name: Les Garants
fr-fleurie-les-garants.summary: A climat in the north of Fleurie on south-west-facing slopes of granite. Pierre-Marie Chermette's Domaine du Vissoux bottles Les Garants, a deeper style of Fleurie.
fr-fleurie-les-garants.terroir: The lieu-dit's 31.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 265 to 340 m, with a mean slope of about 14%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-les-garants.nerd_note: Fleurie lies on a single commune, and almost all of it is planted on pink granite sand, which explains its floral, silky style.
fr-fleurie-les-garants.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-les-labourons.name: Les Labourons
fr-fleurie-les-labourons.summary: The largest climat of Fleurie, on the high western slopes toward the hills, at about 350 to 430 m, facing west and south-west; cooler and later-ripening than the village slopes.
fr-fleurie-les-labourons.terroir: The lieu-dit's 73.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 355 to 425 m, with a mean slope of about 18%, facing broadly west-north-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-les-labourons.nerd_note: The high western climats of Fleurie, toward the Avenas hills, were once considered too cool and are now valued for freshness.
fr-fleurie-les-labourons.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-les-moriers.name: Les Moriers
fr-fleurie-les-moriers.summary: A climat in the north of Fleurie toward Moulin-à-Vent, on granite with some clay, facing east. Michel Chignard's Les Moriers is a reference for structured, age-worthy Fleurie.
fr-fleurie-les-moriers.terroir: The lieu-dit's 42.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 345 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-les-moriers.nerd_note: Les Moriers lies next to Moulin-à-Vent, and its wines share some of their neighbour's structure.
fr-fleurie-les-moriers.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-montgenas.name: Montgenas
fr-fleurie-montgenas.summary: A climat on the slopes north-west of Fleurie village, at about 300 to 370 m, on pink granite; one of the higher, cooler named sites of the cru.
fr-fleurie-montgenas.terroir: The lieu-dit's 34.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 305 to 365 m, with a mean slope of about 19%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-montgenas.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-poncie.name: Poncié
fr-fleurie-poncie.summary: A high, granitic climat in the north of Fleurie near Moulin-à-Vent, one of the proposed premier crus. Poncié gives firm, structured Fleurie; Château de Poncié and Pierre-Marie Chermette's Domaine du Vissoux bottle it.
fr-fleurie-poncie.terroir: The lieu-dit's 66.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 415 m, with a mean slope of about 20%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-poncie.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-fleurie-vers-la-mont.name: Vers la Mont
fr-fleurie-vers-la-mont.summary: A large climat on the slopes rising from Fleurie village toward the chapel hill of La Madone, at about 300 to 430 m on granite, facing south-east.
fr-fleurie-vers-la-mont.terroir: The lieu-dit's 33.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 430 m, with a mean slope of about 19%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-fleurie-vers-la-mont.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Fleurie AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Fleurie when all the grapes come from it.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-au-clos.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Au Closeau
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-au-clos.summary: Au Closeau ('the little enclosure') is a tiny premier cru of 0.53 ha just north of Mazis-Chambertin, at the edge of the village. The wine is a soft, early-drinking Gevrey premier cru.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-au-clos.terroir: Flat, southeast exposure at about 275 m, on deep brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Mazis-Chambertin and beside La Perrière and Les Corbeaux.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-au-clos.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in Gevrey.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-aux-com.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Aux Combottes
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-aux-com.summary:
Aux Combottes is the premier cru islanded among grands crus: Latricières-Chambertin to the north, Mazoyères and Charmes-Chambertin to the east and Clos de la Roche to the south. At 4.6 ha it sits in a slight hollow, which is the usual explanation for its exclusion from grand cru (cold air pools here and the soils are a little deeper). In practice its wines are among the most refined premier crus in Gevrey, with the perfume and silk of the Morey grands crus next door.

Dujac is a major holder, and its Combottes is consistently one of the domaine's best wines below grand cru level.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-aux-com.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 285 m, in a shallow depression. Brown limestone-clay with Bajocian marl at depth.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-aux-com.nerd_note: Aux Combottes is often cited as the clearest case in Burgundy where the soil looks like grand cru but a local cold pocket kept it out.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-bel-air.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Bel Air
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-bel-air.summary:
Bel Air is the premier cru directly above Chambertin and Clos de Bèze, at 2.6 ha, where the slope steepens toward the woods. The wine is lean, fresh and stony, much lighter than the grands crus below, because the soils are thinner and the site cooler.

Ruchottes and Mazis lie to the north, and the vines give way to scrub and woodland just above. In cooler decades it struggled to ripen; in recent hot summers its freshness has become an advantage, and growers increasingly value it as a source of lift for their premier cru blends.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-bel-air.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 300 to 330 m, slope near 23%. Thin soil over hard limestone at the top of the Chambertin slope.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-bel-air.nerd_note: Bel Air shows how fast terroir changes in Burgundy: a few metres upslope from Chambertin, the soil thins and the wine drops a full rank.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-champea.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Champeaux
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-champea.summary:
Champeaux lies at the northern end of the Côte Saint-Jacques, toward Brochon, on a slope of stony, thin soils. At 6.7 ha it is a mid-sized premier cru that makes a lighter, more aromatic Gevrey than Les Cazetiers: red cherry, wild strawberry and a stony, mineral bite, ready earlier.

In the hands of Denis Mortet and Fourrier it has a cult following as one of Gevrey's most transparent premier crus.

Champeaux marks the point where the Côte Saint-Jacques runs out toward Brochon, so it sits below the steep, high Goulots and Combe au Moine and beside the Petits Cazetiers. It is a good example of how Gevrey's northern premier crus differ from the grands crus south of the village: less flesh and power, more transparency and lift, and a stony finish that reflects the shallow soil.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-champea.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 315 to 350 m, on thin, rocky limestone with little topsoil, below Les Goulots and Combe au Moine.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-champea.nerd_note: Champeaux is one of the stoniest vineyards in Gevrey: the topsoil is so thin that the vines root almost directly into fissured limestone.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-champon.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Champonnet
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-champon.summary: A 3.3 ha premier cru on the flat ground just north of Ruchottes-Chambertin, between the village and the grands crus. The wine is a medium-bodied, red-fruited Gevrey premier cru.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-champon.terroir: Gentle northeast exposure at 285 to 295 m, on brown limestone-clay with alluvial gravel.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-champon.nerd_note: Champonnet, Craipillot and Fonteny together sit where the Lavaux stream's alluvial fan meets the slope, so their soils are deeper and more gravelly than the grands crus just south.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-cherbau.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Cherbaudes
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-cherbau.summary:
Cherbaudes sits at 2.2 ha between Mazis-Chambertin and Chapelle-Chambertin, almost surrounded by grands crus. Fourrier's 'Vieilles Vignes' bottling shows the site's best: a silky, perfumed wine with a grand cru's finesse in a lighter frame. The soil is close to that of the neighbouring grands crus, and some growers argue it deserved promotion.

Cherbaudes is effectively a premier cru island inside the grand cru zone: Mazis-Chambertin lies to the west, Chapelle-Chambertin to the south and Chambertin-Clos de Bèze just beyond. It is a vivid example of the INAO's 1930s approach in Gevrey, which classified by reputation and tradition rather than by drawing smooth lines across the slope.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-cherbau.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, almost flat, on brown limestone-clay over Bathonian rock.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-cherbau.nerd_note: It is one of Gevrey's few premier crus that touches four grands crus.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-de.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Clos des Varoilles
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-de.summary:
The Clos des Varoilles is a walled vineyard of 6.0 ha high in the Combe de Lavaux, on its southern flank, facing across the valley toward the Côte Saint-Jacques. It was for decades the flagship monopole of Domaine des Varoilles, and after that estate's division in 2020 the wine has been made by Prieuré-Roch (from the 2021 vintage).

Its wines are sturdy and long-lived, deep in colour, with dark cherry, spice and a firm, slightly wild tannin.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-de.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 310 to 340 m, unusually for a Gevrey premier cru that sits inside the combe rather than on the main slope. Limestone scree and thin brown soils.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-de.nerd_note: The clos is one of the few Gevrey premier crus that faces south-southeast across the Combe de Lavaux rather than east onto the plain.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-du.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Clos du Chapitre
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-du.summary: A small walled clos of 0.98 ha just below Clos Saint-Jacques, on the edge of the village. The chapter in its name was the cathedral chapter that owned vines here before the Revolution. The wine is a supple, fruity Gevrey premier cru.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-du.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 285 to 300 m, on deeper brown limestone-clay at the foot of the Côte Saint-Jacques.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-du.nerd_note: Fixin, the next village north, has a premier cru with the same name.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-pr.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Clos Prieur
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-pr.summary: Only the upper part of the Clos Prieur is premier cru: at 2.0 ha it lies just east of Mazis-Chambertin, while the lower half is village Gevrey. The wine is a fleshy, red-fruited premier cru, softer than Mazis.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-pr.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 270 m, on deep brown limestone-clay.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-pr.nerd_note: The name points to a prior, a sign that the land belonged to a religious house before the Revolution.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-sa.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Clos Saint-Jacques
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-sa.summary:
Clos Saint-Jacques is the premier cru everyone agrees should be a grand cru; it sells for more than most of Gevrey's grands crus. It lies on the Côte Saint-Jacques, the slope that bends round to face southeast just north of the village. In the 1930s the new INAO granted grand cru status in Gevrey only to vineyards adjoining Chambertin or Clos de Bèze; this one is detached on the far side of the village, so it was classed premier cru, even though Lavalle (1855) and Rodier (1920) had put it in the top rank.

The Comte de Moucheron held it as a monopole through the 19th century and sold it in 1954. Today its 6.7 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 6.7 ha) are split between five owners, each with a strip running from top to bottom of the slope: Armand Rousseau (2.2 ha), Sylvie Esmonin (1.6 ha), Bruno Clair and Louis Jadot (1 ha each, from the old Clair-Daü holding) and Fourrier (0.89 ha). Every owner has the same cross-section of soils, so it is a perfect test of winemaking.

The wine joins Gevrey's power to unusual elegance: dense red and black fruit, fine tannin and a cool, mineral finish, built for 20 years or more.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-sa.terroir: Southeast-facing at 290 to 350 m, with a moderate slope. Thin, stony soil on hard Bathonian limestone at the top; deeper brown limestone-clay washed from the Combe de Lavaux lower down. Cold air draining from the combe slows ripening and keeps acidity.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-clos-sa.nerd_note: Until the 1954 sale the bottom of the clos grew alfalfa. Rousseau prices its Clos Saint-Jacques above its Mazis, Ruchottes and Charmes-Chambertin.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-combe-a.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Combe au Moine
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-combe-a.summary:
Combe au Moine, the 'monk's valley', climbs steeply up the side of the Combe de Lavaux above Les Cazetiers. The monks are usually said to be those of Cluny, whose abbey was the dominant landowner in Gevrey in the Middle Ages. At 4.8 ha it is one of the highest premier crus in Gevrey, and the altitude shows: the wines are firm, lean and stony in youth, with sour cherry, herbs and a fresh, persistent finish, and they used to struggle in cool years.

Warmer vintages since 2000 have flattered the site, and in a hot year a Combe au Moine can outshine the lower climats, holding acidity that they lose.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-combe-a.terroir: Very steep, east-facing slope at 325 to 385 m. Thin, stony soil over hard limestone, with scree from the combe's walls. Exposed to cold air from the valley.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-combe-a.nerd_note: Fourrier's Combe au Moine is a Vieilles Vignes cuvée and one of the estate's most sought-after premier crus.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-craipil.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Craipillot
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-craipil.summary: A 2.8 ha premier cru on the gentle lower slope between the village and the grands crus, just south of the Clos du Chapitre. It gives a soft, fruity, early-drinking Gevrey premier cru.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-craipil.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at about 285 m, on deep brown limestone-clay and alluvial gravel from the Combe de Lavaux.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-craipil.nerd_note: Its neighbours Champonnet and Fonteny form a small cluster of premier crus on the village side of Ruchottes-Chambertin.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-en-ergo.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru En Ergot
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-en-ergo.summary: A small premier cru of 1.2 ha below Petite Chapelle, at the bottom of the slope near the Route des Grands Crus. The wine is a soft, fruity Gevrey premier cru.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-en-ergo.terroir: Flat, southeast-facing at 255 to 265 m, on deep brown clay soils. On the map it lies beside Petite Chapelle.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-en-ergo.nerd_note: An *ergot* is a spur, probably the shape of the parcel.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-estourn.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Estournelles-Saint-Jacques
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-estourn.summary:
Estournelles-Saint-Jacques sits above Lavaut Saint-Jacques and west of Clos Saint-Jacques, curling into the Combe de Lavaux. At 2.0 ha it is a small, high site, and its wines are among the most refined of the Côte Saint-Jacques: perfumed, red-fruited and silky, less dense than Clos Saint-Jacques but with a similar cool, mineral finish.

Its position in the combe makes it a late ripener, and it rewards a grower who waits.

In the hierarchy of the Côte Saint-Jacques it is usually placed just behind Clos Saint-Jacques, Lavaut and Les Cazetiers, but in warm vintages its altitude and thin soil give it the freshest balance of the four. Humbert Frères' version is a byword for perfume, and Frédéric Esmonin's shows the firmer, stonier side of the site.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-estourn.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 315 to 355 m on a steep slope. Very thin, stony soil over limestone.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-estourn.nerd_note: Unlike its neighbours on the Côte Saint-Jacques, Estournelles turns to face south-southeast as the slope bends into the combe, so it catches more afternoon sun than Lavaut below.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-fonteny.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Fonteny
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-fonteny.summary:
Fonteny sits just above Ruchottes-Chambertin and Mazis-Chambertin, at 3.7 ha, and gives one of the more elegant premier crus from the village side of the grands crus: red fruit, a silky texture and a stony finish. Joseph Roty's version is a benchmark.

Fonteny belongs to the small group of premier crus on the northern edge of the grand cru zone, between the village and Ruchottes-Chambertin, with Champonnet and Craipillot just below. Its upper edge rises onto thinner, stonier ground, which is why the best Fontenys have more tension than the neighbouring lower-slope premier crus.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-fonteny.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 280 to 300 m, on thin brown limestone over Bathonian rock, rising toward the woods.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-fonteny.nerd_note: Fonteny is one of the few premier crus that sits above two grands crus at once, with Ruchottes and Mazis-Chambertin along its lower edge.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-issarts.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Issarts
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-issarts.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.62 ha above Fonteny and next to Ruchottes-Chambertin. *Issarts* means land cleared from the forest. Faiveley is the main producer and the wine is firm and fresh, with a grand cru neighbour's structure in a lighter frame.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-issarts.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 300 to 315 m, on thin stony limestone soils.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-issarts.nerd_note: Its grand cru neighbour Ruchottes-Chambertin shares the same thin soils over Bathonian rock.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-boss.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru La Bossière
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-boss.summary: La Bossière is a tiny premier cru of 0.45 ha in the Combe de Lavaux, next to the Clos des Varoilles. It is a monopole of Domaine Harmand-Geoffroy, which makes a firm, fresh wine with red fruit, herbs and a lean, stony finish typical of the combe's high sites.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-boss.terroir: East-facing at 325 to 335 m, on steep, thin limestone soils.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-boss.nerd_note: With the Clos des Varoilles and La Romanée, La Bossière is one of three premier crus tucked inside the Combe de Lavaux rather than on the main slope.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-perr.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru La Perrière
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-perr.summary: A small premier cru of 2.5 ha in the lower part of the slope east of Mazis-Chambertin, near the village. The name, as so often in Burgundy, records an old stone quarry. The wine is a supple, fruity Gevrey premier cru.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-perr.terroir: Flat, southeast exposure at about 270 m, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-perr.nerd_note: Gevrey's quarries supplied stone for the village houses and for Dijon's buildings.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-roma.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru La Romanée
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-roma.summary: Gevrey's La Romanée (not to be confused with the Vosne grand cru) is a steep 1.1 ha premier cru above the Clos des Varoilles, inside the Combe de Lavaux. It was long a monopole of Domaine des Varoilles, whose holdings were divided in 2020. The wine is lean, fresh and stony, a high-altitude Gevrey.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-roma.terroir: Very steep, south-southeast-facing at 335 to 360 m, with a median slope near 31%. Thin soil and scree over limestone.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-la-roma.nerd_note: There are three Romanées in Burgundy's premier and grand cru lists: the Vosne grand cru, this Gevrey premier cru and a Chassagne-Montrachet premier cru.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-lavaut-.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Lavaut Saint-Jacques
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-lavaut-.summary:
Lavaut Saint-Jacques (often spelt Lavaux) sits just below and south of Clos Saint-Jacques, at the mouth of the Combe de Lavaux, the deep valley that cuts the hill behind Gevrey. At 9.6 ha it is one of the larger premier crus of the Côte Saint-Jacques, and in good hands it is the closest thing to Clos Saint-Jacques: perfumed, cherry-fruited and lifted, with a cooler, more floral profile than the grands crus south of the village and a long, slightly stony finish.

The cold air that slides out of the combe makes it a later-ripening site, which was a handicap in the 20th century and has become an asset with warmer summers.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-lavaut-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 290 to 320 m, on a gentle slope. Brown limestone soils mixed with scree and gravel brought down by the Lavaux stream, with less clay than the Côte Saint-Jacques' upper climats.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-lavaut-.nerd_note: Its name means 'the valley of Saint James': the combe and the Côte Saint-Jacques both take their name from a statue of Saint James on the pilgrim road to Compostela.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-caz.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Les Cazetiers
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-caz.summary:
Les Cazetiers lies directly north of and above Clos Saint-Jacques on the Côte Saint-Jacques and is usually ranked third among the climats of that slope, after Clos Saint-Jacques and Lavaut. At 9.1 ha it has enough growers to show its character clearly: a deep, structured Gevrey, more muscular and darker-fruited than Clos Saint-Jacques, with a firmer tannin that needs a decade to settle.

The upper part is steep and thin-soiled, the lower part broader and gentler, so producers with vines in both often get the most complete wine.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-caz.terroir: Southeast exposure at 300 to 365 m. Brown limestone over hard Bathonian rock in the upper part, deeper limestone-clay lower down. The slope steepens sharply toward the woods.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-caz.nerd_note: Faiveley's holding grew when it bought Domaine Dupont-Tisserandot, one of the main Cazetiers growers, in 2013.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-cor.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Les Corbeaux
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-cor.summary:
Les Corbeaux ('the crows') is a 3.2 ha premier cru just north of Mazis-Chambertin; the lower part of the lieu-dit is only village Gevrey. The wine is supple and perfumed, with dark cherry and a softer texture than the grand cru next door. Denis Bachelet's tiny old-vine bottling is one of the most coveted Gevrey premier crus.

Its position just north of Mazis-Chambertin, on the flat ground between the village and the grands crus, explains its style: deep soil gives roundness and early charm, while the Mazis influence brings a dark, spicy core. Lucien Boillot's version shows the more structured side of the site.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-cor.terroir: East-facing at 275 to 285 m, almost flat, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-cor.nerd_note: Bachelet makes only a few barrels from very old vines here, and the wine is allocated within days of release.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-gou.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Les Goulots
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-gou.summary: A steep premier cru of 1.8 ha at the top of the slope above Champeaux, at the northern end of the Côte Saint-Jacques. The wine is fresh and lean, with red fruit and a sharp, stony edge.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-gou.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 335 to 380 m, one of the highest and steepest premier crus in Gevrey. Thin soil over limestone and scree.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-les-gou.nerd_note: Fourrier's Goulots is often the most austere of its premier crus in youth and one of the slowest to open; the site's narrow shape is the likely origin of the name (*goulot*, a bottleneck).

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-petite-.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Petite Chapelle
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-petite-.summary:
Petite Chapelle sits directly below Chapelle-Chambertin, at 4.0 ha, on the lower slope toward the Route des Grands Crus. The chapel in both names was built by the monks of the Abbey of Bèze in 1155 and pulled down after the Revolution. The wine is plump and perfumed, a softer, more accessible cousin of the grand cru above.

It is one of the cluster of premier crus pressed against the grands crus on the Route des Grands Crus side of Gevrey, with Cherbaudes to the north and En Ergot to the south. Its deeper soil gives a rounder, earlier wine than Chapelle-Chambertin itself, but the family likeness is clear: red cherry, spice and a supple, perfumed texture.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-petite-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 260 m, almost flat, on deep brown limestone-clay.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-petite-.nerd_note: Petite Chapelle is sometimes labelled 'Champitonnois', the old name of the lieu-dit.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-petits-.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Petits Cazetiers
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-petits-.summary: A 0.94 ha strip on the edge of Les Cazetiers, at the northern end of the Côte Saint-Jacques. It shares the same soils and gives a slightly lighter, more immediate version of the Cazetiers style: dark cherry, spice and a firm, fresh finish.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-petits-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 305 to 330 m on stony brown limestone, between Les Cazetiers and Combe au Moine.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-petits-.nerd_note: Few growers bottle it separately; the name is often folded into a Gevrey premier cru blend.

fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-poissen.name: Gevrey-Chambertin premier cru Poissenot
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-poissen.summary: Poissenot is a steep 2.2 ha premier cru above the Clos des Varoilles, at the edge of the woods in the Combe de Lavaux. It makes a fine-boned, fresh Gevrey with red fruit and a mineral edge, and Humbert Frères' version is the reference.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-poissen.terroir: Very steep, south-southeast-facing at 325 to 395 m, slope around 29%. Thin, stony limestone soils.
fr-gevrey-chambertin-premier-cru-poissen.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus in the Côte de Nuits, touching 390 m at its upper edge.

fr-givry-premier-cru-a-vigne-rouge.name: Givry premier cru A Vigne Rouge
fr-givry-premier-cru-a-vigne-rouge.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-a-vigne-rouge.summary: A Vigne Rouge ('the red vine') is a 3.0 ha Givry premier cru. François Lumpp makes it. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-a-vigne-rouge.terroir: Southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Bois Gautiers and Le Vigron and above Les Grandes Vignes.
fr-givry-premier-cru-a-vigne-rouge.nerd_note: The name suggests it was always a red-wine site.

fr-givry-premier-cru-champ-nalot.name: Givry premier cru Champ Nalot
fr-givry-premier-cru-champ-nalot.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-champ-nalot.summary: Champ Nalot is a 3.2 ha Givry premier cru. Domaine Parize makes it. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-champ-nalot.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos Jus and beside Le Pied de Chaume and Le Champ Lalot.
fr-givry-premier-cru-champ-nalot.nerd_note: Not to be confused with its neighbour Le Champ Lalot.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-charle.name: Givry premier cru Clos Charlé
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-charle.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-charle.summary: The Clos Charlé is a 4.7 ha Givry premier cru below Servoisine. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-charle.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Servoisine and beside La Brûlée.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-charle.nerd_note: It sits between Servoisine and La Brûlée.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-de-la-baraude.name: Givry premier cru Clos de la Baraude
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-de-la-baraude.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-de-la-baraude.summary: The Clos de la Baraude is a 4.2 ha Givry premier cru. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-de-la-baraude.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 295 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Bois Gautiers and above Le Paradis.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cellier-aux.name: Givry premier cru Clos du Cellier aux Moines
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cellier-aux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cellier-aux.summary:
The Clos du Cellier aux Moines is the most famous premier cru of Givry and one of the oldest walled vineyards of the Côte Chalonnaise. It was planted by Cistercian monks of the Abbey of La Ferté in the 12th century, and their cellar, the *cellier* of the name, still stands at the top of the slope. At 13.3 ha it faces south-southwest on a steep hillside above the village, unusual for Burgundy.

Its reds are the most structured of Givry: dark cherry, spice and firm tannin, with a mineral freshness. The legend that Givry was Henri IV's favourite wine is often told here, though it is probably apocryphal. Domaine du Cellier aux Moines, bought by Philippe Pascal in 2004, and Domaine Joblot are the main producers.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cellier-aux.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 240 to 310 m, steep. Thin limestone soils with marl over Jurassic limestone, unusually stony for the Côte Chalonnaise.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cellier-aux.nerd_note: The south-southwest exposure gives more afternoon sun than most Côte d'Or premiers crus, which suits this cooler, more southerly hill country.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cras-long.name: Givry premier cru Clos du Cras long
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cras-long.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cras-long.summary: The Clos du Cras Long is a 2.8 ha Givry premier cru. François Lumpp makes it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-cras-long.terroir: Southeast-facing at 250 to 265 m, moderately steep, stony limestone. On the map it lies below La Grande Berge and beside Crémillons and Le Médenchot.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-vernoy.name: Givry premier cru Clos du Vernoy
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-vernoy.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-vernoy.summary: The Clos du Vernoy is a tiny 0.70 ha Givry premier cru near La Petite Berge.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-vernoy.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 255 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Grande Berge and beside La Petite Berge.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-du-vernoy.nerd_note: *Vernoy* probably refers to alders (*vernes*), which like damp ground.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-jus.name: Givry premier cru Clos Jus
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-jus.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-jus.summary: The Clos Jus is a 6.5 ha Givry premier cru in the commune of Dracy-le-Fort. Lumpp and Ragot make it. The red is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-jus.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone. On the map it lies above Le Champ Lalot and Champ Nalot.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-jus.nerd_note: It lies in Dracy-le-Fort, one of the two communes besides Givry and Jambles that share the appellation.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marceaux.name: Givry premier cru Clos Marceaux
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marceaux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marceaux.summary: The Clos Marceaux is a 3.0 ha Givry premier cru on the gentle slope. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marceaux.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside Les Grandes Vignes.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marceaux.nerd_note: It sits next to Les Grandes Vignes.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marole.name: Givry premier cru Clos Marole
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marole.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marole.summary: The Clos Marole is a 4.5 ha Givry premier cru. Joblot makes it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-marole.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 295 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below En Veau and above Petit Marole and Les Bois Chevaux.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-paul.name: Givry premier cru Clos-Saint-Paul
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-paul.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-paul.summary: The Clos Saint-Paul is a 2.1 ha Givry premier cru next to the Clos Salomon. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-paul.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 260 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos-Saint-Pierre, above Les Grands Prétans and beside Les Bois Chevaux and Clos Salomon.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-paul.nerd_note: It sits between the Clos Salomon and Les Bois Chevaux.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-pierre.name: Givry premier cru Clos-Saint-Pierre
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-pierre.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-pierre.summary: The Clos Saint-Pierre is a 2.7 ha Givry premier cru, a monopole of Domaine Thénard. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-pierre.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 285 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Les Bois Chevaux, Clos Salomon and Clos-Saint-Paul.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-saint-pierre.nerd_note: Thénard is better known for its large holding of Le Montrachet.

fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-salomon.name: Givry premier cru Clos Salomon
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-salomon.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-salomon.summary:
The Clos Salomon is a 7.0 ha walled Givry premier cru, a monopole of Domaine du Clos Salomon. Its red is supple and red-fruited, one of Givry's most elegant.

The clos sits on the gentle slope beside the Clos Saint-Paul and Les Grands Prétans, on limestone and marl.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-salomon.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 275 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl.
fr-givry-premier-cru-clos-salomon.nerd_note: The domaine takes its name from the clos, its flagship wine.

fr-givry-premier-cru-crausot.name: Givry premier cru Crausot
fr-givry-premier-cru-crausot.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-crausot.summary: Crausot is a 5.2 ha Givry premier cru in the commune of Jambles, facing south. François Lumpp makes it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-crausot.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 300 m, moderately steep, stony limestone. On the map it lies below La Plante and La Matrosse and above La Grande Berge.
fr-givry-premier-cru-crausot.nerd_note: It lies in Jambles, west of Givry.

fr-givry-premier-cru-cremillons.name: Givry premier cru Crémillons
fr-givry-premier-cru-cremillons.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-cremillons.summary: Crémillons is a small 1.5 ha Givry premier cru near the Clos du Cras Long.
fr-givry-premier-cru-cremillons.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 255 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Grande Berge and beside Clos du Cras long.
fr-givry-premier-cru-cremillons.nerd_note: It sits below La Grande Berge.

fr-givry-premier-cru-en-choue.name: Givry premier cru En Choué
fr-givry-premier-cru-en-choue.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-en-choue.summary: En Choué is a 8.3 ha Givry premier cru, high on a south-facing slope. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-givry-premier-cru-en-choue.terroir: South-facing at 295 to 350 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Les Galaffres.
fr-givry-premier-cru-en-choue.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus of Givry.

fr-givry-premier-cru-en-veau.name: Givry premier cru En Veau
fr-givry-premier-cru-en-veau.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-en-veau.summary: En Veau is a 4.5 ha Givry premier cru next to the Clos du Cellier aux Moines.
fr-givry-premier-cru-en-veau.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 285 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Combes, above Petit Marole and Clos Marole and beside Clos du Cellier aux Moines.
fr-givry-premier-cru-en-veau.nerd_note: It sits beside the Clos du Cellier aux Moines.

fr-givry-premier-cru-la-brulee.name: Givry premier cru La Brûlée
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-brulee.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-brulee.summary: La Brûlée is a 2.4 ha Givry premier cru on the lower slope. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-brulee.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside Le Pied de Chaume and Clos Charlé.

fr-givry-premier-cru-la-grande-berge.name: Givry premier cru La Grande Berge
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-grande-berge.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-grande-berge.summary: La Grande Berge is a large 13.3 ha Givry premier cru. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-grande-berge.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 295 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Crausot and above Clos du Cras long, La Petite Berge and Clos du Vernoy.

fr-givry-premier-cru-la-matrosse.name: Givry premier cru La Matrosse
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-matrosse.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-matrosse.summary: La Matrosse is a tiny 0.52 ha Givry premier cru in the commune of Jambles.
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-matrosse.terroir: Southwest-facing at 285 to 295 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Plante and above Crausot.
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-matrosse.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus of Givry.

fr-givry-premier-cru-la-petite-berge.name: Givry premier cru La Petite Berge
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-petite-berge.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-petite-berge.summary: La Petite Berge is a 1.6 ha Givry premier cru below La Grande Berge.
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-petite-berge.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 255 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Grande Berge and beside Clos du Vernoy.
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-petite-berge.nerd_note: It sits below La Grande Berge.

fr-givry-premier-cru-la-plante.name: Givry premier cru La Plante
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-plante.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-plante.summary: La Plante is a 4.0 ha Givry premier cru in the commune of Jambles, facing south-southwest.
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-plante.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 290 to 335 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Crausot and La Matrosse.
fr-givry-premier-cru-la-plante.nerd_note: It lies in Jambles, west of Givry.

fr-givry-premier-cru-le-champ-lalot.name: Givry premier cru Le Champ Lalot
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-champ-lalot.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-champ-lalot.summary: Le Champ Lalot is a 8.2 ha Givry premier cru in the commune of Dracy-le-Fort. Michel Sarrazin makes it. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-champ-lalot.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos Jus and beside Champ Nalot.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-champ-lalot.nerd_note: It sits below the Clos Jus.

fr-givry-premier-cru-le-medenchot.name: Givry premier cru Le Médenchot
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-medenchot.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-medenchot.summary: Le Médenchot is a small 0.98 ha Givry premier cru in the commune of Jambles.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-medenchot.terroir: South-facing at 255 to 265 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Grande Berge and beside Clos du Cras long.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-medenchot.nerd_note: It lies in Jambles, west of Givry.

fr-givry-premier-cru-le-paradis.name: Givry premier cru Le Paradis
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-paradis.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-paradis.summary: Le Paradis is a small 0.71 ha Givry premier cru. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-paradis.terroir: South-southeast-facing at about 240 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos de la Baraude and beside Les Grandes Vignes.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-paradis.nerd_note: Mercurey has a premier cru called Clos de Paradis.

fr-givry-premier-cru-le-petit-pretan.name: Givry premier cru Le Petit Prétan
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-petit-pretan.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-petit-pretan.summary: Le Petit Prétan is a small 1.0 ha Givry premier cru next to Les Grands Prétans.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-petit-pretan.terroir: East-facing at 230 to 240 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos-Saint-Paul and Les Bois Chevaux and beside Les Grands Prétans.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-petit-pretan.nerd_note: It sits beside Les Grands Prétans.

fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-de-chaume.name: Givry premier cru Le Pied de Chaume
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-de-chaume.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-de-chaume.summary: Le Pied de Chaume is a 3.8 ha Givry premier cru on the lower slope.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-de-chaume.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside Champ Nalot and La Brûlée.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-de-chaume.nerd_note: It sits near Champ Nalot and La Brûlée.

fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-du-clou.name: Givry premier cru Le Pied du Clou
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-du-clou.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-du-clou.summary: Le Pied du Clou is a small 0.87 ha Givry premier cru on the flat lower ground. It sits on the flat ground at the foot of the Givry slope, at the lowest point of the appellation's premier cru map, and its wine is a supple, fruity Givry.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-du-clou.terroir: East-facing at about 220 m, almost flat, limestone and marl. The deeper soil here gives rounder, earlier wines than the slopes above.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-pied-du-clou.nerd_note: It is the lowest premier cru of Givry.

fr-givry-premier-cru-le-vigron.name: Givry premier cru Le Vigron
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-vigron.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-vigron.summary: Le Vigron is a 3.3 ha Givry premier cru. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-vigron.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 285 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Bois Gautiers and above A Vigne Rouge.
fr-givry-premier-cru-le-vigron.nerd_note: It sits below Les Bois Gautiers.

fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-chevaux.name: Givry premier cru Les Bois Chevaux
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-chevaux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-chevaux.summary: Les Bois Chevaux is a large 12.9 ha Givry premier cru. Thénard makes it. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-chevaux.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 230 to 285 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos-Saint-Pierre and Clos Marole, above Le Petit Prétan and beside Clos-Saint-Paul.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-chevaux.nerd_note: It is one of the largest premier crus of Givry.

fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-gautiers.name: Givry premier cru Les Bois Gautiers
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-gautiers.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-gautiers.summary: Les Bois Gautiers is a 7.3 ha Givry premier cru. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-gautiers.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 255 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Clos de la Baraude, Le Vigron and A Vigne Rouge.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-bois-gautiers.nerd_note: *Bois* refers to the woods once here.

fr-givry-premier-cru-les-combes.name: Givry premier cru Les Combes
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-combes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-combes.summary: Les Combes is a 1.6 ha Givry premier cru above the Clos du Cellier aux Moines.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-combes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 310 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Clos du Cellier aux Moines and En Veau.

fr-givry-premier-cru-les-galaffres.name: Givry premier cru Les Galaffres
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-galaffres.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-galaffres.summary: Les Galaffres is a 2.9 ha Givry premier cru on a south-facing slope below En Choué. Its south-facing slope is one of the warmer sites of Givry.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-galaffres.terroir: South-facing at 280 to 320 m, steep, limestone and marl. The gradient averages about 17%.

fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grandes-vignes.name: Givry premier cru Les Grandes Vignes
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grandes-vignes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grandes-vignes.summary: Les Grandes Vignes is a 2.5 ha Givry premier cru. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grandes-vignes.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below A Vigne Rouge and beside Le Paradis and Clos Marceaux.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grandes-vignes.nerd_note: It sits next to Le Paradis and the Clos Marceaux.

fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grands-pretans.name: Givry premier cru Les Grands Prétans
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grands-pretans.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grands-pretans.summary: Les Grands Prétans is a 6.5 ha Givry premier cru. Michel Sarrazin makes it. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grands-pretans.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 240 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos Salomon and Clos-Saint-Paul and beside Le Petit Prétan.
fr-givry-premier-cru-les-grands-pretans.nerd_note: It sits below the Clos Salomon.

fr-givry-premier-cru-petit-marole.name: Givry premier cru Petit Marole
fr-givry-premier-cru-petit-marole.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-petit-marole.summary: Petit Marole is a 3.1 ha Givry premier cru. François Lumpp makes it. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-givry-premier-cru-petit-marole.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos Marole, Clos du Cellier aux Moines and En Veau.
fr-givry-premier-cru-petit-marole.nerd_note: It sits below the Clos Marole.

fr-givry-premier-cru-servoisine.name: Givry premier cru Servoisine
fr-givry-premier-cru-servoisine.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-givry-premier-cru-servoisine.summary:
Servoisine is a 7.4 ha Givry premier cru below the Clos du Cellier aux Moines, facing south. Domaine Joblot's Clos de la Servoisine is the reference, a firm, red-fruited Givry.

The Clos Charlé lies below it, and its limestone and marl give firm, red-fruited wines.
fr-givry-premier-cru-servoisine.terroir: South-facing at 235 to 270 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl.
fr-givry-premier-cru-servoisine.nerd_note: Joblot is one of the estates that put Givry on the fine-wine map in the 1980s and 1990s.

fr-hermitage-beaume.name: Beaume
fr-hermitage-beaume.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-beaume.summary: A lieu-dit in the middle of the eastern hill, on stony limestone soils mixed with loess. Beaume is part of Jean-Louis Chave's red blend and gives warm, round Syrah.
fr-hermitage-beaume.terroir: The lieu-dit's 7.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 185 m, with a mean slope of about 27%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-beaume.nerd_note: Jean-Louis Chave blends his red Hermitage from parcels in several lieux-dits rather than bottling them separately, a deliberate choice for complexity.
fr-hermitage-beaume.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-diognieres-et-torras.name: Diognières et Torras
fr-hermitage-diognieres-et-torras.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-diognieres-et-torras.summary: A lieu-dit at the foot of the eastern hill that combines Diognières and Torras, on stony alluvial ground, giving supple, ripe Syrah for blends.
fr-hermitage-diognieres-et-torras.terroir: The lieu-dit's 4.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 140 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-diognieres-et-torras.nerd_note: Hermitage was famous enough in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries for Bordeaux merchants to add it to their clarets, a practice known as 'hermitager'.
fr-hermitage-diognieres-et-torras.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-l-hermite.name: L'Hermite
fr-hermitage-l-hermite.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-l-hermite.summary: The top of the hill around the chapel of Saint-Christophe and the hermit's cell that gave Hermitage its name, with thinner, sandy granite soils (*arzelle*). It gives perfumed, finely structured red and fine, mineral white. Chapoutier's L'Ermite is a single-site red and white; Jean-Louis Chave also farms here.
fr-hermitage-l-hermite.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 175 to 270 m, with a mean slope of about 29%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-l-hermite.nerd_note: The legend says the knight Gaspard de Stérimberg retired to a hermitage on the hill in 1224 after the Albigensian Crusade and planted vines there.
fr-hermitage-l-hermite.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-la-croix.name: La Croix
fr-hermitage-la-croix.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-la-croix.summary: Lower slopes on the eastern side of the hill near the town of Tain, on loess and pebbles; a source of supple red and white for blends.
fr-hermitage-la-croix.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 190 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-la-croix.nerd_note: Up to 15% of white Marsanne and Roussanne may be co-fermented with red Hermitage, though few growers use it.
fr-hermitage-la-croix.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-le-meal.name: Le Méal
fr-hermitage-le-meal.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-le-meal.summary:
In the middle of the hill, facing south, on limestone-rich pebbles and loess over granite; warm and rich, Le Méal gives ripe, sumptuous red and white. Its rounded stones are glacial and river deposits left on the slope, and they store heat.

Chapoutier bottles Le Méal separately as red and white, Paul Jaboulet Aîné's La Chapelle draws on it, and Marc Sorrel's Le Gréal blends Le Méal with Les Greffieux.
fr-hermitage-le-meal.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 140 to 225 m, with a mean slope of about 32%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-le-meal.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-les-bessards.name: Les Bessards
fr-hermitage-les-bessards.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-les-bessards.summary:
Les Bessards is the steep western end of the hill of Hermitage, on granite, and the backbone of red Hermitage: its Syrah is dark, firm, tannic and very long-lived, with black fruit, violets and a mineral, almost graphite edge.

Almost every great Hermitage draws on it. Jean-Louis Chave builds his red around Bessards; Chapoutier's Le Pavillon and Paul Jaboulet Aîné's La Chapelle rely heavily on it; Delas bottles a Les Bessards. The granite here is the same rock as Saint-Joseph across the river, from which the Rhône cut off the hill.
fr-hermitage-les-bessards.terroir: The lieu-dit's 20.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 240 m, with a mean slope of about 32%, facing south-west to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-les-bessards.nerd_note: Hermitage is a piece of the Massif Central: the granite of Les Bessards was separated from the west bank when the Rhône shifted its course east of the hill.
fr-hermitage-les-bessards.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-les-diognieres.name: Les Diognières
fr-hermitage-les-diognieres.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-les-diognieres.summary: Flat to gently sloping land at the foot of the eastern hill, on deep, stony alluvium. Les Diognières gives rounder, fleshier red; Ferraton bottles a Les Dionnières, and Chave includes it in his blend.
fr-hermitage-les-diognieres.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 130 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-les-diognieres.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-les-grandes-vignes.name: Les Grandes Vignes
fr-hermitage-les-grandes-vignes.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-les-grandes-vignes.summary: The part of the Hermitage AOC that lies in the commune of Crozes-Hermitage, north-east of the main hill, on higher slopes at about 250 to 320 m. It is a reminder that the appellation's limits follow terroir rather than commune boundaries.
fr-hermitage-les-grandes-vignes.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 250 to 320 m, with a mean slope of about 33%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-les-grandes-vignes.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-les-greffieux.name: Les Greffieux
fr-hermitage-les-greffieux.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-les-greffieux.summary: At the bottom of the hill below Le Méal and Les Bessards, on silty alluvium and scree washed down the slope. Its Syrah is supple, aromatic and earlier-drinking, the softening element of many blends. Marc Sorrel (in Le Gréal) and Chapoutier make single-site versions.
fr-hermitage-les-greffieux.terroir: The lieu-dit's 9.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 120 to 150 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-les-greffieux.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-les-murets.name: Les Murets
fr-hermitage-les-murets.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-les-murets.summary: On the eastern part of the hill, on loess (wind-blown silt) over granite and limestone, facing south. Les Murets is a classic white-wine site; Chapoutier's De l'Orée white comes from here, and the name Chante-Alouette is traditionally linked to this part of the hill.
fr-hermitage-les-murets.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 185 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-les-murets.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-les-rocoules.name: Les Rocoules
fr-hermitage-les-rocoules.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-les-rocoules.summary: A lieu-dit in the east of the hill on loess and limestone, famous for white Hermitage from Marsanne and Roussanne. Chave and Marc Sorrel use it, and Sorrel's white Les Rocoules is a single-site bottling of great longevity.
fr-hermitage-les-rocoules.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 185 m, with a mean slope of about 22%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-les-rocoules.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-les-vercandiere.name: Les Vercandière
fr-hermitage-les-vercandiere.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-les-vercandiere.summary: A small, flat lieu-dit at the foot of the hill, on alluvial soils, a source of supple Syrah for blends.
fr-hermitage-les-vercandiere.terroir: The lieu-dit's 1.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 120 to 120 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-les-vercandiere.nerd_note: The lieux-dits at the foot of the hill are often blended with the steep sites to soften them.
fr-hermitage-les-vercandiere.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-maison-blanche.name: Maison Blanche
fr-hermitage-maison-blanche.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-maison-blanche.summary: A lieu-dit on the eastern, gentler part of the hill around a white house, on loess and limestone pebbles. Its Marsanne gives rich, honeyed white Hermitage, and Chave's white blend includes Maison Blanche.
fr-hermitage-maison-blanche.terroir: The lieu-dit's 5.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 185 to 200 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
