fr-hermitage-maison-blanche.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-peleat.name: Péléat
fr-hermitage-peleat.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-peleat.summary: A small, south-facing lieu-dit in the middle of the hill between Le Méal and L'Hermite, on loess and scree over granite. Péléat is one of the parcels in Jean-Louis Chave's red blend, contributing aromatic finesse.
fr-hermitage-peleat.terroir: The lieu-dit's 2.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 130 to 180 m, with a mean slope of about 17%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-peleat.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-torras-et-les-garennes.name: Torras et les Garennes
fr-hermitage-torras-et-les-garennes.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-torras-et-les-garennes.summary: A small part of the Hermitage AOC in the commune of Larnage, on the eastern flank of the hill, where the white clay of Larnage begins.
fr-hermitage-torras-et-les-garennes.terroir: The lieu-dit's 2.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 140 to 175 m, with a mean slope of about 30%, facing west to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-torras-et-les-garennes.nerd_note: Hermitage covers only about 137 ha, on the communes of Tain-l'Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage and Larnage.
fr-hermitage-torras-et-les-garennes.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-hermitage-varogne.name: Varogne
fr-hermitage-varogne.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-hermitage-varogne.summary: The very steep western tip of the hill above the Rhône, facing west, on granite. Varogne is rarely named on labels but adds firm, dark Syrah to blends, close in style to Les Bessards.
fr-hermitage-varogne.terroir: The lieu-dit's 3.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 130 to 205 m, with a mean slope of about 50%, mostly west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-hermitage-varogne.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Hermitage AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Hermitage when all the grapes come from it.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-basses-mourottes.name: Ladoix premier cru Basses Mourottes
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-basses-mourottes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-basses-mourottes.summary: Les Basses Mourottes is a 2.6 ha Ladoix premier cru on the northeast flank of the hill of Corton, just beside the Corton grand cru climat of the same name. Its red has Corton's firm, earthy frame in a lighter form, and white is also permitted.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-basses-mourottes.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 285 to 305 m, on brown limestone-clay with marl, the same slope as Corton's Mourottes.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-basses-mourottes.nerd_note: Les Mourottes is split between grand cru Corton and Ladoix premier cru, a vivid example of how the classification lines cut through a single slope.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-bois-roussot.name: Ladoix premier cru Bois Roussot
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-bois-roussot.summary: Bois Roussot is a 4.3 ha red-only Ladoix premier cru on the lower northeast slope of the hill of Corton, next to Aloxe-Corton. The wine is firm and dark-fruited, a rustic cousin of Corton.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-bois-roussot.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 285 m, moderately steep, iron-rich brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Corton, above Les Joyeuses and Aloxe-Corton's Les Petites Folières and beside Aloxe-Corton's Les Moutottes.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-bois-roussot.nerd_note: Its upper edge touches the Corton grand cru boundary.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-en-naget.name: Ladoix premier cru En Naget
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-en-naget.summary: En Naget is a 2.6 ha white-only Ladoix premier cru high on the slope west of the village, next to Les Grêchons. The wine is a fresh, mineral Chardonnay.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-en-naget.terroir: Southeast-facing at 300 to 340 m, steep, on thin white marl and limestone.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-en-naget.nerd_note: The whites of Ladoix's upper slopes are a good-value alternative to Corton-Charlemagne, grown on similar marl.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-hautes-mourottes.name: Ladoix premier cru Hautes Mourottes
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-hautes-mourottes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-hautes-mourottes.summary: Les Hautes Mourottes is a steep 2.2 ha Ladoix premier cru above Les Basses Mourottes, on the northeast shoulder of the hill of Corton. The wine, red or white, is firm and fresh.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-hautes-mourottes.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 305 to 355 m, slope around 22%. Thin marly limestone soils, close to those of Corton-Charlemagne above.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-hautes-mourottes.nerd_note: The grand cru Corton Hautes Mourottes lies alongside, on almost identical ground.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-corvee.name: Ladoix premier cru La Corvée
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-corvee.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-corvee.summary: La Corvée is the largest Ladoix premier cru, at 7.2 ha, on the gentle south-facing slope at the northern end of the commune, toward Corgoloin. The wine is a fruity, medium-bodied red, and the appellation also allows white.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-corvee.terroir: Gentle south slope at 245 to 270 m, on brown limestone-clay with gravel.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-corvee.nerd_note: *Corvée* refers to the unpaid labour tenants owed their lord, a common climat name across the Côte.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-micaude.name: Ladoix premier cru La Micaude
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-micaude.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-micaude.summary: La Micaude is a 3.3 ha Ladoix premier cru next to La Corvée, at the northern end of the commune. Capitain-Gagnerot is a known producer. The wine is a supple, fruity red.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-micaude.terroir: South-facing at 245 to 260 m, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-la-micaude.nerd_note: This northern group of Ladoix premier crus lies closer to the Côte de Nuits than to the hill of Corton.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-clou-d-orge.name: Ladoix premier cru Le Clou d'Orge
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-clou-d-orge.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-clou-d-orge.summary: Le Clou d'Orge is a 2.7 ha Ladoix premier cru near La Corvée, on the northern side of the commune. The wine is a soft, red-fruited Ladoix.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-clou-d-orge.terroir: Southwest-facing at 245 to 260 m, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-clou-d-orge.nerd_note: It lies on the northern side of the commune, nearer the Côte de Nuits than the hill of Corton.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-rognet-et-corto.name: Ladoix premier cru Le Rognet et Corton
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-rognet-et-corto.summary: A 1.6 ha white-only Ladoix premier cru high on the northeast flank of the hill of Corton, above the grand cru Corton Le Rognet et Corton. It gives a taut, mineral Chardonnay with something of Corton-Charlemagne's cut.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-rognet-et-corto.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 320 to 345 m, on thin white marl and limestone, the same strata that make Corton-Charlemagne.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-le-rognet-et-corto.nerd_note: The same lieu-dit name covers a red grand cru on the lower slope and this white premier cru above.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-buis.name: Ladoix premier cru Les Buis
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-buis.summary: Les Buis ('box trees') is a small 2.2 ha red-only Ladoix premier cru above La Corvée. The wine is a firm, medium-bodied red.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-buis.terroir: South-facing at 255 to 270 m, moderately steep, on stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above La Corvée.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-buis.nerd_note: Box grows wild on the dry limestone slopes of the Côte, and several climats are named after it.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-grechons-et-fo.name: Ladoix premier cru Les Grêchons et Foutrières
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-grechons-et-fo.summary: Les Grêchons et Foutrières is a 5.9 ha white-only Ladoix premier cru on the high slope west of the village. It gives a taut, mineral Chardonnay.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-grechons-et-fo.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 300 to 345 m, steep, on thin marly limestone. On the map it lies beside En Naget.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-grechons-et-fo.nerd_note: Most bottles are labelled simply 'Les Grêchons'.

fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-joyeuses.name: Ladoix premier cru Les Joyeuses
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-joyeuses.summary: Les Joyeuses is a small 1.5 ha red-only Ladoix premier cru on the lower slope of the hill of Corton, next to Bois Roussot. The wine is supple and fruity.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-joyeuses.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 275 m, on brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Bois Roussot.
fr-ladoix-premier-cru-les-joyeuses.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in Ladoix.

fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bouti.name: Maranges premier cru Clos de la Boutière
fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bouti.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bouti.summary: The Clos de la Boutière is a 2.8 ha premier cru at the Santenay boundary. The red is supple and fruity.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bouti.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 265 to 290 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Clos Roussots and La Fussière and beside Santenay's Clos Rousseau.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bouti.nerd_note: It sits beside Santenay's Clos Rousseau.

fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-fussi.name: Maranges premier cru Clos de la Fussière
fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-fussi.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-fussi.summary: The Clos de la Fussière is a 0.88 ha walled premier cru within La Fussière.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-fussi.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 305 to 340 m, steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Les Clos Roussots.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-clos-de-la-fussi.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as La Fussière.

fr-maranges-premier-cru-la-fussiere.name: Maranges premier cru La Fussière
fr-maranges-premier-cru-la-fussiere.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-maranges-premier-cru-la-fussiere.summary:
La Fussière is the largest premier cru of the Maranges, a 42.6 ha south-facing slope across Dezize-lès-Maranges and Cheilly-lès-Maranges, at the southern tip of the Côte de Beaune. Its reds are the deepest of the appellation: dark-fruited, firm and earthy, good value Côte de Beaune.

Les Clos Roussots and Le Clos des Loyères lie below it. Bachelet-Monnot's version is a reference.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-la-fussiere.terroir: South-facing at 295 to 390 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl. At up to almost 400 m at the top, it is one of the highest premier crus of the Côte de Beaune.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-la-fussiere.nerd_note: The Maranges appellation was created in 1989 from three villages that had sold their wine as Côte de Beaune-Villages.

fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-loye.name: Maranges premier cru Le Clos des Loyères
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-loye.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-loye.summary: Le Clos des Loyères is a 11.4 ha premier cru below La Fussière. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-loye.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 270 to 310 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Fussière and above Les Clos Roussots and Le Clos des Rois.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-loye.nerd_note: It sits between La Fussière and Le Clos des Rois.

fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-rois.name: Maranges premier cru Le Clos des Rois
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-rois.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-rois.summary: Le Clos des Rois is a 7.2 ha premier cru on the lower slope of the Maranges. The red is supple and fruity.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-rois.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 255 to 285 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Clos Roussots and Le Clos des Loyères.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-clos-des-rois.nerd_note: It is the lowest of the Maranges premier crus.

fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-croix-moines.name: Maranges premier cru Le Croix Moines
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-croix-moines.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-croix-moines.summary: Le Croix Moines is a small, steep 1.1 ha premier cru at the top of the Maranges slope. Chevrot makes it. The red is fresh and firm.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-croix-moines.terroir: Very steep, south-facing at 350 to 400 m, slope around 28%, thin stony soil.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-le-croix-moines.nerd_note: At up to 400 m it is among the highest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

fr-maranges-premier-cru-les-clos-roussot.name: Maranges premier cru Les Clos Roussots
fr-maranges-premier-cru-les-clos-roussot.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-maranges-premier-cru-les-clos-roussot.summary: Les Clos Roussots is a large 28.0 ha premier cru below La Fussière, on the border with Santenay's Clos Rousseau. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-les-clos-roussot.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 260 to 310 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Fussière and Le Clos des Loyères and above Le Clos des Rois and Clos de la Boutière.
fr-maranges-premier-cru-les-clos-roussot.nerd_note: The name continues into Santenay as Clos Rousseau.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-de-paradis.name: Mercurey premier cru Clos de Paradis
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-de-paradis.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-de-paradis.summary: The Clos de Paradis is a 7.5 ha Mercurey premier cru in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-de-paradis.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 290 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above La Chassière.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-de-paradis.nerd_note: Givry also has a premier cru called Le Paradis.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-barraul.name: Mercurey premier cru Clos des Barraults
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-barraul.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-barraul.summary: The Clos des Barraults is a 5.0 ha Mercurey premier cru facing southwest. Michel Juillot makes it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-barraul.terroir: Southwest-facing at 260 to 320 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Champs Martin and above Les Crêts and Les Naugues.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-barraul.nerd_note: Its southwest exposure catches the afternoon sun.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-grands-.name: Mercurey premier cru Clos des grands Voyens
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-grands-.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-grands-.summary: The Clos des Grands Voyens is a 4.9 ha Mercurey premier cru, a monopole of Domaine Jeannin-Naltet. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-grands-.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 235 to 250 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Le Clos l'Evêque, Clos Voyens and Les Naugues and beside Grand Clos Fortoul.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-grands-.nerd_note: The Clos Voyens next door is a separate premier cru.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-montaig.name: Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-montaig.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-montaig.summary: The Clos des Montaigus (registered as 'Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus') is a 5.7 ha premier cru below the ruined medieval castle of Montaigu, mostly in the commune of Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-montaig.terroir: East-facing at 270 to 310 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-montaig.nerd_note: The Clos du Château de Montaigu lies within it.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-mygland.name: Mercurey premier cru Clos des Myglands
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-mygland.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-mygland.summary:
The Clos des Myglands is a 6.3 ha monopole of Domaine Faiveley, the largest landowner in Mercurey. Mercurey is the biggest appellation of the Côte Chalonnaise and mostly red, and the Clos des Myglands is one of its most consistent reds: supple, red-fruited and firm, a Burgundy of real class at a modest price.

It sits on the gentle slope beside the Clos l'Evêque, and Faiveley's red is one of the best-value Burgundies from a top house.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-mygland.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 270 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. The gradient is gentle, about 8%, and the soil a mix of limestone and marl typical of the northern Côte Chalonnaise.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-des-mygland.nerd_note: Faiveley has owned vineyards in Mercurey since the 1930s and is the appellation's biggest landowner.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-.name: Mercurey Premier Cru Clos du Château de Montaigu
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-.summary: The Clos du Château de Montaigu is a 1.9 ha walled Mercurey premier cru within the Clos des Montaigus, below the castle ruins. Domaine du Meix-Foulot makes it as a monopole.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 290 to 315 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus and Les Velley.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-.nerd_note: It is the clos closest to the old castle.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-marcilly.name: Mercurey premier cru Clos Marcilly
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-marcilly.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-marcilly.summary: The Clos Marcilly is a 7.5 ha Mercurey premier cru on the gentle lower slope. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-marcilly.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 230 to 240 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-marcilly.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus of Mercurey.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-tonnerre.name: Mercurey premier cru Clos Tonnerre
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-tonnerre.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-tonnerre.summary: The Clos Tonnerre is a 3.0 ha Mercurey premier cru, a monopole of Domaine Michel Juillot. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-tonnerre.terroir: South-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside Les Vasées.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-tonnerre.nerd_note: Not to be confused with Chablis' Montée de Tonnerre.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-voyens.name: Mercurey premier cru Clos Voyens
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-voyens.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-voyens.summary: The Clos Voyens is a 2.5 ha Mercurey premier cru, above the Clos des Grands Voyens. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-voyens.terroir: South-facing at 245 to 270 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Crêts, above Clos des grands Voyens and Les Naugues and beside Le Clos l'Evêque.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-clos-voyens.nerd_note: It sits between Les Crêts and the Clos l'Evêque.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grand-clos-forto.name: Mercurey premier cru Grand Clos Fortoul
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grand-clos-forto.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grand-clos-forto.summary: The Grand Clos Fortoul is a 2.5 ha Mercurey premier cru on the lower slope, next to the Clos des Grands Voyens.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grand-clos-forto.terroir: West-facing at about 235 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Le Clos l'Evêque and beside Clos des grands Voyens.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grand-clos-forto.nerd_note: Its west-facing aspect is unusual among Mercurey's premier crus.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grifferes.name: Mercurey premier cru Griffères
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grifferes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grifferes.summary: Griffères is a tiny 0.37 ha Mercurey premier cru next to the Clos du Roy.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grifferes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 280 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Le Clos du Roy.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-grifferes.nerd_note: It is the smallest premier cru in Mercurey.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-bondue.name: Mercurey premier cru La Bondue
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-bondue.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-bondue.summary: La Bondue is a 4.6 ha Mercurey premier cru. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-bondue.terroir: East-facing at 240 to 270 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Sazenay and above La Levrière.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-cailloute.name: Mercurey premier cru La Cailloute
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-cailloute.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-cailloute.summary: La Cailloute is a small 1.7 ha Mercurey premier cru, a monopole of Domaine Theulot-Juillot. The name refers to its stones (*cailloux*).
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-cailloute.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 300 to 335 m, steep, stony limestone. On the map it lies above Les Croichots and Les Combins.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-cailloute.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus of Mercurey.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-chassiere.name: Mercurey premier cru La Chassière
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-chassiere.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-chassiere.summary: La Chassière is a 4.4 ha Mercurey premier cru in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-chassiere.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos de Paradis and beside Les Fourneaux.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-chassiere.nerd_note: It sits below the Clos de Paradis.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-levriere.name: Mercurey premier cru La Levrière
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-levriere.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-levriere.summary: La Levrière is a 1.3 ha Mercurey premier cru. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-levriere.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Bondue and Sazenay.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-levriere.nerd_note: It sits just below Sazenay, on the eastern side of the appellation.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-mission.name: Mercurey premier cru La Mission
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-mission.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-mission.summary: La Mission is a 1.9 ha Mercurey premier cru, a monopole of the Château de Chamirey. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-mission.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Le Clos du Roy.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-la-mission.nerd_note: Chamirey's château, at the heart of Mercurey, is one of the landmark estates of the Côte Chalonnaise.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-du-roy.name: Mercurey premier cru Le Clos du Roy
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-du-roy.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-du-roy.summary: Le Clos du Roy is a 10.8 ha Mercurey premier cru, a former royal domain. Faiveley and the Château de Chamirey make it. The red is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-du-roy.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 260 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Mission, Les Velley and Griffères.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-du-roy.nerd_note: Like the Clos du Roi in Corton and Beaune, the name recalls royal ownership.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-l-eveque.name: Mercurey premier cru Le Clos l'Evêque
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-l-eveque.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-l-eveque.summary: Le Clos l'Evêque ('the bishop's clos') is the largest Mercurey premier cru, at 17.3 ha, once owned by the bishops of Chalon-sur-Saône. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-l-eveque.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 240 to 285 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos des Myglands, above Clos des grands Voyens and Grand Clos Fortoul and beside Clos Voyens.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-le-clos-l-eveque.nerd_note: The bishops of Chalon owned vineyards across the Côte Chalonnaise.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-byots.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Byots
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-byots.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-byots.summary: Les Byots is a 2.7 ha Mercurey premier cru on the gentle lower slope. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-byots.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Naugues and beside Les Vasées.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-byots.nerd_note: It is one of the lower premier crus of Mercurey.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-champs-marti.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Champs Martin
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-champs-marti.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-champs-marti.summary: Les Champs Martin is a 12.9 ha Mercurey premier cru facing southwest. Michel Juillot and Bruno Lorenzon make it. The red is firm and fresh, and some white is made.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-champs-marti.terroir: Southwest-facing at 265 to 330 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Clos des Barraults and beside Les Combins.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-champs-marti.nerd_note: It is one of the larger premier crus of Mercurey.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-combins.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Combins
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-combins.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-combins.summary: Les Combins is a 5.7 ha Mercurey premier cru facing south. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-combins.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 315 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Croichots and La Cailloute and beside Les Champs Martin.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-combins.nerd_note: It sits between Les Champs Martin and Les Croichots.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-crets.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Crêts
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-crets.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-crets.summary: Les Crêts is a 3.9 ha Mercurey premier cru facing south. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-crets.terroir: South-facing at 250 to 295 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Clos des Barraults and above Les Naugues and Clos Voyens.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-croichots.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Croichots
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-croichots.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-croichots.summary: Les Croichots is a 7.1 ha Mercurey premier cru. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-croichots.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 270 to 335 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Cailloute and above Les Combins.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-croichots.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus of Mercurey.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Fourneaux
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.summary: Les Fourneaux is a 2.8 ha Mercurey premier cru in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 260 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside La Chassière and Les Ruelles.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-fourneaux.nerd_note: Chablis and Savigny also have premier crus named Fourneaux.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-montaigus.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Montaigus
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-montaigus.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-montaigus.summary: Les Montaigus is a 7.7 ha Mercurey premier cru in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu, below the castle of Montaigu. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-montaigus.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 295 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus and above Les Velley.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-montaigus.nerd_note: It lies in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu, the second commune of the Mercurey appellation.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-naugues.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Naugues
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-naugues.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-naugues.summary: Les Naugues is a 4.1 ha Mercurey premier cru. François Raquillet makes it. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-naugues.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Crêts and Clos des Barraults and above Les Vasées and Les Byots.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-naugues.nerd_note: Its south-southwest exposure gives good ripeness.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-puillets.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Puillets
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-puillets.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-puillets.summary: Les Puillets is a 8.5 ha Mercurey premier cru. François Raquillet makes it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-puillets.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 280 to 315 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Saumonts.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-puillets.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus of Mercurey.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-ruelles.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Ruelles
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-ruelles.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-ruelles.summary: Les Ruelles is a 2.5 ha Mercurey premier cru in Saint-Martin-sous-Montaigu. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-ruelles.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside Les Fourneaux.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-saumonts.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Saumonts
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-saumonts.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-saumonts.summary: Les Saumonts is a steep 4.1 ha Mercurey premier cru. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-saumonts.terroir: Steep, south-southwest-facing at 290 to 340 m, slope around 24%, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above Les Puillets.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-saumonts.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus of Mercurey.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-vasees.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Vasées
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-vasees.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-vasees.summary: Les Vasées is a 3.1 ha Mercurey premier cru facing south. The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-vasees.terroir: South-facing at 235 to 250 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Naugues and beside Les Byots and Clos Tonnerre.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-vasees.nerd_note: It sits next to the Clos Tonnerre.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-velley.name: Mercurey premier cru Les Velley
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-velley.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-velley.summary: Les Velley is a 10.8 ha Mercurey premier cru. François Raquillet makes it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-velley.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 300 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Montaigus, Les Montaigus and Mercurey Premier Cru Clos du Château de Montaigu and above Le Clos du Roy.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-les-velley.nerd_note: It lies below the Montaigus climats.

fr-mercurey-premier-cru-sazenay.name: Mercurey premier cru Sazenay
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-sazenay.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay for white
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-sazenay.summary: Sazenay is a 13.2 ha Mercurey premier cru. The Château de Chamirey and Domaine de Suremain make it. The red is firm and red-fruited.
fr-mercurey-premier-cru-sazenay.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 320 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above La Bondue and La Levrière.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-blagny.name: Meursault premier cru Blagny
fr-meursault-premier-cru-blagny.summary:
Meursault premier cru Blagny is the umbrella name for white wine from the hamlet of Blagny, high above Meursault and Puligny. It covers 25.0 ha, including La Pièce sous le Bois, Sous le Dos d'Ane, La Jeunellotte, Sous Blagny and Les Ravelles. The wine is taut, cool and mineral, a high-altitude Meursault.

Blagny is a hamlet of a few houses and a chapel, high on the hill between Meursault and Puligny, and its vines sit 50 to 100 m higher than the Côte's great whites. That altitude gives cooler, later-ripening, more mineral wines, which suit a warming climate; Matrot and Martelet de Cherisey are the main local producers.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-blagny.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 360 m, steep in places, with thin marly limestone soils.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-blagny.nerd_note: White from Blagny is Meursault or Puligny premier cru depending on the commune; red is Blagny AOC.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-charmes.name: Meursault premier cru Charmes
fr-meursault-premier-cru-charmes.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-charmes.summary:
Les Charmes is the largest premier cru of Meursault, about 31 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 31.2 ha), on the gentle lower slope below Perrières and Genevrières, running south to the Puligny boundary. It is split into Charmes Dessus (upper, finer) and Charmes Dessous. The wine is the classic rich Meursault: ripe, round, nutty and buttery, with citrus and a soft, generous texture.

It sits below Les Perrières and Les Genevrières and runs south to touch Puligny's Les Combettes and Les Referts. The upper part, Charmes Dessus, on thinner soil, gives the most refined wines, while Charmes Dessous below is broader and richer. Lafon's and Roulot's Charmes show how much finesse this generous climat can reach.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-charmes.terroir: Gentle east-southeast slope at 235 to 255 m. Deeper brown limestone-clay than the upper premier crus.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-charmes.nerd_note: *Charmes* comes from *chaume*, fallow ground, not from charm.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-clos-des-perrie.name: Meursault premier cru Clos des Perrières
fr-meursault-premier-cru-clos-des-perrie.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-clos-des-perrie.summary:
The Clos des Perrières is a walled 0.94 ha monopole of Domaine Albert Grivault within the lower part of Les Perrières. Many tasters rank it with the best of Meursault, a dense, mineral, long-lived white.

The clos has a little more clay than Perrières Dessus, and Albert Grivault's wine has the Perrières tension in a slightly broader frame. It is one of the longest-lived Meursaults.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-clos-des-perrie.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 265 m, gentle slope, thin stony limestone soil with a little clay. The wall around the clos protects it from wind and slightly warms the vines, which may explain its broader texture compared with Perrières Dessus.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-clos-des-perrie.nerd_note: Grivault also makes Pommard Clos Blanc, but the Clos des Perrières is its flagship.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-genevrieres.name: Meursault premier cru Genevrières
fr-meursault-premier-cru-genevrieres.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-genevrieres.summary:
Les Genevrières lies just north of Les Perrières and above Les Charmes, at about 16.5 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 16.6 ha), split into Genevrières Dessus and Dessous. The name comes from juniper bushes (*genévriers*). Its wine is the most aromatic and floral of the great three Meursault premier crus: white flowers, citrus, spice and a fine, silky texture, less mineral than Perrières but more elegant than Charmes.

Les Genevrières sits between Les Perrières to the south and Le Porusot to the north, with Les Charmes below, and its slightly higher position and thinner soil explain why it is finer than Charmes and more aromatic than Perrières. François Jobard's Genevrières is famous for needing a decade in bottle, and Latour-Giraud, the largest holder, makes a richer, more generous version.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-genevrieres.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 280 m, moderately steep. Stony limestone soils with a little marl, thinner in Genevrières Dessus.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-genevrieres.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Baudot and Philippe le Bon are both Meursault Genevrières.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-la-jeunellotte.name: Meursault premier cru La Jeunellotte
fr-meursault-premier-cru-la-jeunellotte.summary: La Jeunellotte is a 5.0 ha part of Blagny, high above Meursault. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-la-jeunellotte.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 325 to 355 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Puligny-Montrachet's Sous le Puits and Les Ravelles and above Blagny and La Pièce sous le Bois.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-la-jeunellotte.nerd_note: Martelet de Cherisey bottles it as 'La Genelotte', the old spelling.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-la-piece-sous-l.name: Meursault premier cru La Pièce sous le Bois
fr-meursault-premier-cru-la-piece-sous-l.summary:
La Pièce sous le Bois ('the plot under the woods') is a 11.3 ha part of Blagny, high above Meursault. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru, a fresh, mineral wine.

It sits below the woods at the top of the Blagny slope, above Sous le Dos d'Ane and beside La Jeunellotte, on thin marly limestone. Ampeau's version is classic: taut and mineral, slow to open, with the cool freshness of Blagny's altitude.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-la-piece-sous-l.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 310 to 345 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-la-piece-sous-l.nerd_note: The woods above cool the vines and slow ripening.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-le-porusot.name: Meursault premier cru Le Porusot
fr-meursault-premier-cru-le-porusot.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-le-porusot.summary:
Le Porusot is a 4.4 ha premier cru just south of the village, below Les Bouchères. The wine is a fresh, mineral Meursault, often with a stony edge.

Its wines are tauter and more mineral than most Meursault, closer to Perrières than to Charmes in style, and Roulot's Porusots is a reference.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-le-porusot.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. The slope steepens here to about 10%, with stony soil that drains fast and keeps yields low.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-le-porusot.nerd_note: Le Porusot and Porusot are listed separately by INAO, but growers usually call the whole area 'Les Porusots' or 'Poruzots'.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-boucheres.name: Meursault premier cru Les Bouchères
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-boucheres.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-boucheres.summary:
Les Bouchères is a 4.2 ha premier cru just south of the village, above Le Porusot. Roulot makes it. The wine is a fine, mineral Meursault.

Roulot's and Buisson-Charles' versions are fine and mineral, with more tension than the village's broader premiers crus.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-boucheres.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-boucheres.nerd_note: It is one of the smaller premier crus of Meursault.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-caillerets.name: Meursault premier cru Les Caillerets
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-caillerets.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-caillerets.summary: Les Caillerets is a small 1.0 ha Meursault premier cru at the northern end of the commune, against Volnay's Caillerets. Red and white are both made.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-caillerets.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Monthélie's Les Champs Fulliots, above Volnay's Santenots and Les Santenots Blancs and beside Volnay's Clos des 60 ouvrées.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-caillerets.nerd_note: It touches Volnay's Clos des 60 Ouvrées across the commune line.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-cras.name: Meursault premier cru Les Cras
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-cras.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-cras.summary: Les Cras is a 3.5 ha premier cru at the northern end of Meursault, next to the Santenots. Red is permitted and sometimes made here as Meursault premier cru rouge, as well as white.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-cras.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 285 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Volnay's Santenots, Les Plures and Les Santenots Blancs.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-gouttes-d-o.name: Meursault premier cru Les Gouttes d'Or
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-gouttes-d-o.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-gouttes-d-o.summary:
Les Gouttes d'Or ('drops of gold') is a 5.3 ha premier cru at the northern end of Meursault's premier crus, near the village. The wine is rich and golden, with ripe fruit and spice.

Le Porusot and Les Bouchères lie alongside. Lafon's version is one of the most sought-after Gouttes d'Or, and Arnaud Ente's is among the rarest.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-gouttes-d-o.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl. The marl in the soil holds water, which helps the vines through dry summers and gives the wine its round texture.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-gouttes-d-o.nerd_note: With Les Bouchères and Le Porusot it forms the group of premier crus just south of the village houses.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-plures.name: Meursault premier cru Les Plures
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-plures.summary: Les Plures is a 10.4 ha part of the Santenots, in Meursault near Volnay. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru; red is Volnay premier cru Santenots.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-plures.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Cras and Les Santenots Blancs and beside Volnay's Santenots and Les Santenots du Milieu.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-plures.nerd_note: It is the largest of the three Santenots lieux-dits.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-ravelles.name: Meursault premier cru Les Ravelles
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-ravelles.summary: Les Ravelles is a small 1.2 ha part of Blagny, high above Meursault. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-ravelles.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 350 to 380 m, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies above Blagny and Blagny's La Jeunellotte and beside Puligny-Montrachet's Sous le Puits.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-ravelles.nerd_note: At over 350 m it is one of the highest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-santenots-b.name: Meursault premier cru Les Santenots Blancs
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-santenots-b.summary: Les Santenots Blancs is a 2.9 ha part of the Santenots, in Meursault but on the Volnay side. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru; red is Volnay premier cru Santenots.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-santenots-b.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 280 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-santenots-b.nerd_note: The 'Blancs' in the name probably refers to pale soil rather than to white wine.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-santenots-d.name: Meursault premier cru Les Santenots du Milieu
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-santenots-d.summary:
Les Santenots du Milieu is a 8.0 ha part of the Santenots, in Meursault near Volnay. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru; red is Volnay premier cru Santenots, the form in which Comtes Lafon makes its famous Volnay-Santenots-du-Milieu.

It sits on the gentle slope at the northern end of Meursault, below Les Santenots Blancs and beside Volnay's En Chevret, on brown limestone-clay. Most of it is planted to Pinot Noir, sold as Volnay-Santenots, but white from here is a fine, round Meursault premier cru.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-santenots-d.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The soil here has more clay than Meursault's southern premier crus, which suits Pinot Noir and explains why red dominates.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-les-santenots-d.nerd_note: Jacques Prieur's monopole Clos des Santenots is inside it.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-perrieres.name: Meursault premier cru Perrières
fr-meursault-premier-cru-perrieres.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-perrieres.summary:
Les Perrières is the greatest premier cru of Meursault and the one most often called a grand cru in all but name. It lies at the southern end of the village's slope, against Puligny's Champ Canet and Les Combettes, on stony ground that was once quarried (hence *perrières*). The climat, split into Perrières Dessus and Dessous and including the walled Clos des Perrières, covers 13.3 ha on the INAO delimitation. Dr Lavalle classed it as a *tête de cuvée* in 1855.

Its wine is Meursault's most mineral and tense: less buttery and broad than Charmes, with citrus, white flowers, hazelnut and a stony, almost salty finish that can last for a minute. It ages for 15 to 20 years. Coche-Dury's Perrières is one of the most expensive white wines in Burgundy.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-perrieres.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 305 m, moderately steep. Very thin soil over hard limestone and old quarry rubble in Perrières Dessus; a little more clay in Perrières Dessous. The rock is fractured, so roots go deep.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-perrieres.nerd_note: Coche-Dury's Perrières regularly sells for more than many grands crus, a fair measure of how the market ranks the climat.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-porusot.name: Meursault premier cru Porusot
fr-meursault-premier-cru-porusot.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-meursault-premier-cru-porusot.summary: Porusot (often spelt Poruzot) is a 7.1 ha premier cru just south of the village, next to Les Genevrières. The wine is a fresh, mineral Meursault.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-porusot.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 280 m, gentle slope, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Bouchères and beside Genevrières and Le Porusot.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-porusot.nerd_note: Jobard's Poruzot is often the most austere of its premier crus in youth.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-sous-blagny.name: Meursault premier cru Sous Blagny
fr-meursault-premier-cru-sous-blagny.summary: Sous Blagny is a 2.2 ha part of Blagny, just below the hamlet. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-sous-blagny.terroir: East-facing at 300 to 335 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Blagny and Blagny's La Jeunellotte and above Sous le Dos d'Ane and Puligny-Montrachet's Les Chalumaux.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-sous-blagny.nerd_note: Latour's Château de Blagny is a Meursault-Blagny from here.

fr-meursault-premier-cru-sous-le-dos-d-a.name: Meursault premier cru Sous le Dos d'Ane
fr-meursault-premier-cru-sous-le-dos-d-a.summary:
Sous le Dos d'Ane ('under the donkey's back') is a 5.2 ha part of Blagny, below the hamlet. White wine from here is Meursault premier cru. Domaine Leflaive makes a fine version.

It sits on the Blagny slope below La Pièce sous le Bois and above Meursault's Perrières, on marly limestone. Domaine Leflaive's Sous le Dos d'Ane, from one of Puligny's most famous estates, is a fine, mineral wine that shows how close Blagny's whites can come to Puligny.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-sous-le-dos-d-a.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 320 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils.
fr-meursault-premier-cru-sous-le-dos-d-a.nerd_note: The 'donkey's back' is presumably the rounded ridge above the climat.

fr-montagny-premier-cru-champ-toizeau.name: Montagny premier cru Champ Toizeau
fr-montagny-premier-cru-champ-toizeau.summary: Champ Toizeau is a small 1.5 ha Montagny premier cru in Montagny-lès-Buxy.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-champ-toizeau.terroir: Southwest-facing at 320 to 370 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Chaumelottes and above Les Garchères, Vignes sur le Cloux and Vignes Saint-Pierre.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-champ-toizeau.nerd_note: It sits next to Les Garchères.

fr-montagny-premier-cru-chazelle.name: Montagny premier cru Chazelle
fr-montagny-premier-cru-chazelle.summary: Chazelle is a 2.7 ha Montagny premier cru in Jully-lès-Buxy.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-chazelle.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 300 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below La Moullière and Les Coères and beside Les Chaniots.

fr-montagny-premier-cru-cornevent.name: Montagny premier cru Cornevent
fr-montagny-premier-cru-cornevent.summary: Cornevent is a 3.3 ha Montagny premier cru in Buxy. It lies on the east-southeast-facing slope above the Buxy vineyards.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-cornevent.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 275 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. The gradient averages about 12%.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-cornevent.nerd_note: The name probably points to a windy spot.

fr-montagny-premier-cru-creux-de-beaux-c.name: Montagny premier cru Creux de Beaux Champs
fr-montagny-premier-cru-creux-de-beaux-c.summary: Creux de Beaux Champs is a 4.5 ha Montagny premier cru in Montagny-lès-Buxy. The white is fresh and mineral.

fr-montagny-premier-cru-les-coeres.name: Montagny premier cru Les Coères
fr-montagny-premier-cru-les-coeres.summary:
Les Coères is the largest and best-known premier cru of Montagny, a 29.8 ha slope that spreads across Montagny-lès-Buxy, Jully-lès-Buxy and Saint-Vallerin. Montagny is a white-only appellation at the southern end of the Côte Chalonnaise; from 1943 to the late 1980s any Montagny reaching 11.5% alcohol could be called premier cru, until growers voluntarily redrew the map and settled on 49 climats on the best mid and upper slopes. Les Coères gives a fresh, citrus and white-flower Chardonnay with a stony finish.

It sits on the gentle slope across three communes, with Les Chaniots, Les Jardins and Les Las around it. Its whites are fresh and mineral, and Aladame's and Feuillat-Juillot's versions are among the best of Montagny.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-les-coeres.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 260 to 315 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-les-coeres.nerd_note: The 1943 alcohol rule, which tied premier cru to ripeness rather than place, made Montagny a unique case in Burgundy until it was abandoned.

fr-montagny-premier-cru-les-combes.terroir: South-facing at 330 to 360 m, steep, limestone and marl. The gradient averages about 18%.

fr-montagny-premier-cru-vignes-saint-pie.summary: Vignes Saint-Pierre is a 4.1 ha Montagny premier cru in Montagny-lès-Buxy. The white is fresh and mineral.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-vignes-saint-pie.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 300 to 335 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Chaumelottes, Les Combes and Champ Toizeau and beside Vignes sur le Cloux.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-vignes-saint-pie.nerd_note: It sits next to Vignes sur le Cloux.

fr-montagny-premier-cru-vignes-sur-le-cl.name: Montagny premier cru Vignes sur le Cloux
fr-montagny-premier-cru-vignes-sur-le-cl.summary: Vignes sur le Cloux is a 5.5 ha Montagny premier cru in Montagny-lès-Buxy. The white is fresh and mineral.
fr-montagny-premier-cru-vignes-sur-le-cl.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 300 to 350 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Garchères and Vignes Couland, above Les Burnins and beside Vignes Saint-Pierre.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-clos-des-toisie.name: Monthélie premier cru Clos des Toisières
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-clos-des-toisie.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-clos-des-toisie.summary: The Clos des Toisières is a tiny 0.45 ha premier cru near Les Champs Fulliots. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-clos-des-toisie.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 290 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Champs Fulliots.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-clos-des-toisie.nerd_note: At half a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus in Monthélie.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-la-taupine.name: Monthélie premier cru La Taupine
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-la-taupine.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-la-taupine.summary: La Taupine is a small 0.93 ha premier cru near Les Champs Fulliots. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-la-taupine.terroir: Almost flat, south-southwest exposure at about 295 m, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Champs Fulliots, Le Clos Gauthey and Le Cas Rougeot.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-la-taupine.nerd_note: It is one of the cluster of small premier crus between the village and Les Champs Fulliots.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-cas-rougeot.name: Monthélie premier cru Le Cas Rougeot
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-cas-rougeot.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-cas-rougeot.summary: Le Cas Rougeot is a tiny 0.56 ha premier cru near Les Champs Fulliots. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-cas-rougeot.terroir: Almost flat, south-southwest exposure at about 300 m, reddish limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Champs Fulliots, Les Vignes Rondes, Le Clos Gauthey and La Taupine.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-chateau-gail.name: Monthélie premier cru Le Château Gaillard
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-chateau-gail.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-chateau-gail.summary: Le Château Gaillard is a tiny 0.50 ha premier cru at the edge of the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-chateau-gail.terroir: Southwest-facing at 280 to 290 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Le Clos Gauthey and beside Le Village.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-chateau-gail.nerd_note: Despite the name it has nothing to do with Richard the Lionheart's castle in Normandy.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clos-gauthey.name: Monthélie premier cru Le Clos Gauthey
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clos-gauthey.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clos-gauthey.summary: Le Clos Gauthey is a 1.8 ha premier cru just above the village, on the gentle south-facing slope. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clos-gauthey.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 290 to 300 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Vignes Rondes, above Le Château Gaillard and beside La Taupine and Le Cas Rougeot.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clos-gauthey.nerd_note: Gauthey was probably a family name, as with many Burgundian clos named after former owners.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clou-des-che.name: Monthélie premier cru Le Clou des Chênes
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clou-des-che.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clou-des-che.summary: Le Clou des Chênes is a 1.6 ha premier cru above Sur la Velle, adjoining Volnay's Clos des Chênes. The wine is fresh and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clou-des-che.terroir: South-facing at 310 to 330 m, moderately steep, thin stony soils.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-clou-des-che.nerd_note: *Clou* is probably the Burgundian form of *clos*, which would make this the 'oak enclosure', twin to Volnay's Clos des Chênes next door.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-meix-bataill.name: Monthélie premier cru Le Meix Bataille
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-meix-bataill.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-meix-bataill.summary: Le Meix Bataille is a 2.2 ha premier cru just above the village, on the south-facing slope. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-meix-bataill.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 295 to 305 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Riottes and Les Barbières and beside Les Vignes Rondes and Sur la Velle.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-meix-bataill.nerd_note: A *meix* is a plot attached to a house; this one lies at the edge of the village.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-village.name: Monthélie premier cru Le Village
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-village.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-village.summary: Le Village is a tiny 0.20 ha premier cru inside Monthélie village. The wine is usually blended.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-village.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 280 to 290 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Le Château Gaillard.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-le-village.nerd_note: Morey, Pommard and Volnay also have premier crus called Le Village.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-barbieres.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Barbières
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-barbieres.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-barbieres.summary: Les Barbières is a 1.2 ha premier cru above the village, below Le Clou des Chênes. The wine is fresh and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-barbieres.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 305 to 315 m, gentle slope, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Le Clou des Chênes, above Le Meix Bataille and beside Sur la Velle and Les Riottes.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-barbieres.nerd_note: It lies just below the woods of the Monthélie hill.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-champs-full.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Champs Fulliots
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-champs-full.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-champs-full.summary: Les Champs Fulliots is the best-known premier cru of Monthélie, a 7.8 ha climat on the gentle slope that continues Volnay's Clos des Chênes and Clos des 60 Ouvrées across the commune line. Its wines are Volnay's country cousins: perfumed, red-fruited and supple, with a little more earth, and they cost a fraction of the Volnays next door.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-champs-full.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 300 m, almost flat at the top of the Volnay slope. Brown limestone-clay with scree, the same strata as the Clos des Chênes. The plateau-like gradient, about 4%, and its position at the top of the Volnay slope give the wine Volnay's finesse with a little more rusticity.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-champs-full.nerd_note: Monthélie's wines were long sold under the better-known names of Volnay and Pommard, which is one reason the village is still undervalued.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-clous.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Clous
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-clous.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-clous.summary: Les Clous is a 3.4 ha premier cru on the slope toward Auxey-Duresses, near Les Duresses. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Monthélie.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-clous.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 270 to 295 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Duresses.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-duresses.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Duresses
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-duresses.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-duresses.summary: Les Duresses is a 6.6 ha Monthélie premier cru on the east-facing slope toward Auxey-Duresses, continuing Auxey's Les Duresses. The Comtes Lafon make a fine, firm red here. The wine is darker and more structured than the Volnay-side premier crus.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-duresses.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay with marl.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-duresses.nerd_note: The climat straddles the Monthélie and Auxey-Duresses boundary.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-riottes.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Riottes
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-riottes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-riottes.summary: Les Riottes is a 4.0 ha premier cru above the village. The wine is fresh and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-riottes.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 300 to 325 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Le Meix Bataille and beside Les Barbières.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-riottes.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus of Monthélie.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-vignes-rond.name: Monthélie premier cru Les Vignes Rondes
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-vignes-rond.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-vignes-rond.summary: Les Vignes Rondes is a 2.7 ha premier cru just above the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-vignes-rond.terroir: Almost flat, southwest exposure at 295 to 305 m, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Le Clos Gauthey and beside Sur la Velle, Le Meix Bataille and Le Cas Rougeot.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-les-vignes-rond.nerd_note: It sits among the cluster of small premier crus around the village.

fr-monthelie-premier-cru-sur-la-velle.name: Monthélie premier cru Sur la Velle
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-sur-la-velle.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-sur-la-velle.summary: Sur la Velle is a 6.1 ha premier cru just east of the village, beside Volnay's Clos des Chênes. The Château de Monthelie (Domaine de Suremain) makes a reference version. The wine is perfumed and fine.
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-sur-la-velle.terroir: South-facing at 300 to 310 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay over limestone.
producers: Château de Monthelie (Domaine Eric de Suremain)
fr-monthelie-premier-cru-sur-la-velle.nerd_note: It lies just above the village, next to the boundary with Volnay's Clos des Chênes.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-cha.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Aux Charmes
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-cha.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-cha.summary:
A tiny premier cru of 1.2 ha at the northern edge of Morey, wedged between Clos de la Roche, Mazoyères-Chambertin and Charmes-Chambertin. It is little seen on its own, and its wine resembles a soft Mazoyères.

It is the only Morey premier cru that touches three grands crus, Clos de la Roche to the west and Mazoyères- and Charmes-Chambertin to the north, at the point where Morey meets Gevrey. Its wines resemble a soft Mazoyères, with dark cherry and spice and a gentle tannin.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-cha.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 270 m, on brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 4%, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-cha.nerd_note: Aux Charmes shares its name, and probably its soils, with Charmes-Chambertin just over the commune boundary.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-che.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Aux Cheseaux
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-che.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-che.summary: A 1.5 ha premier cru at the northern end of Morey, below Charmes-Chambertin. The wine is a fleshy, perfumed premier cru, and Arlaud's version is the best-known.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-che.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 260 m, flat, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below the grand cru Charmes-Chambertin and the grand cru Mazoyères-Chambertin and beside Aux Charmes and Clos des Ormes.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-aux-che.nerd_note: The name, also written Chezeaux, comes from the Latin *casale*, a farmstead.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-ba.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Clos Baulet
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-ba.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-ba.summary:
Clos Baulet is a walled 0.87 ha premier cru a little below Clos des Lambrays, on the village side of the slope. Domaine des Lambrays makes a Clos Baulet from its parcel, a supple, perfumed wine that tastes like a junior version of its grand cru, and Frédéric Magnien makes another.

The clos sits on the village side of the grand cru band, with Clos Sorbè and Les Blanchards alongside, on deeper soil than the Lambrays slope. That deeper soil gives a softer, rounder wine than the grand cru, and the Lambrays and Magnien bottlings make a useful side-by-side lesson in what a few dozen metres and a classification line mean.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-ba.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-ba.nerd_note: Lambrays' bottling is a useful lesson in Burgundian hierarchy: same owner, same cellar, a few dozen metres downslope, one rank lower.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-de.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Clos des Ormes
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-de.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-de.summary:
The Clos des Ormes ('the elms') sits below Clos de la Roche, at 3.1 ha, at the northern end of Morey toward Gevrey. It makes a dark-fruited, structured Morey premier cru, and Georges Lignier is the best-known holder.

The clos lies against the lower edge of Clos de la Roche at the northern end of Morey, with Aux Charmes and Les Charrières on either side. It shares some of the grand cru's dark fruit and structure on deeper, more clay-rich soil, and Georges Lignier's version is the best-known expression.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-de.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 270 m, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-de.nerd_note: Elms, like the hemp and service trees in other Morey names, recall a farming landscape before vineyards took over the whole slope.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-so.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Clos Sorbè
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-so.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-so.summary: Clos Sorbè (also written Clos Sorbet) is a walled 3.3 ha premier cru below the village and Clos des Lambrays, next to Les Sorbès. The soils are deeper than those of the grands crus, and the wine is round, fruity and early-drinking for a Morey premier cru.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-so.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 270 m on brown limestone-clay.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-clos-so.nerd_note: The name comes from the service tree (*sorbier*), once common in Burgundy's field boundaries.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-cote-ro.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Côte Rotie
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-cote-ro.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-cote-ro.summary:
Morey's Côte Rotie (the 'roasted slope', no relation to the Rhône) is a steep 1.2 ha premier cru directly above Clos des Lambrays and Clos Saint-Denis. The name says it all: a sun-trap on thin, stony soils. The wine is concentrated but fine-boned.

Its thin, rocky ground warms quickly, which is how it got its name. It is the smallest of Morey's high premiers crus, and its wines are concentrated but fine, with the stony finish of the upper slope.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-cote-ro.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 305 to 325 m, slope near 18%. Thin, rocky limestone soils at the top of the grand cru band.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-cote-ro.nerd_note: Its northern Rhône namesake is also a 'roasted' slope: both names describe sun-baked rock rather than any shared history.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-buss.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru La Bussière
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-buss.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-buss.summary:
La Bussière is the premier cru at the southern edge of Morey, just below Bonnes-Mares and next to Chambolle's Les Sentiers. Its heart is the walled Clos de la Bussière, 2.6 ha in total on the INAO delimitation, which was the property of the Cistercian Abbey of La Bussière-sur-Ouche and has been a monopole of Domaine Georges Roumier since 1953.

Roumier's Clos de la Bussière is a darker, earthier, more masculine wine than its Chambolles: black cherry, spice and a firm, slightly rustic tannin that softens after a decade. It is one of the best values in Roumier's range because the domaine's name rides on its Chambolles.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-buss.terroir: Gentle east-northeast slope at 255 to 265 m. Deeper brown limestone-clay than Chambolle's premier crus, with more clay and iron, which gives the wine its extra structure.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-buss.nerd_note: The clos keeps the name of the abbey that owned it: La Bussière-sur-Ouche, a Cistercian house founded in 1131 in the Ouche valley west of Dijon.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-riot.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru La Riotte
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-riot.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-riot.summary:
La Riotte is a 2.5 ha premier cru below Clos de la Roche and Clos Saint-Denis, close to the village. It gives a fleshy, fragrant Morey with dark cherry and spice, and in the hands of Perrot-Minot and Taupenot-Merme it is one of the village's more serious premier crus.

La Riotte sits between the village and the grands crus, with Les Millandes and Les Chenevery around it, on slightly gentler ground than Clos de la Roche. Its wines are rounder and earlier than the grand cru, but in old-vine bottlings they gain real depth: dark cherry, spice and a fine, firm finish.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-riot.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 280 m on brown limestone-clay with some gravel.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-la-riot.nerd_note: Perrot-Minot's La Riotte comes from old vines and is one of the estate's most consistent premier crus.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-le-vill.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Le Village
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-le-vill.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-le-vill.summary: A premier cru of 0.84 ha in the middle of Morey's village, between the houses and Clos des Lambrays. As in several Côte d'Or villages, gardens and plots inside the settlement that had always made good wine were given premier cru status. The wine is a supple Morey premier cru.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-le-vill.terroir: Southeast-facing at 270 to 280 m, on brown limestone-clay inside the village.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-le-vill.nerd_note: Monthélie, Pommard and Volnay also have premier crus called Le Village.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-bla.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Blanchards
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-bla.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-bla.summary: Les Blanchards sits on the lower side of the village, below Clos Saint-Denis, at 2.0 ha. Its name probably refers to pale, marly soil. The wine is a fleshy, perfumed Morey premier cru with something of Clos Saint-Denis' red-fruited charm in a smaller frame.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-bla.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 275 m, on pale limestone-clay with some marl.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-bla.nerd_note: Blanchards, Clos Sorbè and Clos Baulet form a cluster of premier crus on the village side of the grands crus.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Chaffots
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.summary: Les Chaffots sits above Clos Saint-Denis and Clos de la Roche, at 2.6 ha, on one of the higher, steeper parts of Morey's slope. The wine is firm and fresh, with red fruit and a mineral spine, lighter than the grands crus below.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 300 to 330 m. Thin stony soil over hard limestone.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.nerd_note: With Les Genavrières and Monts Luisants it forms the band of high premier crus above Morey's grands crus, where the soils thin out and the wines turn leaner.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Charrières
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.summary:
Les Charrières sits directly below Clos de la Roche, at 2.3 ha. The name refers to a cart track (*charrière*). It is a firm, dark-fruited Morey premier cru that can be excellent in good hands.

It is one of the four premiers crus strung along the grand cru's lower edge, with the Clos des Ormes and Les Faconnières alongside. Its wines share Clos de la Roche's dark fruit, spice and firm structure in a lighter, earlier form, and in good vintages they are among the best values on the Côte de Nuits.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.terroir: East-northeast-facing at about 265 m, on brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 4%, with brown limestone-clay a little deeper than in the grand cru.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-cha.nerd_note: Its upper edge touches Clos de la Roche, one of the Côte de Nuits' most underrated grands crus.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-che.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Chenevery
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-che.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-che.summary: A 1.9 ha premier cru on the lower slope below Les Millandes, near the Route des Grands Crus. The name recalls hemp fields (*chènevière*). The wine is a fleshy, supple Morey premier cru.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-che.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 260 m, almost flat, on deep brown clay.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-che.nerd_note: Hemp was grown widely on the Côte for rope and cloth until the 19th century, and several climats keep the name.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-fac.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Faconnières
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-fac.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-fac.summary:
Les Faconnières lies below Clos de la Roche, at 1.7 ha, between Les Millandes and Les Charrières. It makes a structured, dark-fruited Morey premier cru, close in style to its grand cru neighbour.

Like Les Millandes beside it, Les Faconnières sits on the lower edge of Clos de la Roche, and the two make similar wines: dark-fruited, spicy and firm, with some of the grand cru's iron. Lignier-Michelot's version is the most widely seen.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-fac.terroir: East-facing at 265 to 275 m, on brown limestone-clay. Its gradient is gentle, about 4%, and the soil deeper than in Clos de la Roche above, which gives rounder wines.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-fac.nerd_note: Faconnières is one of four premier crus strung along the lower edge of Clos de la Roche, and the most often bottled on its own.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gen.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Genavrières
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gen.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gen.summary: A small, steep premier cru of 1.1 ha above Clos de la Roche, between Les Chaffots and Monts Luisants. The name refers to juniper (*genièvre*) that grew on these dry slopes. Its wine is lean, firm and stony, in the style of Morey's high climats.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gen.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 305 to 335 m. Thin, rocky limestone soil with little clay.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gen.nerd_note: Its lower edge touches Clos de la Roche, but at this height the soil is much thinner and the wine far more austere.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gru.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Gruenchers
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gru.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gru.summary: A small premier cru of 0.51 ha just below the village, near Les Blanchards. It shares its name with a better-known Chambolle premier cru a short way south. The wine is a perfumed, medium-bodied Morey.
