fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gru.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m on brown limestone-clay.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-gru.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in Morey, and its wine usually disappears into premier cru blends.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-mil.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Millandes
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-mil.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-mil.summary:
Les Millandes sits below Clos de la Roche, at 4.2 ha, and is one of Morey's larger and better-known premier crus. The wine has Clos de la Roche's dark fruit and structure in a softer, earlier form, with a hint of earth and spice.

Les Millandes sits just below Clos de la Roche and Clos Saint-Denis, next to Les Faconnières and La Riotte, and it is one of the most reliable of Morey's lower premier crus. Arlaud and Pierre Amiot both make it in a dark, spicy style that shows its grand cru neighbour's influence.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-mil.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with Bajocian marl at depth.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-mil.nerd_note: Millandes, Faconnières, Charrières and Clos des Ormes form a row of premier crus directly below Clos de la Roche.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-ruc.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Ruchots
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-ruc.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-ruc.summary:
Les Ruchots lies just below Clos de Tart and the Morey section of Bonnes-Mares, at 2.6 ha. It is one of Morey's finest premier crus, with the perfume of Chambolle and the structure of Morey: dark cherry, violet and a firm, fine tannin. Arlaud's Ruchots is the benchmark.

Its position, wedged below Clos de Tart and Bonnes-Mares at the southern edge of Morey, gives it the deepest pedigree of Morey's lower premier crus. It shows what separates Morey from Chambolle next door: a little more earth, spice and grip under the same red-fruited perfume.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-ruc.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 270 m, on brown limestone-clay with more stones than the lower Morey premier crus.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-ruc.nerd_note: Its neighbour across the commune border, Chambolle's Les Sentiers, makes a similar wine with a little less structure.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-sor.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Les Sorbès
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-sor.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-sor.summary: Les Sorbès is a 2.7 ha premier cru on the southern side of the village, next to the Clos Sorbè. It gives a supple, perfumed Morey with soft tannin.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-sor.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Clos Sorbè.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-les-sor.nerd_note: Les Sorbès and Clos Sorbè share the same etymology, the service tree.

fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-monts-l.name: Morey-Saint-Denis premier cru Monts Luisants
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-monts-l.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-monts-l.summary:
Monts Luisants, the 'shining hills', is the highest and steepest premier cru in Morey, climbing above Clos de la Roche toward the woods; the name is usually explained by the way the sun catches the pale limestone. At 5.4 ha it is a cool site that gives the most mineral wines of the village, in both colours.

It is famous above all for white. In 1911 the Ponsot family planted Aligoté here, and for decades their Clos des Monts Luisants blanc was the only premier cru on the Côte made from Aligoté, a quirk of history the rules tolerated. Dujac makes a Chardonnay-based Morey premier cru blanc from the site, and several growers make a taut, high-toned red with red cherry and crushed stone.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-monts-l.terroir: Very steep, east-southeast-facing at 305 to 360 m, slope often above 24%. Thin, stony soils on hard Bathonian limestone at the top of the slope, with marl patches that suit white grapes.
fr-morey-saint-denis-premier-cru-monts-l.nerd_note: Ponsot's 1911 Aligoté vines are among the oldest productive vines on the Côte de Nuits.

fr-morgon-aux-charmes.name: Aux Charmes
fr-morgon-aux-charmes.summary: Les Charmes (in the land register Aux Charmes) is a climat on the high, south-facing slopes in the west of Morgon, on granite sands, giving a lighter, more perfumed Morgon. Jean-Marc Burgaud bottles a Morgon Les Charmes.
fr-morgon-aux-charmes.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 320 to 370 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-aux-charmes.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-bellevue.name: Bellevue
fr-morgon-bellevue.summary: The largest climat of Morgon, about 100 ha of AOC land on the higher ground west of Villié-Morgon, at roughly 335 to 410 m. On granite sands rather than the schist of the Côte du Py, it gives lighter, more aromatic Morgon, and its altitude is an asset in hot vintages.
fr-morgon-bellevue.terroir: The lieu-dit's 101.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 335 to 410 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-bellevue.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-chateau-gaillard.name: Château-Gaillard
fr-morgon-chateau-gaillard.summary: A climat west of Villié-Morgon on gentle south-east-facing slopes. Clos de Mez bottles a Morgon Château Gaillard.
fr-morgon-chateau-gaillard.terroir: Gentle slopes of decomposed granite and schist on the western side of Villié-Morgon. The lieu-dit's 36.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 275 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-chateau-gaillard.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-corcelette.name: Corcelette
fr-morgon-corcelette.summary: A climat in the north-west of Morgon on sandy, pink granite, higher and lighter than the Côte du Py. Corcelette gives perfumed, silky Morgon; Jean Foillard's Corcelette, Daniel Bouland's old-vine bottling and Mee Godard's are admired.
fr-morgon-corcelette.terroir: The lieu-dit's 27.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 390 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-corcelette.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-cotes-du-py.name: Côtes du Py
fr-morgon-cotes-du-py.summary:
The Côte du Py, a dome of ancient rock east of Villié-Morgon often described as an extinct volcano, is the most famous climat of Morgon. Its blue, metamorphic schist and the crumbly, iron- and manganese-stained rock that locals call *roche pourrie* give the most powerful and mineral Gamay of the Beaujolais, dark-fruited and firm, which 'morgonne' with age, taking on cherry kirsch and earthy notes that recall Pinot Noir.

Jean Foillard's Côte du Py, made with minimal sulphur and aged in old Burgundy barrels, is the classic; Jean-Marc Burgaud, Louis-Claude Desvignes, Mee Godard, Dominique Piron and Louis Jadot's Château des Lumières also bottle it.
fr-morgon-cotes-du-py.terroir: The lieu-dit's 69.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 290 to 350 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-cotes-du-py.nerd_note: 'Morgonner' is a Beaujolais verb for the way old Morgon takes on the character of the cru; the Côte du Py is where it happens most clearly.
fr-morgon-cotes-du-py.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-douby.name: Douby
fr-morgon-douby.summary: A climat east of Villié-Morgon below the Côte du Py, on schist and granite. Douby is regularly named among the historic climats of Morgon.
fr-morgon-douby.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 250 to 300 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-douby.nerd_note: Old Morgon is said to 'morgonner': with age the best climats take on a kirsch and earthy depth that can recall Pinot Noir.
fr-morgon-douby.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-fontriante.name: Fontriante
fr-morgon-fontriante.summary: A climat west of Villié-Morgon on slopes facing south-west and south-east, on granite sands; one of the named sites of the cru's western half, which gives fresher, more floral wines than the Côte du Py.
fr-morgon-fontriante.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 270 to 315 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, facing broadly south-south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-fontriante.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-grand-cras.name: Grand Cras
fr-morgon-grand-cras.summary: A climat in the south of Morgon on clay, gravel and granite. Mee Godard bottles a Grand Cras, and Marcel Lapierre's family vineyards include parcels here.
fr-morgon-grand-cras.terroir: The lieu-dit's 34.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 265 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-grand-cras.nerd_note: Marcel Lapierre, Jean Foillard, Guy Breton and Jean-Paul Thévenet, the 'gang of four' of natural Beaujolais in the 1980s, all worked in Villié-Morgon, following the ideas of the négociant and scientist Jules Chauvet.
fr-morgon-grand-cras.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-javernieres.name: Javernières
fr-morgon-javernieres.summary: A climat at the foot of the Côte du Py, where the hill's schist meets clay and iron-rich deposits. Javernières combines the power of the Py with more flesh; Louis-Claude Desvignes's Javernières is the best-known bottling.
fr-morgon-javernieres.terroir: The lieu-dit's 52.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-javernieres.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-la-roche.name: La Roche
fr-morgon-la-roche.summary: A small climat on a rocky (*roche*) shoulder of the Morgon hills at about 320 to 335 m, on granite.
fr-morgon-la-roche.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 320 to 335 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, facing broadly south-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-la-roche.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-le-clachet.name: Le Clachet
fr-morgon-le-clachet.summary: A climat on almost flat land below the Côte du Py, on schist-derived soils and clay, one of the named sites of the eastern Morgon around the hamlet of Le Clachet.
fr-morgon-le-clachet.terroir: The lieu-dit's 21.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 260 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-le-clachet.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-montpelain.name: Montpelain
fr-morgon-montpelain.summary: A climat on the gentle, lower ground of Morgon toward the south and east, facing north-east, on sandy granite and alluvial soils that give supple, early-drinking Gamay.
fr-morgon-montpelain.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-montpelain.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-pizay.name: Pizay
fr-morgon-pizay.summary: The southern part of Morgon around the Château de Pizay, a hotel and wine estate, on low, gentle land of granite sand and alluvium.
fr-morgon-pizay.terroir: The lieu-dit's 38.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 240 m, with a mean slope of about 4%, facing south to south-west (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-pizay.nerd_note: Morgon is the second-largest Beaujolais cru after Brouilly, with about 1,100 ha, which is why its climats matter for telling its wines apart.
fr-morgon-pizay.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-morgon-saint-joseph.name: Saint-Joseph
fr-morgon-saint-joseph.summary: The highest climat of Morgon, at about 425 to 470 m on the western hills toward Chiroubles, on granite. It is a cool, late-ripening corner of the cru (not to be confused with the Rhône appellation of the same name).
fr-morgon-saint-joseph.terroir: The lieu-dit's 19.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 425 to 470 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing broadly east-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-morgon-saint-joseph.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Morgon AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Morgon when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-au-michelon.name: Au Michelon
fr-moulin-a-vent-au-michelon.summary: A large climat in Chénas on higher, south-facing slopes, at about 280 to 365 m, the northern part of the cru.
fr-moulin-a-vent-au-michelon.terroir: The lieu-dit's 45.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 280 to 365 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-au-michelon.nerd_note: Au Michelon is one of the larger named climats of the cru, in the commune of Chénas.
fr-moulin-a-vent-au-michelon.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-au-mont.name: Au Mont
fr-moulin-a-vent-au-mont.summary: A climat high on the Chénas hillside, at about 315 to 400 m on granite, among the highest land of Moulin-à-Vent.
fr-moulin-a-vent-au-mont.terroir: The lieu-dit's 35.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 315 to 400 m, with a mean slope of about 17%, facing broadly east-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-au-mont.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-aux-caves.name: Aux Caves
fr-moulin-a-vent-aux-caves.summary: A climat in Chénas on south-east-facing slopes at about 260 to 305 m, in the northern part of Moulin-à-Vent, on granite.
fr-moulin-a-vent-aux-caves.terroir: The lieu-dit's 23.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 255 to 305 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-aux-caves.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-carquelin.name: Carquelin
fr-moulin-a-vent-carquelin.summary: A climat in Romanèche-Thorins below the windmill. Château des Jacques's Clos du Grand Carquelin and Domaine Labruyère's Le Carquelin come from this sector.
fr-moulin-a-vent-carquelin.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 220 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-carquelin.nerd_note: Moulin-à-Vent is often aged in oak barrels, Burgundy-style, and its best climats can keep for ten years or more.
fr-moulin-a-vent-carquelin.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-champ-de-cour.name: Champ de Cour
fr-moulin-a-vent-champ-de-cour.summary: A south-facing climat below the windmill on granite with clay; its wines are rich and deep. Château des Jacques, Richard Rottiers, Château du Moulin-à-Vent and Domaine Labruyère bottle Champ de Cour separately.
fr-moulin-a-vent-champ-de-cour.terroir: The lieu-dit's 28.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 220 to 245 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-champ-de-cour.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-champagne.name: Champagne
fr-moulin-a-vent-champagne.summary: A climat in Chénas on gentle granite slopes; the name, common in Burgundy and Beaujolais, comes from the Latin *campania*, open country, and has nothing to do with the sparkling wine region.
fr-moulin-a-vent-champagne.terroir: The lieu-dit's 15.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-champagne.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-la-roche.name: La Roche
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-roche.summary: A climat in Romanèche-Thorins near the windmill, on thin, rocky granite (hence the name). Château des Jacques and Thibault Liger-Belair bottle La Roche.
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-roche.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing east to north-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-roche.nerd_note: Romanèche-Thorins is also home to the Hameau du Vin, the wine museum and park created by Georges Duboeuf.
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-roche.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-la-rochelle.name: La Rochelle
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-rochelle.summary: A climat in Chénas on higher, south-east-facing slopes with thin granite soils. La Rochelle gives one of the most mineral, firmly built Moulin-à-Vents; Château du Moulin-à-Vent and Olivier Merlin bottle it.
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-rochelle.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 265 to 310 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-rochelle.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-la-tour-du-bief.name: La Tour du Bief
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-tour-du-bief.summary: A climat in Chénas on gentle granite slopes; Domaine de la Tour du Bief takes its name from it.
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-tour-du-bief.terroir: The lieu-dit's 13.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 225 to 255 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing broadly east-north-east (Copernicus DEM).
producers: Domaine de la Tour du Bief
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-tour-du-bief.nerd_note: Moulin-à-Vent straddles two communes, Romanèche-Thorins in Saône-et-Loire and Chénas in the Rhône, and so two départements.
fr-moulin-a-vent-la-tour-du-bief.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-le-moulin-a-vent.name: Le Moulin à Vent
fr-moulin-a-vent-le-moulin-a-vent.summary: The climat around the sixteenth-century windmill on its hilltop at Romanèche-Thorins, a listed historic monument that gave the cru its name. The pink granite here is famous for its veins of manganese.
fr-moulin-a-vent-le-moulin-a-vent.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 240 to 260 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-le-moulin-a-vent.nerd_note: Moulin-à-Vent is the only Beaujolais cru named after a monument rather than a village.
fr-moulin-a-vent-le-moulin-a-vent.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-le-vieux-bourg.name: Le Vieux Bourg
fr-moulin-a-vent-le-vieux-bourg.summary: A climat around the old village core of Chénas, on higher granite slopes at about 290 to 375 m. The upper slopes of Chénas give firmer, cooler Moulin-à-Vent than the gentle land near the windmill.
fr-moulin-a-vent-le-vieux-bourg.terroir: The lieu-dit's 30.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 295 to 375 m, with a mean slope of about 15%, facing broadly east-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-le-vieux-bourg.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-les-burdelines.name: Les Burdelines
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-burdelines.summary: A climat in Romanèche-Thorins on slopes facing north-east, on granite, one of the larger named sites of the cru.
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-burdelines.terroir: The lieu-dit's 22.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 205 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-burdelines.nerd_note: Manganese in the granite of Moulin-à-Vent is often credited with the structure and longevity of its wines, though the link has never been proven.
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-burdelines.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-les-perrelles.name: Les Perrelles
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-perrelles.summary: One of the lowest climats of Moulin-à-Vent, in Romanèche-Thorins at about 190 to 210 m, on sandy granite and alluvium toward the Saône plain.
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-perrelles.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 190 to 210 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-perrelles.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-les-rouchaux.name: Les Rouchaux
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-rouchaux.summary: A climat in Romanèche-Thorins on gentle slopes facing east, on granite sand. Thibault Liger-Belair, the Nuits-Saint-Georges grower who bought in Moulin-à-Vent in 2009, bottles Les Rouchaux.
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-rouchaux.terroir: The lieu-dit's 15.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 205 to 225 m, with a mean slope of about 5%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-rouchaux.nerd_note: Several Côte d'Or growers have invested in Moulin-à-Vent since the 2000s, drawn by its granite climats and modest land prices.
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-rouchaux.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-les-thorins.name: Les Thorins
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-thorins.summary: Les Thorins, just north of the windmill, is one of the finest climats of Moulin-à-Vent and gave its name to the commune of Romanèche-Thorins. Its pink granite, crossed by veins of manganese, gives deep, structured Gamay that ages like Burgundy. Before the 1936 AOC the wines of the area were often sold as 'Thorins'. Louis Jadot's Château des Jacques bottles a Clos des Thorins.
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-thorins.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 265 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south to south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-thorins.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-les-verillats.name: Les Verillats
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-verillats.summary: A climat in Chénas north of the windmill, on granite. Château du Moulin-à-Vent's Croix des Vérillats takes its name from it.
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-verillats.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 255 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 7%, facing north-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-verillats.nerd_note: Château du Moulin-à-Vent, owned by the Parinet family since 2009, bottles several climats separately.
fr-moulin-a-vent-les-verillats.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-moulin-a-vent-rochenoire.name: Rochenoire
fr-moulin-a-vent-rochenoire.summary: The highest climat of the cru, in Chénas at about 365 to 425 m, on dark granite ('black rock'), facing south.
fr-moulin-a-vent-rochenoire.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 365 to 425 m, with a mean slope of about 24%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-moulin-a-vent-rochenoire.nerd_note: Higher climats such as Rochenoire ripen later and have gained attention in the warm vintages since the 2010s.
fr-moulin-a-vent-rochenoire.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Moulin-à-Vent AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Moulin-à-Vent when all the grapes come from it.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-a.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Argillas
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-a.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-a.summary: Aux Argillas is a 1.6 ha premier cru just north of the town, named for its clay. The wine is a soft, early-drinking Nuits premier cru.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-a.terroir: South-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, clay-limestone soils. On the map it lies below Aux Thorey and beside Aux Bousselots.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-a.nerd_note: Not to be confused with the Clos des Argillières in Prémeaux, at the other end of the appellation.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Boudots
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.summary:
Aux Boudots is the northernmost premier cru of Nuits, at 6.4 ha, adjoining Vosne's Malconsorts. Its wines have Vosne's perfume and Nuits' structure: dark cherry, violet and spice, with a polished tannin. Méo-Camuzet, Grivot and Leroy make the reference versions.

It touches Vosne's Malconsorts across the commune line, with Les Damodes above and Aux Cras to the south, on stony brown limestone over hard rock. Méo-Camuzet's Boudots is one of the domaine's best values, and Leroy's shows the dense, spicy richness that northern Nuits can reach.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony brown limestone over hard rock. The gradient is about 15%, steeper than the southern Nuits premier crus, and the stony soil gives good drainage.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.nerd_note: It is often described as the Vosne of Nuits.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Bousselots
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.summary: Aux Bousselots is a 4.2 ha premier cru just north of the town, on the gentle lower slope. Robert Chevillon's version is well known. The wine is fleshy and red-fruited.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Aux Chaignots and Aux Thorey and beside Aux Argillas.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-b.nerd_note: Bousselots is one of the more affordable of Chevillon's premier crus.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Chaignots
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.summary:
Aux Chaignots is a 5.8 ha premier cru just north of the town, on the slope above Aux Vignerondes. Mugneret-Gibourg, Chevillon and Faiveley make fine versions. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.

It sits on the slope just north of the town, below Les Damodes and beside Aux Murgers and Aux Thorey, on stony limestone-clay. Its wines combine the perfume of the northern premier crus with more grip than Aux Murgers; Mugneret-Gibourg's version is the most sought-after.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 280 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.nerd_note: Mugneret-Gibourg makes only two premier crus: this one and Chambolle's Les Feusselottes.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Champs Perdrix
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.summary: Aux Champs Perdrix is a steep 1.4 ha premier cru above Aux Chaignots, north of the town. The wine is firm and fresh.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 265 to 295 m, thin stony soil. On the map it lies below En la Perrière Noblot and above Aux Chaignots and Aux Thorey.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.nerd_note: It shares the partridge name with Aux Perdrix, at the opposite end of the appellation.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Cras
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.summary: Aux Cras is a 3.0 ha premier cru just south of Aux Boudots, on the northern slope of Nuits. The wine is fine and perfumed, with Vosne's influence.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-c.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below La Richemone and Les Damodes, above Aux Murgers and beside Aux Boudots.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-m.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Murgers
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-m.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-m.summary:
Aux Murgers is a 4.9 ha premier cru north of the town, below Aux Cras. *Murgers* are the stone heaps cleared from the vineyard. Méo-Camuzet and Cathiard both make fine versions: perfumed, dark-fruited and silky.

It sits on the gentle slope north of the town, with La Richemone above, Aux Chaignots alongside and Aux Vignerondes below. Its wines are among the most perfumed of Nuits, with the silky tannin of the northern premier crus rather than the iron grip of Saint-Georges.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-m.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. The stone heaps (*murgers*) that give the climat its name are still visible in places at the edge of the vines.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-m.nerd_note: Cathiard's Aux Murgers is often its most approachable premier cru.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-p.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Perdrix
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-p.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-p.summary:
Aux Perdrix ('the partridges') is a 3.4 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, above the Clos des Corvées. Most of it belongs to Domaine des Perdrix, which makes a dense, dark-fruited wine.

It sits above the Clos des Corvées and below Les Terres Blanches in Prémeaux, on stony limestone-clay with good drainage. The Devillard family's Domaine des Perdrix, which also owns the Château de Chamirey in Mercurey, makes a dark, concentrated, modern-style wine from it.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-p.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-p.nerd_note: The domaine takes its name from the climat, its main holding.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-t.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Thorey
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-t.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-t.summary: Aux Thorey is a 5.7 ha premier cru just north of the town, near the mouth of the Meuzin valley. Sylvain Cathiard's version is well known. The wine is fresh and red-fruited.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-t.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 285 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Aux Champs Perdrix, above Aux Argillas and Aux Bousselots and beside Aux Chaignots.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-t.nerd_note: It is the closest premier cru to the town of Nuits.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-v.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Aux Vignerondes
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-v.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-v.summary: Aux Vignerondes is a 3.9 ha premier cru just north of the town, below Aux Chaignots. The wine is a soft, fruity Nuits premier cru.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-v.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Aux Chaignots and beside Aux Murgers.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-aux-v.nerd_note: It is one of the lower premier crus on the northern side of Nuits.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chain.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Chaines Carteaux
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chain.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chain.summary: Chaines Carteaux is a steep 2.5 ha premier cru above Les Saint-Georges, near Les Vaucrains. Gouges makes it, and the wine is firm, dark-fruited and stony.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chain.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 260 to 320 m, slope around 25%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above Les Vaucrains, Les Saints-Georges and Les Didiers and beside Les Terres Blanches.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chain.nerd_note: Its lower edge looks down onto Les Saint-Georges, about 30 m below.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chate.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Château Gris
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chate.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chate.summary:
Château Gris is a terraced, walled 2.8 ha premier cru above the town, crowned by a small château. It is a monopole of Lupé-Cholet, owned by Albert Bichot. The wine is supple and perfumed, with red fruit.

The terraced clos sits above the town on the slope south of the Meuzin valley, with Les Crots and Rue de Chaux below. Its steep, stony terraces give a lighter, more perfumed wine than the premier crus on the lower slope.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chate.terroir: Steep, terraced, east-facing at 260 to 300 m, slope around 26%. Thin stony soil over hard limestone. The terraces were built to hold soil on a slope that averages about 26%, among the steepest in Nuits.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-chate.nerd_note: Its stone terraces are a rarity on the Côte de Nuits, looking more like a Rhône hillside than Burgundy.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos Arlot
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary:
The Clos de l'Arlot is a walled 4.0 ha monopole of Domaine de l'Arlot in Prémeaux, surrounding the estate buildings. It makes both red and white: the white, mainly Chardonnay, from a pale, marly upper terrace, is one of the few serious whites of the Côte de Nuits.

The clos lies at the foot of the Prémeaux slope, around the estate's buildings, with the Clos de la Maréchale to the south. Its red is perfumed and fine, but the white, from a marly terrace in the upper clos, is the more unusual wine: a citrus-scented, mineral white from the heart of red-wine country.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 220 to 260 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils with a terrace of white marl.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: The clos sits just north of the Clos de la Maréchale, so two of Prémeaux's three big walled monopoles are neighbours.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos de la Maréchale
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary:
The Clos de la Maréchale is one of the largest monopoles in the Côte d'Or, at 9.6 ha, in Prémeaux at the southern end of Nuits. It belongs to the Mugnier family: Faiveley leased and made it from 1950 until 2003, and since the 2004 vintage Frédéric Mugnier has made it himself.

It is a lower-slope site with deeper soils, and Mugnier's red is a supple, fragrant Nuits with red cherry and spice, much lighter than Faiveley's old style. He also makes a small amount of white from Chardonnay planted in the clos.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 240 to 255 m. Deep brown limestone-clay over Prémeaux limestone.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: Mugnier's Maréchale is the best-value wine in an estate otherwise known for Musigny and Amoureuses.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Argillières
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary: The Clos des Argillières is a 4.1 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, named for its clay (*argile*). Daniel Rion and Patrice Rion both make it; the wine is dark and firm.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 270 m, moderately steep, clay-limestone soils.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: Clay content is higher here than in most Nuits premier crus, which gives fuller, rounder wines.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Corvées
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary:
The Clos des Corvées is a 5.2 ha monopole of Prieuré-Roch in Prémeaux. *Corvées* were the feudal labour tenants owed their lord. Prieuré-Roch makes a dark, wild, whole-cluster red from it.

It sits on the gentle slope in the middle of Prémeaux, with Aux Perdrix above, the Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges to the north and the Clos des Corvées Pagets alongside. Prieuré-Roch's whole-bunch, low-sulphur style, inherited from Henri-Frédéric Roch, makes it one of the most distinctive wines of the Côte de Nuits.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 9%, and the soil a brown limestone-clay with white oolite pebbles typical of Prémeaux.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: Henri-Frédéric Roch, of the family that co-owns the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, founded Prieuré-Roch in 1988.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Corvées Pagets
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary: The Clos des Corvées Pagets is a 1.6 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, beside the Clos des Corvées. Arnoux-Lachaux is the best-known holder. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with white oolite pebbles. On the map it lies below Clos des Argillières and Les Argillières and beside Clos des Corvées and Clos Saint-Marc.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: It was carved out of the larger Aux Corvées lieu-dit.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary:
The Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges is a 7.2 ha monopole of Domaine de l'Arlot in Prémeaux, next to Les Didiers. It is the estate's flagship red: perfumed, red-fruited and fine, more elegant than most Nuits premier crus.

The clos sits in the northern part of Prémeaux, with Les Didiers and Aux Perdrix around it and the Clos des Corvées below. Its wines show the finer, more perfumed side of the Prémeaux premier crus, and Arlot's biodynamic farming since the early 2000s has made them more precise and less extracted than in the past.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay. The hard pink Prémeaux limestone lies close beneath the vines here, as in Les Saint-Georges next door.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: Arlot has been owned by AXA Millésimes since 1987 and farmed biodynamically since 2003.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Grandes Vignes
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary: The Clos des Grandes Vignes is a 2.2 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, the only Nuits premier cru below the main road (D974). It was bought in 2012 by Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair, which makes it as a monopole. Both red and white are made.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 220 to 235 m, gentle slope, iron-rich clay-limestone with sand.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: Liger-Belair paid about 3 million euros for it in 2012, from the Château de Puligny-Montrachet, which had bought it from Thomas-Moillard.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary:
The Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges is a walled 3.6 ha monopole of Domaine Henri Gouges within Les Porrets, just south of the town. Gouges' wine is darker and firmer than its Les Cailles, with black fruit and earth, and is one of the best values among serious Nuits premier crus.

The clos sits on the gentle slope just south of the town, next to Les Porrets-Saint-Georges and Roncière, with Les Perrières above. Gouges has owned it for generations, and its wine is the estate's most affordable premier cru: firm, dark and earthy, with the house's typical slow evolution.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: The 'Saint-Georges' tacked onto Porrets is a reminder of how much prestige the great vineyard next door has always carried.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Clos Saint-Marc
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.summary: The Clos Saint-Marc is a 0.92 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, a monopole of Domaine Michèle et Patrice Rion. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 250 m, gentle slope, clay-limestone soils. On the map it lies below Clos des Argillières and beside Clos des Corvées Pagets.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: It lies within the larger Argillières area of Prémeaux.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-en-la.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru En la Perrière Noblot
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-en-la.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-en-la.summary: En la Perrière Noblot is a small 0.64 ha premier cru high above Aux Chaignots, on stony ground once quarried. Machard de Gramont and Alain Michelot make it.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-en-la.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 275 to 300 m, slope around 20%, thin stony soil.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-en-la.nerd_note: Like several Nuits climats, its name records an old quarry (*perrière*) and, probably, a former owner.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-la-ri.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru La Richemone
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-la-ri.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-la-ri.summary: La Richemone is a 2.2 ha premier cru north of the town, above Aux Murgers. Perrot-Minot and Alain Michelot make well-known versions. The wine is deep and spicy.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-la-ri.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Damodes and above Aux Murgers, Aux Cras and Aux Chaignots.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-la-ri.nerd_note: Perrot-Minot's 'Ultra' bottling comes from very old vines here.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-a.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Argillières
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-a.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-a.summary: A tiny 0.24 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, beside the Clos des Argillières. Its wine is usually blended.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-a.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 255 m, steep, clay-limestone soils. On the map it lies above Clos des Corvées Pagets, Clos Arlot and Clos des Corvées and beside Clos des Argillières.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-a.nerd_note: At under a third of a hectare it is one of Nuits' smallest premier crus.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Cailles
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.summary:
Les Cailles lies just north of Les Saint-Georges, at 3.8 ha, on the gentle lower slope. The name may refer to quail (*cailles*) or to stones. It is the most elegant of the great trio south of the town (with Saint-Georges and Vaucrains): perfumed, red-fruited and silky, with Nuits' structure in a finer frame.

Les Porrets and Les Vaucrains lie alongside. Robert Chevillon's old-vine Cailles is the reference and shows why many tasters place Les Cailles just behind Saint-Georges and Vaucrains in the Nuits hierarchy.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 245 to 260 m, on stony brown limestone-clay.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.nerd_note: Chevillon's Les Cailles comes from old vines and is often the first of its big three (with Saint-Georges and Vaucrains) to open.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Chabœufs
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.summary: Les Chabœufs is a 2.8 ha premier cru above Les Cailles and next to Les Vaucrains. Jean-Jacques Confuron's version is well known. The wine is dark-fruited and firm.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 280 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.nerd_note: It sits between Les Vaucrains and Les Perrières, where the slope begins to steepen toward the woods.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Crots
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.summary: Les Crots (hollows) is a 1.1 ha premier cru above Les Pruliers, close to the town. The wine is a firm, mid-weight Nuits premier cru.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 270 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Château Gris, above Les Pruliers and Les Procès and beside Les Hauts Pruliers.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-c.nerd_note: It sits just below the Château Gris terraces.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Damodes
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.summary: Les Damodes is a large, steep 8.8 ha premier cru at the top of the slope north of Nuits, adjoining Vosne. The wine is fresh and lean, with red fruit and mineral tension.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 280 to 335 m, slope around 22%, thin stony soil over hard limestone.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.nerd_note: Its upper edge touches the woods at more than 330 m.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Didiers
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.summary:
Les Didiers is a 2.4 ha premier cru at the Prémeaux boundary, just south of Les Saint-Georges. It is a monopole of the Hospices de Nuits, sold at the Hospices' March auction. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.

The Clos des Forêts Saint-Georges lies alongside and Les Terres Blanches above. Every barrel is sold at the Hospices de Nuits auction to a négociant or private buyer, who finishes and bottles it.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay. The gradient is moderate, about 12%, on stony limestone-clay like Les Saint-Georges.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-d.nerd_note: The Hospices de Nuits auction is the smaller cousin of the Beaune sale, held each March.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-h.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Hauts Pruliers
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-h.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-h.summary: A tiny premier cru of 0.19 ha above Les Pruliers, on a steep strip at the top of the slope. Its wine is usually blended with Les Pruliers or into a Nuits premier cru.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-h.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 265 to 275 m, thin stony soil.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-h.nerd_note: At around a fifth of a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus on the Côte de Nuits.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Perrières
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.summary: Les Perrières sits above Les Porrets and Les Cailles, at 3.3 ha, on stony ground once quarried. It is best known for white: Henri Gouges' 'La Perrière' blanc comes from a white-berried mutation of Pinot Noir found in a Gouges vineyard in the 1930s and propagated here, now known as Pinot Gouges.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 280 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.nerd_note: Gouges' white is one of very few Côte de Nuits whites made from a mutation of Pinot Noir rather than from Chardonnay.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Porrets-Saint-Georges
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.summary: Les Porrets-Saint-Georges lies just north of Les Cailles, at 3.5 ha. The name probably refers to wild leeks (*porrets*). The wine is a structured, dark-fruited Nuits premier cru.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, stony brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Perrières and Les Chabœufs and beside Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges and Les Cailles.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.nerd_note: Henri Gouges' walled Clos des Porrets-Saint-Georges, registered as a separate premier cru name, sits alongside.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Poulettes
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.summary: Les Poulettes is a steep 2.1 ha premier cru high above Les Perrières, south of the town. The wine is firm and fresh, with red fruit.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.terroir: Steep, south-southeast-facing at 270 to 300 m, slope around 26%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above Les Chabœufs and Les Perrières and beside Les Vallerots.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.nerd_note: It is one of the highest and steepest premier crus in Nuits.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Procès
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.summary: Les Procès is a 1.4 ha premier cru at the southern edge of the town, below Les Crots. The name may recall a lawsuit over the land. The wine is a soft, early-drinking Nuits premier cru.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.nerd_note: Its neighbours Rue de Chaux and Les Pruliers complete the cluster of premier crus at the town's southern edge.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Pruliers
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.summary:
Les Pruliers lies just south of the town, at 7.7 ha, below Les Crots and next to Roncière. It makes a dense, firm, earthy Nuits premier cru with dark fruit and a structured tannin. Gouges, Chevillon and Grivot are major growers.

It sits just south of the town, between Les Crots above and Roncière, Les Procès and Rue de Chaux around it, on stony brown soil that gives some of the darkest, firmest wines of the southern half of the appellation. Gouges' Pruliers is one of the domaine's most structured wines.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, stony brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 8%, and the stony brown soil holds enough iron to give the wine its dark colour.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-p.nerd_note: The name probably refers to wild plum or sloe bushes (*prunelliers*).

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-s.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Saints-Georges
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-s.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-s.summary:
Les Saint-Georges (Les Saints-Georges in the register) is the vineyard that gave Nuits its name: the town added 'Saint-Georges' in 1892. It lies just north of the Prémeaux boundary, at about 7.5 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 7.5 ha). When the appellations were drawn in 1936 Nuits ended up with no grand cru at all; the story goes that Henri Gouges, the leading grower of the day, declined to press the vineyard's case.

Since 2007 the growers, led by Thibault Liger-Belair (the largest owner, with just over 2 ha), have campaigned to have it promoted, and the application has been with the INAO for well over a decade. Most observers expect it to become Nuits' first grand cru eventually.

The wine is the most complete of Nuits: deep in colour, with black cherry, iron, spice and a firm but polished tannin that needs ten years. It is more refined than Les Vaucrains above it and denser than Les Cailles to the north.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-s.terroir: Gentle east-southeast slope at 240 to 260 m. Stony brown limestone-clay over hard Prémeaux limestone, with gravel washed down from the slope above; the soil is shallow and drains well.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-s.nerd_note: About 13 owners share the vineyard, and all of them had to agree a common production rulebook before the grand cru file could go forward.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-t.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Terres Blanches
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-t.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-t.summary: Les Terres Blanches is a steep 4.3 ha premier cru in Prémeaux, above Aux Perdrix. The name ('white earths') refers to pale marl soil, and it is one of the few Nuits climats that makes a significant white wine.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-t.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 265 to 305 m, slope around 23%, pale marly limestone soil.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-t.nerd_note: The pale marl that gives it its name suits Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc better than most Nuits soils.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Vallerots
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.summary: Les Vallerots is a 0.88 ha premier cru at the top of the slope above Les Vaucrains. The wine is a lean, mineral Nuits premier cru.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 275 to 300 m, thin soil over hard limestone. On the map it lies above Les Chabœufs and Les Vaucrains and beside Les Poulettes.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest and highest premier crus south of the town.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Les Vaucrains
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.summary:
Les Vaucrains lies above Les Saint-Georges, at 6.2 ha, on steeper and stonier ground, and is often ranked second in Nuits. The name is usually glossed as 'valley of poor soil', and the wine is the most muscular of the village: dense, dark, iron-laden, with firm tannin that needs a decade or more. Gouges and Chevillon make the reference versions.

Its stony soil and steeper slope above Les Saint-Georges give the most tannic and long-lived wines of Nuits, and Gouges' and Chevillon's versions routinely need 15 years to open fully. Where Saint-Georges is complete and polished, Vaucrains is wilder, more angular and more mineral, and the two make the classic Nuits comparison.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 290 m, steeper than Les Saint-Georges. Thin, stony soil with limestone rubble over Prémeaux limestone.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-les-v.nerd_note: Vaucrains is a good example of a Burgundy rule of thumb: the steeper, stonier site above often makes the more tannic wine, the gentler slope below the more complete one.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-ronci.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Roncière
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-ronci.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-ronci.summary: Roncière (bramble ground) is a 2.1 ha premier cru just south of the town, between Les Pruliers and the Clos des Porrets. Robert Chevillon's Roncière is the best-known; the wine is fleshy and red-fruited.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-ronci.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-ronci.nerd_note: It is one of the smaller climats in Chevillon's range of eight Nuits premier crus.

fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-rue-d.name: Nuits-Saint-Georges premier cru Rue de Chaux
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-rue-d.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-rue-d.summary: Rue de Chaux is a 2.1 ha premier cru just south of the town; the name probably refers to lime (*chaux*). The wine is a fleshy, red-fruited Nuits premier cru.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-rue-d.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-nuits-saint-georges-premier-cru-rue-d.nerd_note: It sits at the foot of the Château Gris slope, part of the cluster of small premier crus at the town's southern edge.

fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-clos-.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Clos Berthet
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-clos-.summary: The Clos Berthet is a 1.2 ha white premier cru high above Pernand village, a monopole of Domaine P. Dubreuil-Fontaine. The wine is a fresh, mineral Chardonnay.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-clos-.terroir: Steep, west-southwest-facing at 310 to 345 m, slope around 23%, on thin marl and limestone. The west-southwest exposure is unusual for a Côte d'Or premier cru.
producers: Domaine P. Dubreuil-Fontaine Père et Fils
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-clos-.nerd_note: Its west-facing slope catches the afternoon sun, which helps the white ripen at this altitude.

fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-creux.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Creux de la Net
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-creux.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-creux.summary: Creux de la Net is a 3.8 ha premier cru on the slope above Pernand, next to En Caradeux. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Pernand.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-creux.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 315 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Savigny-lès-Beaune's Les Vergelesses and above En Caradeux and Ile des Vergelesses.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-creux.nerd_note: It faces Savigny's Les Vergelesses across the valley.

fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-en-ca.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru En Caradeux
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-en-ca.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-en-ca.summary:
En Caradeux is a 14.5 ha premier cru on the slope above Pernand village, facing east. Jadot's Clos de la Croix de Pierre is inside it. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Pernand, and white is also made.

En Caradeux sits on the east-facing slope above Pernand village, with Creux de la Net and the Ile des Vergelesses below. It makes both colours, and Jadot's walled Clos de la Croix de Pierre, inside it, is the best-known wine: a firm, red-fruited Pernand with good ageing potential.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-en-ca.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 325 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. The gradient averages about 19%, steep enough to drain well and keep the wines fresh.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-en-ca.nerd_note: Jadot's Clos de la Croix de Pierre is one of the few walled clos in Pernand.

fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-ile-d.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Ile des Vergelesses
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-ile-d.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-ile-d.summary:
The Ile des Vergelesses is the finest red of Pernand-Vergelesses, a 9.4 ha premier cru on the slope that faces Savigny across the valley. It gives a fine, perfumed red with red fruit and a firm, mineral finish, often compared with a light Corton.

It touches Pernand's Les Vergelesses and En Caradeux and, across the boundary, Savigny's Les Vergelesses and Les Basses Vergelesses. Its iron-rich soils give a more structured red than most of Pernand, and Chandon de Briailles' version is a benchmark for the village.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-ile-d.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 285 m, moderately steep, iron-rich brown limestone-clay.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-ile-d.nerd_note: It is the Pernand premier cru that growers most often compare with Corton, and it is usually the most expensive red of the village.

fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-les-f.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Les Fichots
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-les-f.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-les-f.summary: Les Fichots is a 10.9 ha premier cru on the lower slope near the Savigny boundary. The wine is a supple, fruity Pernand.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-les-f.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Ile des Vergelesses and En Caradeux and beside Vergelesses.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-les-f.nerd_note: It sits below the Ile des Vergelesses.

fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-sous-.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Sous Frétille
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-sous-.summary:
Sous Frétille is a 10.3 ha white-only premier cru high on the slope above Pernand village, on the west side of the hill of Corton. It gives a taut, mineral Chardonnay with Corton-Charlemagne's cut at a fraction of the price.

It sits high on the western flank of the hill of Corton, on the same band of white marl that gives Corton-Charlemagne its tension, but facing south toward the grand cru across a little valley. Its whites are lean, citrus-driven and mineral, slower to open than most village whites, and they age well for a decade.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-sous-.terroir: South-facing at 300 to 365 m, steep, on thin white marl and limestone. At 300 to 365 m, with a median gradient near 24%, it is one of the highest and steepest premier crus of the Côte de Beaune.
producers: Domaine P. Dubreuil-Fontaine Père et Fils
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-sous-.nerd_note: It faces south toward Corton-Charlemagne across a small valley.

fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-verge.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Vergelesses
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-verge.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-verge.summary: Les Vergelesses is a 17.6 ha premier cru on the lower slope at the Savigny boundary, sharing its name with the Savigny premier cru next door. The wine is a supple, red-fruited Pernand.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-verge.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 270 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Ile des Vergelesses and Savigny-lès-Beaune's Basses Vergelesses and beside Les Fichots and Savigny-lès-Beaune's Aux Fourneaux.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-verge.nerd_note: The Vergelesses straddle the commune boundary between Pernand and Savigny.

fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-villa.name: Pernand-Vergelesses premier cru Village de Pernand
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-villa.summary: A tiny 0.57 ha white-only premier cru at the edge of Pernand village. The wine is a fresh, mineral Chardonnay.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-villa.terroir: South-facing at 295 to 310 m, on marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Sous Frétille.
fr-pernand-vergelesses-premier-cru-villa.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-blanc.name: Pommard premier cru Clos Blanc
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-blanc.summary: The Clos Blanc is a 4.0 ha premier cru just north of the village, next to the Grands Epenots. Albert Grivault makes it. The wine is red despite the name.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-blanc.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at about 250 m, pale limestone-clay.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-blanc.nerd_note: The name refers to the pale soil, not to white wine: Pommard is a red-only appellation.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-de-la-commar.name: Pommard premier cru Clos de la Commaraine
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-de-la-commar.summary: The Clos de la Commaraine is a walled 3.8 ha monopole just north of Pommard's village, with its own small château. Jaboulet-Vercherre owns it; since 2017 the tenancy has been held by Denise Dupré and Mark Nunnelly, who now make it as Domaine de la Commaraine with Louis-Michel Liger-Belair advising. Before that Louis Jadot made it. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-de-la-commar.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-de-la-commar.nerd_note: Thomas Jefferson is said to have visited and bought its wine while US minister to France.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-de-verger.name: Pommard premier cru Clos de Verger
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-de-verger.summary: The Clos de Verger is a walled 2.1 ha premier cru north of the village. Billard-Gonnet and Pothier-Rieusset make it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-de-verger.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Arvelets and beside Clos de la Commaraine.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-des-epeneaux.name: Pommard premier cru Clos des Epeneaux
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-des-epeneaux.summary:
The Clos des Epeneaux is a walled 5.2 ha monopole of Domaine du Comte Armand, within the Epenots at the northern end of Pommard, in the family since the early 19th century. Under Pascal Marchand (1985 to 1999) and Benjamin Leroux (1999 to 2014) it became the most consistent great Pommard: dense, dark and spicy, with a firm, polished tannin. The estate farms biodynamically.

The clos sits on the gentle lower slope between Les Petits Epenots and Les Grands Epenots, on deep, gravelly brown soil that drains well. Comte Armand's wines are dense and spicy in youth and need ten years or more; they show that the Epenots, not only the Rugiens, can make Pommard of real depth.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-des-epeneaux.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 240 to 250 m. Brown limestone-clay with gravel, over Bathonian limestone.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-clos-des-epeneaux.nerd_note: At over 5 ha it is the largest monopole in Pommard.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-derriere-saint-je.name: Pommard premier cru Derrière Saint-Jean
fr-pommard-premier-cru-derriere-saint-je.summary: Derrière Saint-Jean is a tiny 0.28 ha premier cru inside Pommard village. The wine is usually blended.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-derriere-saint-je.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Poutures and Le Village.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-derriere-saint-je.nerd_note: At a third of a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-en-largilliere.name: Pommard premier cru En Largillière
fr-pommard-premier-cru-en-largilliere.summary: En Largillière (also Les Argillières) is a 4.0 ha premier cru above the Epenots, named for its clay. Lejeune makes it. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-en-largilliere.terroir: Southeast-facing at 250 to 275 m, moderately steep, clay-limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Charmots and Les Pézerolles and above Les Grands Epenots and Les Petits Epenots.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-en-largilliere.nerd_note: *Argile* means clay, and the name turns up in several villages.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-chaniere.name: Pommard premier cru La Chanière
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-chaniere.summary: La Chanière is a 2.8 ha premier cru high in the side valley above Pommard. The wine is fresh and fine.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-chaniere.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 265 to 305 m, steep, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above Les Arvelets and beside La Platière.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-chaniere.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus in Pommard.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-platiere.name: Pommard premier cru La Platière
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-platiere.summary: La Platière is a 2.5 ha premier cru high in the side valley above Pommard. The wine is fresh and fine.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-platiere.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 280 to 305 m, steep, thin stony soil. On the map it lies above Les Arvelets and Les Charmots and beside La Chanière.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-platiere.nerd_note: It faces south-southwest, across the side valley that cuts into the hill behind Pommard.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-refene.name: Pommard premier cru La Refène
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-refene.summary: La Refène is a 2.3 ha premier cru just north of the village, next to the Clos de la Commaraine. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-refene.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Charmots and beside Clos de la Commaraine, Clos Blanc and Les Grands Epenots.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-la-refene.nerd_note: It sits between the Commaraine and the Epenots.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-le-clos-micot.name: Pommard premier cru Le Clos Micot
fr-pommard-premier-cru-le-clos-micot.summary: Le Clos Micot is a 2.8 ha premier cru at the southern end of Pommard, near the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-le-clos-micot.terroir: Almost flat, southeast exposure at about 250 m, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Poutures, Les Bertins and Les Combes Dessus.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-le-clos-micot.nerd_note: It sits among the cluster of small premier crus between the village and Volnay.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-le-village.name: Pommard premier cru Le Village
fr-pommard-premier-cru-le-village.summary: Le Village is a tiny 0.15 ha premier cru inside Pommard village. The wine is usually blended into a Pommard premier cru.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-le-village.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies beside Les Poutures and Derrière Saint-Jean.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-le-village.nerd_note: Morey, Monthélie and Volnay also have premier crus called Le Village.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-arvelets.name: Pommard premier cru Les Arvelets
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-arvelets.summary:
Les Arvelets is a 8.4 ha premier cru on the slope north of the village. Its wine is supple and perfumed, a lighter Pommard.

Les Charmots and La Platière lie around it, and its south-southwest exposure gives ripe, perfumed wines, lighter than the Epenots or Rugiens.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-arvelets.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 255 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-arvelets.nerd_note: Its south-southwest exposure is unusual on the Côte d'Or.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-bertins.name: Pommard premier cru Les Bertins
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-bertins.summary: Les Bertins is a 3.5 ha premier cru at the southern end of Pommard, below Les Fremiers. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-bertins.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Fremiers and beside Les Poutures, Les Combes Dessus and Le Clos Micot.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-bertins.nerd_note: It is one of the lower premier crus on the Volnay side of Pommard.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.name: Pommard premier cru Les Boucherottes
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.summary: Les Boucherottes is a 1.9 ha premier cru at the northern end of Pommard, continuing Beaune's Les Boucherottes. The wine is supple and perfumed.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Beaune's Le Clos des Mouches and Les Saussilles, above Beaune's Les Epenotes and beside Les Petits Epenots.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-boucherottes.nerd_note: The climat straddles the commune boundary.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-chanlins-bas.name: Pommard premier cru Les Chanlins-Bas
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-chanlins-bas.summary: Les Chanlins-Bas is a 4.4 ha premier cru above Rugiens, toward Volnay. The wine is firm and fresh.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-chanlins-bas.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 280 to 320 m, moderately steep, thin stony soils. On the map it lies below Volnay's Pitures Dessus and above Les Rugiens Hauts, Les Rugiens Bas and Les Jarolières.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-chanlins-bas.nerd_note: The upper Chanlins are only village Pommard.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-chaponnieres.name: Pommard premier cru Les Chaponnières
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-chaponnieres.summary:
Les Chaponnières is a 2.9 ha premier cru below Rugiens Bas. Billard-Gonnet makes it. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
