It sits just below Les Rugiens Bas, beside Les Croix Noires and Les Fremiers, and shares some of Rugiens' iron-rich soil. Its wines are firm and dark-fruited, a good-value introduction to the Rugiens style.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-chaponnieres.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-chaponnieres.nerd_note: It sits just below Rugiens Bas and shares some of its iron-rich soil.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-charmots.name: Pommard premier cru Les Charmots
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-charmots.summary: Les Charmots is a 9.6 ha premier cru above the village, on the south-facing slope of the side valley that cuts through Pommard. Aleth Le Royer-Girardin makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-charmots.terroir: South-facing at 260 to 295 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-charmots.nerd_note: The side valley gives Pommard premier crus facing south and even southwest, unusual for the Côte.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-combes-dessus.name: Pommard premier cru Les Combes Dessus
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-combes-dessus.summary: Les Combes Dessus is a 2.8 ha premier cru at the southern end of Pommard, against Volnay. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-combes-dessus.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Fremiers and beside Les Bertins, Volnay's Les Brouillards and Le Clos Micot.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-combes-dessus.nerd_note: It touches Volnay's Les Brouillards across the commune line.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-croix-noires.name: Pommard premier cru Les Croix Noires
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-croix-noires.summary: Les Croix Noires is a small 1.3 ha premier cru below Rugiens Bas. Courcel and Lucien Boillot make it. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-croix-noires.terroir: East-facing at about 255 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Les Poutures and beside Les Chaponnières, Les Fremiers and Les Bertins.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-croix-noires.nerd_note: The black crosses in the name were probably wayside crosses.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-fremiers.name: Pommard premier cru Les Fremiers
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-fremiers.summary:
Les Fremiers is a 5.1 ha premier cru at the southern end of Pommard, next to Volnay's Frémiets. Domaine de Courcel makes it. The wine is perfumed and supple.

It runs into Volnay's Frémiets and Les Brouillards. Its wines are perfumed and supple, with Volnay's grace, and Courcel's Fremiers is a reliable reference.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-fremiers.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-fremiers.nerd_note: It runs into Volnay's Frémiets across the commune line.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-grands-epenot.name: Pommard premier cru Les Grands Epenots
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-grands-epenot.summary:
Les Grands Epenots lies on the gentle lower slope at the northern end of Pommard, toward Beaune, at 10.1 ha. With Les Petits Epenots and the Clos des Epeneaux it forms the Epenots, which Pommard's growers proposed for grand cru with Rugiens in the 2010s. The wine is the most elegant side of Pommard: perfumed, red- and black-fruited, with a silkier tannin than Rugiens.

Domaine de Courcel's Grand Clos des Epenots, about 5 ha within the climat, is the reference.

The Clos des Epeneaux, Les Petits Epenots and La Refène lie around it. The Epenots and the Rugiens have long been regarded as Pommard's two greatest climats; Lavalle in 1855 rated both at the top.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-grands-epenot.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 240 to 255 m. Deeper brown limestone-clay with gravel and some iron, less red than Rugiens.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-grands-epenot.nerd_note: The Epenots are usually said to take their name from thorny bushes (*épines*) that once grew on this ground.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-jarolieres.name: Pommard premier cru Les Jarolières
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-jarolieres.summary:
Les Jarolières is a 3.2 ha premier cru at the southern end of Pommard, against Volnay's Frémiets. Pousse d'Or and Jean-Marc Boillot make it. The wine is perfumed and fine, a Pommard with Volnay's grace.

It runs into Volnay's Frémiets. Its wines have Pommard's structure with Volnay's perfume, and Pousse d'Or's and Jean-Marc Boillot's versions are among the most elegant Pommards.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-jarolieres.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 280 m, moderately steep, red limestone soils.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-jarolieres.nerd_note: It sits just below Les Rugiens on the Volnay side.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-petits-epenot.name: Pommard premier cru Les Petits Epenots
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-petits-epenot.summary:
Les Petits Epenots is the larger half of the Epenots, at 15.1 ha, on the lower slope at the northern end of Pommard against the Beaune boundary. Most of the Clos des Epeneaux lies within it. The wine is perfumed and supple, a little lighter than Grands Epenots.

Les Pézerolles and Les Saussilles lie above it, and the Clos des Epeneaux occupies much of it. Its wines are perfumed and supple, the elegant side of Pommard.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-petits-epenot.terroir: Gentle southeast slope at 235 to 255 m, on brown limestone-clay with gravel.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-petits-epenot.nerd_note: Despite its name it is the largest premier cru in Pommard, at more than 15 ha.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-pezerolles.name: Pommard premier cru Les Pézerolles
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-pezerolles.summary:
Les Pézerolles sits above the Epenots, at 5.9 ha, near the Beaune boundary. Its wine is firmer and more mineral than the Epenots, with red fruit and a lean, elegant structure. De Montille's Pézerolles is a reference.

Les Charmots lies above it. De Montille's and Lafarge's versions show Pommard's more refined side.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-pezerolles.terroir: Southeast-facing at 255 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. The gradient steepens here to about 12%, and the soil thins toward the top, which is why the wine is leaner than the Epenots below.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-pezerolles.nerd_note: It sits above the Epenots at the Beaune end of the village, where the slope begins to steepen.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-poutures.name: Pommard premier cru Les Poutures
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-poutures.summary: Les Poutures is a 4.1 ha premier cru just south of the village. Lejeune makes it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-poutures.terroir: Almost flat, east exposure at 245 to 255 m, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Croix Noires and beside Les Bertins, Le Clos Micot and Le Village.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-poutures.nerd_note: It lies at the edge of the village houses.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-rugiens-bas.name: Pommard premier cru Les Rugiens Bas
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-rugiens-bas.summary:
Les Rugiens Bas is the most famous premier cru in Pommard, and with the Epenots it is one of the two climats that Pommard's growers asked the INAO to promote to grand cru in the 2010s. The name comes from the red (*rouge*) colour of the iron-rich soil, and the lower half of the climat, 5.8 ha on the INAO delimitation, is regarded as the better part.

Its wine is Pommard at full strength but with polish: deep in colour, with black cherry, plum, iron and spice, and a firm, dense tannin that needs ten years or more. Compared with the Epenots it is more structured and mineral; compared with the Rugiens Hauts above, riper and denser. Jules Lavalle rated it the best of Pommard in 1855.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-rugiens-bas.terroir: East-facing at 255 to 280 m, moderately steep, just south of the village toward Volnay. Red, iron-rich clay with limestone scree over Bathonian limestone; the iron oxides give the soil its colour.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-rugiens-bas.nerd_note: Pommard has no grand cru, and Rugiens Bas is usually the first name mentioned when growers make the case for one.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-rugiens-hauts.name: Pommard premier cru Les Rugiens Hauts
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-rugiens-hauts.summary:
Les Rugiens Hauts is the upper half of the Rugiens, at 6.8 ha, rising toward Volnay's Pitures. The soil is thinner and stonier than in Rugiens Bas, and the wine is a little lighter and fresher, with red fruit and a mineral, firm tannin.

It sits above Les Rugiens Bas toward Volnay's Pitures Dessus, on thinner, stonier soil than the lower half. The wines are lighter, more mineral and more perfumed than Rugiens Bas, and in warm vintages they can be the better balanced of the two.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-rugiens-hauts.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 315 m, moderately steep, thin red limestone soils with scree. The gradient averages about 14%, steeper than in Rugiens Bas, and the stony scree drains fast.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-rugiens-hauts.nerd_note: Many labels just say 'Rugiens' and blend the two halves.

fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-saussilles.name: Pommard premier cru Les Saussilles
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-saussilles.summary: Les Saussilles is a 3.8 ha premier cru at the northern end of Pommard, below Beaune's Clos des Mouches. Jean-Marc Boillot makes it. The wine is firm and red-fruited.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-saussilles.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 255 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Beaune's Le Clos des Mouches, above Les Petits Epenots and Les Boucherottes and beside Les Pézerolles.
fr-pommard-premier-cru-les-saussilles.nerd_note: Its upper edge touches Beaune's Clos des Mouches.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-au-vignera.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Au Vignerais
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-au-vignera.summary: Au Vignerais is a 18.7 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly. The wine is ripe and fine.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-au-vignera.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 345 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above La Frérie and beside En Servy.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-au-vignera.nerd_note: It is one of the larger premier crus of Solutré-Pouilly.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-bouthi.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Aux Bouthières
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-bouthi.summary: Aux Bouthières is a 4.9 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly. The wine is ripe and fine.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-bouthi.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 300 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies below Pouilly and above Aux Chailloux.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-chaill.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Aux Chailloux
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-chaill.summary: Aux Chailloux is a 6.7 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly. The name refers to its stones. The wine is ripe and mineral.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-chaill.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, stony limestone. On the map it lies below Aux Bouthières.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-chaill.nerd_note: *Chailloux* is an old word for pebbles.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-quarts.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Aux Quarts
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-quarts.summary: Aux Quarts is a 11.2 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Chaintré, at the southern end of the appellation, next to Pouilly-Vinzelles' Les Quarts.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-quarts.terroir: East-facing at 240 to 280 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above Le Clos Reyssier and Pouilly-Vinzelles's Les Longeays.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-aux-quarts.nerd_note: *Quarts* probably recalls a feudal due of a quarter of the harvest.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-en-france.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru En France
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-en-france.summary: En France is a small 1.9 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Vergisson. It sits on the south-southeast-facing slope in Vergisson, below the village's great limestone rock.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-en-france.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 300 to 335 m, steep, limestone and marl. The gradient averages about 16%.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-en-france.nerd_note: It is one of three Vergisson premier crus promoted in 2020.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-en-servy.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru En Servy
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-en-servy.summary: En Servy is a 4.0 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-en-servy.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 285 to 335 m, steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above La Frérie and beside Au Vignerais.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-en-servy.nerd_note: It sits next to Au Vignerais.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-la-frerie.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru La Frérie
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-la-frerie.summary: La Frérie is a 4.1 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly. The wine is ripe and fine.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-la-frerie.terroir: Southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies below Au Vignerais and En Servy.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-la-marecha.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru La Maréchaude
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-la-marecha.summary: La Maréchaude is a 9.3 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Vergisson, facing south. The wine is ripe and mineral.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-la-marecha.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 320 m, steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Crays and Sur la Roche.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-la-marecha.nerd_note: It sits below Les Crays and Sur la Roche.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos.summary:
Le Clos is a walled 2.7 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé, the monopole of Château-Fuissé, next to the château. The wine is rich and mineral, one of the benchmark Pouilly-Fuissés.

Les Ménétrières and Les Vignes Blanches lie nearby, on the same limestone and clay.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos.terroir: East-facing at 265 to 290 m, gentle slope, limestone and clay.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos.nerd_note: Château-Fuissé, owned by the Vincent family, is one of the historic estates of the village of Fuissé.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-de.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos de Monsieur Noly
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-de.summary: Le Clos de Monsieur Noly is a 2.7 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Chaintré. Domaine Valette makes it. The wine is rich and ripe.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-de.terroir: South-facing at 260 to 280 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-de.nerd_note: It is one of the few premier crus in Burgundy named after a person with his title.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-de.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos de Solutré
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-de.summary: Le Clos de Solutré is a 4.4 ha walled Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru below the Roche de Solutré.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-de.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 290 to 330 m, steep, limestone and clay.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-de.nerd_note: The Roche de Solutré gave its name to the Solutrean, a Palaeolithic culture known from the site at its foot.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-re.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Le Clos Reyssier
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-re.summary: Le Clos Reyssier is a 8.7 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Chaintré. Domaine Valette's Clos Reyssié is the reference: a rich, ripe, long white.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-le-clos-re.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 230 to 270 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies below Aux Quarts.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-brules.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Brulés
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-brules.summary: Les Brûlés is a small 0.83 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé, a sun-baked site. Château-Fuissé makes it.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-brules.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 305 m, steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above Les Ménétrières.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-brules.nerd_note: *Brûlé* means burnt, a common name for sun-traps.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-chevri.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Chevrières
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-chevri.summary: Les Chevrières is a 11.3 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Chaintré. The wine is ripe and fine. It faces south-southwest in Chaintré, at the southern end of the appellation.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-chevri.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 230 to 285 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. The gradient averages about 12%.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-chevri.nerd_note: The name probably refers to goats (*chèvres*) once grazed here.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-crays.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Crays
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-crays.summary: Les Crays is a steep 10.8 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Vergisson, below the great limestone escarpment of the Roche de Vergisson. It was among the 22 climats promoted in 2020, the first premier crus of the Mâconnais. The wine is taut and mineral, with citrus and a stony finish, the most northern-feeling of Pouilly-Fuissé.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-crays.terroir: Steep, south-southwest-facing at 310 to 390 m, slope around 26%. Thin limestone scree and marl at the foot of the rock.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-crays.nerd_note: Vergisson's premier crus are among the highest and latest-ripening of Pouilly-Fuissé.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-menetr.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Ménétrières
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-menetr.summary:
Les Ménétrières is a 5.2 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé. Domaine Ferret's Tête de Cru Les Ménétrières is a reference: rich, ripe and mineral.

It sits between Les Reisses, Les Brûlés and Le Clos, on limestone and clay.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-menetr.terroir: Southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-menetr.nerd_note: Ferret classified its own cuvées as Tête de Cru and Hors Classe long before the official premier crus.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-perrie.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Perrières
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-perrie.summary: Les Perrières is a 5.8 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé, on stony ground once quarried. The wine is mineral and fine.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-perrie.terroir: East-facing at 255 to 320 m, moderately steep, stony limestone. On the map it lies below Les Vignes Blanches.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-perrie.nerd_note: The same name appears on premier crus in Meursault, Puligny, Beaune, Nuits and Saint-Aubin.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-reisse.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Reisses
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-reisse.summary: Les Reisses is a 4.1 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé. The wine is ripe and fine.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-reisse.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 265 to 305 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies beside Les Ménétrières.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-reisse.nerd_note: It sits next to Les Ménétrières.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-vignes.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Les Vignes Blanches
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-vignes.summary: Les Vignes Blanches is a 19.1 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Fuissé. The wine is ripe and mineral.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-vignes.terroir: East-facing at 270 to 350 m, steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above Les Perrières, Le Clos and Les Ménétrières.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-les-vignes.nerd_note: The name suggests a long tradition of white grapes.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-pouilly.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Pouilly
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-pouilly.summary: Pouilly is a 19.4 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru in Solutré-Pouilly, around the hamlet that gave half the appellation its name. The wine is ripe and fine.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-pouilly.terroir: East-facing at 255 to 340 m, moderately steep, limestone and clay. On the map it lies above Aux Bouthières.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-pouilly.nerd_note: The hamlet of Pouilly is part of the commune of Solutré-Pouilly.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-sur-la-roc.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Sur la Roche
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-sur-la-roc.summary: Sur la Roche is a 14.8 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru high on the slope below the Roche de Vergisson. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-sur-la-roc.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 315 to 395 m, steep, thin limestone soils. On the map it lies above La Maréchaude.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-sur-la-roc.nerd_note: The rock of Vergisson, like its neighbour at Solutré, is a landmark limestone escarpment visible across the Mâconnais.

fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-vers-cras.name: Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru Vers Cras
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-vers-cras.summary: Vers Cras is a 23.2 ha Pouilly-Fuissé premier cru straddling Fuissé and Solutré-Pouilly. Château de Beauregard makes it. The wine is ripe and mineral.
fr-pouilly-fuisse-premier-cru-vers-cras.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 260 m, gentle slope, stony limestone and clay.

fr-pouilly-loche-premier-cru-les-mures.name: Pouilly-Loché premier cru les Mûres
fr-pouilly-loche-premier-cru-les-mures.summary: Les Mûres is the only premier cru of Pouilly-Loché, a 7.1 ha climat recognised by the INAO at the end of 2024, with the 2024 vintage the first allowed to use the name. Pouilly-Loché is a small appellation of about 33 ha, overlapping with Pouilly-Vinzelles. The wine is a ripe, mineral Chardonnay.
fr-pouilly-loche-premier-cru-les-mures.terroir: Northeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, gentle slope, clay and limestone.
fr-pouilly-loche-premier-cru-les-mures.nerd_note: The new Loché and Vinzelles premier crus are the first in Burgundy to ban all herbicides, and they require hand harvesting; Loché itself has been part of the commune of Mâcon since the 1970s.

fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-lon.name: Pouilly-Vinzelles premier cru Les Longeays
fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-lon.summary: Les Longeays is a 7.4 ha Pouilly-Vinzelles premier cru recognised by the INAO at the end of 2024, with the 2024 vintage the first to use the name.
fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-lon.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 240 to 270 m, moderately steep, clay and limestone. On the map it lies below Pouilly-Fuissé's Aux Quarts and above Les Quarts.
fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-lon.nerd_note: The work to delimit Vinzelles' premier crus began in 2006 with a geological survey.

fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-pet.name: Pouilly-Vinzelles premier cru Les Pétaux
fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-pet.summary: Les Pétaux is the smallest of the three Pouilly-Vinzelles premier crus, at 2.8 ha, recognised by the INAO at the end of 2024.
fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-pet.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 240 to 265 m, gentle slope, clay and limestone. On the map it lies beside Pouilly-Loché's les Mûres.

fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-qua.name: Pouilly-Vinzelles premier cru Les Quarts
fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-qua.summary: Les Quarts is the largest of the three Pouilly-Vinzelles premier crus recognised by the INAO at the end of 2024, at 12.6 ha, next to Pouilly-Fuissé's Aux Quarts. The 2024 vintage was the first to use the name. Domaine La Soufrandière (the Bret Brothers) made its name here.
fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-qua.terroir: East-facing at 220 to 270 m, moderately steep, clay and limestone.
fr-pouilly-vinzelles-premier-cru-les-qua.nerd_note: The rules for the new premier crus cap yields at 58 hl/ha and require at least 12% alcohol.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Champ Canet
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.summary:
Champ Canet is a 4.7 ha premier cru on the slope above Les Combettes, against Meursault's Perrières. It gives a fresh, mineral Puligny with Perrières' tension. Etienne Sauzet is the largest holder.

Les Chalumaux and La Truffière lie above it. Its wines are tense and mineral, with Perrières' cut; Sauzet's and Carillon's versions show it at its best.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. The gradient is moderate, about 9%, and the stony limestone soil is shallow, which gives the wine its tension.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.nerd_note: Champ Canet sits at almost the same altitude as Meursault's Perrières, and the two wines share a family resemblance.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Champ Gain
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.summary: Champ Gain is a 10.7 ha premier cru high on the slope toward Saint-Aubin. The wine is fresh and lean.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 315 to 360 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below La Garenne, above La Truffière and Les Folatières and beside Saint-Aubin's Les Murgers des dents de chien.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-champ-.nerd_note: Chassagne-Montrachet also has a premier cru called Les Champs Gain.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clavai.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Clavaillon
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clavai.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clavai.summary:
Clavaillon is a 5.6 ha premier cru below Les Folatières. Domaine Leflaive owns most of it. The wine is supple and fruity, an accessible Puligny premier cru.

It sits on the gentle slope below Les Folatières and beside Les Pucelles and the Clos de la Mouchère, on brown limestone-clay. Leflaive's Clavaillon, from the estate's large holding, is a supple, early-drinking Puligny premier cru.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clavai.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clavai.nerd_note: Leflaive's Clavaillon is usually its earliest-drinking premier cru.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Clos de la Garenne
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.summary: The Clos de la Garenne is a walled 1.9 ha premier cru within La Garenne, above Les Folatières. It is a monopole of the Duc de Magenta, made by Louis Jadot. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 280 m, moderately steep, thin stony soils.
producers: Domaine du Duc de Magenta (Louis Jadot)
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.nerd_note: The Duc de Magenta's family descends from Marshal MacMahon, victor of the Battle of Magenta in 1859.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Clos de la Mouchère
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.summary: The Clos de la Mouchère is a walled 3.9 ha monopole of Domaine Henri Boillot (from the Jean Boillot holding), within Les Perrières. The wine is fine and mineral.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 255 m, gentle slope, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Clos de la Garenne and Les Folatières and beside Les Perrières and Clavaillon.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-clos-d.nerd_note: It is one of the few monopoles in Puligny.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-hameau.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Hameau de Blagny
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-hameau.summary: The white side of Hameau de Blagny: 4.2 ha around the hamlet. White wine from here is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru; red is Blagny premier cru.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-hameau.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 315 to 340 m, moderately steep, marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below La Garenne, above Les Chalumaux and La Truffière and beside Meursault's Blagny.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-hameau.nerd_note: Martelet de Cherisey's cellars are in the hamlet itself.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-gar.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru La Garenne
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-gar.summary: The white side of La Garenne: 9.9 ha high above Puligny, near Blagny. White wine from here is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru, a fresh, mineral wine.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-gar.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 375 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Sous le Puits and above Champ Gain, Hameau de Blagny and Saint-Aubin's Les Murgers des dents de chien.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-gar.nerd_note: The Duc de Magenta's Clos de la Garenne lies within it.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-tru.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru La Truffière
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-tru.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-tru.summary: La Truffière ('truffle ground') is a 2.5 ha premier cru high on the slope above Les Folatières, toward Blagny. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-tru.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 295 to 325 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Hameau de Blagny and Champ Gain and above Les Folatières and Champ Canet.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-la-tru.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus on the Puligny side, at over 300 m.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-le-cai.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Le Cailleret
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-le-cai.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-le-cai.summary:
Le Cailleret is the premier cru that touches Le Montrachet's northern edge and Chevalier-Montrachet, and it is widely regarded as the finest premier cru of Puligny. At 3.3 ha (close to 4 ha with the adjoining Les Demoiselles) it sits on the same mid-slope band as the grands crus. Its wine has real grand cru character: concentrated, mineral and long, with citrus, white flowers and a stony, saline finish.

Jean Chartron's walled Clos du Cailleret is a monopole within it, and Domaine de Montille makes a fine Cailleret from vines that came with the Château de Puligny-Montrachet.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-le-cai.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 265 m. Stony limestone-clay with scree over hard limestone, close to the soils of Le Montrachet below Chevalier.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-le-cai.nerd_note: Its name, like Chassagne's Cailleret and Volnay's Caillerets, probably comes from stones (*cailloux*).

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-ch.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Chalumaux
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-ch.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-ch.summary: Les Chalumaux is a 6.0 ha premier cru on the slope above Champ Canet, toward Blagny. Matrot makes it. The wine is fresh and mineral.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-ch.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 285 to 325 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Meursault's Blagny, Blagny's Sous Blagny and Hameau de Blagny and beside Meursault's Sous le Dos d'Ane.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-ch.nerd_note: It sits between Puligny and the hamlet of Blagny.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-co.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Combettes
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-co.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-co.summary:
Les Combettes is a 6.8 ha premier cru at the northern end of Puligny, against Meursault's Perrières and Charmes. It gives a richer, rounder Puligny than most, with some of Meursault's breadth: ripe citrus, hazelnut and a generous texture.

Champ Canet lies above and Les Referts below. Its richer, rounder style comes from its position on the Meursault border; Sauzet's and Leflaive's Combettes combine Meursault's breadth with Puligny's floral lift.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-co.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay in a slight hollow (the *combe* of the name).
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-co.nerd_note: It is the Puligny premier cru that tastes most like Meursault, and it touches both Meursault's Perrières and Charmes.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-de.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Demoiselles
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-de.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-de.summary: Les Demoiselles is a tiny 0.61 ha premier cru at the junction of Le Montrachet, Chevalier-Montrachet, Bâtard-Montrachet and Le Cailleret. Part of the old lieu-dit was absorbed into Chevalier-Montrachet. Guy Amiot makes a fine premier cru from it.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-de.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay like Le Cailleret.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-de.nerd_note: Jadot and Latour's 'Chevalier-Montrachet Les Demoiselles' come from the grand cru part of the same lieu-dit.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-fo.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Folatières
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-fo.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-fo.summary:
Les Folatières is the largest premier cru of Puligny, about 17.6 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 17.7 ha), on the slope above Clavaillon and Les Pucelles, rising toward Blagny. Its wine is fine and floral, with citrus and a mineral finish; the best parcels rival Les Pucelles.

Le Cailleret lies to the south and La Truffière and Champ Gain above, so the climat rises from about 250 to over 300 m. The lower part, close to Les Pucelles, gives the richest wines, the upper part the most mineral. Drouhin's and Jadot's versions are widely available and reliable.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-fo.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 305 m, moderately steep. Stony limestone-clay, thin on the upper part.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-fo.nerd_note: The INAO allows several smaller lieux-dits, including Peux Bois and En la Richarde, to be sold as Folatières.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pe.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Perrières
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pe.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pe.summary:
Les Perrières is a 3.5 ha premier cru on the lower slope at the northern end of Puligny, near the village. The wine is a fine, mineral Puligny.

It sits on the gentle lower slope near the village, below Les Combettes and beside Les Referts, on stony limestone. Its wines are fine and mineral, and Henri Boillot's walled Clos de la Mouchère inside it is its best-known wine.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pe.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 250 m, gentle slope, stony limestone soils.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pe.nerd_note: Henri Boillot's Clos de la Mouchère lies within it.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pu.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Pucelles
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pu.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pu.summary:
Les Pucelles ('the maidens') lies just north of Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet and Bâtard-Montrachet, at 6.8 ha, on the gentle lower slope. It is often ranked with Le Cailleret as Puligny's finest premier cru: its wine is the most elegant and floral of the village, with white flowers, citrus, a silky texture and a fine mineral finish. Domaine Leflaive is the largest holder, with about 3 ha.

Le Cailleret lies above it and Clavaillon beside it. Its deeper, slightly more clay-rich soil gives more breadth than Le Cailleret, but it keeps Puligny's floral, mineral finesse; Leflaive's Pucelles is one of the most famous premier cru whites in the world.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pu.terroir: Gentle east slope at 235 to 250 m. Brown limestone-clay with more clay than Le Cailleret, over limestone.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-pu.nerd_note: Leflaive's 3 ha make Les Pucelles the house's flagship premier cru, and it sits directly against Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet, which Leflaive also owns.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-re.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Les Referts
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-re.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-re.summary:
Les Referts is a 5.8 ha premier cru at the northern end of Puligny, below Les Combettes and next to Meursault's Charmes. The wine is rich and round.

Its wines are rich and round, a Meursault-influenced Puligny; Sauzet's and Carillon's versions are among the best.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-re.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-les-re.nerd_note: Its Meursault neighbour Les Charmes gives a similarly broad wine.

fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-sous-l.name: Puligny-Montrachet premier cru Sous le Puits
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-sous-l.summary: The white side of Sous le Puits: 6.8 ha at the top of the Blagny slope. White wine from here is Puligny-Montrachet premier cru, lean and mineral.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-sous-l.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 340 to 400 m, moderately steep, thin marly limestone soils. On the map it lies above Meursault's Blagny, La Garenne and Blagny's La Jeunellotte and beside Meursault's Les Ravelles.
fr-puligny-montrachet-premier-cru-sous-l.nerd_note: *Puits* means well; the climat probably took its name from the hamlet's well.

fr-rully-premier-cru-agneux.name: Rully premier cru Agneux
fr-rully-premier-cru-agneux.summary: Agneux is a tiny 0.57 ha Rully premier cru on the slope near the village.
fr-rully-premier-cru-agneux.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 270 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Le Meix Caillet and above Molesme and Les Pierres.
fr-rully-premier-cru-agneux.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in Rully.

fr-rully-premier-cru-champs-cloux.name: Rully premier cru Champs Cloux
fr-rully-premier-cru-champs-cloux.summary: Champs Cloux is a 5.2 ha Rully premier cru on the slope north of the village. The white is fresh and fruity.
fr-rully-premier-cru-champs-cloux.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 265 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above La Renarde and beside La Bressande.
fr-rully-premier-cru-champs-cloux.nerd_note: It lies next to La Bressande and La Renarde.

fr-rully-premier-cru-chapitre.name: Rully premier cru Chapitre
fr-rully-premier-cru-chapitre.summary: Chapitre is a 3.8 ha Rully premier cru on the lower slope near the village, once property of a cathedral chapter. Both red and white are made.
fr-rully-premier-cru-chapitre.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 235 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl.
fr-rully-premier-cru-chapitre.nerd_note: Several Burgundian villages have a Chapitre or Clos du Chapitre, a reminder of church ownership before 1789.

fr-rully-premier-cru-clos-du-chaigne.name: Rully premier cru Clos du Chaigne
fr-rully-premier-cru-clos-du-chaigne.summary: The Clos du Chaigne is a 3.2 ha Rully premier cru that lies in the commune of Chagny, at the northern edge of the appellation.
fr-rully-premier-cru-clos-du-chaigne.terroir: East-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl.
fr-rully-premier-cru-clos-du-chaigne.nerd_note: It is one of two Rully premier crus that lie in Chagny rather than Rully.

fr-rully-premier-cru-clos-st-jacques.name: Rully premier cru Clos St Jacques
fr-rully-premier-cru-clos-st-jacques.summary: The Clos Saint-Jacques is a 1.9 ha Rully premier cru that lies in the commune of Chagny, at the northern edge of the appellation.
fr-rully-premier-cru-clos-st-jacques.terroir: East-facing at 255 to 285 m, steep, stony limestone.
fr-rully-premier-cru-clos-st-jacques.nerd_note: Not to be confused with Gevrey's famous Clos Saint-Jacques.

fr-rully-premier-cru-cloux.name: Rully premier cru Cloux
fr-rully-premier-cru-cloux.summary: Les Cloux is a 10.8 ha Rully premier cru on the slope north of the village. The white is fresh and fruity.
fr-rully-premier-cru-cloux.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 230 to 285 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Raclot, Rabourcé and Pillot and above Préaux.
fr-rully-premier-cru-cloux.nerd_note: *Cloux* probably comes from *clos*, an enclosed plot.

fr-rully-premier-cru-gresigny.name: Rully premier cru Grésigny
fr-rully-premier-cru-gresigny.summary:
Grésigny is one of the best-known premier crus of Rully, the northernmost village of the Côte Chalonnaise, a 6.4 ha slope south of the village facing southeast. It is above all a white site: Chardonnay here is taut, citrus-driven and stony, a lighter, crisper cousin of a Côte de Beaune white, and Rully's whites are among the best values in Burgundy.

It sits on the slope south of the village, with Vauvry and Margotés around it, on limestone and marl. Its whites are taut and mineral, and Jacqueson's and Ninot's versions are among the best of Rully.
fr-rully-premier-cru-gresigny.terroir: Southeast-facing at 265 to 310 m, moderately steep. Limestone and marl, with white marl patches that suit Chardonnay.
fr-rully-premier-cru-gresigny.nerd_note: Rully was one of the cradles of Burgundian sparkling wine in the 19th century, and much of its base wine still goes into Crémant de Bourgogne.

fr-rully-premier-cru-la-bressande.name: Rully premier cru La Bressande
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-bressande.summary: La Bressande is a 2.6 ha Rully premier cru on the slope north of the village. Both red and white are made.
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-bressande.terroir: East-facing at 240 to 260 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Le Meix Cadot and beside Champs Cloux.
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-bressande.nerd_note: The name echoes Beaune's and Corton's Bressandes.

fr-rully-premier-cru-la-fosse.name: Rully premier cru La Fosse
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-fosse.summary: La Fosse is a 3.6 ha Rully premier cru on the lower slope near the village. Both red and white are made.
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-fosse.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 245 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Rabourcé and beside Marissou.

fr-rully-premier-cru-la-pucelle.name: Rully premier cru La Pucelle
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-pucelle.summary: La Pucelle ('the maiden', like Puligny's Les Pucelles) is a 6.7 ha Rully premier cru on the slope south of the village. Its whites are fine and floral, among the most elegant of Rully.
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-pucelle.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl.
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-pucelle.nerd_note: The name echoes Puligny's Les Pucelles, and the two whites share a floral, delicate style.

fr-rully-premier-cru-la-renarde.name: Rully premier cru La Renarde
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-renarde.summary: La Renarde is a tiny 0.32 ha Rully premier cru on the slope north of the village.
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-renarde.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 250 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Champs Cloux.
fr-rully-premier-cru-la-renarde.nerd_note: The name, like Corton's Les Renardes, refers to foxes.

fr-rully-premier-cru-le-meix-cadot.name: Rully premier cru Le Meix Cadot
fr-rully-premier-cru-le-meix-cadot.summary: Le Meix Cadot is a 7.1 ha Rully premier cru on the slope near the village. Vincent Dureuil-Janthial's old-vine white is a reference.
fr-rully-premier-cru-le-meix-cadot.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 270 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies above La Bressande.
fr-rully-premier-cru-le-meix-cadot.nerd_note: A *meix* is a plot attached to a house.

fr-rully-premier-cru-le-meix-caillet.name: Rully premier cru Le Meix Caillet
fr-rully-premier-cru-le-meix-caillet.summary: Le Meix Caillet is a small, steep 0.60 ha Rully premier cru on the slope near the village.
fr-rully-premier-cru-le-meix-caillet.terroir: Very steep, southeast-facing at 265 to 300 m, slope around 38%, stony limestone. On the map it lies above Agneux and Pillot.
fr-rully-premier-cru-le-meix-caillet.nerd_note: It is the steepest premier cru in Rully.

fr-rully-premier-cru-les-pierres.name: Rully premier cru Les Pierres
fr-rully-premier-cru-les-pierres.summary: Les Pierres ('the stones') is a small 0.81 ha Rully premier cru south of the village, next to La Pucelle.
fr-rully-premier-cru-les-pierres.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, moderately steep, stony limestone. On the map it lies below Agneux and Montpalais, above Molesme and beside La Pucelle.
fr-rully-premier-cru-les-pierres.nerd_note: The name describes the stony soil.

fr-rully-premier-cru-margotes.name: Rully premier cru Margotés
fr-rully-premier-cru-margotes.summary: Les Margotés is a 5.4 ha Rully premier cru high on the slope south of the village. Its whites are fresh and mineral.
fr-rully-premier-cru-margotes.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 270 to 310 m, moderately steep, stony limestone. On the map it lies beside Grésigny.
fr-rully-premier-cru-margotes.nerd_note: It lies next to Grésigny on the upper slope.

fr-rully-premier-cru-marissou.name: Rully premier cru Marissou
fr-rully-premier-cru-marissou.summary: Marissou is a 7.2 ha Rully premier cru on the lower slope near the village. Both red and white are made.
fr-rully-premier-cru-marissou.terroir: Southeast-facing at 225 to 240 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies beside La Fosse.
fr-rully-premier-cru-marissou.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus of Rully.

fr-rully-premier-cru-molesme.name: Rully premier cru Molesme
fr-rully-premier-cru-molesme.summary: Molesme is a 6.8 ha Rully premier cru on the lower slope south of the village. Both red and white are made.
fr-rully-premier-cru-molesme.terroir: East-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Les Pierres, Pillot and Agneux and above Préaux.
fr-rully-premier-cru-molesme.nerd_note: It shares its name with the Burgundian abbey of Molesme, from which the founders of Cîteaux set out in 1098.

fr-rully-premier-cru-montpalais.name: Rully premier cru Montpalais
fr-rully-premier-cru-montpalais.summary: Montpalais is a steep 6.0 ha Rully premier cru on the slope south of the village. Its whites are fresh and mineral.
fr-rully-premier-cru-montpalais.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 260 to 315 m, slope around 25%, stony limestone. On the map it lies above La Pucelle, Vauvry and Les Pierres.
fr-rully-premier-cru-montpalais.nerd_note: It sits above La Pucelle and Les Pierres.

fr-rully-premier-cru-pillot.name: Rully premier cru Pillot
fr-rully-premier-cru-pillot.summary: Pillot is a steep 2.4 ha Rully premier cru above the village.
fr-rully-premier-cru-pillot.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 250 to 295 m, slope around 27%, stony limestone. On the map it lies below Le Meix Caillet and above Cloux, Préaux and Molesme.

fr-rully-premier-cru-preaux.name: Rully premier cru Préaux
fr-rully-premier-cru-preaux.summary: Préaux is a 6.8 ha Rully premier cru on the lower slope south of the village. Both red and white are made.
fr-rully-premier-cru-preaux.terroir: East-facing at 225 to 240 m, gentle slope, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Molesme, Cloux and Pillot and beside Chapitre.

fr-rully-premier-cru-rabource.name: Rully premier cru Rabourcé
fr-rully-premier-cru-rabource.summary: Rabourcé is a large 10.3 ha Rully premier cru on the steep slope north of the village. Its whites are fresh and mineral, its reds light and red-fruited.
fr-rully-premier-cru-rabource.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 300 m, steep in places, stony limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Raclot and above Cloux and La Fosse.
fr-rully-premier-cru-rabource.nerd_note: It is one of the steepest premier crus in Rully.

fr-rully-premier-cru-raclot.name: Rully premier cru Raclot
fr-rully-premier-cru-raclot.summary: Raclot is a steep 4.7 ha Rully premier cru high above the village.
fr-rully-premier-cru-raclot.terroir: Very steep, east-southeast-facing at 255 to 325 m, slope around 37%, stony limestone. On the map it lies above Cloux, Rabourcé and Pillot.
fr-rully-premier-cru-raclot.nerd_note: It is one of the steepest premier crus in the Côte Chalonnaise.

fr-rully-premier-cru-vauvry.name: Rully premier cru Vauvry
fr-rully-premier-cru-vauvry.summary: Vauvry is a 6.3 ha Rully premier cru on the slope south of the village, next to Grésigny. Its whites are fresh and mineral.
fr-rully-premier-cru-vauvry.terroir: Southeast-facing at 250 to 300 m, moderately steep, limestone and marl. On the map it lies below Grésigny and Montpalais and above La Pucelle.
fr-rully-premier-cru-vauvry.nerd_note: It sits between Grésigny and La Pucelle.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-bas-de-vermar.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Bas de Vermarain à l'Est
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-bas-de-vermar.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-bas-de-vermar.summary: Bas de Vermarain à l'Est is a 3.4 ha premier cru above the village of Saint-Aubin, facing south. The white is fresh and mineral.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-bas-de-vermar.terroir: Steep, south-facing at 285 to 330 m, slope around 23%, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Sur le sentier du Clou and above En Créot and Vignes Moingeon.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-bas-de-vermar.nerd_note: As the 'à l'Est' suggests, only the eastern part of the lieu-dit is premier cru.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-chez.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Derrière Chez Edouard
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-chez.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-chez.summary:
Derrière Chez Edouard ('behind Edouard's house') is a steep 4.0 ha premier cru high above the village of Saint-Aubin. Hubert Lamy's version, including a high-density old-vine cuvée, made the name famous: a taut, mineral white of real concentration, and a fresh red.

It sits on the steep slope high above the village, beside Les Castets and Le Puits, on thin stony limestone. Its whites are taut and mineral, and Lamy's red from here is one of the best of Saint-Aubin.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-chez.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 310 to 375 m, slope around 20%, thin stony limestone soil. At over 300 m and with a median gradient near 20%, it is among the coolest premier crus of Saint-Aubin.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-chez.nerd_note: Lamy planted part of it at about three times the usual Côte d'Or density, to force the roots deeper and keep yields tiny.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-la-t.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Derrière la Tour
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-la-t.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-la-t.summary: Derrière la Tour is a 2.0 ha premier cru just above the village of Saint-Aubin, facing south.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-la-t.terroir: South-facing at 280 to 305 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies beside En Créot.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-derriere-la-t.nerd_note: It is part of the band of south-facing premier crus on the hill behind the village.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-echaille.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Echaille
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-echaille.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-echaille.summary: Echaille is a 1.3 ha premier cru within Sur le Sentier du Clou, above the village.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-echaille.terroir: Southeast-facing at 300 to 325 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Les Travers de Marinot, above Village and beside Sur le sentier du Clou and Marinot.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-echaille.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Sur le Sentier du Clou.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-creot.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru En Créot
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-creot.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-creot.summary: En Créot is a 2.9 ha premier cru just above the village of Saint-Aubin, facing south-southwest.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-creot.terroir: South-southwest-facing at 280 to 315 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Sur le sentier du Clou and Bas de Vermarain à l'Est and beside Vignes Moingeon and Derrière la Tour.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-creot.nerd_note: It sits beside Derrière la Tour, just above the village houses.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-la-ranche.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru En la Ranché
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-la-ranche.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-la-ranche.summary: En la Ranché is a steep 4.0 ha premier cru within Sur le Sentier du Clou, above the village.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-la-ranche.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 280 to 340 m, slope around 26%, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Les Travers de Marinot, above Les Frionnes and Vignes Moingeon and beside Sur le sentier du Clou.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-la-ranche.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Sur le Sentier du Clou.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-montceau.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru En Montceau
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-montceau.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-montceau.summary: En Montceau is a 3.4 ha premier cru within Les Champlots, above the village of Saint-Aubin. The white is fresh and mineral.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-montceau.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 295 to 325 m, steep, thin stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Les Champlots and Sur Gamay and above La Chatenière.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-montceau.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Champlots.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-remilly.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru En Remilly
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-remilly.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-remilly.summary:
En Remilly is the Saint-Aubin premier cru that sits closest to the great white grands crus: its 29.5 ha slope lies just over the hill from Chevalier-Montrachet and Le Montrachet, facing southwest toward Chassagne, and a small part continues into Chassagne itself. Its white is the most complete of Saint-Aubin: citrus, white flowers and a cool, stony, saline finish with more weight than the village's higher sites.

Saint-Aubin was long the poor relation of Puligny and Chassagne, selling its wine in bulk; growers such as Hubert Lamy and Marc Colin showed from the 1990s that En Remilly could make whites of real class at a fraction of the price.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-remilly.terroir: Southwest-facing at 250 to 320 m, steep in places. Thin, stony limestone soil with white marl, over Bathonian limestone; the hill behind shelters it from cold northwest winds.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-remilly.nerd_note: Because it faces southwest, away from the main line of the Côte, En Remilly gets more late-afternoon sun than the east-facing grands crus just over the hill.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-vollon-a-l.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru En Vollon à l'Est
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-vollon-a-l.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-vollon-a-l.summary: En Vollon à l'Est is a tiny 0.41 ha premier cru within Le Charmois, high on the slope toward Chassagne.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-vollon-a-l.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 325 to 345 m, steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above Le Charmois and Les Combes.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-en-vollon-a-l.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name, as Le Charmois or as Les Combes.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-es-champs.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Es Champs
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-es-champs.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-es-champs.summary: Es Champs is a 4.4 ha premier cru within Les Frionnes, just east of the village. The white is fine and supple.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-es-champs.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 285 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Sur le sentier du Clou, Vignes Moingeon and En la Ranché and beside Les Frionnes.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-es-champs.nerd_note: *Es* is the old Burgundian form of 'aux'.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-la-chateniere.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru La Chatenière
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-la-chateniere.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-la-chateniere.summary:
La Chatenière is one of Saint-Aubin's best-known premier crus, a steep 8.3 ha slope above the village facing southwest, between En Remilly and Les Champlots. Its whites are fine and mineral, with citrus and a stony, slightly saline finish, and it also makes a light, fresh red.

Marc Colin's and Hubert Lamy's versions are among the best whites of Saint-Aubin.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-la-chateniere.terroir: Steep, southwest-facing at 265 to 325 m, slope around 24%. Thin stony limestone soil with white marl. The southwest exposure catches the afternoon sun, which gives ripeness despite the altitude.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-la-chateniere.nerd_note: It is an umbrella name too: Le Bas de Gamay à l'Est may be sold as La Chatenière.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-bas-de-gam.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Le Bas de Gamay à l'Est
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-bas-de-gam.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-bas-de-gam.summary: Le Bas de Gamay à l'Est is a steep 1.3 ha premier cru below the hamlet of Gamay, within La Chatenière.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-bas-de-gam.terroir: Steep, west-southwest-facing at 265 to 295 m, slope around 28%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies below La Chatenière, En Remilly and Les Cortons.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-bas-de-gam.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as La Chatenière.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-charmois.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Le Charmois
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-charmois.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-charmois.summary: Le Charmois is a 15.0 ha premier cru within Les Combes, on the slope between Saint-Aubin and Chassagne. Marc Colin makes it. The white is fine and supple.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-charmois.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 340 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above Les Combes, Les Combes au Sud, Chassagne-Montrachet's Les Chaumées and Pitangeret.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-charmois.nerd_note: It is also an umbrella for the tiny En Vollon à l'Est.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-puits.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Le Puits
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-puits.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-puits.summary: Le Puits ('the well') is a small, steep 0.70 ha premier cru above the village of Saint-Aubin.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-puits.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 315 to 355 m, slope around 25%, thin stony soil. On the map it lies below Les Travers de Marinot, above Sur le sentier du Clou and Echaille and beside Derrière Chez Edouard.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-le-puits.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in Saint-Aubin.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-castets.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Castets
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-castets.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-castets.summary: Les Castets is a steep 5.5 ha premier cru high above the village of Saint-Aubin. The white is lean and mineral.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-castets.terroir: Steep, southeast-facing at 310 to 380 m, thin stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above Derrière Chez Edouard and Village.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-castets.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus in Saint-Aubin, climbing toward 380 m.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-champlots.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Champlots
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-champlots.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-champlots.summary: Les Champlots is a 10.8 ha premier cru above the village of Saint-Aubin, on the slope that faces west-southwest across the valley. It is an umbrella for En Montceau. The white is fresh, citrus-driven and mineral.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-champlots.terroir: West-southwest-facing at 300 to 360 m, steep, thin stony limestone soil.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-champlots.nerd_note: Its western exposure is unusual in the Côte d'Or and gives slower, cooler mornings and warm afternoons.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Combes
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes.summary: Les Combes is a 25.8 ha premier cru at the eastern end of Saint-Aubin, against Chassagne's Les Vergers and Les Chaumées, and an umbrella for Le Charmois, Les Combes au Sud and Pitangeret. The white is fine and mineral.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 335 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes.nerd_note: It is the Saint-Aubin premier cru closest to Chassagne's own premier crus.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes-au.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Combes au Sud
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes-au.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes-au.summary: Les Combes au Sud is a 7.8 ha premier cru within Les Combes, at the eastern end of Saint-Aubin near Chassagne.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes-au.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 265 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Les Combes, Le Charmois and En Remilly and beside Pitangeret.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-combes-au.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Combes.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-cortons.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Cortons
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-cortons.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-cortons.summary: Les Cortons is a 7.7 ha premier cru within En Remilly, on the slope toward Chassagne. It has no link with the hill of Corton.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-cortons.terroir: Southwest-facing at 260 to 315 m, steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below La Chatenière, above Le Bas de Gamay à l'Est and Les Combes and beside En Remilly.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-cortons.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as En Remilly.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-frionnes.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Frionnes
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-frionnes.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-frionnes.summary: Les Frionnes is a 12.6 ha premier cru just east of the village of Saint-Aubin, facing southeast. It is an umbrella for Es Champs and Les Perrières. The white is fine and supple, and some light red is also made.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-frionnes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 270 to 300 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-frionnes.nerd_note: It is one of the few Saint-Aubin premier crus facing the same direction as the main Côte.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-murgers-d.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Murgers des dents de chien
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-murgers-d.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-murgers-d.summary:
Les Murgers des Dents de Chien is a 16.0 ha Saint-Aubin premier cru high on the hill above Chevalier-Montrachet, next to Puligny's Champ Gain and the Blagny climats. The name joins *murgers* (heaps of stones cleared from the vines) and 'dog's teeth', the jagged limestone. Its whites are taut, stony and long, among the most mineral of Saint-Aubin.

Its whites have Chevalier-Montrachet's mineral cut in a lighter frame, and Hubert Lamy's version is a reference.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-murgers-d.terroir: South-facing at 320 to 365 m, on a broad shoulder of the hill. Very stony limestone soil with rubble and little topsoil.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-murgers-d.nerd_note: Chassagne's tiny Dent de Chien premier cru lies just downslope, on the Montrachet side.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-perrieres.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Perrières
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-perrieres.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-perrieres.summary: Les Perrières is a 5.3 ha premier cru within Les Frionnes, just east of the village, on stony ground once quarried. The white is fine and mineral.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-perrieres.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 305 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Sur le sentier du Clou and Marinot, above Les Frionnes and beside Village.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-perrieres.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Les Frionnes.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-travers-d.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Les Travers de Marinot
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-travers-d.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-travers-d.summary: Les Travers de Marinot is a very steep 4.0 ha premier cru within Sur le Sentier du Clou, high above the village.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-travers-d.terroir: Very steep, southeast-facing at 320 to 375 m, median slope near 50%.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-les-travers-d.nerd_note: The terrain model gives it a median gradient of around one in two, which would make it one of the steepest premier crus on the Côte d'Or.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-marinot.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Marinot
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-marinot.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-marinot.summary: Marinot is a 1.8 ha premier cru within Sur le Sentier du Clou, above the village.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-marinot.terroir: Southeast-facing at 300 to 325 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Les Travers de Marinot, above Les Frionnes and Les Perrières and beside Echaille.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-marinot.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Sur le Sentier du Clou.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-pitangeret.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Pitangeret
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-pitangeret.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-pitangeret.summary: Pitangeret is a 3.4 ha premier cru within Les Combes, at the Chassagne boundary, where it continues as Chassagne's Petingeret.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-pitangeret.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, stony limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Combes and Le Charmois and beside Chassagne-Montrachet's Les Vergers and Les Combes au Sud.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-pitangeret.nerd_note: The same climat appears in two villages under two spellings.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sous-roche-du.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Sous Roche Dumay
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sous-roche-du.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sous-roche-du.summary: Sous Roche Dumay is a steep 2.2 ha premier cru within Sur Gamay, below a limestone cliff, at the top of Saint-Aubin's slope. The white is lean and mineral.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sous-roche-du.terroir: Very steep, south-southwest-facing at 345 to 400 m, slope around 37%, thin stony soil.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sous-roche-du.nerd_note: At up to 400 m it is one of the highest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-gamay.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Sur Gamay
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-gamay.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-gamay.summary: Sur Gamay is a large 14.7 ha premier cru above the hamlet of Gamay, on the high slope toward Blagny. It is an umbrella for Sous Roche Dumay. The white is fresh and mineral, the red light and fruity.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-gamay.terroir: Southwest-facing at 315 to 390 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soil.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-gamay.nerd_note: The hamlet of Gamay, part of Saint-Aubin, is often said to have given its name to the Gamay grape.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-le-sentie.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Sur le sentier du Clou
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-le-sentie.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-le-sentie.summary: Sur le Sentier du Clou is a 18.0 ha premier cru above the village of Saint-Aubin, facing southeast, and an umbrella for Echaille, En la Ranché, Les Travers de Marinot, Marinot and Vignes Moingeon. The white is fine and mineral, the red light.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-le-sentie.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 365 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-sur-le-sentie.nerd_note: Wines from its five sub-climats may all be sold under the Sur le Sentier du Clou name.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-vignes-moinge.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Vignes Moingeon
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-vignes-moinge.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-vignes-moinge.summary: Vignes Moingeon is a 4.8 ha premier cru within Sur le Sentier du Clou, just above the village.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-vignes-moinge.terroir: East-facing at 280 to 335 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Sur le sentier du Clou and En la Ranché and above Es Champs and Les Frionnes.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-vignes-moinge.nerd_note: It may be sold under its own name or as Sur le Sentier du Clou.

fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-village.name: Saint-Aubin premier cru Village
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-village.grapes: Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted); Pinot Noir for the rarer reds
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-village.summary: Village is a 2.8 ha premier cru at the edge of the village of Saint-Aubin. The wine is a fresh white or a light red.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-village.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 310 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies below Sur le sentier du Clou and Echaille, above Les Frionnes and beside Les Perrières.
fr-saint-aubin-premier-cru-village.nerd_note: Several Côte d'Or villages have a premier cru named for the village itself.

fr-saint-joseph-le-paradis-mauves.name: Le Paradis (Mauves)
fr-saint-joseph-le-paradis-mauves.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-saint-joseph-le-paradis-mauves.summary: A lieu-dit at Mauves, one of the original Saint-Joseph communes. Pierre Coursodon's Paradis Saint-Pierre, a long-lived red, takes part of its name from it.
fr-saint-joseph-le-paradis-mauves.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 160 to 315 m, with a mean slope of about 42%, mostly east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-saint-joseph-le-paradis-mauves.nerd_note: Mauves was one of the six original Saint-Joseph communes of 1956, with Glun, Tournon, Saint-Jean-de-Muzols, Lemps and Vion.
fr-saint-joseph-le-paradis-mauves.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Saint-Joseph AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Saint-Joseph when all the grapes come from it.

fr-saint-joseph-les-oliviers.name: Les Oliviers
fr-saint-joseph-les-oliviers.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-saint-joseph-les-oliviers.summary: A lieu-dit at Tournon. Pierre Gonon's white Saint-Joseph Les Oliviers, from Marsanne and Roussanne, is one of the best whites of the northern Rhône.
fr-saint-joseph-les-oliviers.terroir: The lieu-dit's 11.3 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 175 m, with a mean slope of about 21%, facing broadly south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-saint-joseph-les-oliviers.nerd_note: White Saint-Joseph is made from Marsanne and Roussanne, and is a small share of the appellation.
fr-saint-joseph-les-oliviers.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Saint-Joseph AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Saint-Joseph when all the grapes come from it.

fr-saint-joseph-saint-joseph.name: Saint - Joseph
fr-saint-joseph-saint-joseph.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-saint-joseph-saint-joseph.summary: The hillside at Tournon that gave its name to the whole appellation: the Jesuits of Tournon owned a vineyard here called 'Clos de Saint-Joseph', whose wine was known in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. When the AOC was created in 1956 it covered only six communes around Tournon and Mauves; it was later extended along 50 km of the west bank.
fr-saint-joseph-saint-joseph.terroir: The lieu-dit's 18.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 125 to 250 m, with a mean slope of about 38%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-saint-joseph-saint-joseph.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Saint-Joseph AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Saint-Joseph when all the grapes come from it.

fr-saint-joseph-sainte-epine.name: Sainte-Épine
fr-saint-joseph-sainte-epine.grapes: Syrah; Marsanne and Roussanne for white
fr-saint-joseph-sainte-epine.summary: A steep granite slope at Saint-Jean-de-Muzols, north of Tournon, and one of the historic heartlands of Saint-Joseph. Delas's Saint-Joseph Sainte-Épine, from old vines, is its best-known bottling: firm, dark and peppery.
fr-saint-joseph-sainte-epine.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.4 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 135 to 215 m, with a mean slope of about 35%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-saint-joseph-sainte-epine.nerd_note: The granite hills between Tournon and Saint-Jean-de-Muzols are the historic heart of Saint-Joseph, before the appellation was stretched to 26 communes.
fr-saint-joseph-sainte-epine.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Saint-Joseph AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Saint-Joseph when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-chene-marchand.name: Chêne Marchand
fr-sancerre-chene-marchand.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-chene-marchand.summary: A famous lieu-dit of Bué on gentle, south-east-facing slopes of *caillottes*, the hard, stony Oxfordian limestone that gives Sancerre its tense, flinty style. Le Chêne Marchand is bottled by several Bué estates, among them Jean-Max Roger, and is one of the classic names of the village.
fr-sancerre-chene-marchand.terroir: The lieu-dit's 27.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 10%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-chene-marchand.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-grand-chemarin.name: Grand Chemarin
fr-sancerre-grand-chemarin.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-grand-chemarin.summary: A lieu-dit of Bué beside Chêne Marchand, on limestone (*caillottes*) and *terres blanches*, facing south-east. Le Grand Chemarin and its neighbour Petit Chemarin are among the most cited sites of the village.
fr-sancerre-grand-chemarin.terroir: The lieu-dit's 29.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 285 m, with a mean slope of about 11%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-grand-chemarin.nerd_note: Bué and Chavignol are the two most famous villages of the Sancerre appellation, which covers 14 communes.
fr-sancerre-grand-chemarin.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-la-cote-des-montdamnes.name: La Côte des Montdamnes
fr-sancerre-la-cote-des-montdamnes.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-la-cote-des-montdamnes.summary:
The main slope of the Monts Damnés above the hamlet of Chavignol, a very steep amphitheatre of Kimmeridgian marl (*terres blanches*) facing south and south-east. The slope is so hard to work that it was said to be 'damned', and it gives the most powerful, long-lived Sancerre: dense, chalky and saline, often opening after five or ten years.

François and Pascal Cotat, whose late-picked, barrel-fermented wines from Les Monts Damnés, La Grande Côte and Les Culs de Beaujeu are cult bottles, Gérard Boulay, and Henri Bourgeois (Le MD de Bourgeois) farm here.
fr-sancerre-la-cote-des-montdamnes.terroir: The lieu-dit's 32.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 240 to 330 m, with a mean slope of about 26%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-la-cote-des-montdamnes.nerd_note: The same Kimmeridgian marl, with tiny fossil oysters (Exogyra virgula), runs under Chablis, about 120 km to the north-east.
fr-sancerre-la-cote-des-montdamnes.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-la-montee-de-saint-romble.name: La Montée de Saint-Romble
fr-sancerre-la-montee-de-saint-romble.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-la-montee-de-saint-romble.summary: A large lieu-dit in Sury-en-Vaux on slopes facing north and north-west, named after Saint Romble, a local hermit saint; its cooler exposure gives tense, citrus-driven Sauvignon.
