fr-sancerre-la-montee-de-saint-romble.terroir: The lieu-dit's 29.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 235 to 295 m, with a mean slope of about 19%, mostly north-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-la-montee-de-saint-romble.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-la-poussie.name: La Poussie
fr-sancerre-la-poussie.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-la-poussie.summary: A steep amphitheatre above Bué, facing south-west, on Kimmeridgian marl: one of the most spectacular slopes of the appellation, long famous through the Cordier family's Château de la Poussie.
fr-sancerre-la-poussie.terroir: The lieu-dit's 8.9 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 305 to 350 m, with a mean slope of about 30%, facing broadly south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-la-poussie.nerd_note: Sancerre's three main soils are terres blanches (Kimmeridgian marl), caillottes (stony limestone) and silex (flinty clay), and growers often blend all three.
fr-sancerre-la-poussie.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-le-cul-de-beaujeu.name: Le Cul de Beaujeu
fr-sancerre-le-cul-de-beaujeu.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-le-cul-de-beaujeu.summary: A very steep slope above Chavignol, facing south-east, on Kimmeridgian marl: one of the trio of great Chavignol sites with the Monts Damnés and La Grande Côte. The Cotat cousins' Les Culs de Beaujeu and Lucien Crochet's Le Cul de Beaujeu are references.
fr-sancerre-le-cul-de-beaujeu.terroir: The lieu-dit's 12.5 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 245 to 330 m, with a mean slope of about 33%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-le-cul-de-beaujeu.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-les-montdamnes.name: Les Montdamnes
fr-sancerre-les-montdamnes.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-les-montdamnes.summary: A small cadastral piece of the Monts Damnés slope above Chavignol, separate from the main Côte des Montdamnes, on the same steep Kimmeridgian marl.
fr-sancerre-les-montdamnes.terroir: The lieu-dit's 1.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 260 to 295 m, with a mean slope of about 32%, facing south-east to south (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-les-montdamnes.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-les-monts-damnes.name: Les Monts Damnés
fr-sancerre-les-monts-damnes.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-les-monts-damnes.summary: The part of the Monts Damnés slope that lies in the commune of Verdigny, next to the main Côte des Montdamnes above Chavignol, on the same Kimmeridgian marl.
fr-sancerre-les-monts-damnes.terroir: The lieu-dit's 3.1 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 285 to 325 m, with a mean slope of about 16%, mostly north-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-les-monts-damnes.nerd_note: The Monts Damnés lieu-dit is split between the communes of Sancerre (Chavignol) and Verdigny in the land register.
fr-sancerre-les-monts-damnes.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-les-romains.name: Les Romains
fr-sancerre-les-romains.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-les-romains.summary: A lieu-dit near Sancerre, facing south-west, on flinty clay (*silex*), a name linked by local tradition to Roman remains. Domaine Vacheron's Les Romains, from biodynamically farmed vines, is the reference: smoky, precise and long.
fr-sancerre-les-romains.terroir: The lieu-dit's 16.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 230 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 14%, mostly south-west-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-les-romains.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-sancerre-petit-chemarin.name: Petit Chemarin
fr-sancerre-petit-chemarin.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc; Pinot Noir for red and rosé
fr-sancerre-petit-chemarin.summary: The smaller neighbour of Grand Chemarin in Bué, on south-east-facing slopes of limestone (*caillottes*) and *terres blanches*; one of the cluster of famous Bué lieux-dits with Chêne Marchand.
fr-sancerre-petit-chemarin.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.6 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 255 to 280 m, with a mean slope of about 8%, facing broadly east-south-east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-sancerre-petit-chemarin.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Sancerre AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Sancerre when all the grapes come from it.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-beauregard.name: Santenay premier cru Beauregard
fr-santenay-premier-cru-beauregard.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-beauregard.summary: Beauregard ('fine view') is a 18.1 ha premier cru on the steep slope above the village of Santenay. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-beauregard.terroir: Steep, south-southeast-facing at 250 to 325 m, slope around 18%, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above Les Gravières, La Comme and Clos des Mouches and beside Clos Faubard.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-beauregard.nerd_note: Its upper reaches look over the Dheune valley toward the Côte Chalonnaise.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-beaurepaire.name: Santenay premier cru Beaurepaire
fr-santenay-premier-cru-beaurepaire.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-beaurepaire.summary: Beaurepaire is a steep 14.7 ha premier cru above Santenay-le-Haut, facing south. It makes both a fresh red and a mineral white.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-beaurepaire.terroir: Steep, south-facing at 250 to 350 m, slope around 24%, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above La Maladière.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-beaurepaire.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus in Santenay.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-de-tavannes.name: Santenay premier cru Clos de Tavannes
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-de-tavannes.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-de-tavannes.summary: The Clos de Tavannes is a 5.3 ha premier cru within Les Gravières, against Chassagne's Morgeot. Its red is one of the most structured of Santenay. Pousse d'Or makes a well-known version.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-de-tavannes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, gravelly limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Les Gravières and beside Chassagne-Montrachet's Morgeot, Chassagne-Montrachet's Les Brussonnes and Chassagne-Montrachet's La Grande Borne.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-de-tavannes.nerd_note: The INAO lists it both alone and as Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-des-mouches.name: Santenay premier cru Clos des Mouches
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-des-mouches.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-des-mouches.summary: Santenay's Clos des Mouches is a 2.8 ha premier cru above the village, not to be confused with Beaune's famous namesake. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-des-mouches.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 255 to 275 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-des-mouches.nerd_note: Beaune's Clos des Mouches is about 15 km to the north; the shared name is a coincidence of old field names.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-faubard.name: Santenay premier cru Clos Faubard
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-faubard.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-faubard.summary: The Clos Faubard is a 4.0 ha premier cru above the village of Santenay. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-faubard.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soil. On the map it lies above Clos des Mouches and beside Beauregard.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-faubard.nerd_note: It sits between Beauregard and the Clos des Mouches.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-rousseau.name: Santenay premier cru Clos Rousseau
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-rousseau.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-rousseau.summary: The Clos Rousseau is a 15.8 ha premier cru at the southern end of Santenay, against the Maranges. The red is supple and fruity.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-rousseau.terroir: Southeast-facing at 260 to 300 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Grand Clos Rousseau, Maranges's La Fussière and Maranges's Les Clos Roussots and beside Maranges's Clos de la Boutière.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-clos-rousseau.nerd_note: It continues into the Maranges as Les Clos Roussots.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-grand-clos-rouss.name: Santenay premier cru Grand Clos Rousseau
fr-santenay-premier-cru-grand-clos-rouss.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-grand-clos-rouss.summary: The Grand Clos Rousseau is a 8.0 ha premier cru above the Clos Rousseau, at the southern end of Santenay. The red is firm and fresh.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-grand-clos-rouss.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 335 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Maranges's La Fussière and above Clos Rousseau.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-grand-clos-rouss.nerd_note: It borders the Maranges' La Fussière.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-comme.name: Santenay premier cru La Comme
fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-comme.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-comme.summary: La Comme is a large 22.0 ha premier cru above Les Gravières, on the slope toward Chassagne. Its red is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-comme.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 305 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Beauregard and Chassagne-Montrachet's Bois de Chassagne and above Les Gravières and Chassagne-Montrachet's Morgeot.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-comme.nerd_note: It borders Chassagne's Bois de Chassagne and Clos Pitois to the north.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-maladiere.name: Santenay premier cru La Maladière
fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-maladiere.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-maladiere.summary: La Maladière is a 13.6 ha premier cru above Santenay, toward Dezize. The name refers to a medieval leper hospital (*maladrerie*). The red is supple and red-fruited.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-maladiere.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 305 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-la-maladiere.nerd_note: Many Burgundy villages have a Maladière, usually on the edge of the old settlement, where the sick were kept apart.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres.name: Santenay premier cru Les Gravières
fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres.summary:
Les Gravières is the best-known premier cru of Santenay, a 29.5 ha slope just south of Chassagne's Morgeot, at the northern end of the commune. The name comes from its gravelly soil. The red is the finest of Santenay: perfumed, red-fruited and firm, with more finesse than the village's other reds; a little white is also made.

It sits on the gentle slope at the northern end of Santenay, against Chassagne's Morgeot, with La Comme above and Passetemps below. Its gravelly soil gives the finest red of Santenay, and Vincent's, Girardin's and Belland's versions are references.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres.terroir: Southeast-facing at 220 to 260 m, gentle slope. Gravelly limestone-clay over limestone, free-draining.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres.nerd_note: It is an umbrella for the Clos de Tavannes, which also has its own premier cru name.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres-cl.name: Santenay premier cru Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes
fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres-cl.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres-cl.summary: Les Gravières-Clos de Tavannes is the double name under which the Clos de Tavannes (5.3 ha) may be sold, within Les Gravières.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres-cl.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 255 m, gentle slope, gravelly limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Les Gravières and beside Chassagne-Montrachet's Morgeot, Chassagne-Montrachet's Les Brussonnes and Chassagne-Montrachet's La Grande Borne.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-les-gravieres-cl.nerd_note: It is one of a handful of premier crus that may carry two climat names on the label.

fr-santenay-premier-cru-passetemps.name: Santenay premier cru Passetemps
fr-santenay-premier-cru-passetemps.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-santenay-premier-cru-passetemps.summary: Passetemps ('pastime') is a 11.7 ha premier cru below the village of Santenay. The red is supple and fruity.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-passetemps.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 225 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Clos des Mouches and beside Les Gravières.
fr-santenay-premier-cru-passetemps.nerd_note: Santenay was also a spa town: its lithium-rich spring drew visitors in the 19th century, and the village still has a casino.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cl.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Clous
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cl.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cl.summary: Aux Clous is a 10.0 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, next to Aux Serpentières. The wine is a supple, red-fruited Savigny.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cl.terroir: Gentle south slope at 255 to 285 m, on brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Aux Guettes and beside Aux Serpentières.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-cl.nerd_note: It lies at the foot of Aux Guettes, on the warm, south-facing side of the valley.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-fo.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Fourneaux
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-fo.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-fo.summary: Aux Fourneaux is a 6.2 ha premier cru at the foot of Savigny's north slope, near the Pernand boundary. Simon Bize and Chandon de Briailles make it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-fo.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-fo.nerd_note: Fourneaux (ovens or kilns) is a recurring climat name; there are also premier crus called Les Fourneaux in Chablis and Mercurey.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gr.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Gravains
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gr.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gr.summary: Aux Gravains is a 6.3 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, named for its gravel. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gr.terroir: Gentle south slope at 255 to 265 m, on gravelly limestone soils. On the map it lies below Petits Godeaux and beside Aux Serpentières and Les Lavières.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gr.nerd_note: Gravel washed down from the slopes above gives the soils here good drainage.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gu.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Guettes
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gu.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gu.summary:
Aux Guettes is a large, steep 14.5 ha premier cru high on Savigny's north slope, above Aux Serpentières. The wine is firm, structured and long-lived, the most tannic of the village.

Aux Serpentières and Aux Clous lie below it, and its almost due-south exposure on thin, stony limestone gives both ripeness and tannin. Bize's and Pavelot's Guettes are among the longest-lived reds of the village.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gu.terroir: Steep, south-facing at 275 to 330 m, slope around 21%. Thin, stony limestone soils. At 275 to 330 m, it is the highest premier cru on the Pernand side of Savigny.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-gu.nerd_note: Its steep slope and south exposure make it one of the warmest sites in Savigny.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-se.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Aux Serpentières
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-se.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-se.summary: Aux Serpentières is a 12.7 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, below Aux Guettes. The wine is supple and red-fruited, with a gentle tannin.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-se.terroir: Gentle south slope at 255 to 280 m, on brown limestone-clay with gravel.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-aux-se.nerd_note: It sits on the warm, south-facing side of the Savigny valley, where the Rhoin stream leaves the hills.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-basses.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Basses Vergelesses
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-basses.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-basses.summary: Les Basses Vergelesses is a small 1.7 ha premier cru on the lower part of the Vergelesses slope, at the Pernand boundary. The wine is a supple, red-fruited Savigny.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-basses.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Bataillère, above Les Lavières and Pernand-Vergelesses's Vergelesses and beside Pernand-Vergelesses's Ile des Vergelesses.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-basses.nerd_note: It sits between Pernand's Ile des Vergelesses and Savigny's Les Lavières.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-batail.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Bataillère
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-batail.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-batail.summary: La Bataillère is a 1.8 ha premier cru on the Vergelesses slope. Domaine Albert Morot makes it as a monopole, labelled 'La Bataillère aux Vergelesses'. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-batail.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 275 to 295 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-batail.nerd_note: Morot's labels attach the better-known Vergelesses name to Bataillère, a common Burgundian practice for small climats.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-champ-.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Champ Chevrey
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-champ-.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-champ-.summary: Champ Chevrey is a 1.4 ha premier cru at the foot of Savigny's north slope, a monopole of Domaine Tollot-Beaut. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-champ-.terroir: South-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Lavières and beside Aux Fourneaux.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-champ-.nerd_note: Tollot-Beaut's Champ Chevrey is one of the few monopoles in Savigny.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-la-dom.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru La Dominode
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-la-dom.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-la-dom.summary:
La Dominode is the best-known premier cru on Savigny's south slope, the one that faces Beaune. At 7.9 ha it lies on the gentle lower slope, and it is famous for its old vines: Bruno Clair's Dominode comes from vines planted in 1902. The wine is deeper and more structured than the north-side premier crus, with dark fruit and earth.

It sits on the gentle lower part of the Beaune-facing slope, with Les Jarrons and Les Hauts Jarrons above and Les Narbantons and Les Marconnets alongside. Its old vines and deeper, more clay-rich soil give Savigny's darkest, most structured reds, and Pavelot and Camus-Bruchon make classic versions alongside Bruno Clair's centenarian vines.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-la-dom.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay with more clay than the north slope.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-la-dom.nerd_note: Its northeast-facing slope is unusual for a premier cru, but the old vines more than make up for the cooler exposure.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ch.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Charnières
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ch.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ch.summary: Les Charnières is a 2.0 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, near Les Lavières. The wine is a supple Savigny premier cru.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ch.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 280 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Talmettes and above Les Lavières.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ch.nerd_note: It is one of the smaller premier crus of the Vergelesses side.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Hauts Jarrons
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.summary: Les Hauts Jarrons is a 4.4 ha premier cru above Les Jarrons, on Savigny's south slope. The wine is firm and fresh.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 260 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above La Dominode, Les Hauts Marconnets and Les Rouvrettes and beside Redrescul.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.nerd_note: Its northeast exposure makes it one of the cooler premier crus in the village.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Hauts Marconnets
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.summary: Les Hauts Marconnets is a 5.4 ha premier cru above Les Marconnets, on Savigny's south slope. The wine is firm and fresh.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 280 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Hauts Jarrons and above Les Marconnets, Les Peuillets and La Dominode.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ha.nerd_note: It is one of the higher premier crus on the Beaune side of Savigny.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ja.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Jarrons
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ja.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ja.summary: Les Jarrons is a 1.5 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, above La Dominode. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Savigny.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ja.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 250 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Hauts Jarrons, above Les Narbantons and beside La Dominode and Les Rouvrettes.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ja.nerd_note: Les Jarrons and Les Hauts Jarrons together sit just above La Dominode on the Beaune-facing slope.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-la.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Lavières
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-la.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-la.summary:
Les Lavières is Savigny's largest premier cru on the north side of the village, at 17.9 ha, on the gentle south-facing slope below the Vergelesses. The name comes from *laves*, the flat limestone slabs that cover the ground. The wine is perfumed, red-fruited and silky, the most charming of Savigny's premier crus.

Les Talmettes and the Vergelesses lie above it, Aux Gravains and Aux Fourneaux alongside. The flat stones in its soil warm quickly, which helps explain its ripe, charming wines; Chandon de Briailles and Tollot-Beaut make classic versions.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-la.terroir: Gentle south slope at 255 to 275 m. Stony limestone soils covered in flat slabs of rock.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-la.nerd_note: *Laves*, the flat limestone slabs that give Lavières its name, were the traditional roofing stone of the Côte's dry-stone vineyard huts.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ma.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Marconnets
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ma.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ma.summary: Les Marconnets is a 3.0 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, at the Beaune boundary. It continues Beaune's Les Marconnets. Simon Bize makes it. The wine is firm and dark-fruited.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ma.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ma.nerd_note: The climat straddles the commune boundary, so Marconnets exists as both a Savigny and a Beaune premier cru.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-na.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Narbantons
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-na.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-na.summary: Les Narbantons is a 9.6 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, next to La Dominode. Leroy, Pavelot and Écard make it. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-na.terroir: East-northeast-facing at about 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below La Dominode, Les Jarrons and Les Rouvrettes and beside Les Peuillets.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-na.nerd_note: Leroy bottles it, a sign of the climat's standing among Savigny's growers.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-pe.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Peuillets
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-pe.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-pe.summary: Les Peuillets is a large 16.0 ha premier cru on the lowest part of Savigny's south slope, toward Beaune. The wine is a fruity, early-drinking Savigny.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-pe.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at 240 to 250 m, on deep brown clay with gravel.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-pe.nerd_note: At around 240 m it is one of the lowest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ro.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Rouvrettes
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ro.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ro.summary: Les Rouvrettes is a 2.7 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, below Redrescul. The wine is a firm, red-fruited Savigny.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ro.terroir: East-northeast-facing at 255 to 270 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Redrescul and Les Hauts Jarrons, above Les Narbantons and beside Les Jarrons.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ro.nerd_note: The name probably refers to small oaks (*rouvres*), a reminder that woodland once came further down the slope.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ta.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Talmettes
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ta.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ta.summary: Les Talmettes is a 3.1 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, between Les Vergelesses and Les Lavières. Simon Bize makes it. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ta.terroir: South-facing at 275 to 320 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Les Vergelesses and above Les Lavières and Les Charnières.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ta.nerd_note: It sits midway up the slope between the Vergelesses and Lavières.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ve.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Les Vergelesses
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ve.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ve.summary:
Les Vergelesses (often labelled Aux Vergelesses) is Savigny's most celebrated premier cru, a 15.2 ha slope on the north side of the village that continues the hill of Pernand's Ile des Vergelesses. Its red is the finest and longest-lived of the village: red cherry, raspberry and spice, with a firm but fine tannin and a mineral, slightly iron-tinged finish.

Simon Bize, Chandon de Briailles and Pavelot make the reference wines, and a little white is also made.

Les Basses Vergelesses, La Bataillère and Les Lavières lie below it, and it touches Pernand's Ile des Vergelesses and Creux de la Net. Its altitude and iron-rich soils give the most structured red of the village; Simon Bize's version, from an estate that has done much to raise Savigny's reputation, is the reference.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ve.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 335 m, moderately steep. Iron-rich brown limestone with marl and ferruginous oolite, at the top of Savigny's north slope.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-les-ve.nerd_note: The Vergelesses run across the boundary into Pernand-Vergelesses, so the same name appears on two villages' premier crus.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-petits.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Petits Godeaux
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-petits.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-petits.summary: Petits Godeaux is a tiny 0.69 ha premier cru on Savigny's north slope, near Les Lavières. The wine is usually blended into a Savigny premier cru.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-petits.terroir: South-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Aux Serpentières, Les Lavières and Aux Gravains.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-petits.nerd_note: At under a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus in Savigny.

fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-redres.name: Savigny-lès-Beaune premier cru Redrescul
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-redres.grapes: Pinot Noir for red; Chardonnay (Pinot Blanc permitted) for white
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-redres.summary: Redrescul is a tiny, steep 0.58 ha premier cru on Savigny's south slope, above Les Rouvrettes. The wine is usually blended.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-redres.terroir: Very steep, east-northeast-facing at 265 to 290 m, slope around 31%. On the map it lies above Les Rouvrettes and beside Les Hauts Jarrons.
fr-savigny-les-beaune-premier-cru-redres.nerd_note: With a median slope near a third, it is one of the steepest premier crus in the Côte de Beaune.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-carelle-sous-la-ch.name: Volnay premier cru Carelle sous la Chapelle
fr-volnay-premier-cru-carelle-sous-la-ch.summary: Carelle sous la Chapelle is a 5.0 ha premier cru below the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-carelle-sous-la-ch.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies above Le Ronceret and La Gigotte and beside Champans and Les Mitans.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-carelle-sous-la-ch.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Général Muteau includes Carelle sous la Chapelle.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-champans.name: Volnay premier cru Champans
fr-volnay-premier-cru-champans.summary:
Champans is a 11.1 ha premier cru on the mid-slope below Taille Pieds and the village. Its wine is fuller and rounder than the upper-slope climats, with dark cherry and a velvety texture.

Les Caillerets lies alongside and Le Ronceret below. The Marquis d'Angerville, de Montille, Lafon, Voillot and Jacques Prieur all make it, which makes it one of the best places to compare Volnay styles.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-champans.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 280 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay with more clay than the upper climats.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-champans.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Blondeau includes Champans.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-l-audignac.name: Volnay premier cru Clos de l'Audignac
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-l-audignac.summary: The Clos de l'Audignac is a walled 1.1 ha monopole of Domaine de la Pousse d'Or, within the village. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-l-audignac.terroir: East-facing at 275 to 300 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Taille Pieds, above Clos du Verseuil and Clos de la Chapelle and beside Le Village.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-l-audignac.nerd_note: It is one of three monopoles held by Pousse d'Or in Volnay.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-barre.name: Volnay premier cru Clos de la Barre
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-barre.summary: The Clos de la Barre is a walled 1.3 ha monopole of Maison Louis Jadot, within the village. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-barre.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Le Village, above Les Angles and Les Mitans and beside Clos de la Bousse-d'Or.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-barre.nerd_note: Not to be confused with the Clos de la Barre in Meursault, a village climat of the Comtes Lafon.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bousse-.name: Volnay premier cru Clos de la Bousse-d'Or
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bousse-.summary:
The Clos de la Bousse d'Or is a walled 2.1 ha monopole of Domaine de la Pousse d'Or, within the village. The domaine's name echoes that of the clos. The wine is fine and red-fruited.

The clos sits within the village, below Le Village and the Clos du Château des Ducs and beside the Clos de la Chapelle, on brown limestone-clay. Its wines are fine, perfumed and long-lived, a classic expression of the gentle, village-heart slope of Volnay.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bousse-.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 280 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 7%, and the soil a deep brown limestone-clay, as in the other clos around the village.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-bousse-.nerd_note: The domaine has been owned by Patrick Landanger since 1997.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-cave-de.name: Volnay premier cru Clos de la Cave des Ducs
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-cave-de.summary: The Clos de la Cave des Ducs is a tiny 0.64 ha walled monopole within the village, next to the ducal cellars. Benjamin Leroux makes it. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-cave-de.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 295 to 305 m, moderately steep, thin limestone soils. On the map it lies above Le Village.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-cave-de.nerd_note: The cellars of the Dukes of Burgundy gave it its name.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-chapell.name: Volnay premier cru Clos de la Chapelle
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-chapell.summary: The Clos de la Chapelle is a small 0.56 ha walled monopole within the village, made by Domaine Clos de la Chapelle. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-chapell.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 265 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Clos de l'Audignac and Le Village and beside Clos de la Bousse-d'Or and Clos du Verseuil.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-chapell.nerd_note: The domaine takes its name from the clos.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-rougeot.name: Volnay premier cru Clos de la Rougeotte
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-rougeot.summary: The Clos de la Rougeotte is a small 0.52 ha walled clos just north of the village, adjoining Frémiets. Bouchard Père et Fils makes it. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-rougeot.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 275 to 285 m, moderately steep, red stony limestone soils.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-de-la-rougeot.nerd_note: The INAO lists it both alone and as Frémiets Clos de la Rougeotte.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-60-ouvree.name: Volnay premier cru Clos des 60 ouvrées
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-60-ouvree.summary:
The Clos des 60 Ouvrées is a 2.4 ha walled monopole of Domaine de la Pousse d'Or within Les Caillerets. An *ouvrée* is the area one man could work in a day, about 4.3 ares, so 60 ouvrées is roughly 2.6 ha. The wine is the purest Caillerets: perfumed, red-fruited and silky, with a mineral finish.

The clos sits on the southern part of Les Caillerets, toward Meursault's Les Caillerets and below the Clos des Chênes, on stony limestone-clay. It is the wine that made the Pousse d'Or's reputation under Gérard Potel from the 1960s, and it remains one of the most complete Volnays: fine-grained, perfumed and long.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-60-ouvree.terroir: Southeast-facing at 275 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone-clay.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-60-ouvree.nerd_note: The *ouvrée*, the old Burgundian unit of vineyard area, is still used in conversation by growers today.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-chenes.name: Volnay premier cru Clos des Chênes
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-chenes.summary:
The Clos des Chênes ('oaks') is a large 15.4 ha premier cru high on the slope south of the village, toward Monthélie. It is one of Volnay's most structured premier crus, with red and black fruit and a firm, mineral finish. Michel Lafarge's Clos des Chênes is a benchmark.

It is the largest of Volnay's top premier crus, high on the slope above Taille Pieds and Les Caillerets, running toward Monthélie's Les Champs Fulliots and Sur la Velle. The altitude and stony soil give a firmer, more structured Volnay than the village's lower climats, and Lafarge's and Lafon's versions age for decades.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-chenes.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 320 m, moderately steep, thin stony limestone soils with scree.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-chenes.nerd_note: Its upper reaches look over the Monthélie side valley.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-ducs.name: Volnay premier cru Clos des Ducs
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-ducs.summary:
The Clos des Ducs is a walled 2.4 ha monopole of Domaine Marquis d'Angerville, just above the village, near the site of the castle of the Dukes of Burgundy. It is regarded as the most perfumed and refined of Volnay's great premier crus: red cherry, rose, spice and a silky, mineral structure that ages for decades.

The d'Angerville family were among the pioneers of domaine bottling in the 1930s, alongside Henri Gouges and Armand Rousseau, and Guillaume d'Angerville, son of the late Marquis Jacques, has run the estate since 2003.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-ducs.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 325 m, moderately steep. Thin white limestone soils with scree over hard Bathonian limestone; very little clay.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-des-ducs.nerd_note: The estate propagates its own Pinot Noir selection, known as 'Pinot d'Angerville', which it has kept for generations.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-de.name: Volnay premier cru Clos du Château des Ducs
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-de.summary: The Clos du Château des Ducs is a tiny 0.57 ha walled monopole of Domaine Michel Lafarge, within the village, on the site of the castle of the Dukes of Burgundy. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-de.terroir: Southeast-facing at 280 to 290 m, moderately steep, thin limestone soils.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-du-chateau-de.nerd_note: It is the smallest of the walled clos clustered around the old ducal site in the village.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-du-verseuil.name: Volnay premier cru Clos du Verseuil
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-du-verseuil.summary: The Clos du Verseuil is a tiny 0.69 ha walled monopole of Domaine Yvon Clerget, within the village. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-du-verseuil.terroir: East-facing at 265 to 280 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Taille Pieds and Clos de l'Audignac, above Champans and beside Clos de la Chapelle.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-clos-du-verseuil.nerd_note: The Clerget family is said to have made wine in Volnay since the 13th century.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-en-chevret.name: Volnay premier cru En Chevret
fr-volnay-premier-cru-en-chevret.summary: En Chevret is a 6.1 ha premier cru on the mid-slope below Les Caillerets, toward Meursault. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-en-chevret.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 265 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Caillerets, above Robardelle and beside Santenots and Meursault's Les Santenots du Milieu.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-en-chevret.nerd_note: The name probably refers to goats (*chèvres*).

fr-volnay-premier-cru-fremiets.name: Volnay premier cru Frémiets
fr-volnay-premier-cru-fremiets.summary:
Frémiets is a 5.9 ha premier cru on the slope north of the village, toward Pommard. D'Angerville and Voillot make it. The wine is fine and red-fruited.

It sits on the slope just north of the village, below Pitures Dessus and above Les Brouillards and Les Angles, touching Pommard's Les Jarolières and Les Fremiers. Its wines have more structure than most Volnays, a Pommard influence, and d'Angerville's Fremiet is a good example.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-fremiets.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 290 m, moderately steep, stony limestone soils.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-fremiets.nerd_note: It continues Pommard's Les Fremiers across the commune line.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-fremiets-clos-de-l.name: Volnay premier cru Frémiets - Clos de la Rougeotte
fr-volnay-premier-cru-fremiets-clos-de-l.summary: Frémiets Clos de la Rougeotte is a walled 1.5 ha monopole of Bouchard Père et Fils within Frémiets, just north of the village. The wine is fine and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-fremiets-clos-de-l.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 290 m, moderately steep, red stony limestone soils. On the map it lies below Pitures Dessus, above Frémiets and Les Angles and beside Clos de la Rougeotte.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-la-gigotte.name: Volnay premier cru La Gigotte
fr-volnay-premier-cru-la-gigotte.summary: La Gigotte is a small 0.54 ha premier cru below the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-la-gigotte.terroir: Southeast-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Carelle sous la Chapelle and beside Les Mitans.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-la-gigotte.nerd_note: It is one of the smallest premier crus in Volnay.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-lassolle.name: Volnay premier cru Lassolle
fr-volnay-premier-cru-lassolle.summary: Lassolle is a tiny 0.22 ha premier cru above the village, next to the Clos des Ducs. The wine is usually blended.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-lassolle.terroir: East-southeast-facing at about 310 m, moderately steep, thin limestone soils. On the map it lies above Clos des Ducs and Le Village.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-lassolle.nerd_note: At under a quarter of a hectare it is one of the smallest premier crus in Burgundy.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-le-ronceret.name: Volnay premier cru Le Ronceret
fr-volnay-premier-cru-le-ronceret.summary: Le Ronceret is a 3.6 ha premier cru on the lower slope below Champans. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-le-ronceret.terroir: Southeast-facing at 240 to 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Champans, Carelle sous la Chapelle and Les Caillerets and beside Les Lurets.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-le-ronceret.nerd_note: The name probably refers to brambles (*ronces*).

fr-volnay-premier-cru-le-village.name: Volnay premier cru Le Village
fr-volnay-premier-cru-le-village.summary: Le Village is a 3.0 ha premier cru inside Volnay village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-le-village.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Clos des Ducs, above Clos de la Bousse-d'Or and Clos de la Barre and beside Clos du Château des Ducs.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-le-village.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvée Général Muteau includes Le Village.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-angles.name: Volnay premier cru Les Angles
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-angles.summary: Les Angles is a 4.6 ha premier cru below the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-angles.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 255 to 275 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Frémiets, Clos de la Barre and Frémiets Clos de la Rougeotte and above Les Brouillards.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-angles.nerd_note: It sits between Les Brouillards and the village.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-brouillards.name: Volnay premier cru Les Brouillards
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-brouillards.summary:
Les Brouillards ('the mists') is a 5.6 ha premier cru on the lower slope north of the village, toward Pommard. The wine is supple and perfumed.

Les Mitans and Les Angles lie alongside, and it touches Pommard's Les Combes Dessus and Les Fremiers. De Montille's version is a delicate, early-drinking classic.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-brouillards.terroir: East-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. The gradient is gentle, about 4%, and the soil deeper than in the upper climats, giving a softer wine.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-brouillards.nerd_note: The name means 'the mists'; it is one of the few Volnay premier crus on the Pommard side of the village.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-caillerets.name: Volnay premier cru Les Caillerets
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-caillerets.summary:
Les Caillerets is usually ranked the finest premier cru of Volnay, a 12.1 ha climat on the mid-slope south of the village, toward Meursault. The name comes from its stones (*cailloux*). Its wine combines Volnay's perfume with real depth: red cherry, raspberry, violet and spice, a silky texture and a long, mineral finish, more structured than most Volnay.

The Clos des 60 Ouvrées, Pousse d'Or's monopole, lies within it and has its own premier cru name. Other leading holders include the Marquis d'Angerville, Bouchard Père et Fils (its 'Ancienne Cuvée Carnot'), Michel Lafarge and Joseph Voillot.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-caillerets.terroir: Southeast-facing at 245 to 290 m. Stony red-brown limestone-clay over hard limestone, with scree on the upper part and more clay below.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-caillerets.nerd_note: Bouchard's 'Caillerets Ancienne Cuvée Carnot' is named after the Carnot family, the parcel's former owners.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-lurets.name: Volnay premier cru Les Lurets
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-lurets.summary: Les Lurets is a 2.1 ha premier cru on the lower slope south of the village. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-lurets.terroir: Southeast-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Les Caillerets and En Chevret and beside Robardelle and Le Ronceret.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-lurets.nerd_note: It is one of the lowest premier crus in Volnay.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-mitans.name: Volnay premier cru Les Mitans
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-mitans.summary:
Les Mitans ('the middle') is a 8.6 ha premier cru on the lower slope below the village. De Montille and d'Angerville make it. The wine is fine and red-fruited.

It sits on the gentle slope below the village, between Les Brouillards and Carelle sous la Chapelle, on brown limestone-clay. Its wines are fine and red-fruited, with a little more depth than Les Brouillards, and d'Angerville's and de Montille's versions are references.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-mitans.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 245 to 260 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-les-mitans.nerd_note: It lies midway between the village and the Route nationale.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-pitures-dessus.name: Volnay premier cru Pitures Dessus
fr-volnay-premier-cru-pitures-dessus.summary: Pitures Dessus is a 6.7 ha premier cru high on the slope above the village, toward Pommard. The wine is fresh and fine.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-pitures-dessus.terroir: Southeast-facing at 285 to 340 m, steep, thin stony limestone soils. On the map it lies above Pommard's Les Chanlins-Bas, Frémiets and Frémiets Clos de la Rougeotte and beside Clos des Ducs.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-pitures-dessus.nerd_note: It is one of the highest premier crus in Volnay.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-robardelle.name: Volnay premier cru Robardelle
fr-volnay-premier-cru-robardelle.summary: Robardelle is a 2.9 ha premier cru on the lower slope south of the village, toward Meursault. The wine is supple and red-fruited.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-robardelle.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 235 to 245 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay. On the map it lies below Santenots, En Chevret and Les Caillerets and beside Les Lurets.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-robardelle.nerd_note: It sits just above the Santenots.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-santenots.name: Volnay premier cru Santenots
fr-volnay-premier-cru-santenots.summary:
Santenots is the strangest premier cru in Volnay: it lies entirely in the commune of Meursault, on the slope south of Volnay's Caillerets, but its red wine is sold as Volnay premier cru (Volnay-Santenots), while white from the same vines is Meursault premier cru. The umbrella covers 29.0 ha, including Les Santenots du Milieu, Les Santenots Blancs and Les Plures.

The wine is Volnay with a Meursault accent: fuller, darker and earthier than the Volnays of the village, with black cherry and spice. Comtes Lafon's Santenots-du-Milieu and Jacques Prieur's Clos des Santenots are the benchmarks.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-santenots.terroir: Southeast-facing at 230 to 275 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay with more marl and clay than Volnay's own premier crus.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-santenots.nerd_note: The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Jehan de Massol and Gauvain are Volnay-Santenots.

fr-volnay-premier-cru-taille-pieds.name: Volnay premier cru Taille Pieds
fr-volnay-premier-cru-taille-pieds.summary:
Taille Pieds (Taillepieds) is a 7.2 ha premier cru on the steep slope just south of the village. The name is usually explained as 'cut feet', from the effort of working the steep slope. Its wines are among the most refined in Volnay: perfumed, red-fruited, silky and long, with a mineral finish. De Montille's Taillepieds is a reference.

The Clos des Chênes lies above and Champans below, with the Clos de l'Audignac and the Clos du Verseuil toward the village. Its thin white limestone gives the most aerial Volnay of all: rose, red cherry and a fine, mineral spine. The Hospices de Beaune's cuvées Blondeau and Général Muteau both include Taille Pieds.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-taille-pieds.terroir: Steep, east-southeast-facing at 270 to 320 m, slope around 14%. Thin white limestone soils with scree.
fr-volnay-premier-cru-taille-pieds.nerd_note: Taille Pieds, Clos des Ducs and Caillerets are usually named as Volnay's top three premier crus.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-au-dessus-d.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Au-dessus des Malconsorts
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-au-dessus-d.summary: Au-dessus des Malconsorts ('above Malconsorts') is a steep 1.1 ha strip at the top of the slope, between Malconsorts and La Tâche's upper reaches. The soil is thin and the wine lighter and fresher than Malconsorts, with red fruit and a stony finish.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-au-dessus-d.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 280 to 310 m, slope around 23%. Thin stony soil over hard limestone.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-au-dessus-d.nerd_note: Its lower edge touches La Tâche, the most consistent of the Vosne grands crus.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-brulees.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Aux Brulées
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-brulees.summary:
Aux Brulées sits above Richebourg, at 4.6 ha, between Les Beaux Monts and Cros Parantoux, and in the best hands it is one of Vosne's three or four finest premier crus. The name ('the burnt ones') points to its warm, sun-catching position on the upper slope. The wine is rich and spicy, with dark cherry, plum and a velvety, ample texture; it is more generous than Cros Parantoux next door and has some of Richebourg's opulence.

Méo-Camuzet, Grivot, Leroy and Bruno Clavelier all make fine versions, and Méo's was made by Henri Jayer, who farmed the estate's vines as a sharecropper until 1988.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-brulees.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 305 m, moderately steep. Thin brown limestone soil over hard rock at the top of the slope.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-brulees.nerd_note: The Brulées, Cros Parantoux and the upper Richebourg sit on the same band of thin soil over hard limestone, but Brulées faces more to the southeast and ripens earlier.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-malcons.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Aux Malconsorts
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-malcons.summary:
Aux Malconsorts lies immediately south of La Tâche, at the southern end of Vosne, on the border with Nuits-Saint-Georges. The part next to La Tâche is regarded as grand cru in all but name, and its wines have La Tâche's spice and depth: dark cherry, Asian spices and a velvet tannin.

The INAO delimitation gives 5.9 ha. Domaine de Montille makes a 'Cuvée Christiane' from the oldest vines next to La Tâche, part of the old Thomas-Moillard holding that de Montille and Dujac bought in 2005. Sylvain Cathiard's Malconsorts is a reference, and Lamarche and Hudelot-Noëllat also make it.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-malcons.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 285 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay with plenty of stones, over Bajocian and Bathonian limestone; the upper part is close in soil to La Tâche.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-malcons.nerd_note: The name is usually translated as 'bad companions', though no one knows who the troublemakers were.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-raignot.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Aux Raignots
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-raignot.summary:
Aux Raignots (also Reignots) is a steep 1.6 ha premier cru above La Romanée and La Grande Rue. Comte Liger-Belair's version is a benchmark. The wine is fine, mineral and perfumed, a higher, leaner cousin of the grands crus below.

The climat climbs steeply above La Romanée, the Liger-Belair grand cru, and its upper part reaches the woods. Comte Liger-Belair's Reignots, from the family's historic holding, is usually the most refined of its premier crus, with the perfume of the grands crus below in a cooler, more mineral frame.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-raignot.terroir: Steep, east-facing at 275 to 340 m, slope around 22%. Thin soil and rubble over hard limestone.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-aux-raignot.nerd_note: Its lower edge touches three grands crus: La Romanée, La Grande Rue and Richebourg.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-clos-des-re.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Clos des Réas
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-clos-des-re.summary:
The Clos des Réas is a walled 2.1 ha premier cru on the southern edge of Vosne's village, a monopole of Domaine Michel Gros. The wine is supple and perfumed, with red fruit and silky tannin.

The clos sits on flat ground at the southern edge of the village, next to Les Chaumes, and Michel Gros' version is the archetype of a charming, early-drinking Vosne premier cru: red cherry, spice and silk. It is one of the few monopoles in Vosne outside the grands crus.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-clos-des-re.terroir: Almost flat, east-southeast exposure at about 245 m, on deep brown limestone-clay. The almost flat ground, about 3% gradient, and deep soil explain the wine's soft, early charm.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-clos-des-re.nerd_note: The Gros family has owned the clos since 1860.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-cros-parant.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Cros Parantoux
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-cros-parant.summary:
Cros Parantoux is the premier cru that Henri Jayer made into a legend. It is a little hollow (*cros*) of about 1 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 1.0 ha) tucked above Richebourg, cooler and higher than the grands crus below it. After phylloxera it lay abandoned and during the Second World War it grew Jerusalem artichokes; from 1951 Jayer cleared and replanted it, famously using dynamite to break the rock.

Jayer's Cros Parantoux from the 1970s to the mid-1990s are among the most expensive red wines ever sold at auction. Today the vineyard is split between Emmanuel Rouget, Jayer's nephew and successor (about 0.7 ha), and Domaine Méo-Camuzet (about 0.3 ha), whose parcel Jayer farmed as a sharecropper until 1988.

The wine is less exuberant than Richebourg and more mineral: dark cherry, violet, spice and a cool, precise structure that needs ten years or more.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-cros-parant.terroir: A small fold in the slope at 280 to 300 m, opening to the east and northeast, so it gets less afternoon sun than Richebourg. Thin soil and rubble over hard limestone at the top of the slope; the cooler exposure gives later ripening and higher acidity.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-cros-parant.nerd_note: Rouget still makes the wine in Jayer's cellar style, and both his and Méo-Camuzet's bottles are among the most tightly allocated in Burgundy.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-en-orveaux.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru En Orveaux
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-en-orveaux.summary:
En Orveaux is a 1.9 ha premier cru in Flagey-Echezeaux, sold as Vosne-Romanée, on the slope near the Combe d'Orveau above Echezeaux. Cathiard's En Orveaux is the best-known. The wine is cool and fine-boned.

It sits on the slope above the Echezeaux grand cru, on cool ground near the Combe d'Orveau, and its wines are among the most delicate and perfumed of the Vosne premier crus. Sylvain Cathiard's En Orveaux is the classic: red fruit, flowers and fine, silky tannin.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-en-orveaux.terroir: Northeast-facing at 280 to 310 m, moderately steep, on thin brown limestone soils. The northeast-facing slope is cool, which slows ripening and preserves the wine's delicate perfume.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-en-orveaux.nerd_note: Part of the lieu-dit En Orveaux is grand cru Echezeaux; only the upper part is premier cru.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-la-croix-ra.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru La Croix Rameau
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-la-croix-ra.summary:
La Croix Rameau is the smallest premier cru of Vosne at 0.60 ha, a pocket against the northern edge of Romanée-Saint-Vivant. Its soils and position are hard to distinguish from the grand cru, and growers have long argued it should be part of it. Lamarche, Cacheux and Coudray-Bizot share it.

Its soils are deep brown limestone-clay, like those of the lower Romanée-Saint-Vivant, and its wines show the same floral, spicy character in a slightly softer form. Lamarche's version, from a domaine whose own grand cru La Grande Rue was promoted in 1992, is the best-known.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-la-croix-ra.terroir: East-facing at about 250 m, gentle slope, brown limestone-clay like Romanée-Saint-Vivant.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-la-croix-ra.nerd_note: At about 0.6 ha it is smaller than several single-family holdings in the neighbouring grand cru.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-beaux-m.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Beaux Monts
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-beaux-m.summary:
Les Beaux Monts lies largely in the commune of Flagey-Echezeaux but is sold as Vosne-Romanée premier cru. At 12.0 ha it climbs the slope above Echezeaux and Les Suchots, and is split into Beaux Monts Bas and Hauts. The wines are fine, cool and perfumed, with more mineral tension than Les Suchots.

Leroy, Jean Grivot and Louis Jadot are major holders.

The INAO figures show that about 7.6 of its 12 ha lie in Flagey-Echezeaux and the rest in Vosne. It sits above the Suchots and next to the upper Echezeaux, on thinner, cooler ground than the lower premier crus, which is why it was a late-ripening site in the 20th century and has become one of the most sought-after Vosne premier crus in the warmer 21st.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-beaux-m.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 270 to 325 m, moderately steep. Thin brown limestone soils with stony rubble, over hard Bathonian limestone.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-beaux-m.nerd_note: Its lower section, Les Beaux Monts Bas, touches Echezeaux, while the top reaches the woods at more than 320 m.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-chaumes.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Chaumes
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-chaumes.summary:
Les Chaumes sits below La Tâche and Malconsorts on the flatter lower slope, at 6.9 ha. The wine is fruity, supple and early-drinking, a generous Vosne premier cru.

It lies on the flat lower ground east of Malconsorts and La Tâche, next to the Clos des Réas and running south to Nuits' Aux Boudots. Deep soil and gentle slope make it the most approachable of Vosne's premier crus, ready after five years, but the top versions from Méo-Camuzet and Arnoux-Lachaux have real depth.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-chaumes.terroir: Gentle east slope at 245 to 255 m, on deep brown limestone-clay. At around 245 to 255 m, it is one of the lowest premier crus of Vosne.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-chaumes.nerd_note: *Chaumes* means fallow or stubble ground, a common name for low-lying fields.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-gaudich.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Gaudichots
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-gaudich.summary: Les Gaudichots is a tiny remnant: most of the original lieu-dit was absorbed into La Tâche in the 1930s, after the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti bought the Liger-Belair La Tâche and the Gaudichots parcels were allowed to take the grand cru name. The 0.80 ha that remain premier cru lie beside and above La Tâche.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-gaudich.terroir: East-facing at 250 to 310 m, moderately steep, on thin stony limestone soils.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-gaudich.nerd_note: Forey is the main producer of Les Gaudichots premier cru today.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-petis-m.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Petis Monts
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-petis-m.summary:
Les Petits Monts (written 'Les Petis Monts' in the INAO register) is a steep 3.7 ha premier cru at the top of the slope above Richebourg and La Romanée. The wine is fine and cool, with red fruit and a mineral finish.

It sits on the steep upper slope above Richebourg and La Romanée, between Aux Raignots and Cros Parantoux, on thin soil over hard limestone. The register's 'Les Petis Monts' is a spelling quirk; labels say Les Petits Monts. Drouhin's version is the most widely available and shows the climat's cool, mineral elegance.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-petis-m.terroir: Steep, east-northeast-facing at 280 to 340 m. Thin, rocky soil on hard limestone. The northeast exposure and thin soil make it one of the coolest premier crus of Vosne.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-petis-m.nerd_note: Its neighbour Cros Parantoux sits just below its northern end.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-rouges.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Rouges
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-rouges.summary: Les Rouges is a high 2.6 ha premier cru in Flagey-Echezeaux, sold as Vosne-Romanée, above Echezeaux and Les Beaux Monts. The name comes from its reddish soil. The wine is fresh and cool, with red fruit.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-rouges.terroir: East-facing at 295 to 335 m, steep, on thin reddish limestone soils.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-rouges.nerd_note: Like the Beaux Monts and En Orveaux, it lies in Flagey but takes the Vosne name.

fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-suchots.name: Vosne-Romanée premier cru Les Suchots
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-suchots.summary:
Les Suchots is the largest premier cru in Vosne, at about 13 ha (the INAO delimitation gives 13.1 ha), on the gentle slope between Richebourg and Romanée-Saint-Vivant to the south and Echezeaux to the north. It is ranked just behind Cros Parantoux and Malconsorts, and its best wines rival Echezeaux.

The wine is perfumed and generous, with red and black cherry, spice and Vosne's silky, layered texture; it is slightly softer than Malconsorts. Comte Liger-Belair, Hudelot-Noëllat, Arnoux-Lachaux and Grivot all make fine versions.

Because it is large and lies between three grands crus, Les Suchots varies: the upper part, below the Beaux Monts and Aux Brulées and next to Richebourg, gives the most intense wines, while the lower part near La Croix Rameau and Romanée-Saint-Vivant is softer and more fragrant. Many growers argue that the best parcels deserve grand cru status as much as some of Echezeaux.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-suchots.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, gentle slope. Brown limestone-clay, deeper than in the grands crus above, over Bajocian limestone.
fr-vosne-romanee-premier-cru-les-suchots.nerd_note: Les Suchots touches three grands crus: Richebourg, Romanée-Saint-Vivant and Echezeaux.

fr-vougeot-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perrie.name: Vougeot premier cru Clos de la Perrière
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perrie.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perrie.summary:
The Clos de la Perrière is a walled 2.1 ha premier cru just outside the north wall of Clos de Vougeot, next to Les Amoureuses and Musigny. It was an old quarry, hence the name, and it is a monopole of Domaine Bertagna. The wine is supple and perfumed, with Chambolle's grace and Vougeot's warmth.

The clos sits on the steeper ground just outside the northwest corner of the Clos de Vougeot walls, between Musigny and Les Amoureuses above and the Petits Vougeots below. That thin, stony upper-slope soil explains its finesse, which many find closer to Chambolle than to the broader wines of the lower Clos de Vougeot.
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perrie.terroir: East-southeast-facing at 250 to 270 m, moderately steep. Thin stony limestone soils.
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-clos-de-la-perrie.nerd_note: Clos de Vougeot's grand cru vines begin on the other side of the wall, one of the sharpest classification boundaries on the Côte.

fr-vougeot-premier-cru-le-clos-blanc.name: Vougeot premier cru Le Clos Blanc
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-le-clos-blanc.summary:
Le Clos Blanc de Vougeot is one of the few walled white-wine vineyards on the Côte de Nuits. It is said to have been planted in 1110 by the Cistercian monks of Cîteaux, just outside the walls of their Clos de Vougeot. At 2.3 ha it is today a monopole of Domaine de la Vougeraie, which took it over from L'Héritier-Guyot.

The wine is mainly Chardonnay, and it is firmer and more mineral than most Côte de Beaune whites: lemon, white flowers and a salty, stony finish.
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-le-clos-blanc.terroir: Gentle east-northeast slope at 245 to 255 m, just north of the Clos de Vougeot walls. White marl and limestone soils, paler and more calcareous than the brown soils of the clos.
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-le-clos-blanc.nerd_note: The clos takes its name from its white grapes and pale soil, not from any colour of wine.

fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-cras.name: Vougeot premier cru Les Crâs
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-cras.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-cras.summary: Les Crâs is a 3.8 ha premier cru at the northeastern corner of Vougeot, just outside the walls of the Clos and next to the Route des Grands Crus. The wine is a supple, perfumed Vougeot premier cru, mostly red.
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-cras.terroir: Almost flat, northeast exposure at about 245 m, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-cras.nerd_note: *Cras* means stony ground, and the same name turns up in Chambolle, Nuits and Meursault.

fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-petits-vougeo.name: Vougeot premier cru Les Petits Vougeots
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-petits-vougeo.grapes: Pinot Noir; Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc for the rare whites
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-petits-vougeo.summary:
Les Petits Vougeots is the largest of Vougeot's four premier crus, at 5.2 ha, just outside the north wall of Clos de Vougeot below Les Amoureuses. It gives a supple, perfumed red with Chambolle's red fruit and silk.

It sits directly below Les Amoureuses and outside the northern wall of the Clos de Vougeot, on deeper, more clay-rich soil than its Chambolle neighbour. The result is a wine with Chambolle's red fruit and perfume and a little more weight, often a good-value alternative to the grand cru next door.
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-petits-vougeo.terroir: East-facing at 240 to 255 m, gentle slope, on brown limestone-clay.
fr-vougeot-premier-cru-les-petits-vougeo.nerd_note: Vougeot is one of the smallest communes in Burgundy, and almost all of its vineyard is either Clos de Vougeot grand cru or these four premier crus.

fr-vouvray-le-clos-baudoin.name: Le Clos Baudoin
fr-vouvray-le-clos-baudoin.summary: A small walled vineyard (often spelled Clos Baudoin) on the slopes of Vouvray, once owned by the Poniatowski family and farmed by François Chidaine since 2006. His Clos Baudoin is a tense, mineral Vouvray from old vines.
fr-vouvray-le-clos-baudoin.terroir: The lieu-dit's 2.7 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 90 to 100 m, with a mean slope of about 9%, mostly south-east-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-vouvray-le-clos-baudoin.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.

fr-vouvray-le-clos-du-bourg.name: Le Clos du Bourg
fr-vouvray-le-clos-du-bourg.summary: A walled vineyard in the heart of Vouvray, on shallow clay and limestone over tuffeau, bought by Domaine Huet in 1953. Often considered the greatest of Huet's sites, Clos du Bourg gives the most powerful and complete Chenin of the estate.
fr-vouvray-le-clos-du-bourg.terroir: The lieu-dit's 6.0 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 85 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-vouvray-le-clos-du-bourg.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.

fr-vouvray-le-haut-lieu.name: Le Haut Lieu
fr-vouvray-le-haut-lieu.summary:
The plateau above Vouvray where Domaine Huet began: Victor Huet and his son Gaston bought Le Haut-Lieu in 1928. On deep clay over limestone (*argile à silex* over tuffeau), it gives the most open, supple of Huet's three single vineyards, in styles from sec to moelleux and sparkling depending on the year.

Gaston Huet, mayor of Vouvray for decades, made the estate a reference for Chenin Blanc; it converted to biodynamics in 1990.
fr-vouvray-le-haut-lieu.terroir: The lieu-dit's 10.8 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 95 to 105 m, on almost flat land (Copernicus DEM).
fr-vouvray-le-haut-lieu.nerd_note: Huet decides each vintage whether a site makes sec, demi-sec or moelleux, so the same vineyard can give three different wines in three years.
fr-vouvray-le-haut-lieu.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.

fr-vouvray-le-marigny.name: Le Marigny
fr-vouvray-le-marigny.summary: A large lieu-dit on the plateau above Vouvray, on clay with flint (*perruches*) over tuffeau, the classic soils of the Vouvray plateau above the Loire.
fr-vouvray-le-marigny.terroir: The lieu-dit's 17.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 80 to 95 m, with a mean slope of about 6%, facing south-east to east (Copernicus DEM).
fr-vouvray-le-marigny.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.

fr-vouvray-le-mont.name: Le Mont
fr-vouvray-le-mont.summary: A steep, south-facing slope at the edge of the tuffeau escarpment above the Loire, with thin, stony soils of flinty clay (*silex*) over limestone. Domaine Huet bought Le Mont in 1957; it gives its most mineral, tightly wound Vouvray, slow to open and very long-lived.
fr-vouvray-le-mont.terroir: The lieu-dit's 7.2 ha of AOC-delimited land lies at about 60 to 100 m, with a mean slope of about 21%, mostly south-facing (Copernicus DEM).
fr-vouvray-le-mont.classification: Lieu-dit (named place in the land register) within the Vouvray AOC. It is not a separate appellation, but the name may appear on the label after Vouvray when all the grapes come from it.
